Document Title: Directive (EU) 2022/2464 amending Regulation (EU) No 537/2014, Directive 2004/109/EC, Directive 2006/43/EC and Directive 2013/34/EU, as regards corporate sustainability reporting (Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive)
Family Title: Directive (EU) 2022/2464 amending Regulation (EU) No 537/2014 and others, as regards corporate sustainability reporting (Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive or CSRD)
Family Summary: This Directive amends the previous directive governing the reporting of non-financial information in financial disclosures. It extends the scope of reporting obligations to a much wider set of companies headquartered or operating in the European Union. They new obligations will apply from the 2024 financial year.The Directive requires member states to introduce measures to ensure that sustainability disclosures include information on plans and strategies to ensure a corporate entity's business model and strategy are compatible with the transition to a sustainable economy, the global temperate target of 1.5 Degrees, and the goal of achieving climate neutrality by 2050, as well as the exposure of the entity to coal, oil and gas.The Commission is mandated to adopt delegated acts supplementing the Directive and providing sustainability reporting standards for both large entities and small and medium sized businesses. These shall specify that reporting should include scope 1, 2 and "where relevant" scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions. Businesses are also required to report on social and human rights factors. Reporting standards should be aligned with the work of the Task Force for Climate Related Financial Disclosures.

Document Title: Directive (EU) 2023/1791 on energy efficiency and amending Regulation (EU) 2023/955 (recast)
Family Title: Directive (EU) 2023/1791 on energy efficiency and amending Regulation (EU) 2023/955 (recast) (Energy Efficiency Directive or EED)
Family Summary: Part of the EU's 'Fit for 55' package, a legislative package that aims to align the EU's climate, energy, land use, transport, and taxation policies with a GhG emissions reduction target of 55% by 2030 (compared with 1990 levels), this revised Directive require Member States to integrate the ‘energy efficiency first’ principle into all planning, policy and major investment decisions, with a view to meeting an increased EU target of no more than 1,023 Mt of oil equivalent (Mtoe) to be used in 2030. Annual energy savings by Member States will reach 1.5% by 2030, on average. The Directive obliges the public sector to reduce its final energy consumption by 1.9% each year (with the option to exclude public transport and armed forces). Member states are also obliged to ensure that at least 3% of publicly owned buildings are renovated each year to a net-zero/ zero-emissions standard.

Document Title: Future Made in Australia (Guarantee of Origin) Act 2024
Family Title: Future Made in Australia (Guarantee of Origin) Act 2024
Family Summary:
The Guarantee of Origin (GO) scheme is a voluntary framework for emissions accounting of products, and certification of renewable electricity. It supports the Australian Government’s Future Made in Australia plan to attract investment in low-carbon products and renewable electricity. 

It provides a transparent, publicly accessible record of the emissions associated with the production of key commodities and renewable electricity, rather than branding or certifying against a particular standard. This helps:

  •  producers make credible claims about their electricity generation and manufacturing activities;
  • enables consumers to make informed purchasing decisions; and
  • supports Australian businesses to access emerging low-emissions markets in Australia and overseas.

Document Title: Australian Government Drought Plan
Family Title: Australian Government Drought Plan
Family Summary:
This plan covers the period from 2024 to 2029. It is focused on farming businesses and communities, who are mostaffected by drought, particularly in the context of climate change.

The Australian Government’s approach to supporting the agricultural sector to manage drought is built around a3-stage cycle:• Preparing – before drought, prepare for drier times ahead;• Responding – during drought, implement plans and strategies to manage the impacts; and• Recovering – after drought, recover and consider lessons learned.

The purpose of this plan is to:• explain the Australian Government’s drought policy;• provide greater transparency about government drought decision-making;• specify key drought-related programs that support farming businesses and communities across the drought cycle;• show how governments and stakeholders can work together on drought-related issues;• explain the monitoring, evaluation and learning arrangements for drought policy; and• show how drought policy links to other government policies.

Document Title: Australia's Strategy for Nature 2024-2030
Family Title: Australia's Strategy for Nature 2024-2030
Family Summary:
The Strategy for Nature is a shared roadmap to better understand, care for and sustainably manage nature. One of the targets is to minimise the impact of climate change on biodiversity. The goals are to:

  1. Connect all Australians with nature;
  2. Care for nature in all its diversity; and
  3. Share and build knowledge.

Document Title: Transport and Infrastructure Net Zero Roadmap and Action Plan
Family Title: Transport and Infrastructure Net Zero Roadmap and Action Plan
Family Summary:
The Transport and Infrastructure Net Zero Roadmap and Action Plan is the sector plan for transport and transport infrastructure. It covers all transport modes and considers cross cutting issues including low carbon fuels, freight and supply chains, systemwide efficiencies and transport infrastructure.

This Plan is guided by five guiding principles: maximise emissions reduction, provide value for money, maximise economic opportunity, be inclusive and equitable and be evidence-based.

The priority actions are:

  • Invest in enabling low and zero emissions transport infrastructure;
  • Electrify and increase transport’s energy performance;
  • Switch to low carbon alternatives (LCLFs) to power transport where electrification is not feasible;
  • Innovate to expand cost competitive transport technology options; and
  • Scale up efforts to reduce embodied emissions in transport infrastructure.

Document Title: Resources Sector Plan
Family Title: Resources Sector Plan
Family Summary:
This Plan covers how the Australian resource sector will transition to a net zero economy. It does this by analysing opportunities in each sub-sector of minerals; oil and gas, including liquified natural gas; and coal resources.

The key objectives of the plan are:

  • Position Australia as a leading global supplier of low-emissions commodities;
  • Accelerate technology development and attract strategic investment across the sector; and
  • Lead a fair and equitable transition, with benefits for all Australians.

The decarbonisation pillars and actions are:

  • Reduce fuel combustion emissions through electrification and low-carbon fuels;
  • Reduce fugitive emissions through ventilation air methane (VAM) abatement, pre-drainage of coal methane, and reduced routine venting and flaring; and
  • Scale up carbon management technologies through carbon capture and storage.

Document Title: Net Zero in Government Operations Strategy
Family Title: Net Zero in Government Operations Strategy
Family Summary:
The Net Zero in Government Operations Strategy describes the approach for implementing the Australian Government’s commitment to achieve net zero in government operations by 2030. This target was included in Australia’s Nationally Determined Contribution Communication 2022 under the Paris Agreement. The Australian Government reaffirmed this ambitious target when it was one of 19 global partners to launch the Net Zero Government Initiative at the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change Conference of Parties meeting (COP27) in November 2022, and published its roadmap at COP28 on how it will reach net zero government operations through the Strategy.

A 2026-27 mid-term review will consider overall progress to date, domestic and international expectations at that time on climate action in government operations, and any recommended changes to policy or strategy to ensure the Government is still meeting its commitment to demonstrate leadership. The Net Zero in Government Operations Strategy supersedes the Energy Efficiency in Government Operations policy.

There are departmental emissions reduction plans following this Strategy.

Document Title: Net Zero Plan
Family Title: Net Zero Plan
Family Summary:
The Australian Government has set a target to reduce emissions to 62-70% below 2005 levels by 2035. The Net Zero Plan sets out how Australia will achieve a fair, orderly and efficient transition to net zero. It provides a framework for action that builds on Australia’s natural strengths, to ensure all Australians benefit.

The Plan demonstrates how Australia can transition while:

  • growing the economy
  • reducing cost pressures on households and businesses
  • creating new jobs.

The Plan identifies 5 priorities to guide Australia's transition to net zero:

  • Clean electricity across the economy.
  • Lowering emissions by electrification and efficiency.
  • Expanding clean fuel use.
  • Accelerating new technologies.
  • Net carbon removals scaled up.

The net zero plan is supported by six sector emissions reduction plans: electricity and energy; agriculture and land; the built environment; industry; resources; and transport.

Document Title: Net Zero Economy Authority Act 2024
Family Title: Net Zero Economy Authority Act 2024
Family Summary:
The Net Zero Economy Authority commenced as an independent statutory authority in accordance with the Net Zero Economy Authority Act 2024 on 11 December 2024. This Authority promotes economic transformation as Australia transitions to a net zero emissions economy.

The object of this Act is to:

(a) promote orderly and positive economic transformation as the world decarbonises; and

(b) facilitate the achievement of Australia’s greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets; and

(c) ensure Australia’s regions, communities and workers are supported to manage the impacts, and share in the benefits, of Australia’s transition to a net zero emissions economy.

Document Title: Nature Positive Plan: better for the environment, better for business
Family Title: Nature Positive Plan: better for the environment, better for business
Family Summary:
This Plan sets out the Australian government’s commitment to reform Australia’s environmental laws to better protect, restore and manage our unique environment.

The government supports the recommendation of the review that proponents be required to publish their expected Scope 1 and 2 emissions. Further, proponents will be required to disclose how their project aligns with Australia’s national and international obligations to reduce emissions. The changing climate will also be a mandatory consideration in environmental planning approaches. Improvements in information and guidance will support these reforms.

The government recognises the risks global warming poses to Australia’s unique ecosystems and the link between climate and biodiversity. They will address this by embedding climate considerations in all roles and functions of government. In addition to their commitments to reduce national emissions to 43% below 2005 levels by 2030, and to achieve net zero emissions by 2050, the government will integrate climate change considerations, where relevant, throughout national environmental law without duplicating existing mechanisms for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. This includes improved transparency in project assessments; improved planning and landscape-scale approaches to facilitate adaptation to climate change; and improved information and climate-impact modelling.

Document Title: 2024 National Waste Policy Action Plan
Family Title: 2024 National Waste Policy Action Plan
Family Summary:
The 2024 National Waste Policy Action Plan implements the 2018 National Waste Policy, which provides a framework for waste and resource recovery in Australia to achieve sustainable development goals (SDGs), including SDG 13: Climate Action. It includes targets and priorities to guide investment and efforts to 2030.

The seven targets are:

  1. Ban on export of waste plastic, paper, glass and tyres, commencing in the second half of 2020;
  2. Reduce total waste generated in Australia by 10% per person by 2030;
  3. 80% average resource recovery rate from all waste streams following the waste hierarchy by 2030;
  4. Significantly increase the use of recycled content by governments and industry;
  5. Continued phase out of problematic and unnecessary plastics;
  6. Halve the amount of organic waste sent to landfill for disposal by 2030; and
  7. Make comprehensive, economy-wide and timely data publicly available to support better consumer, investment and policy decisions.

Document Title: National Strategy for Food Security in Remote Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Communities 2025-2035
Family Title: National Strategy for Food Security in Remote Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Communities 2025-2035
Family Summary:
This Strategy aims to coordinate action across Australia to address the unique and specific food security needs of First Nations people living in remote communities, including to improve the preparedness and resilience of First Nations communities to the impact of climate change.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people have sustained vast and varied food systems that maintained collective healthand wellbeing for tens of thousands of years. The disruption of traditional ways of gathering and preparing food has had a significant impact on food security and health outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. Many remote communities now experience food insecurity at a much higher rate than Australians as a whole.

Document Title: National Greenhouse and Energy Act 2007
Family Title: National Greenhouse and Energy Act 2007
Family Summary:
The first object of this Act is to introduce a single national reporting framework for the reporting and dissemination of information related to greenhouse gas emissions, greenhouse gas projects, energy consumption and energy production of corporations to: (b) inform government policy formulation and the Australian public; and (c) meet Australia’s international reporting obligations; and (d) assist Commonwealth, State and Territory government programs and activities; and (e) avoid the duplication of similar reporting requirements in the States and Territories.

The second object of this Act is to contribute to the achievement of Australia’s greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets by ensuring that each of the following outcomes (the safeguard outcomes) are achieved: (a) net covered emissions of greenhouse gases from the operation of a designated large facility do not exceed the baseline applicable to the facility; (b) total net safeguard emissions for all of the financial years between 1 July 2020 and 30 June 2030 do not exceed a total of 1,233 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalence; (c) net safeguard emissions decline to: (i) no more than 100 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalence for the financial year beginning on 1 July 2029; and (ii) zero for any financial year to begin after 30 June 2049; (d) the 5-year rolling average safeguard emissions for each financial year that begins after 30 June 2024 are lower than the past 5-year rolling average safeguard emissions for that financial year; (e) the responsible emitter for each designated large facility has a material incentive to invest in reducing covered emissions from the operation of the facility; (f) the competitiveness of trade-exposed industries is appropriately supported as Australia and its regions seize the opportunities of the move to a global net zero economy.

Document Title: Industry Sector Plan
Family Title: Industry Sector Plan
Family Summary:
The Industry Sector Plan covers how the Australian industrial and waste sectors will transition to a net zero economy. It addresses 9 industrial subsectors that represent the greatest opportunity and need for decarbonisation, and those most impacted by the economy’s transition. These are: 

  • alumina and aluminium manufacturing;
  • food and beverages manufacturing;
  • metals refining and smelting;
  • cement and concrete production;
  • iron and steel manufacturing;
  • pulp, paper and paperboard manufacturing;
  • chemicals and plastics manufacturing;
  • manufacturing and additional industries; and
  • waste and resource recovery.

Document Title: Future Made in Australia (Production Tax Credit and Other Measures) Act 2025
Family Title: Future Made in Australia (Production Tax Credit and Other Measures) Act 2025
Family Summary:
This legislation implements production tax incentives for renewable hydrogen and critical minerals.

The incentives are:

  1. Hydrogen Production Tax Incentive worth $2 per kilogram of renewable hydrogen produced between 2027–2028 and 2039–40 for up to ten years per project.
  2. Critical Minerals Production Tax Incentive worth ten per cent of relevant processing and refining costs for Australia’s 31 critical minerals, for critical minerals processed and refined between 2027–28 and 2039–40, for up to ten years per project.

The incentives will support Australia’s efforts to decarbonise our industries, and produce and process more of the minerals needed for the energy transition.

Document Title: First National Drought Agreement 2018-2024
Family Title: National Drought Agreement
Family Summary:
The National Drought Agreement (NDA) is an agreement between the Commonwealth of Australia and New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland, Western Australia, South Australia, Tasmania, the Australian Capital Territory, and the Northern Territory.

Parties acknowledge that drought is one of a number of business risks that farmers and other businesses should actively prepare for and adapt to. Promoting and enabling a culture of self-responsibility is a shared goal, and drought policy and programs should support the agricultural sector and rural communities to prepare for drought and climate variability to enhance their long-term sustainability and resilience. Climate science states Australia can expect increased and more extreme climate variability.

Family Summary:

The Second National Action Plan reflects what communities say is needed to mature the system, considers the existing and future opportunities for disaster risk reduction and resilience activities across Australia, and aligns them towards our risk reduction goals.

Document Title: Electricity and Energy Sector Plan
Family Title: Electricity and Energy Sector Plan
Family Summary:
The Electricity and Energy Sector Plan sets out a roadmap for the next stages of our energy transformation to help households, industry and governments to navigate and prosper as Australia decarbonises its energy system. 

The pathway to 2050 sets out 3 shifts in our energy system to get to net zero:

  • Use energy more efficiently. Using all energy – including electricity, gas and liquid fuels – wisely will reduce how much energy we need and how much infrastructure we need to support this.
  • Electrify and fuel-switch. Changing how we power activities will allow us to take advantage of cheaper, cleaner energy sources, including renewable electricity.
  • Scale clean energy supply. Growing how much clean energy we can deliver will allow us to keep powering homes, businesses and industry as we reduce fossil fuel use.

The Plan focuses on actions to take Australia to 2035, and set Australia up for beyond 2035, based on the following phases of transformation:

  • Now to 2030. Reducing electricity sector emissions to reach 82% renewable generation while other sectors decarbonise through electrification.
  • 2030 to 2035. Continue decarbonising transport, built environment and industry sectors through electrification and energy efficiency.

Document Title: Disaster Ready Fund Act 2019
Family Title: Disaster Ready Fund Act 2019
Family Summary:
This Act establishes the Disaster Ready Fund, which will enhance Australia's ability to make arrangements with persons or bodies in relation to natural disasters; and make grants to persons or bodies in relation to natural disasters.

The Disaster Ready Fund consists of the Disaster Ready Fund Special Account; and the investments of the Disaster Ready Fund. The Future Fund Board is responsible for deciding how to invest the Disaster Ready Fund. In doing so, the Future Fund Board is bound by the Disaster Ready Fund Investment Mandate given to it by the responsible Ministers.

The Emergency Management Minister may, on behalf of the Commonwealth: make an arrangement with a person or body in relation to a natural disaster; and make a grant to a person or body in relation to a natural disaster.

This Act establishes the Disaster Ready Fund Payments Special Account. Amounts will be transferred from the Disaster Ready Fund Special Account to the Disaster Ready Fund Payments Special Account. The purposes of the Disaster Ready Fund Payments Special Account are to pay amounts payable by the Commonwealth under arrangements relating to a natural disaster, and to make grants relating to a natural disaster. Amounts will be transferred from the Disaster Ready Fund Special Account to the Federation Reform Fund for the purposes of making grants to the States and Territories in relation to natural disasters.

Document Title: Critical Infrastructure Resilience Strategy
Family Title: Critical Infrastructure Resilience Strategy
Family Summary: The Critical Infrastructure Resilience Strategy will uplift the security and resilience of Australia's critical infrastructure in the face of all hazards and advance national security, the economy and social prosperity. Disruptions to critical infrastructure systems can result from all types of natural and human-made hazards and threats, such as major weather events or human error. Such disruptions can create a cascade of consequences with profound effects on societies, communities and interconnected infrastructure systems. This Strategy aims to take into account extreme weather events, which are climate impacts that affect critical infrastructure resilience.

Document Title: Climate Change Authority Engagement Strategy 2023-25
Family Title: Climate Change Authority Engagement Strategy 2023-25
Family Summary:
The Climate Change Authority is a statutory agency established under the Climate Change Authority Act 2011. Their purpose is to provide evidence-based advice on the response to climate change in order to:

  • accelerate emissions reductions and help Australia play its role in the global effort to limit temperature increases; and
  • enhance Australia’s prosperity and resilience as the climate changes and the world transitions to net zero emissions.

This Strategy lists down engagement approaches and consultation principles, which contractors are also required to follow.

Document Title: Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011
Family Title: Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011
Family Summary:
The Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011 set up a scheme for the issue of Australian Carbon Credit Units (ACCUs) in relation to eligible offsets projects. It was part of a package of three Acts to establish the Carbon Farming Initiative, including the Australian National Registry of Emissions Units Act 2011 and the Carbon Credits (Consequential Amendments) Act 2011. The package of Acts established the existence of ACCUs as personal property, which are generally transferable, and can be sold domestically or internationally subject to regulation.

The Act contains provisions for the Emissions Reduction Fund, and provides for the Clean Energy Regulator to conduct auctions and enter into contracts to purchase emissions reductions; enable a broader range of emissions reduction projects to be approved; and amend the project eligibility criteria and processes for approving projects and crediting carbon credit units.

Document Title: Built Environment Sector Plan
Family Title: Built Environment Sector Plan
Family Summary:
Actions under this Plan seek to achieve the following key outcomes:

  • A low‑emissions and low‑energy built environment to support Australia’s emissions reduction targets;
  • A built environment that is fit for purpose, liveable, provides thermal comfort and is resilient to a changing climate; and
  • A fair and equitable built environment transition where no one is left behind.

Foundation actions are: accelerate electrification and increase energy performance; ensure a fair and equitable transition; support consumers to make informed decisions; continue collaboration with states and territories; support materials efficiency; innovate to expand emissions reduction; and create a resilient built environment.

Document Title: Aviation White Paper
Family Title: Aviation White Paper
Family Summary:
The White Paper and the development of its 56 policy initiatives was informed by extensive consultation on the Aviation Green Paper with the aviation industry, state and territory governments, and the Australian community. These 56 policy initiatives cover 10 key areas including:

  • a better passenger experience
  • a competitive and efficient aviation sector
  • a skilled, secure and productive workforce
  • maximising aviation’s contribution to net zero
  • connecting regional Australia
  • regenerating General Aviation
  • a balanced approach to airport planning and noise
  • world leading safety, security and airspace regulation
  • enabling new aviation technologies
  • connecting Australia to the world 

Climate-related initiatives include providing funding to regional airports to increase climate resilience and requirign additional information in airport master plans to address climate change resilience and decarbonisation.

Document Title: National Disaster Risk Reduction Framework
Family Title: National Disaster Risk Reduction Framework
Family Summary:
The National Disaster Risk Reduction Framework is a multisector collaboration led by the National Resilience Taskforcewithin the Australian Government Department of Home Affairs. The National Disaster Risk Reduction Framework outlines a national, comprehensive approach to proactively reducing disaster risk, now and into the future.

The 2030 Vision for Disaster Risk Reduction in Australia is to actively reduce disaster risk and limit the impacts of disasters oncommunities and economies. All sectors of society understand and respond to social, environmental, technological and demographic changes which have the potential to prevent, create or exacerbate disaster risks.All sectors of society:– make disaster risk-informed decisions,– are accountable for reducing risks within their control, and– invest in reducing disaster risk in order to limit the cost of disasters when they occur.

Document Title: Agriculture and Land Sector Plan
Family Title: Agriculture and Land Sector Plan
Family Summary:
The Agriculture and Land Sector Plan establishes a framework for the sectors to contribute to Australia’s net zero target. The framework includes three strategic objectives to underpin agriculture and land’s contribution to net zero:

  1. Australian producers remain global leaders in low-emissions food and fibre production;
  2. support of diverse landscapes, balancing agricultural production, carbon storage and nature repair; and
  3. decarbonisation of agriculture and land must deliver real benefits for regional communities, producers and land managers, including First Nations peoples.

Four foundational areas for action will guide efforts and investment:

  1. Understand emissions at the enterprise and national level;
  2. support innovation to deliver commercially viable abatement options;
  3. strengthen on-ground action; and
  4. enhance land’s role in a net zero economy.

Document Title: 2024 Integrated System Plan
Family Title: 2024 Integrated System Plan
Family Summary:
The Integrated System Plan (ISP) is a 25-year roadmap to transition the National Electricity Market (NEM) to net zero by 2050, released by the Australian Energy Market Operator. The Plan confirms that renewable energy connected with transmission and distribution, firmed with storage and backed up by gas-powered generation, is the lowest-cost way to supply electricity to homes and businesses as Australia transitions to a net zero economy.

The Plan identifies almost 10,000km of new transmission lines are required by 2050 to connect new sources of generation and meet reliability targets at the lowest cost to consumers. Five projects, or 2,500 km, are already underway as committed and anticipated projects. The plan identifies a further 12 projects that are actionable and should continue through planning and delivery.

Crucial technologies factored into the roadmap are domestic rooftop solar panels and associated batteries, smart systems and electric vehicles, also known as consumer energy resources. Home batteries, if well-coordinated, can save consumers around $4.1 billion in avoided costs for additional grid-scale investment.

Document Title: Addendum to 2019 Trajectory for Low Energy Buildings - Existing Buildings
Family Title: Trajectory for Low Energy Buildings
Family Summary:
The Trajectory is a national strategy for Commonwealth, State and Territory action across all buildings.

The Trajectory has been created by the Commonwealth, States and Territories under the leadership of the Energy and Climate Change Ministerial Council (ECMC).

The Trajectory provides an opportunity to work towards a net zero emissions building sector by 2050 while:

  • lowering costs for households and businesses
  • improving building comfort for all Australians.

The updated Trajectory replaces the 2019 Trajectory for Low Energy Buildings and its Addendum.

Building on the ambition of 2019, the updated Trajectory reflects the following current and emerging drivers of change:

  • net zero ambitions
  • energy efficiency
  • fuel switching and electrification
  • energy demand flexibility
  • embodied carbon emissions
  • resilience
  • green finance
  • refrigerant emissions.

The updated objectives of the Trajectory are to:

  • reduce energy costs for households and businesses
  • drive emissions towards net zero
  • reduce and manage demand on the electricity grid
  • keep people healthy, comfortable and safe from climate hazards
  • ensure equitable access to energy performance benefits.

Document Title: New Energy Vehicle Industry Development Plan (2021-2035)
Family Title: New Energy Vehicle Industry Development Plan and 2020 New Energy Vehicle Promotion Subsidy Plan
Family Summary: The New Energy Vehicle Industry Development Plan aims at supporting the development of electric , plug-in hybrid electric and fuel cell vehicles in the country over the period 2021-2035. The 2020 New Energy Vehicle Promotion Subsidy Plan sets governmental support for the years 2020 to 2022 to accelerate the electrification of vehicles in the fields of public transport, urban public transport, road passenger transport, rental (including online car-hailing), environmental sanitation, urban logistics and distribution, postal express, civil aviation, airport, and party and government organs that meet the requirements of the public sector.

Document Title: Renewable Energy Law of the People's Republic of China
Family Title: Renewable Energy Law of the People's Republic of China
Family Summary:
This Act describes duties of the government, business and other users in renewable energy development and use. It includes measures and goals relating to mandatory grid connection, price management regulation, differentiated pricing, special funds and tax reliefs, and sets the goal to realise 15% of China's energy from renewable sources by 2020. The Act requires the government to encourage and support the application of renewable energy in various areas. The Act also requires that the government budget establishes a renewable energy development fund.

In terms of monitoring arrangements, it requires that energy authorities of the State Council are responsible for organising and co-ordinating national surveys and management of renewable energy resources, and work with related departments to establish technical regulations for resource surveys. Relevant departments of the State Council, within their respective authorities, are responsible for related renewable energy resource surveys. The survey results will be summarised by the energy authority in the State Council.

Energy authorities of the State Council must set mid- and long-term targets for the total volume of renewable energy at the national level, which shall be implemented and released to the pubic after being approved by the State Council. Notice 25/2021 determines the objectives for solar and wind in particular for the year 2021.

A report of the Congress' Law Enforcement Inspection Team of the Standing Committee inspecting the implementation of the law was published in December 2019. A draft amendment of the law was published in 2020 for consultation.

Document Title: Climate Action Act
Family Title: Climate Action Act (Act XVI of 2024, Chapter 643)
Family Summary:
This Act establishes a legal framework for climate action and provides for the establishment of the Climate Action Authority, the national competent authority responsible for the exercise of climate action, to coordinate and oversee mitigation and adaptation policy and measures and any matters ancillary thereto, and to provide for the reporting of such climate action.

This Act contains provisions establishing duties: that it shall be the duty of every person, together with the Government to protect the climate and assist in the taking of preventive and remedial measures to protect the climate; and that it shall be the duty of the Government to protect the climate for the present and future generations. It also contains provisions relating to a Climate Action Fund.

This Act is a reform of the previous Climate Action Act, Act XVII of 2015 (Chapter 543), which has been repealed. The reforms include a Climate Action Authority responsible for the regulation regarding climate related matters in Malta, including setting national or sector-specific targets in consultation with respective Ministries and to prepare the national long-term strategy, the national adaptation strategy and the National Energy and Climate Plan. Another reform is the introduction of the National Climate Action Council comprised of experts in any climate-related fields including scientific, public policy, finance, economic and social fields, who will be an independent statutory body providing advice to the Maltese government on climate action in Malta.

Document Title: State planning guidelines for climate and energy
Family Title: State planning guidelines for climate and energy
Family Summary:
The purpose of the guidelines is to ensure that climate and energy are emphasized in planning according to the Planning and Building Act 2008 and other government exercises and activities in the state, municipalities and county authorities. Climate includes both the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, carbon capture and storage and adaptation to expected climate change. The guidelines clarify the state's expectations of how this should be done, and the state's contribution to the knowledge base and guidance.

The guidelines should contribute to:

a.Norway's national climate goals as set out in the Climate Act;

b.the basis of life and natural diversity for current and future generations;

c.good security of energy supply;

d.society and ecosystems' preparation for and adaptation to climate change; and

e. the work to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, more efficient and flexible energy use, better climate adaptation and other environmental goals;

f. the clarification of roles and responsibilities of state, county authorities and municipalities; and

g. municipalities and county authorities prioritising climate and energy considerations in their exercise of authority, and the municipalities in their activities.

Document Title: Regulations on the exploitation of subsea reservoirs on the continental shelf for the storage of CO2 and on the transport of CO2 on the continental shelf
Family Title: Regulations on the storage of CO2 and on the transport of CO2 on the continental shelf
Family Summary: These are the Regulations on the exploitation of subsea reservoirs on the continental shelf for the storage of CO2 and on the transport of CO2 on the continental shelf. The purpose is to contribute to sustainable energy and industrial production by facilitating the utilization of undersea reservoirs on the continental shelf for environmentally safe storage of CO2 as a measure to combat climate change. The Regulations provide for research and exploration permits to be granted by the State, liability in the event of pollution damage, and safety requirements.

Document Title: Regulations on quota obligation and trading in quotas for greenhouse gas emissions (climate quota regulations)
Family Title: Greenhouse Gas Emission Trading Act, No. 99 of 2004
Family Summary: The Act aims to limit emissions of GHGs in a cost-effective manner by means of a system involving the duty to surrender GHG emission allowances and freely transferable emission allowances. It establishes government authority over the number of allowances to be allocated and which of these allowances will be issued free of charge. It regulates reporting and control related to emissions and allowances and sets out penal measures for those operators not complying with reporting obligations. It authorises the Norwegian Emissions Trading Registry to contain information on the allocation, issue, holding, transfer, surrender and cancellation of allowances. The pollution control authorities will control and verify the reports on GHG emissions submitted by each operator.

Document Title: Regulations on environmental impact assessments
Family Title: Regulations on environmental impact assessments
Family Summary: These Regulations require an assessment of how vulnerable a municipal or zoning plan or designated measure (e.g. crude oil refineries, power plants, smelting installations, chemical installations, railway lines, large buildings etc.) is to climate change and natural hazards such as floods, landslides, storm surges and sea level rise. The impact assessment shall identify, describe and assess impacts resulting from climate change, including risks from sea level rise, storm surges, floods and landslides.

Document Title: Public Procurement Regulations
Family Title: Public Procurement Act 2016
Family Summary:
Section 5 of this Act states that state, county and municipal authorities and public law bodies shall adapt their procurement practices so that they contribute to reducing harmful environmental impacts and promoting climate-friendly solutions where relevant. This shall be done, among other things, by the contracting authority taking life-cycle costs into account.

From 1 January 2024, the provisions of Public Procurement Regulations which mandates that climate and environmental considerations must generally be weighted with a minimum of 30 per cent in public procurements, came into effect Alternatively, climate and environmental requirements can be included in the specifications if it is clear that this will provide a better climate and environmental effect. The aim of the climate and environmental requirements is to reduce the GHG emissions or environmental impact of public procurements.

Document Title: National Soil Strategy
Family Title: National Soil Strategy
Family Summary:
The National Soil Strategy is Australia’s first national policy on soil. It was released in May 2021 and sets out how Australia will value, manage and improve its soil for the next 20 years. Healthy soils are central to delivering resilience to climate change and natural disasters, meeting Australia's emission reduction targets, growing its agriculture industry, and securing human health, food and water security, biodiversity and economic growth.

The strategy’s 3 goals are:

  1. prioritise soil health
  2. empower soil innovation and stewards
  3. strengthen soil knowledge and capability.

Document Title: Guyana Low Carbon Development Strategy 2030
Family Title: Guyana Low Carbon Development Strategy 2030
Family Summary:
Guyana's Low Carbon Development Strategy 2030 forms the backbone of the country's efforts to mitigate and adapt to climate change from 2022-2030. The four primary objeectives of the strategy are: to value ecosystem services through voluntary global carbon markets and a bilateral partnership with Norway; to invest in clean energy, boosting green economic growth; to protect against climate change and biodiversity loss domestically; and to contribute to global climate goals

To maintain ecosystem services, the strategy aims to ensure that mining activities are low-impact and certified with respect to their effects on forestry. It also aims to sustainably regulate commercial forestry, expand natural mangrove systems as coastal protection, protect watersheds and enhance monitoring/research capacity nationally.

To achieve a clean electricity supply, the strategy plans to meet growing demand via a mixture of hydroelectricity and natural gas, with solar energy also playing a key role and combining with enhanced battery storage to provision off-grid regions. It also promotes early measures to electrify transport, including tax reductions for electric vehicles and the subsidised construction of charging stations.

To adapt to climate risks, a key element of the strategy is riverine and coastal flood prevention, through soft (mangroves and ecosystem restoration) and hard techniques. This aims to safeguard against these major risks to the agricultural and urban sectors concentrated around the coast.

On a global level the strategy supports carbon pricing and the achievement of net zero goals by 2050 and a 28% reduction in oil demand by 2030, while acknowledging the significant role of oil in Guyana's economy and emphasising the need for major incumbents in the sector to contribute to the same goals.

Document Title: Coordinated Interagency Transmission Authorizations and Permits Program (CITAP)
Family Title: Coordinated Interagency Transmission Authorizations and Permits Program (CITAP)
Family Summary: This program sets a 2-year timeline for the federal permitting process for transmission infrastructure, making the process more efficient without sacrificing the quality of environmental reviews. The program seeks to spur economic growth and modernize aging electric grid infrastructure by expanding access to clean energy and advanced energy technologies.

Family Summary:

  • a skilled, portable and adaptable workforce; and
  • an informed understanding and acceptance of freight operations.

Document Title: Guyana National Land Use Plan
Family Title: Guyana National Land Use Plan (2013)
Family Summary: Guyana's National Land Use Plan provides a long-term strategic framework to guide land development nationally. Rather than designating specific zones for particular uses, it aims to provide a range of comprehensive viable and sustainable options. The plan names climate change adaptation as a key motivating factor, emphasising the need to develop away from the coastal plain, where flood risks will increase over time and rainfall patterns will shift. It also acknowledges the national and global importance of Guyana's forests and their carbon stock for climate change mitigation, and aims to ensure that new developments do not contribute to deforestation where possible.

Document Title: Guyana's National Forest Plan
Family Title: Guyana's National Forest Plan
Family Summary: The National Forest Plan provides a set of actions and interventions to effectively and sustainably manage Guyana's forest resources, accompanying the National Forest Policy Statement (2018). The plan is driven by four 'specific objectives': deriving sustainable economic benefits; enhancing conservation; enhancing governance to promote sustainable management; and building human and institutional capacity to achieve the above goals. Its interventions for economic benefits are primarily aimed at forestry efficiency improvements and job/revenue growth while reducing deforestation. Its conservation interventions aim to reduce forest fires and pest/disease outbreaks, and improve forest quality monitoring, all while maintaining the share of forest goods and services in GDP. Its governance interventions aim to generally streamline forestry-related proceedings and reduce costs, while maintaining strong and transparent stakeholder contact. Its capacity building interventions aim to enhance research outputs and public engagement, promoting efficiency gains downstream of this.

Family Title: National Freight and Supply Chain Strategy National Action Plan 2025-2029
Family Summary:
The National Freight and Supply Chain Strategy (Strategy) sets the agenda for a collaborative approach to deliver government action across all freight modes. The Strategy aims to ensure freight and supply chains continue to provide reliable access to vital goods and materials from across the globe, as well as support valuable export supply chains that are vital to Australia’s economy. In relation to climate, Australia will decarbonise transport and increase resilience. It will expand on the risk assessment by conducting supply chain resilience modelling on a 5-yearly basis, incorporating the latest data on freight demand and climate risk, and invest in the whole-of-life resilience of land transport infrastructure to address emerging issues associated with natural disasters, climate risk, and security, thereby enabling freight and supply chain resilience.

Document Title: Offshore Electricity Infrastructure Act 2021
Family Title: Offshore Electricity Infrastructure Act 2021
Family Summary:
The Offshore Electricity Infrastructure Act 2021 (OEI Act) sets out a licensing and regulatory framework for the construction, installation, operation, maintenance and decommissioning of offshore renewable energy and offshore electricity transmission infrastructure.  The OEI Act framework applies to offshore locations from three nautical miles from the coast to the boundary of Australia’s exclusive economic zone (coastal waters remain the responsibility of the adjacent state and Northern Territory governments). The OEI Act framework operates under the principle of shared use of the offshore marine environment, recognising all users and balancing competing interests.

Under the OEI Act framework, the Minister for Energy makes all licensing decisions, including declaring areas suitable for offshore renewable energy infrastructure, both at a commercial scale and for research and development of new and emerging technologies. The declaration of an offshore area is informed through consultation with stakeholders including existing marine users, state and territory governments and Federal Government agencies with responsibilities in the marine area and the community.

In deciding whether an area is suitable for offshore renewable energy infrastructure, the Minister must have regard to the following:

(a) the potential impacts of the construction, installation, commissioning, operation, maintenance or decommissioning of offshore renewable energy infrastructure in the area on other marine users and interests;

(b) any submissions received in accordance with particular notice of proposal from the Minister;

(c) any advice received as a result of a designated consultation;

(d) Australia’s international obligations in relation to the area;

(e) Australia’s greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets.

Document Title: National Framework for Climate Services - Ethiopia: Coordination Guideline
Family Title: National Framework for Climate Services - Strategic Plan: 2021-2030
Family Summary: The vision behind Ethiopia’s National Framework for Climate Services (NFCS) Strategic Plan is “seeing Ethiopians whose livelihoods are resilient through climate-informed decisions.” More specifically, it aims to help five priority sectors (health, agriculture, disaster risk management, water resources and environment) achieve their development and adaptation goals in the face of a variable and changing climate. This will be accomplished by supporting decision-makers to use weather and climate information to understand, anticipate and manage climate-related risks. The NFCS Strategic Plan also strengthens climate services as an adaptation measure, contributing to Ethiopia’s National Adaptation Plan (NAP).The NFCS Strategic Plan is guided by a theory of change which recognizes that Ethiopia’s development across climate-sensitive sectors will be more resilient to climate impacts if targeted decision-makers from local to national levels understand, anticipate, and effectively manage climate-related risks.

Document Title: Directive 2008/98/EC - Waste Framework Directive (Consolidated text)
Family Title: Directive 2008/98/EC on waste, amended by Directive (EU) 2018/851 and last amended by Directive (EU) 2025/1892  - (Waste Framework Directive)
Family Summary: The Waste Framework Directive establishes a legal framework for treating waste in the European Union (EU). The framework establishes the core principles of waste management across the EU to protect human health and the environment while promoting resource efficiency and a circular economy. It introduces the waste hierarchy — prioritising prevention, reuse, recycling, recovery, and finally disposal — and enshrines the “polluter pays” principle along with extended producer responsibility, ensuring producers bear financial or organisational responsibility for their products’ end-of-life management. The 2018 amendment (Directive 2018/851) strengthened the circular economy focus by setting new recycling targets, improving separate collection systems, and promoting measures for waste prevention and reuse. The last amendment (Directive (EU) 2025/1892 excluded from the scope of the directive gaseous effluents emitted into the atmosphere and carbon dioxide captured and transported for the purposes of geological storage and geologically stored.

Document Title: National Climate Resilience and Adaptation Strategy 2021-2025
Family Title: National Climate Resilience and Adaptation Strategy
Family Summary:
The National Climate Resilience and Adaptation Strategy (the Strategy) positions Australia to better anticipate, manage and adapt to climate change. The Strategy is designed to support governments, communities and businesses to better adapt, recognising that adaptation is a shared responsibility that requires sustained and ongoing action. The Strategy operates across four domains — natural, built, social and economic — to drive forward adaptation. It recognises that effective adaptation must be: informed by the best available science and information; delivered through partnerships and investments; and guided by effective governance and coordination.

The Strategy details three objectives to enable more effective adaptation across Australia:

  • Drive investment and action through collaboration;
  • Improve climate information and services; and
  • Assess progress and improve over time.

Document Title: National Strategy for Digital Agriculture and its Action Plan (2023-2027)
Family Title: National Strategy for Digital Agriculture in Niger and its Action Plan (2023-2027)
Family Summary:
The National Strategy for Digital Agriculture in Niger (2023–2035) aims to harness digital technologies to strengthen food security and rural livelihoods through a sustainable transformation of the agricultural sector. Its vision emphasizes climate-resilient agriculture by ensuring the sustainable use of rural ecosystems, supporting efficient production systems, improving value chains, and expanding access to diversified food products. The strategy identifies four overarching objectives that align with Niger’s broader development agenda: sustainable management of agricultural ecosystems, improved agronomic and environmental performance of farms, stronger agricultural value chains, and increased use of digital services by rural communities.

To achieve these goals, the 2023–2027 Action Plan outlines six priority areas, many of which directly address climate change adaptation and resilience. These include deploying digital tools for preserving ecosystems, biodiversity, soils, and water resources; supporting secure land and pastoral management in the context of growing pressures on natural resources; and promoting efficient, climate-smart production systems that strengthen food and nutrition security. The plan also emphasises building rural actors’ digital skills, improving access to information and services, and enhancing market opportunities. Overall, this strategy will reinforce the country's capacity to adapt to climate change while fostering inclusive rural development.

Document Title: National Action Plan For Capacity Building For Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2018)
Family Title: National Action Plan For Capacity Building For Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2018)
Family Summary:
The National Action Plan for Capacity Building for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Preparedness, and Emergency Response (2015-2018) is structured around four main priorities.

The first priority is the Institutional Framework, which focuses on making DRR a national and local priority and establishing a clear institutional structure to manage related activities. The second priority, Risk and Disaster Identification, aims to pinpoint, assess, and monitor disaster risks while also strengthening early warning systems. The third priority is centered on Knowledge, Innovation, and Education, advocating for the use of these tools to foster a national culture of safety and resilience across all levels of society. The final operational priority of the Plan is to Reduce Risk Factors.

Ultimately, this plan is designed to enhance Disaster Preparedness so that when catastrophes occur, interventions can be carried out more effectively at every level.

Document Title: National Wetlands Policy (PNZH)
Family Title: National Wetlands Policy (PNZH)
Family Summary:
The National Policy on Wetland Management (PNZH) in Niger aims primarily to improve food security and population well-being through the sustainable management and enhancement of wetland resources. The Policy's vision is that by 2030, wetland ecosystems will be conserved, viable, and sustainably managed to provide essential goods and services, ultimately reducing poverty and contributing to global biodiversity conservation.

The PNZH is built upon four priority strategic axes, including Knowledge and Degradation Control and the Rational Use of wetlands. Critically, the Policy's strategic actions include a focus on climate change and disaster risk management (item 8.2). Specifically, the PNZH aims to leverage wetlands' natural function to mitigate the effects of climate change and reduce disaster risks, such as severe flooding and droughts, thereby reinforcing the overall resilience of local populations and ecosystems. Implementation relies on core guiding principles, requiring the participation of all stakeholders in securing sites, developing management plans, and integrating wetland issues into national and local development policies.

Document Title: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction
Family Title: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction
Family Summary:
Niger's National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) establishes a vision for 2030 centered on responsible, effective, and inclusive governance of disaster risks to ensure sustainable development. The Strategy's implementation is founded on core principles, including the primary responsibility of the State for prevention, balanced by the sharing of responsibilities and means across all levels of administration and communities. It strongly prioritizes prevention over recovery, advocating for public and private investments that tackle underlying risk factors, and institutionalizing the principle of "rebuilding better" after a disaster. Furthermore, the Strategy mandates inclusion by specifically integrating the needs of the most vulnerable groups, highlighting the importance of the Gender principle and ensuring the full participation of people with disabilities.

The overarching aim is to substantially reduce the losses and damages associated with disasters by strengthening the resilience of the population and socioeconomic infrastructure. To achieve this, the Strategy aligns with the Sendai Framework around four Strategic Axes and objectives: understanding disaster risks in all their dimensions; strengthening risk governance capacity; increasing investment in economic, social, cultural, and environmental resilience; and enhancing preparedness for effective response and recovery. This comprehensive approach is designed to address the underlying factors of risk and vulnerability across the nation.

Document Title: National Strategy for Adaptation to Climate Change in the Agricultural Sector (SPN2A-2035): Action Plan 2022–2026
Family Title: National Strategy for Adaptation to Climate Change in the Agricultural Sector (SPN2A-2035) - Action Plan 2022–2026
Family Summary:
The National Strategy for Adaptation to Climate Change in the Agricultural Sector (SPN2A-2035) and its Action Plan (2022-2026) is Niger's central framework for transitioning the AFOLU (Agriculture, Forestry, and Other Land Use) sector towards climate-smart agriculture. The strategy's main objective is to strengthen the climate resilience of producers and reduce the vulnerability of the rural population to climate risks, thereby fighting poverty and food and nutritional insecurity.

The strategy's implementation is structured around an adaptation continuum that integrates four distinct types of responses to climate change: (i) reducing vulnerability factors; (ii) strengthening response capacity; (iii) improving climate change risk management; and (iv) minimizing climate change impacts. Additionally, the planned activities provide significant mitigation co-benefits, contributing to global efforts to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.

The 2022–2026 Action Plan is the indispensable, budgeted five-year blueprint that details activities across six axes of intervention. These axes focus on: preserving natural resources, developing climate-smart agro-sylvopastoral and fisheries systems, reinforcing producer resilience, and integrating adaptation into sectoral planning.

Document Title: Strategic Development Plan 2022–2026 for Fisan
Family Title: Strategic Development Plan 2022–2026 for Fisan
Family Summary: The Investment Fund for Food and Nutritional Security (FISAN) has the objective to facilitate private and community investment in all segments of the food and agri-food value chains with the ultimate goal of increasing the volume and quality of agricultural financing offers. All orientations aim to align with policies and strategies at international, national and sectoral levels to ensure food security, improve nutrition and promote sustainable rural agriculture. FISAN will intervene by i) targeting interventions based on three dimensions (sub-regional geographical concentration, value chains and density of units) ii) a particular focus on support for young people and start-ups iii) strengthening the resilience of private agricultural operators to climate change; iv) an inclusive approach that takes gender issues into account; v) enhanced access to information through a local communication strategy; vi) performance-based partnership management; vii) rigorous fiduciary risk management; and viii) digitalisation as a factor for inclusive development.

Document Title: National Action Programme to Combat Desertification and Manage Natural Resources (PAN-LCD/GRN)
Family Title: National Action Programme to Combat Desertification and Manage Natural Resources
Family Summary:
The National Action Programme to Combat Desertification and Manage Natural Resources (PAN-LCD/GRN) is a multisectoral document covering the whole of Niger. Its main objectives are to improve and sustain productive capital (soil, water, etc.) on the one hand, and the living environment on the other.

The document's general objectives are: to identify the factors contributing to desertification and the concrete measures to be taken to combat it and mitigate the effects of drought; to create conditions conducive to improving food security, resolving the domestic energy crisis, promoting the economic development of local communities, and empowering them to manage natural resources.

Document Title: Agriculture Policy
Family Title: Agriculture Policy
Family Summary: The Agricultural Policy aims to modernise and diversify agriculture while strengthening resilience to climate change and environmental risks. Its four strategic axes focus on increasing and diversifying production through irrigation and modernised rain-fed crops; ensuring regular supply to rural and urban markets; improving populations’ resilience to climate shocks, crises, and disasters; and enhancing nutritional outcomes. The policy promotes climate-smart practices, sustainable land and water management, and development of resilient crop varieties, while fostering inclusive food systems and strong governance through partnerships between the State, local authorities, private sector, and civil society. Aligned with global frameworks such as the SDGs, COP21, and AGIR, it seeks to support sustainable agricultural growth, food security, and long-term ecosystem preservation.

Document Title: Implementation Plan for the National Framework for Climate Services (CNSC)
Family Title: Implementation Plan for the National Framework for Climate Services (CNSC)
Family Summary:
This plan outlines a comprehensive approach to integrating climate information into decision-making processes across key sectors such as agriculture, water resources, health, energy, and disaster risk management. Its primary objective is to establish a robust system that links climate data to actionable strategies, thereby enhancing the country's resilience to climate-related challenges. The plan is structured around six main components:

  • Enabling Environment: Creating a supportive framework for the implementation of the plan.
  • Climate Information Production: Generating relevant climate data and services.
  • Communication Strategy: Developing effective communication channels to disseminate climate information.
  • Sectoral Collaboration Projects: Facilitating joint initiatives across sectors for efficient use of climate services.
  • Capacity Building: Enhancing the skills and knowledge of stakeholders involved in climate-related activities.
  • Plan Management: Overseeing the implementation and coordination of the plan's activities.

By focusing on these areas, the CNSC aims to establish a solid climate knowledge base and a national chain that links climate information to action, supported by multidisciplinary working groups in each sector. This approach is designed to facilitate informed decision-making at the national level, thereby improving the resilience of society to climate risks.

Document Title: 3N Initiative Action Plan 2021-2025
Family Title: 3N Initiative Action Plan 2021-2025
Family Summary:
The 3N Initiative is the national strategy for food and nutrition security and sustainable agricultural development. It is designed around five strategic areas covering various complementary fields that constitute the specificity of this innovative strategy, recognised as such since its inception in 2011. These five (5) strategic areas are translated into five (5) strategic programmes: (i) increasing and diversifying agro-sylvo-pastoral and fisheries production; (ii) ensuring a regular supply of agricultural and agri-food products to rural and urban markets; (iii) improving the resilience of populations to climate change, crises and disasters; (iv) improving the nutritional status of Nigeriens; and (v) facilitating, coordinating and driving reforms. It also defines a coherent set of normative measures and investment actions to be carried out in the short, medium and long term through the relevant ministries and administrations.

The 2021-2025 Action Plan consists of ten (10) operational programmes derived from the five (5) strategic programmes of the 3N Initiative and reflecting the six (6) priorities of the Renaissance Programme Act III: i) water management for irrigation; ii) environmental restoration; iii) the Maison de Paysan (Farmer's House); iv) the development of value chains for agro-sylvo-pastoral and fishery products; v) the resilience of populations to climate shocks and hazards; and vi) improving the nutritional status of Nigeriens.

Document Title: Methodological Guide For Quantifying Budgetary Risks Related To Natural Disasters
Family Title: Methodological Guide For Quantifying Budgetary Risks Related To Natural Disasters
Family Summary: Natural disasters stemming from climate change are an increasingly frequent and costly phenomenon in Niger, significantly undermining the country’s economic performance and putting a heavy strain on its public finances. The purpose of the new methodological guide is to provide detailed instructions for quantifying these climate-related natural disaster fiscal risks. Its goal is to answer a crucial question: What are the potential impacts that future disasters could have on key budgetary aggregates, such as government revenue, expenditure, and even debt, in the coming years?

Document Title: Climate Risk Assessment Methodology for Projects in the Public Investment Management System
Family Title: Climate Risk Assessment Methodology for Projects in the Public Investment Management System
Family Summary: Climate change poses a major threat to public investments, increasing risks and uncertainties that demand resilient infrastructure. For Niger, which is highly vulnerable—especially to frequent, severe floods—resilient and green public investments are essential to strengthen its adaptive capacity and support its transition to green infrastructure. Hence, the main objective of the strategy document is to gradually develop a "Climate Risk Assessment Methodology for projects in the Public Investment Management system" for Niger. This methodology will be implemented during the design and proposal stages for all Public Investment Program (PIP) projects. It is specifically designed to ensure that projects undertake progressively more sophisticated climate risk assessments as they advance, ultimately guaranteeing the long-term resilience and success of the nation's public investments.

Document Title: Federal Law 14.904/2024

The law establishes that the national plan for adapting to climate change will set out guidelines for state and municipal plans and will ensure priority support for the most vulnerable municipalities exposed to climate threats, as well as encouraging inter-municipal consortia and regional arrangements to implement the measures it provides for. It modifies article 5 of Law 12.114/2009.

Document Title: Fourth National Environmental Action Programme (2022-2026)
Family Title: Fourth National Environmental Action Programme (2022-2026)
Family Summary:
Georgia's Fourth National Environmental Action Programme (NEAP 4) for 2022-2026 aims to improve environmental quality and governance, primarily by fulfilling obligations under the EU-Georgia Association Agreement. The Programme is structured around dual objectives: enhancing legal and administrative frameworks, and implementing focused, sectoral actions to protect key natural resources. Governance improvements include streamlining documentation for Environmental and Strategic Impact Assessments (EIA/SEA), implementing integrated permits for industries, strengthening environmental law enforcement capacity, and to increase transparency, effectiveness, and public participation in environmental decision-making.

Key areas of focus include climate action, such as improving early warning systems and managing climate data, and promoting biodiversity conservation by preventing habitat degradation, establishing interlinked protected areas, and improving sustainable forest management.

Its primary goal is to transform Georgia into a country that actively prioritizes waste prevention and maximizes recycling over traditional disposal methods.The strategy will bring positive results in terms of environmental protection. It will also have a positive effect on the health of the population, especially in the areas of occupational health and safety. The introduction of a modern waste management model in the country will promote the use of waste as a resource, reduce the disposal of biodegradable waste and the emission of greenhouse gases. Document Title: A roadmap for multi-hazard, impact-based early warning 2023-2030
Family Title: A roadmap for multi-hazard, impact-based early warning 2023-2030
Family Summary: Ethiopia’s early warning systems, developed over a 50-year span, faced challenges such as fragmentation, inadequate funding, and a lack of proactive measures. The focus on crisis management, rather than anticipatory actions, led to inefficient resource allocation. To address these issues, the Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission (EDRMC) and stakeholders propose transforming the early warning system into a comprehensive Multi-Hazard, Impact-Based Early Warning and Early Action System (MH-IB-EW-EAS).This integrated approach encompasses hazard monitoring, forecasting, risk assessment, communication, and preparedness. Aligned with the Sendai Framework’s four pathways - disaster risk knowledge; monitoring, observation, and forecasting; warning communication; and early action and response – the MH-IB-EW-EAS aims to foster resilient communities through proactive measures and effective response strategies. The implementation of the roadmap requires the participation and contribution of multiple stakeholders from the federal to the community level.

Document Title: DISASTER RISK MANAGEMENT ACT, 2023
Family Title: Disaster Risk Management Act (2023-91)
Family Summary:
This Act lays down provisions on the establishment and duties of the National Disaster Council, National Emergency Operations Committee, Recovery Coordination Committee, Disaster Resilience Committee, Clusters, Local government disaster committees, National Disaster Management Office, Disaster Coordinator and the National Emergency Operations Center. It also sets out rules as regards disaster planning at the national and local levels; declaration of state of disaster by executive orders; establishment and utilization of the Disaster Assistance Account; offences and penalties; and public cooperation to successfully prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters.

The objectives of this Act are:

  • to establish an institutional structure for the delivery of disaster management and climate and disaster risk reduction measures throughout the Republic, including by promoting cooperation between the government agencies, and with local governments, non-governmental organizations and the private sector;
  • to provide a planning framework for disaster management and for disaster resilience through climate and disaster risk reduction throughout the Republic;
  • to provide arrangements for the effective management and coordination of preparedness for, responses to and recovery from disasters, including arrangements for access to external support;
  • to promote and integrate measures to reduce climate and disaster risk in social, livelihood and development planning and practices throughout the Republic.

Document Title: National Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Plan (2021-2027)
Family Title: National Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Plan (2021-2027)
Family Summary:
The National Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Plan of Thailand (2021–2027) outlines the country’s framework for managing disaster risks in an era of rapid global change. Anchored in the 20-Year National Strategy, the plan incorporates the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy, the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (SFDRR). It sets out a vision for a resilient Thai society that can effectively reduce existing risks, prevent new ones, and respond quickly and systematically when disasters occur. The plan emphasizes building public awareness, preparedness, and adaptive capacity so that communities can “know, adapt, and recover quickly in a sustainable way.”

To achieve this, the plan defines two main strategic areas: reducing disaster risks and standardizing disaster management. It includes measures such as strengthening risk assessment systems, developing risk reduction mechanisms, fostering innovation and information systems, promoting partnerships across sectors, and enhancing regional and international cooperation. It also highlights integrated emergency response, sustainable recovery efforts based on the principle of “Build Back Better,” and mechanisms for monitoring, evaluation, and continuous improvement. The policy reflects Thailand’s commitment to safety, resilience, and long-term sustainable development through a whole-of-society approach.

It aims to ensure the sustainable promotion and integration of renewable sources in Lithuania's energy supply, improving climate mitigation efforts and energy security. The law also enshrines a target for a renewables share of 55% of final energy consumption by 2030, as well as targets to increase district heating and deployment of green non-biological fuels such as hydrogen.

Document Title: Law of the Republic of Lithuania on Alternative Fuels
Family Title: Law of the Republic of Lithuania on Alternative Fuels
Family Summary: The Law on Alternative Fuels aims to promote the development and expansion of alternative fuels in the transport sector, to reduce net greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate climate change. The law establishes ministerial responsibilities for its implementation and requires the formation of a policy for the development of alternative fuels. It also contains obligations to implement biofuel quality indicators, promote low-pollution zones and build comprehensive governance frameworks around alternative fuels as their usage grows. Article 16 institutes specific binding targets for natural gas suppliers in the fuel/transport sector, mandating yearly targets for the proportion of biofuels (or renewable synthetic alternatives) to be included in their supply mix. From 2030 this target will be at least 16.8% of the total supplied mix. The law sets out a substantial high-level regulatory framework around alternative fuel use, including sanctioning procedure for violation of its regulations.

These actions are intended to increase energy security and contribute to climate mitigation efforts. The guidelines aim for a buildout of ten hydrogen refuelling points nationally by 2030, the first of which is expected in 2024, and also for 5% of new vehicles purchased to be hydrogen-powered by 2030. Other measures are suggested such as tax relief for consumers, and direct purchases of hydrogen-powered vehicles in public procurement.

Document Title: General Plan for the Territory of the Republic of Lithuania

Document Title: Action Plan for the Development of Electric Vehicle Use and Charging Infrastructure

It also promotes the acquisition of a significant electric vehicle stock by the public sector, and suggests adding electric vehicle ownership incentives to subsidies for private renewable energy generation products (i.e. solar installations).
