The strategy acknowledges the significant contribution of tourism to greenhouse gas emissions, and recommends low-carbon measures such as enhanced rail and cycling infrastructure, renewable energy installation/purchase in new tourism developments, and ecologically appropriate tree-planting to partially offset emissions.

Document Title: Regulation on the establishment of the inter-sector co-ordination Commission for policy and mitigation and adaptation measures for climate change
Family Title: Regulation on the establishment of the inter-sector co-ordination Commission for policy and mitigation and adaptation measures for climate change
Family Summary: This decision establishes a commission to provide recommendations to the Croatian government on overarching climate policy, and the mitigation and adaptation measures it contains. This commission will recommend, monitor and evaluate climate policy, and will appoint technical working groups on low-carbon development and mitigation, drawn from a range of expert sources inside and outside the state. The decision places administrative and technical responsibilities for this commission onto the Ministry of Environment and Energy.

Document Title: Regulation on the Monitoring of Greenhouse Gas Emissions, Policies and Mitigation Measures in the Republic of Croatia (Official Gazette 5/17)
Family Title: Regulation on the Monitoring of Greenhouse Gas Emissions, Policies and Mitigation Measures in the Republic of Croatia (Official Gazette 5/17)
Family Summary: The regulation establishes a national system for calculating and reporting anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and removals. It assigns ministerial responsibilities, defines implementation reporting structures (including to the UNFCCC via national and biennial reports), and gives the key types of statistics to be included in the overall emissions reporting.

Document Title: Programme for the Development of Green Infrastructure in Urban Areas for the period 2021-2030
Family Title: Programme for the Development of Green Infrastructure in Urban Areas for the period 2021-2030
Family Summary: The Programme for the Development of Green Infrastructure in Urban Areas for the period 2021-2030 aims to promote green urban development, at a higher standard than existing services and with strong public awareness of its benefits. The programme acknowledges climate change as a major threat to the development and maintenance of urban areas, with the most significant direct hazards including flooding, extreme heat and wind. It recognises the uneven and sparse distribution of existing green infrastructure, and promotes capacity building for effective planning, as well as an allocation of funding to new green projects. Through projects increasing energy efficiency, the programme also aims to mitigate greenhouse emissions and their effect on climate change.

Document Title: Energy Development Strategy of the Republic of Croatia until 2030 with an outlook to 2050
Family Title: Energy Development Strategy of the Republic of Croatia until 2030 with an outlook to 2050
Family Summary: The Energy Development Strategy recognises climate change mitigation and adaptation as major goals, and aims to harmonise low-carbon energy development with energy security, affordability and quality in the long-term. The strategy aims to increase domestic energy production and connectivity, integrate smoothly into the international market, increase efficiency at every part of the supply chain, increase renewable supply share, develop bioeconomy and sustainable waste management, and provide risk-reduction funds for the accelerated research/development of new energy technologies. The strategy acknowledges that reaching the most optimistic green energy transition scenario will primarily hinge on the development rate of energy renovation in buildings, and decarbonisation of the transport sector.

Document Title: Decree on the Quotas for Incentivising the Production of Electricity from Renewable Energy Sources and Highly-Efficient Cogeneration
Family Title: Decree on the Quotas for Incentivising the Production of Electricity from Renewable Energy Sources and Highly-Efficient Cogeneration
Family Summary: This document sets quotas for the subsidised production of energy from renewable energy sources and cogeneration.

Document Title: Adverse Weather and Health Plan 2024-2025
Family Title: Adverse Weather and Health Plan (2024-2025 and 2025-2026)
Family Summary:
The first edition of the Adverse Weather and Health Plan (AWHP) aims to protect individuals and communities from the health effects of adverse weather and to build community resilience in England. The Plan is focused on achieving the following four goals: Prevent the increase in years of life lost due to adverse weather events, prevent mortality due to adverse weather events, prevent morbidity due to adverse weather events and reduce the use of healthcare services due to adverse weather events.

The Second Edition of the AWHP has been developed based on feedback, recommendations from reports, and reflections from the experience of implementing the first edition of the plan. The plan is centered around the same four goals, and includes nine action areas for delivery, namely 1) service delivery 2) capacity building 3) organisational arrangements 4) communication 5) risk management 6) early warning systems 7) data analysis 8) quality assurance 9) policy development and accountability. The second edition is also expanded to include a review of the AHWP guidance and further clarificaion of the role of the AWHP in improving long-term resilience.

Document Title: Agreement announcing the North Pacific Marine and Regional Ecological Management Program (Acuerdo por el que se da a conocer el Programa de Ordenamiento Ecológico Marino y Regional del Pacífico Norte)
Family Title: Agreement announcing the North Pacific Marine and Regional Ecological Management Program (Acuerdo que da a conocer el Programa de Ordenamiento Ecológico Marino y Regional del Pacífico Norte)
Family Summary: This policy establishes the Marine and Regional Ecological Zoning Programme for Mexico's Northern Pacific, mandating integrated spatial planning to align coastal and marine development with constitutional mandates for environmental protection and sustainable development. The programme employs systems dynamics modelling to forecast environmental conflicts across sectors (including tourism, fisheries, aquaculture, and agriculture) designating Environmental Management Units (UGAs) to regulate land and sea use. It prioritises biodiversity conservation (e.g., whale habitats, turtle nesting grounds) while promoting sustainable economic activities, emphasising intergovernmental coordination between federal agencies, state governments, and local authorities to balance ecological preservation with socioeconomic objectives.The policy addresses climate change through vulnerability assessments and adaptive spatial planning. It identifies low-lying sandy zones and coastal lagoons as highly exposed to sea-level rise, erosion, and extreme weather events, projecting impacts such as habitat loss and water scarcity. Key adaptation measures include restricting development below 5m elevation, protecting coastal ecosystems (mangroves, dunes, seagrasses) as natural buffers, mandating wastewater treatment to maintain water quality, and implementing sustainable water resource management to mitigate aquifer depletion.

Document Title: Second National Environmental Action Programme of Georgia (2012-2016)
Family Title: Fourth National Environmental Action Programme (2022-2026)
Family Summary:
Georgia's Fourth National Environmental Action Programme (NEAP 4) for 2022-2026 aims to improve environmental quality and governance, primarily by fulfilling obligations under the EU-Georgia Association Agreement. The Programme is structured around dual objectives: enhancing legal and administrative frameworks, and implementing focused, sectoral actions to protect key natural resources. Document Title: Resolution No. 341 on the Amendment to Resolution No. 54 on the Creation of the Climate Change Council
Family Title: Resolution 54/2020 establishing the Climate Change Council
Family Summary:
This resolution creates the Climate Change Council and defines its composition and mission.The resolution was amended 3 times, in 2021, 2023 and 2025 adjusting the members of the Climate Change Council, and the last amendment also brought modifications in the Climate Change Council Statute. The Council is composed of representatives of several Ministries and public authorities. The Council’s core mission is to ensure the efficient implementation of the Paris Agreement. The Council is in charge of: - deliberating on the issues related to the preparation and implementation of the NDC, reviews, recommending and submitting updated NDCs to the Secretariat of the Convention;

- discussing the national system for measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) within the Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF), to implement the Paris Agreement in Georgia, and, in case it is approved, shall initiate the decision-making process by the government of Georgia;

- reviewing the national communications of Georgia to the Convention, biennial update reports and the reports on the fulfilment of the nationally determined contribution, and, if those are approved, shall initiate the decision-making process by the government of Georgia;

- reviewing the national program of Georgia prepared for the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and, in case it is approved, shall address the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia with the relevant recommendation;

- reviewing the projects to be submitted to the Green Climate Fund (GCF), Convention Adaptation Fund (AF), Climate Technologies Centre and Network (CTCN) and other financial institutions working on the climate change issues, and, in case the project is approved, shall address the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia with the recommendation to support the projects; - reviewing the national strategies and plans related to climate change and, in case of approval, shall initiate the decision-making process by the government of Georgia;

- establishing and approve the task forces for relevant economic sectors;

- With the view to achieving the objectives of the Council and participating in its activities, the Council can invite representatives from other ministries, government agencies and organisations, private sector, international organisations, as well as other experts and stakeholders.

Family Summary: The White Paper on the Climate Change Law of Georgia illustrates a holistic approach to gender considerations. This inclusion recognizes the diverse impacts of climate change on women and men, highlighting the importance of gender- responsive approaches throughout all facets of climate action. Specifically, within the adaptation section, the White Paper underscores the need for NDC and mitigation actions to be inclusive and gender-responsive. It advocates for prioritizing the specific needs, challenges, and priorities of vulnerable groups, such as women, adolescents, internally displaced people, and ethnic minorities. By fostering inclusive engagement with diverse stakeholders, including marginalized communities and civil society organizations, the White Paper aims to promote empowerment and resilience-building among these groups. This approach not only aligns with global agreements like the Paris Agreement but also reflects Georgia’s commitment to advancing social justice and gender equality in its mitigation efforts.

Document Title: Decree No. 2019-027/MESUDD
Family Title: Decree No. 2019-027/MESUDD implementing Law No. 2018-28, establishing the principles of Environmental Assessment
Family Summary: The Decree n° 2019-027/PRN/MESU/DD provides the detailed application principles for the Law 2018-28, establishing the fundamental principles of Environmental Assessment (EA) in Niger, designating the Bureau National d’Évaluations Environnementales (BNEE) as the primary responsible body. The decree specifies four assessment types, with the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (EIES) for projects and the Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment (EESS) for public policies, plans, and programs being the central tools for assessing climate change impacts. Through the EIES, the decree ensures that individual projects are evaluated for their vulnerability to climate risks (such as increased flooding or drought) and their contribution to environmental degradation or mitigation efforts. The EESS, on the other hand, guarantees that new government policies, plans, and programs integrate climate change adaptation and mitigation strategies at a high, strategic level.

Document Title: Strategy for climate change adaptation, disaster risk reduction and the fight against hunger
Family Title: Strategy for climate change adaptation, disaster risk reduction and the fight against hunger
Family Summary:
This Strategy focuses on climate change adaptation, which has been identified as a priority area in Norwegian development policy. The Norwegian government recognises that while it is vital to reduce emissions, priority must also be given to increasing support for climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction in development cooperation and global climate action; climate-resilient development is needed across the world and developing countries must be given support to achieve this.

This strategy lays the foundation for intensified Norwegian efforts to assist vulnerable societies in adapting to climate change. The strategy identifies priority focus areas and tools for enhancing climate change adaptation. The focus areas are: early warning systems and climate services; nature-based solutions; climate-resilient food production; infrastructure; and innovative development financing mechanisms.

This strategy is linked to Norway’s Humanitarian Strategy. It follows up a priority area in the work to prevent humanitarian emergencies, with a focus on climate-related crises, as most natural disasters today are relatedto climate change.

Document Title: Energy for work – long-term value creation from Norwegian energy resources (Meld. St. 36 2020-2021)
Family Title: Energy for work – long-term value creation from Norwegian energy resources (Meld. St. 36 2020-2021)
Family Summary:
Under this white paper, the Norwegian government will maintain Norway's position as an energy nation and lay the foundation for energy resources to continue to be used to create value, jobs and welfare in Norway. This is a policy for long-term value creation from Norwegian energy resources organized according to four goals:

  1. value creation that provides the basis for jobs in Norway;
  2. electrification will make Norway greener and better;

3. establishment of new, profitable industries; and

4. further develop a future-oriented oil and gas industry within the framework of the climate goals.

Actions include:

  • require companies to make climate risks visible in their development plans;
  • facilitate the further development of both the oil and gas industry and other marine industries;
  • support the industry's work to increase value creation through efficiency, digitalization and innovation; and
  • continue the focus on petroleum-based research to increase value creation, strengthen international competitiveness and reduce the climate and environmental impact of the business.

Family Title: Longship – Carbon capture and storage (Meld. St. 33 2019-2020)
Family Summary:
The Norwegian Government has decided to call the Norwegian project on carbon capture, transport and storage Longship, in Norwegian ‘Langskip’, as the characteristic shape, and flexible, supple construction of the Vikings’ longships made them one of the greatest innovations and most ground-breaking ship-building technologies of their day. LLike those who built the longships, the Norwegians also aim to take their technology out into the world, but only by peaceful means. Longship will bring Norway to the forefront of the development of a technology that could prove decisive in achieving our climate targets.

This policy document includes a section on how carbon capture and storage (CCS) can be made successful, which includes market development; having other countries support CCS; research, development and demonstration; and government contribution to developing technology. It also includes a development plan for the Northern Lights CCS project, which is a subsea reservoir for CCS.

Document Title: National Strategy for reducing social inequalities in health (Meld. St. 15 2022-2023)
Family Title: National Strategy for reducing social inequalities in health (Meld. St. 15 2022-2023)
Family Summary:
This Strategy contains actions to address social health disparities in public health work, which are particularly applicable to the contexts of climate change, demographic changes and international cooperation. It recognises that those with the lowest socio-economic backgrounds and children are the most vulnerable, and the climate crisis can threaten the development, upbringing and education of children, their access to clean water, health and sufficient, healthy and safe food and survival.

Under the section on climate adaptation, the government will:

  • strengthen knowledge in municipalities about the consequences of and measures against heat waves with the aim of protecting vulnerable groups, including how important it is to preserve and plant trees and other vegetation in cities and towns, and about the health risks of heat waves;
  • ask the Norwegian Food Safety Authority to prepare to meet the challenges that climate change and a tense international situation pose for the Norwegian food system, in order to ensure access to sufficient, safe and healthy food; and

Document Title: The Government's action plan for green shipping

Family Summary:
This action plan presents the Government’s policy for cutting domestic greenhouse gas emissions, strengthening the Norwegian maritime industry and playing a part in the global technological developments needed for the world to achieve the targets of the Paris Agreement. Measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions result in cuts in emissions of other pollutants as well, for example sulphur (SOx) and nitrogen (NOx) emissions.

The third part contains an account of the different vessel categories and describes how the Government intends to accelerate the development of low- and zero-emission solutions. The fourth part discusses infrastructure for green shipping, and the fifth and final part gives an account of the Government’s policy instruments for promoting green shipping.

Document Title: Norway’s strategy for promoting food security in development policy
Family Title: Norway’s strategy for promoting food security in development policy
Family Summary:
This Strategy is aimed at strengthening food systems in developing countries. The vision is to promote, within sustainable frameworks, local production of nutritious food that is processed and sold locally and regionally, thus increasing the incomes of small-scale food producers, stimulating local job creation throughout the value chain, and expanding access to healthy food.

There is an emphasis on increasing local climate-resilient food production, increasing local value creation and income for food producers, reducing malnutrition and malnourishment and reducing the extent of hunger crises, as outlined in the implementation section of the Strategy. The Strategy is guided by the role of women, persons with disabilities, and youth and young adults. The Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation (Norad) actively works on value chain developments through its partners, especially in southern Africa, where bottlenecks have been identified in value chains and targeted initiatives are being implemented. Examples of such bottlenecks may include a lack of storage facilities, credit, local refinement possibilities or market access. Norad collaborates with the private sector to solve these challenges.

Document Title: Norway’s strategy for developing a green, circular economy
Family Title: Norway’s strategy for developing a green, circular economy
Family Summary:

It includes specific action points for the sectors that have been identified as having the greatest potential for circularity and green competitiveness in Norway: the bio-based sectors; the process industries; construction and buildings; and service industries, including retail and wholesale trade.

Ciruclar economy will at the same time result in progress towards Norway’s climate and environmental policy targets, including Norway’s efforts to achieve the UN Sustainable Development Goals. In relation to climate-related actions:, the Norwegian government will:

  • promote a development pathway in which circular solutions within the bio-based sectors and more use of renewable resources to replace non-renewable alternatives are used to make the greatest possible contribution to progress towards climate and environmental targets and to sustainable value creation;
  • and support initiatives for high climate and environmental standards as a basis for moresustainable products and value chains under the EU Circular Economy Action Plan.

Family Summary:
This Action Plan shows how the government's policy will contribute to the sustainable use and conservation of natural diversity. The measures are meant to ensure that society's use of nature occurs in a way that makes it possible to use nature and live good lives throughout the country in the future.

The proposals in this action plan will, as far as possible, safeguard the interests of both nature and climate, and measures under all 23 goals (of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework) can contribute to development that both preserves natural diversity, reduces greenhouse gas emissions and strengthens society and nature's ability to withstand climate change. In some cases, however, climate and nature considerations will conflict with each other, for example, to the development of renewable energy and the transmission of such energy through power grids and to the extraction of minerals and the establishment of industry that are important for the green shift, as this requires land. The government addresses these issues but emphasises that trade-offs between climate and nature must be made in the ongoing political work of every government.

Document Title: Maldives Energy Efficiency Guideline for Buildings
Family Title: Maldives Energy Efficiency Guideline for Buildings
Family Summary:
Energy efficiency and conservation are crucial for the Maldives to mitigate climate change risks and achieve energy security. Maldives has a high dependence on fossil fuels to meet all of its domestic energy demand, and the use of fossil fuels has resulted in huge greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and its associated climate change risks. Maldives is also vulnerable to global oil price shocks due to dependence on imported fossil fuels. This Guideline mainstreams energy efficiency in building design practices to achieve a substantial reduction of energy consumption from buildings.

Actions include encouraging energy efficiency both at the construction stage and during the lifetime of the building, e.g. by climate-sensitive design which takes account of the orientation and surrounding features to control wind effects while optimising sunlight, daylight, and solar gain benefits.

Document Title: The Government’s Bioeconomy Strategy
Family Title: The Government’s Bioeconomy Strategy
Family Summary:
This Strategy targets sustainable, effective and profitable production, extraction and use of renewable, biological resources into food, feed, ingredients, health products, energy, materials, chemicals, paper, textiles and numerous other products. National focus on the bioeconomy should lead to increased value creation and employment, reduced emission of climate gasses, as well as more efficient, profitable and sustainable use of renewable biological resources.

This Strategy regards the internalisation of negative effects on the climate and the environment in the product prices would be the most efficient way of promoting the bioeconomy. Climate-related measures include:

  • Developing know-how on climate effects from increased use of bio-based alternatives to fossil-based materials and chemicals;
  • Establishing a new investment company which will contribute to the reduction of climate gas emissions;
  • Ensuring a public procurement practise contributing to the reduction of environmentally degrading effects and an advancement of climate friendly solutions, where relevant, which includes taking life cycle costs into consideration;

  • Upgrading industry skills regarding efficient, climate friendly and sustainable production and extraction.

The Norwegian government recognises that while it is vital to reduce emissions, priority must also be given to increasing support for climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction in development cooperation and global climate action; climate-resilient development is needed across the world and developing countries must be given support to achieve this.

This strategy lays the foundation for intensified Norwegian efforts to assist vulnerable societies in adapting to climate change. The strategy identifies priority focus areas and tools for enhancing climate change adaptation. The focus areas are: early warning systems and climate services; nature-based solutions; climate-resilient food production; infrastructure; and innovative development financing mechanisms.

This strategy is linked to Norway’s Humanitarian Strategy. It follows up a priority area in the work to prevent humanitarian emergencies, with a focus on climate-related crises, as most natural disasters today are relatedto climate change.

Ciruclar economy will at the same time result in progress towards Norway’s climate and environmental policy targets, including Norway’s efforts to achieve the UN Sustainable Development Goals. In relation to climate-related actions:, the Norwegian government will:

The measures selected for this Action Plan were compiled firstly from the mitigation measures that have been included in the Maldives’ Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), and then from the planned measures from different sectors which were not part of the NDC. These sectoral measures are collectively termed ‘air quality measures’ in comparing their effects with the NDC measures. Scientific and political conversations increasingly recognised that air pollution and climate change are closely linked. Several air pollutants and greenhouse gases have common sources. This Action Plan therefore designs mitigation strategies with both in mind, to deliver multiple benefits, helping to achieve rapid near-term climate goals, as well as to achieve real-world benefits for the ecosystem and human health.

Family Summary:
The Energy Policy and Strategy 2024–2029 outlines a series of innovative initiatives, bold targets, and strategic investments that will propel Maldives towards a more sustainable future. By harnessing renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, and ocean energies, Maldives will reduce its dependence on fossil fuels, lower its greenhouse gas emissions, and create a more sustainable and resilient energy infrastructure. This document serves as guidance for stakeholders across government, industry, and civil society to collaborate in driving the transition to a cleaner and more sustainable energy future.

Key objectives of the Maldives Energy Policy include:

  1. Diversifying the energy mix: Promoting the development and utilization of renewable energy sources, such as solar, wind, biomass and ocean energies, to reduce the country's dependence on imported fossil fuels and enhance energy security;
  2. Improving energy efficiency: Implementing measures to enhance energy efficiency across all sectors to reduce energy consumption and lower greenhouse gas emissions;
  3. Enhancing access to energy services: Ensuring universal access to affordable, reliable, and modern energy services for all citizens;
  4. Strengthening energy governance: Enhancing institutional capacity, regulatory frameworks, and governance structures to facilitate the effective implementation of energy policies and programs; and
  5. Promoting public awareness and engagement: Raising awareness about the importance of sustainable energy practices and promoting community participation in energy conservation and renewable energy initiatives.

The policies are:

  • Policy 1: Increase the Share of Renewable Energy in the National Energy Mix;
  • Policy 2: Promote Energy Efficiency and Conservation;
  • Policy 3: Improve Energy Security and Affordability;
  • Policy 4: Strengthen Institutional Capacity and Regulatory Framework of the Energy Sector; and
  • Policy 5: Promote Energy Research and Development.

  2. Evaluating maximum potential for renewable energy integration into the grid;
  3. Decarbonising transport;
  4. Leapfrogging solarisation of islands;
  5. Mainstreaming efficient consumption;
  6. Setting up a fair and cost-reflective electricity tariff and replacing the indirect subsidy mechanism with a targeted subsidy;
  7. Transitioning to cleaner fuels in Greater Male;

  9. Preparing smart, flexible and reliable grids;

Document Title: Magey Saafu Raajje National Waste & Resource Management Policy and Strategy 2024–2028
Family Title: Magey Saafu Raajje National Waste & Resource Management Policy and Strategy 2024–2028
Family Summary:
This Policy outlines a comprehensive framework for implementing a sustainable solid waste management system in the Maldives, to minimise the negative impact of waste on the environment, climate and public health. lt aims to consolidate existing waste management projects under a unified framework, enhancing efficiency and effectiveness while integrating with other national policies related to protecting human health and environment. Central to the policy is the promotion of a circular economy, encouraging the reuse and recycling of materials to minimise waste generation, including the phasing out of single-use plastics. The policy introduces Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) mechanisms that will establish responsibilities at all levels of the production and consumption chain, including producers, importers, traders, and consumers, and is based on the polluter's pay principle, where the costs of waste management must be borne by the waste producer or by the legal entity managing waste on behalf of others.

To foster consumer behavioural change and community engagement, the policy emphasises increasing sustainable waste management practices through education and awareness campaigns, engaging citizens, communities, schools, NGOs, and other stakeholders in waste management efforts. In addition, by utilising waste as a resource, the policy seeks to drive socio-economic growth and development, creating green jobs and promoting sustainable economic activities. Investments in waste management infrastructure and the adoption of advanced technologies are prioritised. Public-private partnerships are encouraged to enhance collaborative efforts between the government, private sector, and civil society.

Family Title: Resilience Program for the Safeguarding of the Fatherland (PRSP)
Family Summary:
The Resilience Program for the Safeguarding of the Fatherland (Programme de Résilience pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie - PRSP, 2024-2026) is Niger's core national strategy aimed at guiding the country out of its current crisis, with a global objective to impulse a new dynamic of endogenous development. The PRSP was formulated in a challenging context marked by several overlapping crises of Geopolitical Instability, Environmental degradation intensified by the effects of climate change (such as droughts and floods), Socio-Demographic Pressure, and Security and Migration.

The PRSP is intended to establish this new vision, redefine relations with international partners based on mutual interests, and leverage the growing influence of new actors and channels of communication to mobilise the population. The core strategy focuses on sovereignty and responsibility, mandating the effective participation of all citizens to achieve the plan's goals.

Document Title: National Policy On The Environment And Sustainable Development
Family Title: National Policy On The Environment And Sustainable Development
Family Summary:
The National Policy on Environment and Sustainable Development addresses the challenges posed by environmental degradation in Niger, recognising that it is a major impediment to development and that vulnerable populations, especially women, are the most impacted by the scarcity of natural resources exacerbated by climate variability.The policy's four strategic axes are inherently linked to climate action:

  • Sustainable Management of Land and Water: This axis directly targets practices necessary for adaptation, such as combating land degradation and desertification, which are intensified by climate change (droughts and extreme rainfall).
  • Sustainable Environmental Management: This ensures the protection of the living environment against pollution and supports mitigation efforts.
  • Management of Biological Diversity: This involves protecting and enhancing biodiversity, including working to establish protected areas, which are crucial for maintaining resilient ecosystems and carbon sequestration.
  • Sectoral Governance: This provides the institutional backing to mobilize resources for these climate-critical interventions.

Overall, the PNEDD serves as a core framework for promoting the sustainable management of natural resources and the massive use of Renewable Energies, key strategies essential for achieving climate change mitigation (reducing greenhouse gas emissions) while simultaneously building the adaptation capacity needed to secure food, water, and well-being for the Nigerien population.

Document Title: National Strategy for the Sustainable Development of Aquaculture
Family Title: National Strategy for the Sustainable Development of Aquaculture
Family Summary: The National Strategy for Sustainable Development of Aquaculture (SNDDA) in Niger aims to transition the aquaculture sub-sector into a sustainable and competitive engine that enhances food and nutritional sovereignty and creates decent jobs for youth by 2035. The strategy is organised around four key objectives, with a direct link to environmental resilience. Especially, objective 2 directly addresses climate change by prioritizing the Improvement of Resilience and Adaptation to Climate Change within aquaculture production. This objective also focuses on securing land and water resources, ensuring the availability of quality feed, and improving cooperation regarding shared ecosystems, all of which are essential for stable production in a changing climate.The SNDDA is operationalized through an Action Plan detailing priority programs and projects. This plan outlines the specific, budgeted activities needed to achieve the strategic objectives, ensuring the transition toward commercially viable aquaculture that is robust enough to withstand the shocks and variability induced by climate change.

Family Title: New Vehicle Efficiency Standard 2025-2029 (NVES) Act
Family Summary: Under the NVES, emissions intensity limits (g CO2/km) are applied to suppliers across the fleet of new vehicles they sell annually, with higher limits permitted for heavier vehicles. There are no restrictions on the types of vehicles that may be sold; however, emissions-intensive vehicle sales must be offset through the sale of more fuel-efficient vehicles or the purchase of credits from other suppliers. During the consultation period for the legislation in early 2024, adjustments were made to the proposed standard. These included classifying some four-wheel drives as light commercial vehicles (LCVs) rather than passenger vehicles (PVs), thereby subjecting them to higher CO2 limits. Additionally, the government increased the emissions intensity target for LCVs and raised the breakpoints for both LCVs and PVs, providing heavier vehicles with greater allowances for emissions.

Document Title: Decree 86/2023 on combating climate change
Family Title: Decree 86/2023 on combating climate change
Family Summary:
This Decree's (pages 2179 to 2193 of the Gazette) objectives are as follows:

a) To strengthen the institutional framework for combating climate change, establish the responsibilities of the bodies and agencies of the Central State Administration, the business sector, the provincial governors of the People's Power and the municipal administration councils; of the State, the business sector, the provincial governors of the People's Power, and the municipal administration councils;

b) promote climate change adaptation and mitigation actions linked to food security, renewable energy use, energy efficiency, and integrated forest management, land use planning and urban planning instruments, cultural heritage, fisheries, agriculture, health, tourism, construction, transportation, and industry;

c) prioritise attention to climate change adaptation measures and disaster risk reduction management, with an emphasis on protecting people in vulnerable populations; land use planning and those resulting from the implementation of sectoral and coastal zone management policies;

d) strengthen mitigation actions, in accordance with the country's economic and social development priorities;

e) prioritise investments for the implementation of national measures and actions to address climate change in terms of mitigation and adaptation; and

f) promote scientific and technological training and innovation in line with climate change mitigation and adaptation actions.

This Decree contains provisions on the institutional framework for addressing climate change; the planning and orgaisation of government bodies; surveillance, early warning and assessment; the climate change information system; and the financing of actions to combat climate change and economic instruments.

Family Title: National Action Plan for Integrated Water Resource Management (PANGIRE)
Family Summary: The National Action Plan for Integrated Water Resource Management (PANGIRE) serves as Niger's operational framework for implementing the National Water Policy (2017-2030), with the core goal of defining and integrating national actions across water-related sectors. While its objectives include improving water knowledge, expanding access to drinking water and sanitation (considering gender), and enhancing water governance, the Plan places a significant emphasis on protecting and preserving the environment and developing resilience to the effects of climate change.The PANGIRE is structured into four components, with Component 3: Preservation of the Environment and Development of Climate Change Resilience being highly relevant to climate concerns. This component mandates actions such as reforesting degraded areas, rehabilitating oasis depressions to promote irrigated agriculture, protecting koris (temporary stream beds), and managing wetlands. Crucially, it specifically calls for the development of a pilot action plan to enhance population resilience to climate change and the creation of an action plan to combat water erosion and sand encroachment. The remaining components support this effort by focusing on improving knowledge of water resources (Component 1), mobilizing and optimizing water resources for socio-economic activities (Component 2), and strengthening water governance and capacity (Component 4). Implementation of the PANGIRE is structured into short, medium, and long-term programs, with a dedicated framework for coordination and monitoring.

Family Summary:

  • Improve resilience of energy infrastructure to the impacts of climate change and natural disasters;

  • Reduce reliance on imported fossil fuels and gradually decarbonise the transport sector.

Family Summary: Colombia’s National Energy Plan (PEN) 2022–2052, launched in 2023 as an updated version of the original NEP 2020–2050, lays out a pathway for integrating wind, solar and geothermal energy into the country’s electricity mix. The key objectives of the Plan are (i)Diversification of the Energy Matrix, reducing Colombia's dependence on fossil fuels by promoting the integration of renewable energy sources; (ii) Sustainable Development; (iii) Energy Efficiency by outlining strategies to improve efficiency across various sectors, aiming to reduce energy consumption and associated costs; and (iv) Universal Access to Energy and technological innovation.

Document Title: Climate Change Act, 2024
Family Title: Climate Change Act, 2024
Family Summary:
This Act sets out the strategic direction of travel for national climate change policy in South Africa and establishes the key institutional arrangements for climate governance at the national level. The recitals emphasise that responding to climate change raises unique challenges to effective governance and requires a nationally driven, coordinated and cooperative legal and administrative response. The Act is divided into six chapters and four schedules.

Chapter 1 sets out definitions, objectives and principles of the Act. For example, it defines just transition as a "shift towards a low-carbon, climate-resilient economy and society and ecologically sustainable economies and societies which contribute toward the creation of decent work for all, social inclusion and the eradication of poverty". Key objectives include protecting and preserving the planet for the benefit of present and future generations, and making a fair contribution to the global effort to stabilise greenhouse gas emissions. There are 12 principles which guide the interpretation and application of the Act. This includes the need for decision-making to consider the special needs and circumstance of localities and people that are particularly vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change. The Act expressly names workers, women (especially poor and rural women), children, the aged, the poor, the sick and the physically challenged. Section 3(j) indirectly refers to the polluter pays principle, as it acknowledges that the costs of adaptation and mitigation must be "paid for by those responsible for causing the adverse impact". The application of this Act must also be guided by national environmental management principles set out in the National Environmental Management Act.

Chapter 2 establishes the main institutional arrangements. Section 7(1) requires public bodies that perform a function affected by climate change, or entrusted with powers aimed at achieving a sustainable environment to review and if necessary, amend and harmonise their policies to ensure that climate change is taken into consideration. It also allows organised labour, civil society and business to advise on the state's climate change response. Sections 8 and 9 establishes Provincial and Municipal Forums on Climate Change. These are intergovernmental bodies, designed to coordinate climate change response actions. Section 10 grants authority to the President to establish a Presidential Climate Commission, which may consist of up to 30 members, comprising representatives of government, organised labour, civil society and business to advise, monitor and evaluate the state's climate change response.

Chapter 3 sets out requirements for climate actions by provinces and municipalities. Each province, metropolitan or district municipality must have a climate change needs and response assesment within one year of the publication of the National Adaptation Strategy and this assessment must be reviewed and if necessary amended at least once every five years. Within two years of the assessment, the mayor (or MEC) must develop and implement a climate change response implementation plan and review, or if necessary, amend the plan at least once every five years.

Chapter 4 focuses on institutional arrangements for climate change adaptation policy. Within one year of this Act, the Minister must determine national adaptation objectives, indicators and a deadline by which the objectives should be incorporated into national planning instruments. Within one year of this Act, the Minister must also develop adaptation scenarios. Within two years of this Act, the Minister must publish a National Adaptation Strategy and Plan, to be reviewed and if necessary amended every five years. Within two years of publishing the National Adaptation Strategy and Plan, the Minister must also develop and implement a Sector Adaptation Strategy and Plan (to be reviewed and if necessary, amended every five years). Schedule 2 sets out the national departments and state-owned entities required to develop a Sector Adaptation Strategy and Plan, whom must also report progress to the Cabinet Minister for environmental affairs every five years. Section 20 also requires the Minister to publish a Synthesis Adaptation Report for consideration by Cabinet.

Chapter 5 establishes the framework for mitigation, although the targets sit outside of the Act. The Minister, in consultation with the Cabinet, is required to determine the national greenhouse gas emissions trajectory (quantitative targets) and publish this in the Gazette. In the meantime, an emissions trajectory is set out in Schedule 3: greenhouse gas emisisons will peak between 2020-2025 in a range with a lower limit of 398 Megatonnes (109kg) (Mt) CO2-eq and upper limits of 583 Mt CO2-eq and 614 Mt CO2-eq for 2020 and 2025; plateau for up to 10 years after the peak within the range with a lower limit of 398 Mt CO2-eq and an upper limit of 614 Mt CO2-eq; and from 2036 onwards, decline in absolute terms to a range with a lower limit of 212 Mt CO2-eq and an upper limit of 428 Mt CO2-eq by 2050. The trajectory must be reviewed every five years.

Under Section 22, the Minister must, within one year of this Act, publish the greenhouse gas emitting sectors and sub-sectors that are subject to sectoral emissions targets. These must include quantitative and qualitative emissions reduction goals for the first five years, the subsequent five to 1- years and for a 10- to 15-year period thereafter. The Minister responsible for each sector and sub-sector must then, within one year of publication of the sectoral emissions targets, develop and implement policies and measures to achieve those targets.

Sections 23 and 24 require the Minister to determine and allocate carbon budgets to persons that conduct activities that emit greenhouse gases above certain thresholds (determined by the Minister). If allocated a carbon budget, such person must prepare and submit a greenhouse gas mitigation plan for approval. These will be budgets for at least three successive five-year periods and will specify the maximum amount of emissions that may be emitted during the first five-year period. Section 25 also requires the Minister to regulate phasing down or phasing out of synthetic greenhouse gases. Section 26 establishes an institutional arrangement to facilitate creation of a National Greenhouse Gas Inventory and Inventory Report.

Chapter 6 grants powers to the Minister to make additional regulations relating to this Act, and requires public consultation procedures to be followed when implementing multiple provisions of the Act. Section 32 also establishes penalties if a person required to prepare a mitigation plan under Section 24 fails to do so.

Document Title: New Vehicle Efficiency Standard Act 2024
Family Title: New Vehicle Efficiency Standard Act 2024
Family Summary:
The New Vehicle Efficiency Standard Act 2024 establishes Australia's first legally binding fuel efficiency standards to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from specified road vehicles.

The objectives of the Act are to:

(a) Establish a vehicle emissions standard covering certain vehicles that will:

(i) Create economic incentives for the manufacturers and suppliers of such vehicles to provide models to the Australian market that emit less carbon dioxide; and

(ii) Provide consumers in Australia with a choice of vehicles that meet their work and lifestyle needs while also meeting the environmental expectations of the community; and

(iii) Be transparent, flexible and able to be calibrated over time according to policy needs; and

(iv) Be robust and based on the best available evidence and data; and

(b) Reduce carbon dioxide emissions in the transport sector, thereby contributing to the achievement of Australia’s greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets; and

(c) Give effect to certain obligations that Australia has as a party to the Climate Change Convention, the Kyoto Protocol, and the Paris Agreement.

Document Title: National Plan For Integrated Management of Urban Solid Waste
Family Title: National Plan For Integrated Management of Urban Solid Waste
Family Summary: The National Plan for Integrated Management of Urban Solid Waste is a nationwide strategy aimed at improving quality of life and ensuring a healthy environment for Paraguay’s urban populations by 2030. It is structured around five key strategies: strengthening the institutional framework for waste management; expanding universal access to urban sanitation services; promoting waste prevention, reuse, and treatment; ensuring proper final disposal through sanitary landfills while closing and remediating open dumps; and advancing community environmental education, training, and technological development.

Document Title: Decree 10247/07
Family Title: Law 3001/06 strengthening the adaptation capacity of ecosystems and the protection of their biodiversity through the payment of ecosystem services
Family Summary: This law promotes the conservation, protection, recovery and sustainable development of the country's biological diversity and natural resources, through the fair, timely and adequate valuation and remuneration of environmental services. Article 2 lists carbon absorption as one of the environmental services in scope. This law was partially implemented by Decree 10247/07, which defines that owners of rural properties in the Eastern Region of more than twenty hectares, who have maintained more than twenty-five per cent (25%) of the area of natural forests (i.e., above that percentage), who have registered in the Special Register of Natural Forests, may certify the environmental services produced by their forests and then negotiate the Environmental Services Certificates.
Instrument: Standards, obligations and norms|Regulation;Nature based solutions and ecosystem restoration|Direct Investment

Document Title: Marco de Politica del Sector Agropecuario (MPSA) 2020–2030
Family Title: Agricultural Sector Policy Framework (MPSA) 2020–2030
Family Summary:
The Agricultural Sector Policy Framework (MPSA) 2020–2030 provides a national roadmap for Paraguay’s agrarian sector, integrating environmental, social, and economic dimensions along with agro-industry. It focuses on three main pillars: developing competitive markets for agricultural, livestock, and forestry products; securing access to rural land through property regularization; and strengthening public support services such as research, extension, animal and plant health, land governance, and financing.

It includes issues related to climate change mitigation and adaptation, such as working on the development of a program that includes varieties adapted to climate and soil conditions, as well as improvements in rice production. Additionally, it also includes the design of mechanisms for implementing better agronomic and soil management practices and promotes sustainable forestry practices, afforestation and reforestation for energy purposes, and the valorization of native forests through mechanisms like international carbon credit sales.

The policy framework was approved by Resolution 466/2020.

Document Title: National Implementation Plan of the Sendai Framework 2018-2022
Family Title: National Implementation Plan of the Sendai Framework 2018-2022
Family Summary: The Plan constitutes an important public policy tool that will contribute to ensuring that State actions, at different levels, focus on comprehensive disaster risk management and reduction, as cross-cutting pillars for the development of policies in sectoral plans. It is a short-, medium-, and long-term multisectoral planning tool for achieving the objective and seven targets of the Sendai Framework, which allows progress toward strengthening resilience in Paraguay. Furthermore, with this Plan, the country meets the Sendai Framework's goal of "increasing the number of countries with disaster risk reduction strategies and/or plans by 2020."
