Document Title: Guidelines to mainstream climate change in the National Policy for Sustainable Mobility
Family Title: National Policy for Sustainable Urban Mobility of Ecuador (PNMUS) 2023–2030
Family Summary: The National Policy for Sustainable Urban Mobility (PNMUS) 2023–2030 provides a strategic framework to address the environmental, economic, and social challenges of current mobility systems in Ecuador. Guided by the Constitution, the Organic Law on Land Transport, Traffic, and Road Safety, and international commitments such as the Paris Agreement and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, the policy aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve accessibility, and promote sustainable urban planning.On climate change, the plan incorporates three climate-focused approaches to enhance urban resilience and reduce environmental impacts: (1) promoting sustainable and efficient mobility modes, such as public transport and active transportation, to reduce private vehicle reliance; (2) developing resilient infrastructure to adapt to climate change, including climate-proof urban spaces and facilities; and (3) mitigating the effects of urban heat waves through nature-based solutions, such as green streets, shaded spaces, and microclimates. These approaches align with the policy's broader goals of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and fostering climate-resilient cities.The PNMUS serves as a comprehensive guide for local governments, supporting the implementation of Sustainable Urban Mobility Plans (PMUS) and providing technical and financial resources for cities to transition toward low-carbon and inclusive mobility systems.

Document Title: Resolution SGR 469-2023 - National guidelines for the design, implementation, operation and sustainability of warning systems ( RESOLUCIÓN Nro. SGR-469-2023 - Lineamientos nacionales para el diseño, implementación, funcionamiento y sostenibilidad de los sistemas de alerta)
Family Title: Resolution SGR 469-2023 - National guidelines for the design, implementation, operation and sustainability of warning systems
Family Summary:
Approximately 62 million people have been directly affected by disasters, and most of them live in countries without functioning early warning systems. This situation clearly indicates that unless greater investment is made in building resilience by expanding the coverage of early warning systems, developing countries will face an increase in the number of people affected by hazards, especially as the population continues to grow.

According to the records of the Adverse Events Monitoring Directorate of the Risk Management Secretariat, there has been a considerable increase in the number of people directly affected by disasters in Ecuador over the past 12 years. The year 2021 was the year with the highest number of people affected, with 585,160. Due to its geographical location, Ecuador faces a variety of natural, socio-natural and anthropogenic hazards, resulting in frequent disasters with a significant impact on the population, economy and livelihoods. The most recurrent hazards in Ecuador include earthquakes, mass movements, floods and volcanic hazards.

Document Title: Standards to mainstream risk management in Ministries, State Secretariats and public institutions (Estándares para transversalizar la gestión de riesgos en los Ministerios, Secretarías de Estado e instituciones públicas)
Family Title: Standards to mainstream risk management in Ministries, State Secretariats and public institutions
Family Summary:
Establish general guidelines for mainstreaming Risk Management in Ministries, State Secretariats and Public Institutions, with respect to their competence in the national territory, through a Management Model that allows coordination with the actors of the National Decentralized Management System of Risks (SNDGR).

This document applies to Ministries, State Secretariats and Public Institutions at the national level and their respective deconcentrated levels.

Document Title: Organic Law for the comprehensive planning of the special territorial district of the Amazon
Family Title: Organic Law for the comprehensive planning of the special territorial district of the Amazon
Family Summary: The Organic Law for the Comprehensive Planning of the Special Territorial District of the Amazon establishes a framework for integrated territorial planning that addresses social, economic, cultural, and environmental dimensions of the Amazon region. Guided by the principles of Sumak Kawsay (living well) and Ecuador's Constitution, the law prioritises sustainable development, the protection of ecosystems and biodiversity, and the rights of nature. It also emphasises equitable development, respect for cultural heritage, and the active participation of Indigenous communities, peoples, and nationalities in planning and decision-making.A focus on climate change is considered within the law, particularly in its mandates to incorporate climate criteria into local and national planning. Articles 23 and 55 require the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from deforestation and forest degradation, the promotion of sustainable forest and agroforestry management, and the implementation of adaptation and mitigation measures. Article 56 outlines priorities for climate action, including protecting vulnerable populations, biodiversity, and infrastructure, and aligning local efforts with the National Climate Change Strategy. The law underscores coordination among government levels and stakeholders to ensure a unified and effective response to climate challenges in the Amazon.

Document Title: Ministerial Agreement 056 establishing a framework for the REDD+ implementation
Family Title: Ministerial Agreement 056 establishing a framework for the REDD+ implementation
Family Summary:
The Ministerial Agreement 056 establishes the regulatory framework for the registration, approval, monitoring, and evaluation of implementing partners and action plans under Ecuador's REDD+ initiative. Aligned with constitutional mandates on environment and climate provisions, including Articles 275 and 414, the agreement seeks to reduce deforestation, limit greenhouse gas emissions, and promote ecosystem restoration, in accordance with the Plan de Acción REDD+ "Bosques para el Buen Vivir" (2016–2025).

The Ministry of Environment, as the national REDD+ authority, is responsible for overseeing the registration process and tracking the progress of REDD+ plans. Implementing partners are required to ensure social and environmental safeguards, involve local stakeholders, and report semiannually on financial and operational progress. The agreement also mandates compliance with Free, Prior, and Informed Consent processes when activities occur on collective lands, ensuring equitable participation and benefit-sharing among all stakeholders.

Document Title: Ministerial Agreement No. 141. Establishment of National Environmental Authority Standards for Carbon Neutrality
Family Title: Ministerial Agreement No. 141. Establishment of National Environmental Authority Standards for Carbon Neutrality
Family Summary: The Ministerial Agreement No. 141 establishes the framework for Ecuador’s National Environmental Authority to regulate and promote carbon neutrality initiatives. It defines a governance structure led by the Minister of Environment, Water, and Ecological Transition and outlines the responsibilities of the National Environmental Authority for Carbon Neutrality, including administering the "Carbon Neutral Seal". The Carbon Neutral Seal serves as official recognition for entities achieving verified carbon-neutral status through compliance with established criteria and technical standards.This Ministerial Agreement emphasises the state’s constitutional commitments to a healthy environment, efficient energy use, and the adoption of environmentally sustainable practices to mitigate climate change. It establishes a centralised registry to document programs, projects, and consultants involved in carbon-neutral activities, promoting transparency and public access. Additionally, the agreement supports collaboration across governmental, private, and public sectors to advance Ecuador’s climate policies and sustainable development goals. It facilitates the development of technical standards, validation processes, and recognition systems, positioning the country as a leader in climate action and carbon neutrality efforts.

Document Title: Ministerial Agreement 116 establishing the REDD+ Action Plan “Forest for the good living” and the general REDD+ implementation
Family Title: Ministerial Agreement 116 establishing the REDD+ Action Plan “Forest for the good living” and the general REDD+ implementation
Family Summary: Ministerial Agreement 116 establishes the REDD+ Action Plan “Forrest for the good living” (“Bosques para el Buen Vivir”) as a national framework for mitigating climate change through sustainable forest management. Anchored in Ecuador’s Constitution, including Articles 14, 74, and 414, the plan aims to address the primary causes of deforestation and reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the land-use sector. It aligns with international commitments such as UNFCCC Decision 1/CP.16, emphasising compatibility with national development goals and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).The plan is guided by principles of participatory governance, equity, transparency, and financial efficiency. It ensures the protection of individual and collective rights, integrates a gender perspective in its implementation, and prohibits the commercialisation of emission reductions in carbon markets. Funding mechanisms include private sector contributions, incentivised through tax and fiscal benefits, while a national safeguards information system will monitor and report on REDD+ actions and compliance with social and environmental safeguards.By institutionalizing this framework, Ecuador aims to tackle deforestation and climate change while promoting sustainable development and the equitable use of natural resources, in line with the constitutional principle of Buen Vivir (Good Living).

Document Title: Green Hydrogen Roadmap for Ecuador
Family Title: Green Hydrogen Roadmap for Ecuador
Family Summary: The Green Hydrogen Roadmap outlines Ecuador's strategic plan for producing and utilising green hydrogen as a cornerstone of its energy transition. With an electricity matrix largely based on renewable hydropower (approximately 60% of installed capacity and 78% of generation in 2021), Ecuador aims to leverage its renewable resources and existing infrastructure to develop a green hydrogen economy.The roadmap emphasises the need to establish a regulatory framework to attract national and international investments, reduce production costs through incentives, and foster technological and knowledge transfer through regional and global partnerships. Key sectors such as agriculture, energy, and industrial manufacturing are identified as beneficiaries of green hydrogen and its derivatives, such as methanol and synthetic fuels. Additionally, green hydrogen is seen as a tool for reducing dependence on fossil fuels, creating jobs, and enabling the export of value-added sustainable products.The roadmap is structured into three phases: (i) initial (2025), (ii) medium-term deployment (2030), and (iii) long-term consolidation (2050), with ambitious capacity goals for green hydrogen production. It sets forth actions in research and development, regulatory frameworks, infrastructure development, and international cooperation to ensure the roadmap’s successful implementation.

Document Title: Organic Law on energy competitiveness
Family Title: Organic Law on energy competitiveness
Family Summary: The Organic Law on Energy Competitiveness establishes a framework to address Ecuador's energy crisis by promoting sustainable and cost-effective energy solutions. It aims to optimise public and private resource management in the electricity sector, improve energy self-sufficiency, and ensure alignment with constitutional mandates, including environmental protection and the promotion of clean, low-impact energy technologies. The law emphasises equitable access to energy while fostering the adoption of renewable energy sources and distributed generation systems for residential and institutional use.The regulation encourages the use of renewable and clean energy through mechanisms such as bidirectional metering and compensation for surplus energy fed into the public grid. It also guarantees environmental oversight by the competent regulatory agency and prohibits the privatisation of publicly funded energy infrastructure. By integrating sustainability and efficiency into energy policy, the law supports Ecuador's commitment to transitioning toward a more resilient, decentralized, and environmentally responsible energy system.

Document Title: Ministerial Agreement No. 137. Guidelines for Climate Change Plans of Autonomous Governments
Family Title: Ministerial Agreement No. 137. Guidelines for Climate Change Plans of Autonomous Governments
Family Summary: Ministerial Agreement No. 137 establishes guidelines for creating climate change plans, programs, and strategies by Ecuador's Autonomous Decentralized Governments (GADs). The framework aligns with Ecuador's constitutional commitment to environmental sustainability and climate action, ensuring that local planning integrates climate considerations. The agreement aims to enhance the alignment of local efforts with the National Climate Change Strategy, Development and Territorial Organisation Plans (PDOT), and national reporting mechanisms.The regulation outlines a structured approach for Autonomous Decentralized Governments to identify climate threats, assess vulnerabilities, evaluate mitigation opportunities, and prioritise adaptation and mitigation measures. These measures are to be detailed through descriptive profiles, monitoring indicators, and cost estimations. Additionally, it requires ongoing monitoring and periodic reporting to the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Ecological Transition. Through these guidelines, GADs can formalise their climate initiatives and obtain official approval, fostering cohesive and effective climate action across local and national levels.

Document Title: Organic Law on Social Housing
Family Title: Organic Law on Social Housing
Family Summary:
This Organic Law establishes the legal framework to ensure access to adequate and dignified housing. Rooted in Ecuador’s Constitution, the law considers the right to live in a healthy and ecologically balanced environment (Sumak Kawsay) and prioritises the principles of universal access, equality, sustainability, and cultural respect in housing and habitat policies.

The law mandates the creation of social housing plans as part of local land-use and territorial planning, integrating climate change adaptation and mitigation measures. It promotes environmentally sustainable construction practices, conservation of natural ecosystems, and the rational use of resources. Key elements include promoting resilient urban planning, preserving agricultural lands, and fostering the use of ancestral and local knowledge in housing solutions. The regulation also prioritises equitable access to social housing for vulnerable populations, including women heads of households and economically disadvantaged families.

Climate change considerations are embedded through the promotion of energy-efficient infrastructure, sustainable mobility systems, and resilient urban designs to withstand climate-related risks. The law highlights the responsibility of both public and private sectors to ensure sustainability, accountability, and participatory governance in the production and management of social housing.

Document Title: National Drought Plan. Together building resilience 2021-2025
Family Title: National Drought Plan. Together building resilience 2021-2025
Family Summary:
The National Drought Plan - Together building resilience (“PNS”) of Ecuador provides a strategic framework to address the growing challenges of drought, which severely impact the country's agricultural production, hydroelectric power generation, and water and sanitation systems. Developed by the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Ecological Transition (MAATE) in collaboration with the National Risk and Emergency Management Service (SNGRE), the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MAG), and the CIIFEN (International Research Center on El Niño Phenomenon) through the Euroclima+ project, the PNS aims to mitigate drought risks while enhancing resilience at the national level.

The plan highlights the devastating effects of drought, including crop and livestock losses, water shortages, and ecosystem imbalances, which exacerbate economic losses, food insecurity, and health issues. With a long-term perspective, it prioritises reducing drought risk through integrated planning, intersectoral coordination, and leveraging climate data to establish effective monitoring systems. By focusing on sectors like territorial planning, agriculture, water resources, risk management, and the environment, the plan addresses gaps in information and capacity, promoting evidence-based strategies and collaboration among public and private stakeholders, academia, and civil society.

The PNS aligns national policies with global frameworks and emphasises the development of innovative programs for risk reduction, response, and recovery. It sets objectives to strengthen the adaptive capacity of vulnerable communities, minimise economic losses, enhance drought monitoring, and generate evidence of the impacts of drought under current and future climate scenarios.
Keyword: Adaptation;Climate Change Risks;Disaster Risk Management;Water Management

Document Title: Organic Law on Comprehensive Disaster Risk Management
Family Title: Organic Law on Comprehensive Disaster Risk Management
Family Summary: The Organic Law on Comprehensive Disaster Risk Management establishes the framework for planning, organising, and coordinating policies and services to address the risks associated with natural and anthropogenic disasters, pandemics, and emergencies. This law aims to reduce vulnerability, safeguard human lives, communities, and nature, and enhance resilience through comprehensive risk management. It provides for the integration of disaster risk management into national, sectoral, and local planning, ensuring alignment with the National Development Plan and environmental conservation efforts.Key principles of this law include equity, solidarity, responsibility, and the protection of vulnerable groups, nature, and ecosystems. It mandates a cross-sectoral approach, integrating climate change adaptation and mitigation with disaster risk management, and emphasises the importance of prevention measures, early warning systems, and recovery planning. The law also recognises the cultural and territorial rights of Indigenous peoples and promotes their participation in risk management processes.In the climate realm, the law prioritises complementarity between disaster risk management, environmental policies, and climate change actions. It establishes links with instruments such as the National Development Plan, climate adaptation and mitigation plans, and water resource management plans as essential tools for disaster risk planning.

Document Title: Regulation to the Organic Code of the Environment
Family Title: Regulation to the Organic Code of the Environment
Family Summary: The Regulation to the Organic Code of the Environment (RCOA) establishes detailed guidelines for implementing Ecuador's environmental policies, focusing -among others- on sustainable development, biodiversity conservation, and climate change management. Aligned with the principles of the Constitution, the regulation emphasises the right to a healthy and ecologically balanced environment as essential for sustainability and the Sumak Kawsay (living well). The framework mandates all public, private, and community actors to integrate environmental considerations into their operations and decision-making processes.The regulation addresses climate change through dedicated chapters and sections. It highlights the need for sectoral and local planning that incorporates climate resilience measures, promotes sustainable forest and agroforestry management, and reduces greenhouse gas emissions. It mandates the inclusion of climate change criteria in national and local territorial plans and requires all levels of government to align with the National Climate Change Strategy. Key instruments include the National Adaptation Plan, National Mitigation Plan, and Ecuador’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).To support these efforts, the Regulation to the Organic Code of the Environment outlines mechanisms for climate financing, technological transfer, and knowledge management. It emphasises intersectoral coordination, capacity building, and the use of traditional and ancestral knowledge in addressing climate challenges. Specific measures, such as prioritising sustainable mobility, restoring degraded ecosystems, managing wildfire risks, and creating carbon-neutral initiatives, underscore the regulation’s commitment to integrating climate action into Ecuador's broader environmental governance framework.

Document Title: The National Plan for Disaster Response
Family Title: The National Plan for Disaster Response
Family Summary: The objective of the National Plan for Disaster Response is to guarantee attention to the population affected by dangerous, natural or anthropogenic events, with the establishment of procedures and protocols, generating adequate coordination and inter-institutional coordination. The plan notably focuses on natural disasters as flood and drought. Specific objectives are 1) to provide to the institutions of the National DGR System a tool that guides the fulfillment of the functions, procedures and actions that they must develop during the response to emergencies and disasters, 2) protect life and assets of the affected population, 3)maintain governance and governability during the response, 4) guarantee the planned and orderly intervention of the authorities and institutions through the Emergency Operations Committees, 4)optimize time and available resources during response operation,5) generate the foundations for the recovery process.

Document Title: Law no.78/2017 ratifying the Paris Agreement
Family Title: Law no.78/2017 ratifying the Paris Agreement
Family Summary: Law no.78/2017 ratifies the Paris Agreement of December 12th 2015, committing Moldova to climate change mitigation targets and adaptation standards.

Document Title: Decision no. 108/2019 on the approval of the Methodology for calculating the impact of biofuels and bioliquids on greenhouse gas emissions
Family Title: Decision no. 108/2019 on the approval of the Methodology for calculating the impact of biofuels and bioliquids on greenhouse gas emissions
Family Summary: Decision no. 108/2019 approves a methodology for calculating the impact of biofuels and bioliquids on greenhouse gas emissions, and places responsibility for its implementation on the Ministry for Agriculture, Regional Development and Environment. This decision is passed persuant to Law no. 10/2016 on promoting the use of energy from renewable sources.

Document Title: Decision no.444/2020 on the establishment of a mechanism for coordinating activities in the field of climate change
Family Title: Decision no. 444/2020 on the establishment of a mechanism for coordinating activities in the field of climate change
Family Summary: Decision no. 444/2020 establishes the National Commission on Climate Change and defines its ministerial composition, duties and intersectoral co-ordination roles. The decision also gives regulations and procedures for the implementation of 'NAMA' (Nationally Appropriate Mitigation Action) projects to mitigate climate change, and provides a detailed approval process. The procedure of a NAP (National Adaptation Process) is also defined. The roles and responsibilities of the National Commission are further defined in Decision no. 425/2024.

Document Title: Law no. 368/2023 on hydrological and meteorological activity
Family Title: Law no. 368/2023 on hydrological and meteorological activity
Family Summary: Law no. 368/2023 on hydrological and meteorological activity provides a framework for the relationship between meteorological/hydrological activity and the sustainable functioning and development of society in Moldova. The law applies to any human meteorological or hydrological activity, and enshrines the value of warning systems, data accessibility, global causes/impacts, and international standardisation/comparability of reporting. Scientific study and reporting of climate change data is explicitly established as a core element of meteorological and hydrological activity, which should be reported nationally and co-ordinated with global scientific efforts.

Document Title: Government Decision no. 373/2018 on the National Pollutant Release and Transfer Register
Family Title: Government Decision no. 373/2018 on the National Pollutant Release and Transfer Register
Family Summary: Government Decision no. 373/2018 establishes a National Pollutant Release and Transfer Register, an automated and centralised system operated by the Ministry of Environment. This system records air, soil and water pollutants, as well as off-site transfers of polluting material. The decision stipulates that this registry must be made available to the public through sharing the UNFCCC and a range of other means, with a separate procedure for exceptions.

Document Title: Law no. 43/2023 on fluorinated greenhouse gases
Family Title: Law No. 43/2023 on fluorinated greenhouse gases
Family Summary: Law No. 43/2023 transposes EU Regulation No. 517/2014, and provides a framework for the regulation of fluorinated greenhouse gas emissions, applying to hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons and sulfur hexafluoride. This law approves the Hydrofluorocarbon Phase-out Programme, and establishes other powers and duties held by the Ministry of Environment including enforcement of maximum market volume quotas, supervision of reporting standards and sanctioning of noncompliant subnational entities. The law also places reporting, certification, reclamation and leakage-prevention responsibilities on any enterprises or operators using fluorinated greenhouse gases.

Document Title: GD no. 425/2024 on the organization and operation of the National Commission on Climate Change
Family Title: GD no. 425/2024 on the organization and operation of the National Commission on Climate Change
Family Summary: GD no. 425/2024 defines and regulates the functions of the National Commission on Climate Change. It establishes the main objectives of the commission - to promote cross-sectoral cooperation, mainstream climate considerations in new policy, co-ordinate climate mitigation/adaptation funding streams, and ensure transparent dialogue with the public. This decision also defines the ministerial composition of the commission, and its powers and rights.

Document Title: Decision no. 1009 of 10.12.2014 approving the Climate Change Adaptation Strategy by 2020
Family Title: Decision no. 1009/2014 approving the Climate Change Adaptation Strategy by 2020
Family Summary: This 2014 decision by the Government of the republic of Moldova adopts the Government's Climate Change Adaptation Strategy and the action plan to implement it. The decision includes provisions for the implementation of the plan to be monitored by the Ministry of the Environment and tasks the central government with developing sectoral strategies to implement the plan and local governments with taking action to meet the plan's targets. The strategy and action plan are attached as annexes to the decision and cover a wide range of measures to address climate impacts in the agricultural sector, water resources management sector, health sector, forest sector, energy sector and transport sector. The strategy aims to increase the capacity of Moldova to adapt and respond to actual or potential climate change effects and has three specific objectives: 1. Create by 2018 the institutional framework in the field of climate change that would assure the efficient implementation of adaptation measures at the national, sector and local levels. 2. Create by 2020 a mechanism to monitor the climate change impacts, the related social and economic vulnerability and for the management/dissemination of the information on risks and climate disasters. 3. Assure the development of climate resilience by reducing at least by 50% the climate change risks and facilitate climate change adaptation in six priority sectors by 2020.

Document Title: National Strategy for Agricultural and Rural Development (NSARD/SNDAR) for the years 2023-2030
Family Title: National Strategy for Agricultural and Rural Development (NSARD/SNDAR) for the years 2023-2030
Family Summary:
The 2014-2020 iteration of the National Strategy for Agricultural and Rural Development aims to ensure a sustainable management of natural resources in agriculture. This should notably be done by increasing the use of renewable energy resources in the sector, and by reducing the vulnerability of crop productions to climate change.

Document Title: Indigenous Plan for Climate Action and Disaster Risk Reduction (PIAC-RRD)
Family Title: Indigenous Plan for Climate Action and Disaster Risk Reduction (PIAC-RRD)
Family Summary:
The PIAC-RRD is a participatory plan developed by 13 member indigenous associations across both the Eastern and Western (Chaco) regions of Paraguay. Its purpose is to enable indigenous peoples to adapt to climate change, reduce disaster risk, preserve their forests and biodiversity, and integrate their traditional knowledge with technological tools. Overall, the plan aims to strengthen indigenous resilience, protect territories, and ensure that adaptation and mitigation are grounded in indigenous perspectives, cultures, intergenerational knowledge, and fairness.

The plan is organised in 4 main axes: (i) Livelihoods, Forests and Biodiversity, (ii) Energy, (iii) Health and Water, (iv) Risks and Disasters, Infrastructure and Roads.

Document Title: Decree 2.553/2024 - Energy Policy of the Republic of Paraguay to 2050
Family Title: Decree 2.553/2024 - Energy Policy of the Republic of Paraguay to 2050
Family Summary:
Decree 2.553/2024 repealed decree 6092/2016 and approved the new Energy Policy of the Republic of Paraguay to 2050.

The vision of this new policy is to consolidate an energy matrix that meets the country's needs, with sustainable use and exploitation of national natural resources and energy, within a framework of regional integration, as an essential element of the comprehensive development of the entire population and the productive and social sectors.

The policy outlines five main goals for the energy sector:

  1. Sustainable and resilient energy supply – Ensure a reliable energy system that supports the population’s well-being and economic development, prioritizing the use of national energy and mining resources.
  2. Leverage energy sector strengths – Use the sector’s competitive advantages to drive socio-economic growth, energy transition, job creation, and global integration.
  3. Regional energy hub – Position the country as a central player in regional energy integration.
  4. Equitable energy access – Guarantee affordable, safe, and sustainable energy for vulnerable groups.
  5. Active participation of stakeholders – Strengthen the role of consumers and other key actors in shaping the energy sector.

Document Title: Government Agreement 73-2021 (Acuerdo Gubernativo 73-2021)
Family Title: Internal Organic Regulations of the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources (Reglamento Orgánico Interno del Ministerio de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales)
Family Summary: Government Agreement No. 73-2021 establishes the organic structure and functions of Guatemala's Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources (MARN), with particular emphasis on climate change governance and environmental management. The regulation reorganises MARN to enhance implementation of environmental policies, including conservation, protection, and improvement of environmental resources, while specifically incorporating climate change adaptation, mitigation, and vulnerability reduction as core ministerial functions. The framework aligns with Guatemala's international environmental obligations and domestic legislation, including the Climate Change Adaptation and Greenhouse Gas Mitigation Law (Decree No. 7-2013).The restructuring creates a dedicated Vice-Ministry for Natural Resources and Climate Change, comprising specialised departments for climate vulnerability and adaptation, mitigation strategies, climate science and metrics, risk prevention, and land degradation control. This institutional framework establishes systematic approaches to greenhouse gas monitoring, climate data integration, and multi-sectoral coordination for climate action. The regulation mandates development of climate adaptation and mitigation strategies, implementation of the national climate change information system, and coordination of international climate commitments, including reporting under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, thereby institutionalising climate governance within Guatemala's environmental administration.

Document Title: Guatemala's Gender and Climate Change Action Plan (PAGcc-Guatemala) [Plan de Acción de Género y Cambio Climático de Guatemala (PAGcc-Guatemala)]
Family Title: Guatemala's Gender and Climate Change Action Plan (PAGcc) [Plan de Acción de Género y Cambio Climático de Guatemala (PAGcc)]
Family Summary:
The Gender and Climate Change Action Plan of Guatemala (PAGcc) represents a comprehensive policy framework designed to integrate gender-responsive and intersectional approaches into the country's climate commitments and actions. Developed through collaborative and consensual processes involving expert consultations, participatory workshops, and social validation by indigenous communities, youth, and civil society organisations, the plan seeks to address gender gaps within Guatemala's climate change response whilst aligning with national policy frameworks and international agreements.

The plan's climate change and energy transition elements are structured around five priority sectors corresponding to Guatemala's Nationally Determined Contribution: agriculture, coastal zones, forestry, environmental protected areas, and energy and water management. Each sector incorporates gender analysis resulting in specific sub-plans with dedicated objectives, actions, and indicators designed to ensure that climate adaptation and mitigation interventions are accessible to and beneficial for women, men, indigenous peoples, local communities, and young people. The overarching objective guarantees that Guatemala's national climate commitments are implemented through an intersectional and socially inclusive lens with a gender perspective, ensuring equitable access to, participation in, and benefits from climate adaptation and mitigation measures across all demographic groups and sectors.

Document Title: National Energy Plan 2017-2032 (Plan Nacional de Energía 2017-2032)
Family Title: National Energy Plan 2017-2032 (Plan Nacional de Energía 2017-2032)
Family Summary:
The National Energy Plan 2017–2032 provides Guatemala’s overarching strategy for aligning the development of the energy sector with national and international climate commitments, including the Ley Marco de Cambio Climático, the Política Energética 2013–2027, the Política Nacional de Cambio Climático, the National Development Plan K’atun 2032, and the Sustainable Development Goals. Its central aim is to reduce national vulnerability to climate change by building adaptive capacity and advancing mitigation actions through reduced greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The plan defines three strategic axes: (i) Sustainable use of renewable resources, (ii) Energy efficiency and savings, and (iii) Reduction of GHG emissions. These axes are designed to guide all sub‑sectors and stakeholders of the energy system, from central and municipal government to civil society and the private sector.

The plan promotes a transition towards a more sustainable and diversified energy matrix, emphasising the expansion of renewable electricity generation while maintaining energy security. It strengthens the regulatory and institutional frameworks for efficiency measures, notably through the preparation of a dedicated Plan Nacional de Eficiencia Energética, and highlights the socio‑economic co‑benefits of reduced fuel imports, greater electricity coverage, and improved productivity. A central mitigation target is the 29.2 per cent reduction of GHG emissions by 2032, lowering projected emissions from 16.82 MtCO₂e under a business‑as‑usual scenario to 11.91 MtCO₂e. This commitment directly contributes to Guatemala’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) under the UNFCCC, including the unconditional target of 11.2 per cent emissions reduction by 2030. In parallel, the plan seeks to curtail reliance on traditional biomass, particularly in the residential sector, given its contribution both to deforestation and to emission growth, while also extending electricity access and reinforcing national energy security.

Document Title: National Energy Plan 2019-2032 (Plan Nacional de energía 2019-2032)
Family Title: National Energy Efficiency Plan 2019-2032 (Plan Nacional de Eficiencia Energética 2019-2032)
Family Summary:
Guatemala’s National Energy Plan 2019–2032 sets the strategic framework for reducing greenhouse gas emissions from the energy sector by promoting energy efficiency and savings, prioritising sustainable renewable energy to diversify the electricity generation mix, and substituting traditional fuelwood with cleaner energy sources and technologies. Led by the Ministry of Energy and Mines and aligned with the Energy Policy 2013–2027, it organises action under three axes: sustainable use of natural resources; energy efficiency and savings; and reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.

Within this framework, the National Energy Efficiency Plan 2019–2032 establishes a cross‑sectoral programme to characterise and manage energy demand in the residential, industrial, transport, commerce and services, public services, and academic sectors. Guided by principles of legislation, standardisation and culture, it envisages the development and application of energy regulations, the use of voluntary standards that may be made mandatory by regulators, market‑shaping norms for consumers, and public awareness and behavioural change to optimise end‑use efficiency. The plan sets a projected avoided‑energy target of 69,790 TJ (terajoules) by 2032 relative to a business‑as‑usual scenario—equivalent to a 15.1% reduction in national energy consumption—aiming to deliver cost and productivity gains while contributing to national emissions reductions.

Document Title: National Policy for the Prevention and Control of Forest Fires and Integrated Fire Management (Política Nacional de Prevención y Control de Incendios Forestales y Manejo Integrado del Fuego)
Family Title: National Policy for the Prevention and Control of Forest Fires and Integrated Fire Management (Política Nacional de Prevención y Control de Incendios Forestales y Manejo Integrado del Fuego)
Family Summary:
The National Policy for the Prevention and Control of Forest Fires and Integrated Fire Management aims to protect Guatemala's forests and natural ecosystems from the damaging effects of fires. The policy establishes the 'Sistema Nacional de Prevención y Control de Incendios Forestales' (SIPECIF) as the central body responsible for preventing, controlling, and extinguishing forest fires, and for developing policies on integrated fire management. A core objective is to reduce the number of fires and their negative impacts, which include not only ecological damage but also the contribution to climate change through increased atmospheric carbon dioxide. The policy seeks to change traditional practices involving the indiscriminate use of fire in agriculture and livestock farming, promoting the long-term elimination of such methods.

The policy explicitly links forest fires to climate change, highlighting that the resulting deforestation and increased carbon emissions contribute to the greenhouse effect. Its key climate change elements include a specific objective to "reduce the number of forest fires [and] the inappropriate use of fire to decrease carbon dioxide emissions." It also promotes alternative practices to slash-and-burn agriculture and cattle ranching. The policy further identifies the importance of linking its initiatives to international frameworks like Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD), recognising the potential for international funding related to these climate goals. By establishing monitoring and evaluation systems for burned areas, the policy aims to quantify the carbon losses and inform rehabilitation efforts, thus treating forest fires not merely as a conservation issue but as a significant element of the national climate change mitigation strategy.

Document Title: Republic of Moldova Environmental Strategy for 2024-2030
Family Title: Republic of Moldova Environmental Strategy for 2024-2030
Family Summary:
The Environment Strategy for Moldova for 2014-2023 was adopted by the Moldovan Government via decision No. 301 of 24.04.2014. The second of the strategy's key objectives includes the integration of "environmental protection, sustainable development, and green economy principles, of climate change adaptation principles into all sectors of the national economy". The strategy includes an emissions reduction target of 20% by 2020 and sets out a number of actions with regard to the institutional management of environmental matters and knowledge dissemination activities.

The Environment Strategy for 2024-2030 was approved via Government Decision no. 409/2024 and also sets climate change mitigation and adaptation as key priorities. On combating climate change the strategy emphasises the role of the forestry, agricultural and transport sectors, summarising and promoting existing measures to decarbonise and build resilience in these areas. On adaptation to climate change, the strategy emphasises capacity-building as well as the implementation and enhancement of existing sectoral measures. Nature restoration, technological modernisation and enhanced regulation feature prominently across sectors.

Document Title: National Bovine Livestock Policy (Política Ganadera Bovina Nacional)
Family Title: National Bovine Livestock Policy (Política Ganadera Bovina Nacional)
Family Summary:
The National Bovine Livestock Policy developed by the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Food (MAGA), aims to promote the sustainable development of the national cattle subsector by enhancing the production and value chains of meat and dairy products. The policy formulation process integrated technical knowledge, historical context, and broad stakeholder consultation, recognising the complex social, economic, environmental, and institutional factors influencing the sector. It emphasises a long-term, interdisciplinary, and intersectoral approach to address challenges such as technological lag, environmental impacts, and climate change, while fostering environmentally responsible livestock practices.

The policy identifies key issues including the migration of cattle farming to ecologically fragile areas due to land-use changes, the persistence of extensive production models unsuited to new soil conditions, and the adverse effects of climate variability on pasture availability and herd productivity. It advocates for the adoption of silvopastoral systems, soil restoration, and water resource protection to improve feed management and animal health. Institutional strengthening is prioritised, with MAGA as the principal public actor providing veterinary services and development support, alongside efforts to enhance the capacity and competitiveness of small and medium producers through stronger private sector organisation. The overarching objective is to increase national meat and milk production sustainably, improve agro-industrial efficiency, and contribute to food security and rural livelihoods, supported by strategic initiatives such as the creation of a development fund, inter-institutional alliances, rural learning centres, and the promotion of climate-resilient production models.

Document Title: Government Agreement No. 211-2005 - Regulations of the Law of Incentives for the Development of Renewable Energy Projects (Acuerdo Gubernativo No. 211-2005 - Reglamento de la Ley de Incentivos para el Desarrollo de Proyectos de Energía Renovable)
Family Title: Regulations of the Law on Incentives for the Development of Renewable Energy Projects (Reglamento de la Ley de Incentivos para el Desarrollo de Proyectos de Energía Renovable)
Family Summary:
This Government Agreement No. 211-2005 establishes the regulatory framework for implementing Guatemala's Law on Incentives for Renewable Energy Projects, providing detailed procedural mechanisms for accessing fiscal, economic, and administrative benefits. The regulation specifies comprehensive application requirements for individuals, legal entities, municipalities, and the National Electrification Institute, mandating submission of detailed project documentation including pre-feasibility studies, technical and financial analyses, and itemised lists of required machinery, equipment, and materials with tariff classifications and intended utilisation.

The framework establishes a two-tier administrative process involving technical evaluation by the competent directorate within twenty days, followed by ministerial resolution within ten days, whilst providing mechanisms for requesting additional information and granting extensions where justified. It creates ongoing compliance obligations including semi-annual progress reporting, archaeological discovery notification, tax payment verification for equipment sales, and project suspension reporting. The regulation establishes detailed supervision and verification mechanisms permitting ministerial, directorate, and tax authority personnel access to project areas, whilst mandating cooperation with tax auditors conducting fiscal verification to ensure proper application of incentives in accordance with the Tax Code and preventing misuse of tax exemptions.

Document Title: National Policy on Biological Diversity - Guatemala 2011 (Política Nacional de Diversidad Biológica - Guatemala 2011)
Family Title: National Policy on Biological Diversity (Política Nacional de Diversidad Biológica)
Family Summary: This policy establishes Guatemala's comprehensive framework for biodiversity conservation and sustainable use, explicitly recognising the fundamental role of biological diversity in sustainable development, climate change adaptation, human health, reduction of socio-environmental vulnerability, and food security. Developed following Guatemala's recognition as a Megadiverse Country by the Conference of the Parties in Nagoya (2010), the policy responds to the dual challenge of Guatemala's exceptional biological wealth and its classification as one of Latin America's most climate-vulnerable nations. The policy is structured around five thematic axes: knowledge and valuation; conservation and restoration; sustainable utilisation; biodiversity in climate change adaptation; and policy instrumentalisation. The fourth axis specifically addresses climate change, promoting biodiversity as a tool for strengthening adaptation and mitigation mechanisms whilst reducing ecosystem, species and genetic vulnerability. This climate-focused component encompasses research partnerships for conservation strategies that enhance adaptation and mitigation options, integration of traditional and local knowledge in climate response measures, and identification of opportunities for benefit-sharing through mechanisms such as REDD+, payment for ecosystem services, and carbon bonds.

Document Title: National Fire Management Strategy for Guatemala for the period 2023 to 2032 (Estrategia Nacional para la Gestión del Fuego para Guatemala para el período 2023 al 2032)
Family Title: National Comprehensive Fire Management Strategy (Estrategia Nacional de Manejo Integral del Fuego)
Family Summary:
The National Comprehensive Fire Management Strategy is a comprehensive strategic framework developed in response to increasing environmental and climatic changes that have exacerbated the frequency, intensity, and severity of forest and wildland-urban interface fires in Guatemala. Recognising the significant social, economic, and environmental impacts of these fires (including deforestation, greenhouse gas emissions, and human casualties) the strategy was formulated through a participatory, interinstitutional process involving key national agencies such as CONRED, INAB, CONAP, MARN, MAGA, and international partners like the US Forest Service. The strategy aims to provide a long-term, integrated approach to fire management that balances the mitigation of negative impacts with the promotion of beneficial ecological and societal effects of fire.

The strategy establishes seven strategic lines of action encompassing governance and institutional coordination, fire prevention through legal frameworks and education, specialised fire response systems, knowledge management and technological development, restoration of fire-affected areas, and the development of local fire management plans for priority sites. It emphasises interinstitutional cooperation, standardisation, and interoperability in planning and operations, alongside community engagement and capacity building. The strategy also recognises the ecological role of fire and its potential as a climate change mitigation tool, advocating for a holistic approach that integrates biodiversity conservation, social equity, and cultural diversity. It aligns with international frameworks and sustainable development goals, aiming to strengthen Guatemala’s resilience to fire-related risks through science-based policies, coordinated governance, and inclusive participation.

Document Title: Moldova Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2025-2030
Family Title: Moldova Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2025-2030
Family Summary: Moldova's Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) for 2025-2030 is based on existing national policies and strategies, and addresses five overarching dimensions of progress for the country's energy system: decarbonisation; energy efficiency; energy security; internal energy markets; research, innovation and competitiveness. The NECP aims to highlight existing, planned and potential policies/investments over the 2025-2030 period. Targets in the plan include a 27% renewable share of gross final energy consumption by 2030, and secondarily a maximum final energy consumption of 2.8 million tonnes of oil equivalent (Mtoe), which is to be achieved by energy efficiency measures. The decarbonisation measures in this plan include financial instruments (ie. integration into EU cross-border emissions trading), biological measures (ie. afforestation, low-carbon cattle feed), renewable energy installations, electrification of public transport, promotion of biogas and biofuels.

Document Title: Guatemala's National REDD+ Strategy (2020-2050) (ENREDD+) Forest | People | Future [Estrategia Nacional REDD+ Guatemala (2020-2050) (ENREDD+) Bosque | Gente | Futuro]
Family Title: Guatemala National REDD+ Strategy (2020-2050) (ENREDD+) [Estrategia Nacional REDD+ Guatemala (2020-2050) (ENREDD+)]
Family Summary:
The Guatemala National REDD+ Strategy (2020-2050) (ENREDD+) constitutes a comprehensive forest-based climate mitigation framework developed in response to Guatemala's commitments under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change and its Nationally Determined Contribution. Led by the Government of Guatemala with participation from over 240 local organisations and supported by the Inter-American Development Bank through Forest Carbon Partnership Facility funding, the strategy operates through three phases: preparation, implementation, and results-based payments. The ENREDD+ aims to articulate governance mechanisms that enable full and effective participation of stakeholders, including women, men, indigenous peoples, and local communities, in reversing deforestation and forest degradation causes to reduce greenhouse gas emissions whilst increasing environmental goods and services from forest ecosystems and agricultural lands.

The strategy's climate change and energy transition elements centre on ambitious emission reduction targets and forest conservation goals aligned with the National Development Plan K'atun 2032 and Sustainable Development Goals. The ENREDD+ establishes specific targets including achieving 29% natural forest coverage and 32% total forest coverage by 2032, alongside a 3% increase in forest coverage through ecological restoration. From an emissions perspective, the strategy targets reductions of approximately 12 million tCO2e by 2025 and 238.3 million tCO2e by 2050. The framework addresses five primary deforestation and degradation causes: unsustainable forest product exploitation, cattle ranching expansion, agricultural expansion, forest fires, and pests and diseases. Structured around four strategic axes encompassing 14 strategic lines, the ENREDD+ integrates governance strengthening, deforestation cause mitigation, degradation prevention, and forest restoration to increase carbon stocks.

Document Title: Indicative Expansion Plan of the Generation System 2020-2050 (Plan de expansión indicativo del Sistema de Generación 2020-2050)
Family Title: Indicative Expansion Plan of the Generation System 2020-2050 (Plan de expansión indicativo del Sistema de Generación 2020-2050)
Family Summary:
TheIndicative Expansion Plan of the Generation System 2020-2050, developed by the Ministry of Energy and Mines through its Unidad de Planeación Energético Minera, establishes the long-term vision for Guatemala’s electricity generation system, ensuring national energy security while advancing the objectives of the national legal and policy framework. Structured in two parts, the plan first analyses the socio-economic, macroeconomic, hydrological, and emissions context of the energy sector, and then projects demand growth, resource availability, and investment requirements under ten modelled scenarios up to 2050. From a total of 60 candidate plants (2758 MW) considered—of which over 80 per cent rely on renewable resources—the scenarios assess expansion costs ($4.8–6.8 billion), the role of fossil and renewable sources, and the impact on diversification, system reliability, and greenhouse gas emissions.

The plan concludes that existing capacity is sufficient to cover demand until 2030, yet highlights the need to periodically reassess hydrological models and climate impacts. Opportunities for renewable development emerge across successive periods: geothermal, hydroelectric and biogas (2020–2025); solar (2024–2027); and wind (2027–2035). Key objectives include diversifying the generation matrix, prioritising renewable technologies with firm capacity, gradually substituting fossil fuels through geothermal and natural gas opportunities, and ensuring transmission infrastructure to integrate new capacity. A further emphasis is placed on expanding generation in high-demand areas or those with future growth potential to stimulate economic development and job creation. Recommendations highlight the importance of regional interconnections (notably with Mexico), state or public-private investment in geothermal and solar projects, and continuous monitoring of demand scenarios, particularly in the context of energy-intensive industries and dry-season hydrological variability

Document Title: Energy Policy 2019-2050 (Política Energética 2019-2050)
Family Title: Energy Policy 2019-2050 (Política Energética 2019-2050)
Family Summary:
The Energy Policy 2019-2050 of Guatemala establishes long-term guidelines to ensure a sustainable, reliable, and competitively priced energy supply that supports economic growth and societal well-being. The policy emphasises efficient resource use and infrastructure modernisation while fulfilling national and international environmental commitments, particularly regarding greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction. It seeks to revise existing energy policy targets based on current needs and future scenarios, promote regulatory mechanisms to achieve these goals, foster sectoral participation through dialogue, and implement an integrated information system for monitoring and control.

Key strategic principles include diversification of energy supply to reduce dependency risks, enhancing system resilience through capacity reserves and contingency planning, and recognising the global integration of energy markets. The policy prioritises the transition towards renewable energy sources and the adoption of efficient technologies, particularly in the transport sector, where diversification of fuels (e.g., LPG, biocombustibles, natural gas) and mass transit systems are promoted to reduce fossil fuel dependence. It also addresses the need for regulatory updates aligned with international climate commitments. The policy incorporates a comprehensive greenhouse gas inventory system based on IPCC methodologies, highlighting the sector’s growing emissions due to increased energy demand. Operational actions focus on expanding renewable energy participation, improving emission measurement and verification, and supporting climate change mitigation efforts within the energy sector.

Document Title: Ministry of Energy and Mines - Government Agreement 159-2023 (Ministerio de Energía y Minas - Acuerdo Gubernativo 159-2023)
Family Title: General Regulations of the Fuel Alcohol Law (Reglamento general de la Ley del Alcohol Carburante)
Family Summary:
This regulation establishes the operational framework for Guatemala's Fuel Alcohol Law (Decree-Law No. 17-85), specifically designed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the transport sector through mandatory blending of renewable alcohol fuels with gasoline. The regulation updates previous regulatory provisions to align with current technological advances and international climate commitments, particularly Guatemala's Nationally Determined Contributions under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. It establishes comprehensive procedures for the production, storage, handling, use, transport, and commercialisation of fuel alcohol, while creating institutional mechanisms for monitoring greenhouse gas emission reductions and promoting sustainable mobility.

The framework prioritises advanced ethanol with lower carbon intensity, requiring distributors to blend a minimum of sixty percent advanced ethanol in the total alcohol fuel mixture, with flexibility for market disruption circumstances. It establishes technical standards for fuel quality, mandates emission reduction monitoring through internationally recognised methodologies, and creates certification requirements for greenhouse gas emission calculations. The regulation incorporates lifecycle emission assessments, prioritises low-emission fuels, and establishes registration requirements for producers, thereby institutionalising a systematic approach to decarbonising Guatemala's transport sector while aiming to ensure compliance with international environmental obligations and constitutional protections for environmental sustainability.

Document Title: Decree Law Number 17-85 (Decreto Ley Número 17-85)
Family Title: Decree 17-1985 establishing the Fuel Alcohol Law (Decreto 17-1985 que establece la Ley del Alcohol Carburante)
Family Summary: Decree-Law No. 17-85 establishes the legal framework governing the production, storage, handling, use, transport, and commercialisation of fuel alcohol and its mixtures. Driven by a state energy policy prioritising the substitution of petroleum products with domestically sourced renewable energy, the legislation aims to foster investment in national agro-industry and generate employment. To this end, it promotes the use of national raw materials for fuel alcohol production, with a crucial safeguard to ensure this does not prejudice the supply of agricultural products for food or existing agro-industrial needs. Furthermore, the Decree-Law institutes a quarterly production tax on fuel alcohol, with the collected funds exclusively earmarked for the research, training, development, and promotion of new and renewable energy sources, thereby directly supporting broader national energy transition efforts.

Document Title: Energy Strategy of the Republic of Moldova until 2030 (ESM 2030)
Family Title: Energy Strategy of the Republic of Moldova until 2030 (ESM 2030)
Family Summary: The Energy Strategy of the Republic of Moldova until 2030 (ESM 2030) aims to improve the sustainability, security and affordability of Moldova's energy supply. The strategy states that renewable sources and efficiency should be balanced against a need for energy market liberalisation, but includes targets for a 20% renewable share of gross final energy consumption by 2020, and an overall 25% reduction in greenhouse emissions nationally between 1990 and 2020. The strategy also aims for a 10% share of biofuels in national consumption, and contains a brief provision accepting the potential development of carbon capture and storage (CCS) facilities.

Document Title: National Forest Extension and Rehabilitation Programme for the period 2023-2032
Family Title: National Forest Extension and Rehabilitation Programme for the period 2023-2032
Family Summary: Moldova's National Forest Extension and Rehabilitation Programme for the period 2023-2032 both recognises climate change as a threat to forestry resources, and aims to mitigate national emissions by increasing the land area used for forestry in Moldova. The programme contains provisions to plant 100,000 ha of new forest and restore 35,000 ha of existing degraded forest. This would represent a 56% increase in current annual carbon sequestration capacity in the forestry sector. To ensure climate resilience of these plantings, it suggests optimising species mixes and planting methods to withstand projected temperature and precipitation changes.

Document Title: K'atun Where Our Guatemala 2032 (K'atun Nuestra Guatemala 2032)
Family Title: K'atun National Development Plan: Our Guatemala 2032 (CONADUR) [Plan Nacional de Desarrollo K’atun: Nuestra Guatemala 2032 (CONADUR)]
Family Summary: The K'atun National Development Plan establishes a long-term governance framework for sustainable development, grounded in Maya cosmology and structured around a 20-year K’atun cycle. Its core climate change and energy transition elements encompass two prioritised strategic axes: adaptation and mitigation to climate change, and conservation and sustainable use of forests and biodiversity for adaptation and mitigation. The Plan mandates the stabilisation of national per capita CO₂-equivalent emissions at 2.5 tonnes and aims to enhance adaptive capacity and resilience of both ecosystems and vulnerable populations, particularly through integrated water resource management, disaster risk reduction, and food security interventions. It sets quantified targets including the maintenance of at least 29% of national territory under natural forest cover, the establishment of 2.6% forest plantation cover, the achievement of zero net deforestation within core protected areas, and the reduction of species classified as at risk of extinction to below 14%. Implementation prioritises community-based participation, the integration of ancestral knowledge, and the strengthening of the Sistema Guatemalteco de Áreas Protegidas (SIGAP), targeting a management effectiveness score exceeding 600 points. The Plan further promotes climate-resilient agricultural productivity through the expansion of efficient irrigation systems on high-potential lands and facilitates economic benefits via carbon credit mechanisms. These objectives are operationalised through the national planning system (Sistema de Consejos de Desarrollo Urbano y Rural), which coordinates public investment, policy alignment, and territorial governance to address structural inequalities and environmental vulnerabilities.

Family Title: National Strategy for Biological Diversity and its Action Plan 2012-2022 (Estrategia Nacional de Diversidad Biológica y su Plan de Acción 2012-2022)
Family Summary:
The National Strategy for Biological Diversity and its Action Plan 2012-2022, developed under Guatemala’s commitments to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), provides the national framework for conserving, valuing, and sustainably using biological diversity, while ensuring its integration into broader development and climate change policies. The strategy responds to accelerating biodiversity loss, deforestation, and ecosystem degradation, which undermine rural livelihoods, food security, and national economic sectors such as forestry, hydropower, and tourism. Recognising biodiversity as a foundation of national development and a critical instrument for climate change adaptation, it aligns with the Política Nacional de Diversidad Biológica and incorporates cross‑sectoral objectives that link environmental governance with poverty reduction and sustainable development.

The strategy is structured around five thematic axes: (i) knowledge and valuation of biodiversity, including scientific research and traditional practices; (ii) conservation and restoration, emphasising in situ and ex situ measures, ecosystem recovery, and community engagement; (iii) sustainable use, through productive systems and equitable benefit-sharing; (iv) biodiversity and climate change, promoting adaptive and mitigation strategies and financing mechanisms such as REDD+, payments for ecosystem services, and carbon markets; and (v) implementation and governance, which seeks to strengthen legal, institutional, and financial capacities. Specific lines of action focus on reducing deforestation and degradation to lower greenhouse gas emissions, securing ecosystem services related to water, food, and energy, and reducing socio‑environmental vulnerability. The plan establishes a monitoring and evaluation framework, with indicators to assess outcomes and to foster accountability across government ministries, local authorities, the Consejo Nacional de Áreas Protegidas (CONAP), civil society, indigenous organisations, and the private sector.

Moldova's NSARD for 2023-2030 also emphasises the importance of climate change adaptation and mitigation, with measures for capacity building, impact/vulnerability reporting systems and technological modernisation in the agricultural sector.

The strategy includes an emissions reduction target of 20% by 2020 and sets out a number of actions with regard to the institutional management of environmental matters and knowledge dissemination activities.

The Environment Strategy for 2024-2030 was approved via Government Decision no. 409/2024 and also sets climate change mitigation and adaptation as key priorities. On combating climate change the strategy emphasises the role of the forestry, agricultural and transport sectors, summarising and promoting existing measures to decarbonise and build resilience in these areas. On adaptation to climate change, the strategy emphasises capacity-building as well as the implementation and enhancement of existing sectoral measures. Nature restoration, technological modernisation and enhanced regulation feature prominently across sectors.

Family Summary:
This regulation serves as the implementing framework for Guatemala’s PROBOSQUE Law, detailing the procedures and mechanisms for its effective application. The regulation aligns with the objectives of the parent law, aiming to increase forest cover, promote sustainable forest management, and enhance rural livelihoods through targeted incentives. It outlines specific provisions for project eligibility, incentive allocation, and compliance requirements, ensuring the programme’s alignment with national environmental and developmental priorities.

The regulation reinforces PROBOSQUE’s climate change mitigation and adaptation goals by establishing clear criteria for forest conservation and restoration projects. It defines eligible activities, such as industrial and energy-oriented forest plantations, agroforestry systems, and the restoration of degraded forest lands, all of which contribute to carbon sequestration and biodiversity preservation. The regulation prioritises projects in protected areas, watersheds, and areas of high ecological value, ensuring that incentives are directed toward regions with significant climate benefits. For energy transition, the regulation supports the development of forest plantations for biomass production, promoting renewable energy sources while reducing pressure on natural forests. Additionally, it mandates fire prevention measures and pest management to safeguard forest health, enhancing ecosystem resilience to climate change. The establishment of monitoring and evaluation mechanisms ensures transparency and accountability in project implementation, further reinforcing the regulation’s role in advancing Guatemala’s climate and energy objectives.

Family Summary: The Supreme Decree approving Peru’s Sustainable Construction Technical Code introduces mandatory, nationwide standards that complement the National Building Regulations and align the built-environment sector with the country’s climate and Sustainable Development Goal commitments. The Code sets performance-based requirements for new buildings and urban developments to cut greenhouse-gas emissions, enhance climate-resilience and improve quality of life through energy and water efficiency, waste minimisation, indoor-environment quality and promotion of sustainable mobility. Key provisions mandate the use of xerophytic or native plant species in private and public green areas according to bioclimatic zones, efficient irrigation, and the integration of renewable energy systems—allowing alternative designs or exemptions where on-site renewables achieve equivalent or superior energy- or water-use benchmarks. Collectively, the instrument positions sustainable construction as a core mechanism for meeting Peru’s NDC targets while fostering inclusive, low-impact urban growth.

Document Title: Law No. 32.276 amending Law 28054 - Biofuel Market Promotion Law, to strengthen biofuel production and promote their consumption (Ley No. 32.276 que modifica la Ley 28054 - Ley de Promoción del Mercado de Biocombustibles, a fin de fortalecer la producción de biocombustibles y promover su consumo)
Family Title: Biofuel Market Promotion Law
Family Summary: The Law's primary objective is to incentivise the diversification of the fuel industry by promoting investment in the production of biofuels, defined as any chemical fuel type originating in agricultural products to a standard defined by the national government. The policies defined in the legislation, to be implemented by the executive branch, are: - to strengthen the scientific research system necessary to developing biofuels - to educate workers about innovative fuel technologies - to incentivise the application of biofuel technologies - to incentivise private capital investment in biofuel production - to incentivise the commercialisation of biofuels - to promote the production of biofuels in rainforest regions within the framework of sustainable development The Law outlines co-ordination with anti-drug programmes, so that national and interna-tional funds designated to The War on Drugs are used to incentivise farmers to cultivate crops designated for biofuels rather than production of coca plants. The legislation calls for the creation of a technical commission, which will create quality standards related to the production of various biofuels. The executive authority issued a decree to regulate the Law nearly two years after its promulgation. The Decree offers further legal definitions of terminology (such as biodiesel, denaturised chemical compounds etc.) as well as specifying the chemical make up of commercialised biodiesel (95% gasoline, 5% biodiesel) and ethanol fuel (92.2% gasoline, 7.8% ethanol). Additionally, the Decree identifies different funding streams to accomplish the legislative objectives established in Law No. 28054, including through the National Clean Development Mechanism, government-backed credits and funds designated for The War on Drugs.The Act No. 32.276 modifies Articles 2, 3, and 4 of Peru’s Law 28054, expanding the legal definition of ‘biofuel’, now requiring that such fuels be derived from biomass through low-carbon technologies and meet established environmental and social sustainability criteria over their lifecycle, as well as comply with nationally mandated quality standards. The amendment further refines the state’s policy architecture by directing the Executive to incentivise private-sector participation in biofuel production. Family Summary: This supreme decree approves Peru's National Environmental Policy to 2030, establishing a comprehensive framework to address the public problem of "diminishing goods and services provided by ecosystems affecting people's development and environmental sustainability." The policy identifies that approximately 18 million hectares of Peru's ecosystems show degradation, with the Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry (LULUCF) sector accounting for 53% of the country's net GHG emissions according to the 2016 National GHG Inventory. The policy establishes eight priority objectives, including Objective 5 (increasing climate change adaptation) targeting a 20% reduction in climate-related damages and losses, and Objective 8 (reducing GHG emissions) aiming for 100% compliance with NDC emission targets. Implementation involves mandatory compliance by all public administration entities, with the Ministry of Environment conducting policy through its Directorate General of Environmental Management Policies and Instruments. The policy integrates ecosystem-based approaches, promotes eco-efficient production processes, strengthens environmental governance with citizen participation, and emphasises the recovery of ecosystem services to ensure sustainable development whilst meeting Peru's international climate commitments.

Central to this framework is the explicit integration of climate change and environmental sustainability. Specifically, National Objective 2 commits to the sustainable management of the territory in order to prevent and reduce risks affecting people and their livelihoods, expressly situated within the context of a changing climate.

The plan operationalises this commitment through a series of strategic priorities and immediate actions. These include measures aimed at catalysing an energy transition, such as replacing the fossil fuel-based transport matrix with electric vehicles and promoting the importation of components for solar energy systems. Furthermore, the strategy emphasises the need to strengthen the integral management of climate change, including the monitoring of greenhouse gas emissions reductions and the effective utilisation of international climate finance. Collectively, these provisions are designed to enhance Peru's adaptive capacity and address systemic environmental challenges, including deforestation and waste management, thereby aligning national development with principles of climate resilience and environmental stewardship.

Rooted in the UNFCCC framework (Decisions 1/CP.21 and 2/CP.24) and the domestic Climate Change Framework Law (Law No. 30754), the Platform ensures the systematic incorporation of indigenous knowledge, practices and proposals into national adaptation and mitigation policy.

Its functions extend from generating and disseminating indigenous proposals on adaptation, mitigation and forest management, to monitoring the implementation of policies such as the National Strategy on Forests and Climate Change. It also tracks financing flows, safeguards traditional knowledge systems, and creates a channel of structured dialogue between indigenous constituencies and national decision‑makers. In this way, the Platform seeks to embed indigenous perspectives into Peru’s long‑term climate and energy transition strategies, while simultaneously reinforcing social inclusion and environmental integrity.

Family Summary: This Peruvian Supreme Decree establishes operational provisions for the National Registry of Mitigation Measures (RENAMI), a measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) tool administered by the Ministry of Environment through its Directorate General of Climate Change and Desertification. The registry comprises three components: mitigation measures forming Peru's Nationally Determined Contribution (declarative nature), carbon market mitigation measures under cooperative approaches and their emission reduction units (constitutive nature), and voluntary carbon market mitigation measures (declarative nature). The decree establishes that carbon market measures under cooperative approaches, implemented through Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement, generate emission reduction units eligible for international transfer to meet other countries' NDCs or international mitigation purposes such as CORSIA, whilst voluntary carbon market measures may contribute to Peru's NDC implementation within corresponding emission sectors.

The Plan articulates six strategic sectoral objectives that directly address climate change mitigation and adaptation whilst advancing the energy transition: reducing biodiversity degradation and ecosystem service loss; controlling environmental pollution across air, water and soil components; strengthening the transition to a circular economy with enhanced solid waste management; reducing climate risks and greenhouse gas emissions in alignment with Peru's Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement; improving decentralised environmental governance with territorial focus; and enhancing citizens' environmental behaviour.
