Family Summary: Peru’s Supreme Decree adopting the National Agrarian Policy 2021-2030 charts a decade-long programme to lift the “low level of agrarian competitive development” that characterises a sector dominated by small-scale family farming (97 % of producers). Grounded in statistical evidence from CENAGRO and ENAHO, the Policy sets a 36 % improvement target by 2030, to be achieved through three priority objectives, fourteen policy guidelines and twenty-two public services. Central measures include: deepening farmers’ vertical integration into value chains; reducing the proportion of subsistence holdings; and enhancing the sustainable management of soil, water and forest resources. Climate variability and change are recognised as cross-cutting stressors that erode ecosystem services and rural incomes, especially in the Andean and Amazon regions; hence the Policy embeds resource-efficient practices, risk-informed planning and support for technological upgrading, all intended to bolster food security, rural livelihoods and Peru’s progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals.

Family Summary:
The National Policy on Gender Equality (PNIG) is a foundational multisectoral instrument designed to address structural discrimination against women in Peru. The Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations is tasked with its overall direction and evaluation, with the policy's objectives strategically aligned with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The PNIG’s core purpose is to dismantle the systemic causes of inequality affecting women by integrating a gender perspective across all domains of public administration.

A distinctive feature of the policy is its explicit recognition of the nexus between gender vulnerability and climate change. It identifies the increasing risk of natural disasters as a critical national challenge, positing that the impacts of climate change are not gender-neutral but disproportionately affect women, thereby limiting their adaptive capacity. Consequently, the PNIG mandates the integration of a gender perspective into all national and sub-national policies related to disaster risk management and climate change adaptation. This approach is designed to work in concert with Peru's Gender and Climate Change Action Plan, seeking to ensure that climate resilience strategies are equitable and to promote the effective participation of women in decision-making processes concerning environmental governance.

The policy emphasizes reducing vulnerability through disaster risk management, climate adaptation, and the use of science and technology, aligning with international climate commitments such as the Paris Agreement. The PEDN also outlines immediate actions to address climate impacts, including optimizing non-reimbursable climate funds, enhancing public education on waste management, promoting solar energy adoption, and transitioning to electric vehicles. These measures aim to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, strengthen climate adaptation, and foster sustainable economic growth. The plan integrates climate action with broader goals of social equity, digital transformation, and institutional strengthening, reflecting Setzer’s emphasis on pragmatic policy innovation. By linking climate resilience to territorial management, the PEDN positions climate change as a cross-cutting priority, requiring systemic reforms in governance, infrastructure, and resource use. The law explicitly acknowledges the critical role of forests and other natural ecosystems in mitigating climate change, as demonstrated by Articles 72–74, which mandate state action to prevent deforestation and degradation, promote reforestation and ecological restoration, and support adaptation and mitigation strategies in vulnerable ecosystems such as Andean and dry forests. These provisions reflect a strong policy emphasis on enhancing carbon sequestration, maintaining hydrological cycles, and reinforcing ecosystem integrity as core components of national climate strategy.

The law further advances climate and energy transition goals by promoting sustainable forest management practices, including the establishment of forest plantations on degraded or non-forest land (particularly with native species) to restore ecosystems, improve soil quality, enhance habitat connectivity, and generate renewable biomass for energy.

Family Title: Supreme Decree No. 006-2020-MINAM. Establishes the High-Level Commission on Climate Change (Decreto Supremo Nº 006-2020-MINAM. Crea Comisión de Alto Nivel de Cambio Climático)
Family Summary:
The Decree Supreme establishing the Permanent Multisectoral Commission known as the High-Level Commission on Climate Change (CANCC) creates a formal, institutional mechanism for coordinating national climate policy in Peru. The instrument is grounded in constitutional provisions affirming the right to an adequate and balanced environment (Article 2, inciso 22 of the Constitution), as well as Peru’s international obligations under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The creation of the CANCC responds directly to the mandate contained in Law No. 30754, the Climate Change Framework Law, which establishes the need for a high-level intergovernmental body to support the formulation, review, and reporting of nationally determined contributions (NDCs) in alignment with international commitments. As a permanent body, the CANCC operates under the technical oversight of the Ministry of Environment and is presided over by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, reflecting its central role in cross-sectoral governance.

The Commission’s primary functions are defined in Article 3 and include: (i) proposing adaptation and mitigation measures within the framework of the National Strategy on Climate Change; (ii) supervising the development and updating of methodologies for greenhouse gas (GHG) emission projections; (iii) formulating recommendations for inclusion in the NDCs; (iv) assessing proposals from regional and local governments to inform progressive strengthening of national targets; (v) preparing and submitting technical reports on the NDCs every five years to the UNFCCC focal point; and (vi) evaluating recommendations from the National Commission on Climate Change (CNCC) and the Indigenous Peoples’ Platform for Climate Change, with a view to their implementation. The structure of the Commission ensures multisectoral representation, including government institutions, civil society, scientific bodies, and Indigenous organisations, thereby embedding principles of participatory governance, transparency, and accountability into the national climate policy architecture.

Family Summary: This Supreme Decree establishes Peru’s long‑term framework (Política Nacional: Estrategia Nacional ante el Cambio Climático al 2050) for addressing climate change impacts while guiding a transition towards a low‑carbon and climate‑resilient development model. It sets out binding measures for adaptation and mitigation, supported by ongoing monitoring and evaluation in alignment with international climate commitments, notably the Paris Agreement.The Strategy seeks to reduce climate‑related damages by at least 20% by 2030 and 30% by 2050, focusing on sectors highly exposed to risks such as health, agriculture, fisheries, forests, water resources, tourism and transport. In mitigation, Peru commits to peak greenhouse gas emissions at 179 MtCO₂e in 2030 and achieve net‑zero emissions by 2050 through energy system decarbonisation, higher efficiency, enhanced forest conservation, circular economy approaches and sustainable agriculture. To deliver these goals, the policy outlines seven priority objectives, including reducing vulnerability among marginalised groups, promoting resilient infrastructure, fostering sustainable land use, expanding renewable energy and clean transport, and advancing governance through scientific research, citizen participation and the creation of “green jobs.” In this way, the strategy envisions a just and inclusive transition that curtails emissions and safeguards livelihoods across the country.

The policy establishes eight priority objectives, including Objective 5 (increasing climate change adaptation) targeting a 20% reduction in climate-related damages and losses, and Objective 8 (reducing GHG emissions) aiming for 100% compliance with NDC emission targets. Family Summary:
The Decree Supreme No. 012-2021-MINAM adapts the National Commission on Climate Change (Comisión Nacional sobre el Cambio Climático) to the legal framework established by Law No. 30754, the Climate Change Framework Law, and its implementing regulations. The instrument formalises the Commission as a permanent, multisectoral body under the technical supervision of the Ministry of Environment, with the primary function of monitoring the implementation of national climate policies and international commitments under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The Commission is designed as a consultative and oversight mechanism that facilitates coordination between state institutions and civil society actors across all levels of government. Its mandate includes tracking compliance with national climate objectives, evaluating policy effectiveness, and generating technical recommendations for decision-making at both institutional and governmental levels.

The Commission’s composition reflects a structured approach to inclusive governance: it comprises 22 state representatives (designated from key ministries, regional and municipal associations, and intergovernmental bodies) and 22 non-state representatives drawn from diverse civil society groups, including Indigenous organisations (PPICC), Afro-Peruvian networks, environmental NGOs, youth collectives, women’s coalitions, trade unions, academic institutions, professional colleges, and private-sector associations. All members, whether state or non-state, possess equal voting rights, reinforcing principles of participatory legitimacy. The Secretariat Technical is housed within the Ministry of Environment and provides administrative and analytical support, while the Commission may convene specialised technical working groups and seek expert input from affiliated public institutions such as SENAMHI, CONCYTEC, SERFOR, SERNANP, OEFA, and CEPLAN. The body operates under an internal regulation that governs procedural matters, including quorum requirements, voting procedures, and meeting schedules. By institutionalising multi-stakeholder engagement and establishing clear mechanisms for information exchange, reporting, and accountability, the decree aims to strength Peru’s domestic climate governance architecture, ensuring alignment with international obligations, particularly those related to transparency, periodic NDC reporting, and the integration of subnational inputs into national climate planning.

As a result of administrative reorganisations, the Supreme Decree N° 005-2023-MINAM modifies the composition of the High-Level Climate Change Commission (CANCC), expanding its membership to include five additional ministries: Defense, Interior, Justice and Human Rights, Labor and Employment Promotion, and Foreign Trade and Tourism. This modification aims to enhance inter-ministerial coordination and strengthen Peru's national climate change response strategy by broadening governmental participation in climate action planning and implementation. The decree seeks to create a more comprehensive and integrated approach to developing and executing national climate change mitigation and adaptation measures, reflecting a whole-of-government strategy in addressing climate challenges.

Collectively, these provisions are designed to enhance Peru's adaptive capacity and address systemic environmental challenges, including deforestation and waste management, thereby aligning national development with principles of climate resilience and environmental stewardship.

Family Title: National Strategy for Biological Diversity to 2050 (Estrategia Nacional de Diversidad Biológica al 2050)
Family Summary: Peru’s National Strategy for Biological Diversity to 2050 establishes a long-term framework to address biodiversity loss through integrated, participatory governance aligned with climate resilience and sustainable development. Central to the strategy are five strategic objectives targeting land-use change, climate impacts, pollution, invasive species, and institutional weaknesses. These objectives operationalise principles such as the precautionary principle (Rio Declaration, Principle 15), intercultural equity, and human rights-based approaches, ensuring alignment with international obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and the Paris Agreement. The strategy mandates ecosystem-based adaptation, including restoring 10% of degraded ecosystems and species affected by climate change, while integrating traditional ecological knowledge to strengthen adaptive capacity. It addresses climate-biodiversity linkages by prioritising mitigation of climate-driven threats (e.g., deforestation, water pollution) and promoting nature-based solutions, such as community-led water harvesting projects. The "Enfoque Territorial" (territorial approach) ensures localised, context-specific actions, while the Enfoque "Una Salud" (One Health) links ecosystem health to human and animal well-being.

Family Summary:
The Supreme Decree updates the National Strategic Development Plan ( Plan Estratégico de Desarrollo Nacional "PEDN") to 2050, outlining a long-term vision for Peru’s socio-economic and environmental development. Central to this framework is Objective 2, which prioritizes gestión sostenible del territorio (sustainable territorial management) to mitigate climate-related risks, protect livelihoods, and integrate climate resilience into national planning. The policy emphasizes reducing vulnerability through disaster risk management, climate adaptation, and the use of science and technology, aligning with international climate commitments such as the Paris Agreement. It underscores the need for coordinated governance across sectors, including water resource management, biodiversity conservation, and territorial ordering, to address structural challenges like climate change, inequality, and institutional weaknesses. The PEDN also outlines immediate actions to address climate impacts, including optimizing non-reimbursable climate funds, enhancing public education on waste management, promoting solar energy adoption, and transitioning to electric vehicles. These measures aim to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, strengthen climate adaptation, and foster sustainable economic growth. The plan integrates climate action with broader goals of social equity, digital transformation, and institutional strengthening, reflecting Setzer’s emphasis on pragmatic policy innovation. By linking climate resilience to territorial management, the PEDN positions climate change as a cross-cutting priority, requiring systemic reforms in governance, infrastructure, and resource use. The document highlights the interplay between national development and global climate imperatives, ensuring that Peru’s trajectory aligns with both domestic needs and international obligations, while addressing historical structural challenges such as corruption and institutional fragility.

The "Enfoque Territorial" (territorial approach) ensures localised, context-specific actions, while the Enfoque "Una Salud" (One Health) links ecosystem health to human and animal well-being.

Document Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 00389-2024-MINAM (Resolución Ministerial N° 00389-2024-MINAM)
Family Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 00389-2024-MINAM. Guidelines for the process, management, and provision of periodic information on the approach to and compliance with REDD+ safeguards (Resolución Ministerial N°00389-2024-MINAM. Lineamiento para el proceso, gestión y provisión de información periódica sobre el abordaje y respeto de las salvaguardas REDD+)
Family Summary: This Peruvian ministerial resolution establishes guidelines for the processing, management and periodic provision of information on the approach to and respect for REDD+ safeguards. The instrument operationalises the Safeguards Information Module (MIS REDD+) as the mechanism through which the Ministry of Environment, via its Directorate General of Climate Change and Desertification, processes and disseminates information on compliance with the seven UNFCCC-recognised REDD+ safeguards (Cancun Decision 1/CP.16). These safeguards encompass complementarity with national forest programmes and international agreements, transparency in forest governance, respect for indigenous peoples' rights and knowledge, full and effective stakeholder participation, compatibility with forest conservation and biodiversity, actions to address reversal risks, and measures to reduce emissions displacement. The guidelines delineate roles for state actors (competent climate change authorities at all government levels) and non-state actors (private entities and indigenous peoples implementing REDD+ actions), establishing procedures for information collection, analysis, management and culturally appropriate dissemination to ensure transparency and continuous improvement in safeguard implementation whilst reducing social and environmental risks and enhancing co-benefits from REDD+ activities.

Document Title: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction (2023-2030)
Family Title: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction (2023-2030)
Family Summary:
Jordan is affected by various risks, including flash floods, landslides and droughts. This Strategy outlines the strategic objectives, which are to improve the legal and institutional basis for disaster risk reduction (DRR); raise awareness of DRR; promote and support scientific research; sustain coordination and promote collaboration among stakeholders; and to integrate DRR and crisis management concepts within relevant national strategies, policies and priorities. It also covers the key challenges and gaps to be addressed; the alignment of this Strategy with national priorities, strategies and policies; the proposed tools for implementing this Strategy; and the Three-Year Action Plan listing six projects.

The proposed tools for implementing the strategy include decentralisation; creating partnerships at various levels; technology and innovation; resource mobilisation and financing; and identification of responsibilities and duties of all stakeholders in disaster preparedness, response and recovery.

Document Title: Supreme Decree approving the update of the National Strategic Development Plan to 2050 - Supreme Decree No. 103-2023-PCM (Decreto Supremo que aprueba la actualización del Plan Estratégico de Desarrollo Nacional al 2050 - Decreto Supremo N° 103-2023-PCM)
Family Title: Updated Strategic Plan for National Development to 2050 ("PEDN al 2050") [Plan Estratégico de Desarrollo Nacional al 2050 actualizado ("PEDN al 2050")]
Family Summary:
The updated Strategic Plan for National Development to 2050 (PEDN al 2050), approved by Supreme Decree N° 103-2023-PCM, constitutes Peru's principal long-term strategic planning instrument. Issued by the National Centre for Strategic Planning (CEPLAN), it articulates a national vision and establishes four overarching National Objectives designed to guide public policy formulation across all levels of government. Central to this framework is the explicit integration of climate change and environmental sustainability. Specifically, National Objective 2 commits to the sustainable management of the territory in order to prevent and reduce risks affecting people and their livelihoods, expressly situated within the context of a changing climate.

The plan operationalises this commitment through a series of strategic priorities and immediate actions. These include measures aimed at catalysing an energy transition, such as replacing the fossil fuel-based transport matrix with electric vehicles and promoting the importation of components for solar energy systems. Furthermore, the strategy emphasises the need to strengthen the integral management of climate change, including the monitoring of greenhouse gas emissions reductions and the effective utilisation of international climate finance. Collectively, these provisions are designed to enhance Peru's adaptive capacity and address systemic environmental challenges, including deforestation and waste management, thereby aligning national development with principles of climate resilience and environmental stewardship.

Document Title: Roadmap to a circular economy in water and sanitation by 2030 (Hoja de Ruta hacia una economía circular en agua y saneamiento al 2030)
Family Title: Roadmap to a circular economy in water and sanitation by 2030 (Hoja de Ruta hacia una economía circular en agua y saneamiento al 2030)
Family Summary: Peru’s 2030 Roadmap for a Circular Economy in Water and Sanitation (Hoja de Ruta AS), stewarded by the Ministry of Housing, Construction and Sanitation, sets out a sector-wide shift from the prevailing linear model towards closed-loop management of water, energy and residuals. Framed by the National Competitiveness and Productivity Policy and consistent with earlier circular-economy roadmaps for industry, fisheries and agriculture, the document adopts the forthcoming ISO 59004 definition of circularity. It places climate change at the centre of sectoral planning: utilities must draw up mitigation-and-adaptation plans, embed disaster-risk actions in their Optimised Master Plans and tariff reviews, and comply with national risk-management norms, recognising that nine out of ten climate-related disasters are water-borne.

Document Title: Peru's National Energy Policy 2010-2040 approved - Supreme Decree No. 064-2010-EM (Aprueban la Política Energética Nacional del Perú 2010-2040 - Decreto Supremo Nº 064-2010-EM)
Family Title: National Energy Policy (Política Energética Nacional)
Family Summary: Peru’s National Energy Policy 2010-2040 (Supreme Decree 064-2010-EM) sets out a long-term blueprint for a reliable, affordable and technologically modern energy system that underpins sustainable development. Guided by nine objectives, the policy prioritises a diversified energy mix centred on renewable sources, hydro-power and systemic energy-efficiency; universal access to electricity and modern fuels; and competitive, transparent markets supported by robust infrastructure and stable regulation. It calls for progressive decarbonisation (minimising environmental impacts, establishing emission, mitigation standards, and enabling participation in carbon-credit markets) while encouraging natural-gas expansion as a transition fuel across households, transport and industry. Complementary measures promote exploration and self-sufficiency, institutional strengthening, research and innovation, and eventual integration with regional energy markets, thereby embedding climate-resilient, low-carbon principles throughout Peru’s energy governance architecture.

Document Title: Reconstruction with Changes - Comprehensive Reconstruction with Changes Plan (Reconstrucción con Cambios - Plan Integral de Reconstrucción con Cambios)
Family Title: Comprehensive Plan for Reconstruction with Changes (Plan Integral para la Reconstrucción con Cambios)
Family Summary: The Comprehensive Plan for Reconstruction with Changes (Plan Integral de Reconstrucción con Cambios "PIRCC") addresses the aftermath of El Niño Costero, a climatic phenomenon that caused widespread damage to infrastructure, livelihoods, and communities in Peru. Its primary objective is to rehabilitate and reconstruct public infrastructure—such as roads, schools, health facilities, and water systems—while prioritizing the recovery of vulnerable populations displaced by floods, landslides, and other disasters. The plan emphasizes climate-resilient reconstruction and disaster risk reduction, integrating adaptive measures to prevent future vulnerabilities. The PIRCC outlines two core intervention types: (1) rehabilitation and replacement of damaged infrastructure to restore essential services, and (2) preventive measures such as river desilting, flood barriers, and urban planning reforms to reduce exposure to climate-related hazards. It incorporates sustainable construction standards, including climate-resilient materials, energy-efficient systems, and disaster-safe housing, ensuring long-term resilience. The plan also prioritizes territorial ordering and sustainable land use, addressing the root causes of vulnerability linked to unregulated urban growth.

Document Title: Supreme Decree adapting the National Commission on Climate Change to Law No. 30754, Framework Law on Climate Change - Supreme Decree No. 012-2021-MINAM (Decreto Supremo que adecua la Comisión Nacional sobre el Cambio Climático a la Ley N° 30754, Ley Marco sobre Cambio Climático - Decreto Supremo Nº 012-2021-MINAM)
Family Title: Supreme Decree No. 012-2021-MINAM. Adapts the National Commission on Climate Change (Decreto Supremo Nº 012-2021-MINAM. Adecúa la Comisión Nacional sobre el Cambio Climático)
Family Summary:
The Decree Supreme No. 012-2021-MINAM adapts the National Commission on Climate Change (Comisión Nacional sobre el Cambio Climático) to the legal framework established by Law No. 30754, the Climate Change Framework Law, and its implementing regulations. The instrument formalises the Commission as a permanent, multisectoral body under the technical supervision of the Ministry of Environment, with the primary function of monitoring the implementation of national climate policies and international commitments under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The Commission is designed as a consultative and oversight mechanism that facilitates coordination between state institutions and civil society actors across all levels of government. Its mandate includes tracking compliance with national climate objectives, evaluating policy effectiveness, and generating technical recommendations for decision-making at both institutional and governmental levels.

The Commission’s composition reflects a structured approach to inclusive governance: it comprises 22 state representatives (designated from key ministries, regional and municipal associations, and intergovernmental bodies) and 22 non-state representatives drawn from diverse civil society groups, including Indigenous organisations (PPICC), Afro-Peruvian networks, environmental NGOs, youth collectives, women’s coalitions, trade unions, academic institutions, professional colleges, and private-sector associations. All members, whether state or non-state, possess equal voting rights, reinforcing principles of participatory legitimacy. The Secretariat Technical is housed within the Ministry of Environment and provides administrative and analytical support, while the Commission may convene specialised technical working groups and seek expert input from affiliated public institutions such as SENAMHI, CONCYTEC, SERFOR, SERNANP, OEFA, and CEPLAN. The body operates under an internal regulation that governs procedural matters, including quorum requirements, voting procedures, and meeting schedules. By institutionalising multi-stakeholder engagement and establishing clear mechanisms for information exchange, reporting, and accountability, the decree aims to strength Peru’s domestic climate governance architecture, ensuring alignment with international obligations, particularly those related to transparency, periodic NDC reporting, and the integration of subnational inputs into national climate planning.

As a result of administrative reorganisations, the Supreme Decree N° 005-2023-MINAM modifies the composition of the High-Level Climate Change Commission (CANCC), expanding its membership to include five additional ministries: Defense, Interior, Justice and Human Rights, Labor and Employment Promotion, and Foreign Trade and Tourism. This modification aims to enhance inter-ministerial coordination and strengthen Peru's national climate change response strategy by broadening governmental participation in climate action planning and implementation. The decree seeks to create a more comprehensive and integrated approach to developing and executing national climate change mitigation and adaptation measures, reflecting a whole-of-government strategy in addressing climate challenges.

Document Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 364-2024-Housing (Resolución Ministerial No. 364-2024-Vivienda)
Family Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 364-2023-Housing. Regulates the development and monitoring of Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation Plans (CMAPs) in Sanitation Service Providers (EPS) [Resolución Ministerial Nº 364-2023-Vivienda. Regula la elaboración y seguimiento de los Planes de Mitigación y Adaptación al Cambio Climático (PMACC) en las Empresas Prestadoras de Servicios de Saneamiento (EPS)]
Family Summary: This ministerial resolution, issued by Peru’s Ministry of Housing, Construction, and Sanitation (MVCS), mandates the development and implementation of Planes de Mitigación y Adaptación al Cambio Climático (PMACC) by sanitary companies (Empresas Prestadoras de Servicios de Saneamiento "EPS"). Aligned with Peru’s Contribución Nacionalmente Determinada (NDC) and the Paris Agreement, the policy seeks to enhance climate resilience and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in the sanitation sector. Under the framework of Peru’s Climate Change Framework Law (Ley N° 30754), the resolution emphasises mitigation through GHG emission reductions from wastewater management and energy consumption, and adaptation via improved water resource management to address climate risks. EPS must utilise the Sistema de Información de Gestión de Saneamiento (SIGASS) to assess climate exposures, prioritising systems with high user populations or vulnerability to climate hazards.

Document Title: Guidelines for the identification and classification of REDD+ actions (Lineamientos para la identificación y clasificación de las acciones REDD+)
Family Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 143-2021-MINAM. Guidelines for the identification and classification of REDD+ Actions (Resolución Ministerial Nº143-2021-MINAM. Lineamiento para la identificación y clasificación de las Acciones REDD+ )
Family Summary: Peru's framework for REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and forest Degradation) actions, established through this Ministerial Resolution, operationalises the country's commitments under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the 2018 Climate Change Framework Law (Law No. 30754). The framework identifies eight specific REDD+ actions aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions from the Land Use, Land Use Change and Forestry sector whilst enhancing forest ecosystem resilience, particularly for indigenous peoples and rural communities who depend on these ecosystems.The identified REDD+ actions encompass deforestation-free sustainable family agriculture, sustainable forest management, indigenous-led integrated territorial management (RIA and RIAC), community forest management, forest conservation on indigenous and peasant community lands, titling and governance mechanisms with community monitoring, strengthening of Protected Natural Areas, and landscape-scale forest restoration and reforestation activities. The framework emphasises participatory and transparent climate change management measures, positioning Peru's Ministry of Environment as the national authority responsible for monitoring and evaluating climate change management implementation across all government levels.

Document Title: Guidelines for the preparation of regional greenhouse gas inventories (Pautas para la elaboración de inventarios regionales de gases de efecto invernadero)
Family Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 090-2022-MINAM. Guidelines to be followed for the preparation of Regional Greenhouse Gas Inventories (IRGEI) [Resolución Ministerial Nº090-2022-MINAM. Pautas que deben seguirse para la elaboración de los Inventarios Regionales de Gases de Efecto Invernadero (IRGEI)]
Family Summary: Peru's Ministerial Resolution N° 090-2022-MINAM establishes comprehensive guidelines for the elaboration of Regional Greenhouse Gas Inventories, providing regional governments with standardised methodological tools to quantify emissions and removals at the departmental level. These guidelines align with the IPCC 2006 methodology and support the implementation of Regional Climate Change Strategies by enabling the identification of emission sources across four key sectors: Energy, Industrial Processes and Product Use, Agriculture/Forestry/Land Use, and Waste. The framework ensures consistency between regional inventories and the National Greenhouse Gas Inventory (INFOCARBONO), whilst providing calculation spreadsheets and technical guidance adapted to departmental characteristics and economic activities.

Document Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 358-2023-MINAM (Resolución Ministerial N° 358-2023-MINAM)
Family Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 358-2023-MINAM. Guidelines for the operation of the Citizen Service Module for REDD+ (Resolución Ministerial Nº 358-2023-MINAM. Lineamiento para el funcionamiento del Módulo de Atención Ciudadana para REDD+)
Family Summary: The Ministerial Resolution N° 358-2023-MINAM establishes a Citizen Attention Mechanism (MAC REDD+) to operationalise Peru's national climate change policy framework, specifically implementing the provisions of Law N° 30754 on Climate Change. The mechanism provides a structured administrative process for receiving and addressing citizen inquiries related to REDD+ initiatives, including forest conservation strategies, emissions reduction efforts, and indigenous engagement in climate action. It delineates specific channels for citizen interaction, including presential, virtual, and telephonic platforms, and outlines the scope of acceptable inquiries ranging from document requests to technical consultations and complaints, with particular attention to intercultural accessibility and comprehensive stakeholder participation.

Document Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 00283-2024-MINAM (Resolución Ministerial N° 00283-2024-MINAM)
Family Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 00283-2024-MINAM. Guidelines for the reception, administration, and distribution of REDD+ financing in Peru (Resolución Ministerial N°00283-2024-MINAM. Lineamiento para la recepción, administración y distribución del financiamiento REDD+ en el Perú)
Family Summary: This Peruvian ministerial resolution establishes guidelines for the reception, administration and distribution of REDD+ financing across its three phases: preparation, implementation, and results-based payments. The instrument delineates three administrative modalities for managing REDD+ funds: through public entity budgetary allocations subject to the National Public Budget System; via PROFONANPE (the National Fund for State Protected Natural Areas) specifically for funds from the Joint Declaration of Intent with Germany, Norway and the United Kingdom; and through direct donor administration mechanisms such as trusts. The resolution mandates that the Ministry of Environment and donors jointly determine the appropriate modality based on costs, execution timelines and required human resources, with such determination to be formalised in bilateral or multilateral agreements. For results-based payments, the guidelines stipulate that benefit distribution must be equitable, culturally appropriate and participatory, with the Ministry establishing criteria for beneficiary identification in consultation with state and non-state actors, including indigenous peoples, whilst ensuring continued reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from the Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry sector.

Document Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 196-2021-MINAM (Resolución Ministerial N° 196-2021-MINAM)
Family Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 196-2021-MINAM. Methodological guidelines for the formulation and updating of Local Climate Change Plans (Resolución Ministerial Nº196-2021-MINAM. Lineamientos metodológicos para la formulación y la actualización de los Planes Locales de Cambio Climático)
Family Summary: Peru's Ministerial Resolution N° 152-2021-MINAM establishes methodological guidelines for the formulation and updating of Regional Climate Change Strategies (ERCC), positioning them as mandatory instruments that operationalise climate action at the subnational level. These strategies, aligned with Peru's National Climate Change Strategy and Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), must incorporate both adaptation and mitigation measures across five mitigation sectors (energy, industrial processes, agriculture, land use and forestry, and waste) and seven adaptation areas (water, agriculture, forests, health, fisheries and aquaculture, tourism, and transport). The guidelines mandate that regional governments integrate climate measures into their Regional Development Plans, Strategic Institutional Plans, Operational Plans, budget programmes, and investment projects.The resolution outlines a structured five-phase methodology comprising Organisation, Territory Analysis, Planning, Implementation, and Monitoring and Evaluation, emphasising participatory processes that ensure effective engagement with state and non-state actors, particularly indigenous peoples. Regional governments must establish working groups within their Regional Environmental Commissions to lead strategy development, ensuring climate risk analysis, identification of greenhouse gas emission sources, and determination of adaptation and mitigation measures with enabling conditions.

Document Title: Resolution 153/2018 on Losses and Damages in Disasters
Family Title: Resolution 153/2018 on Losses and Damages in Disasters
Family Summary:
This Resolution provides for the procedure for the evaluation, certification, pricing, accounting, financing, taxation and control of loss and damage occurring in the case of disasters.

The objective of this procedure is to regulate, in the event of a disaster, the evaluation and certification of damages, the accounting of losses and damages, the prices of goods and services offered to victims to compensate for the damages, the provision of financial resources to compensate for the corresponding expenses for the losses and damages caused, as well as the adjustments for the payment of taxes that apply under these circumstances. This includes losses and damages caused by the impact of disaster hazards during the response and recovery stages of disaster situations.

Resolution 159/2019 amended this Resolution to include details relating to transportation budgets.

Document Title: Programme for Mainstreaming Gender in Climate Change Efforts in Jordan
Family Title: Programme for Mainstreaming Gender in Climate Change Efforts in Jordan
Family Summary:
The objective of this Programme is to ensure that national climate change efforts in Jordan mainstream gender considerations so that women and men can have access to, participate in, contribute to and hence optimally benefit from climate change initiatives, programs, policies and funds.

This Programme defines the role of the Ministry of Environment, as the implementing agent, and covers the priority sectors of water; energy; agriculture and food security; and waste reduction and management. It also covers the following institutional imperatives for the successful implementation of the programme.:

  1. Intergovernmental coordination for supporting the mainstreaming of gender in climate change efforts;
  2. Ensure that gender criteria (where relevant) are incorporated in the development of projects and programmes associated with climate change in Jordan;
  3. Strengthen capacity of implementers of the Programme; and
  4. Secure ongoing commitments from funders to support the Programme for Mainstreaming Gender in Climate Change Efforts in Jordan.

Document Title: Law No. 145 on Territorial and Urban Planning and Land Management
Family Title: Law No. 145 on Territorial and Urban Planning and Land Management
Family Summary:
The objectives of this Law are to define the instruments of territorial and urban planning, their content, scope, reach, approval bodies, and management. Urbanisation and building approvals are regulated to be granted through the final approval of the building permit, when the territorial and urban planning determinations and regulations established in the territorial and urban planning instruments, the technical standards for construction, the prevention of natural and anthropogenic hazards, and the impact of climate change have been complied with. The Ministry of Science, Technology and the Environment and the Ministry of Construction are responsible for ensuring the integration of climate change adaptation in land use and urban planning, and housing construction, respectively.

On undevelopable land, the competent authority may, in exceptional cases, authorise the construction of isolated infrastructure, buildings, and dwellings necessary for the exploitation of these territories, avoiding risk situations by ensuring preventive protection or adaptation works in the face of exposure to natural or anthropogenic hazards or the expected impact of climate change.

In coastal areas and areas vulnerable to climate change, planning shall take into account the principles of depopulation and reduction of population density, as appropriate.

Family Title: Resolution 26/2023 on Sustainable Consumption and Production, the Circular Economy and Plastics
Family Summary:
This Resolution (at pages 2288 to 2293 of the Gazette) contains regulations for work in sustainable consumption and production, the circular economy, and the gradual reduction of disposable or single-use plastics. The purpose of these regulations is to implement an environmental policy and management tool that will lead all sectors of society to orient their consumption and production patterns toward sustainability, thereby achieving a transition to higher levels of environmental protection and quality of life.

Actions include strengthening climate resilience and tackling climate cahnge both in terms of adaptation and mitigation in food systems and the tourism sector.

Document Title: National Energy Efficiency Strategy, 2019

Actions include developing minimum energy performance standards for electrical and mechanical equipment used in various sectors and conducting energy audits.
