Family Title: Decree-Law 77/2023 on Coastlines
Family Summary:
The purpose of this Decree-Law is to establish the set of mechanisms, actions, and instruments that must be applied in the coastal and protection zone, aimed at its sustainable use, as well as the protection of human settlements and the processes of economic and social development therein.

Climate-related provisions include:

  • Article 12: The Land Use and Urban Planning of the Coastal Zone aims to reduce the degree of exposure to hazards that may affect it, mainly those associated with climate change. Actions include contributing, through land use and urban planning management tools, to the progressive organisation of essential protection works to safeguard buildings exposed to the hazards identified in medium- and long-term climate scenarios, as well as the corresponding hazard, vulnerability, and risk studies.
  • Article 50.2: The Ministry of Science, Technology, and Environment is responsible for evaluating those cays with the characteristics indicated above, based on available scientific and technological results, medium- and long-term climate scenarios, and current strategic development plans and programs.

This Decree-Law is supported by Decree 97 - Regulations of Decree-Law 77 on Coastlines.

Document Title: Law 155/2022 on the Protection of Cultural and Natural Heritage
Family Title: Law 155/2022 on the Protection of Cultural and Natural Heritage
Family Summary:
This Law regulates the mechanisms and processes for the protection of cultural and natural heritage, and the rights and responsibilities of various entities. To grant cultural heritage a role in collective life and integrate its protection into territorial and urban planning instruments, the State, through the competent authorities, adopts measures aimed at, amongst other things, establishing strategies, risk plans, and protocols for the protection of cultural heritage in the event of disasters, vandalism, and armed conflict, as well as adaptation to climate change.

To give natural heritage a social function and integrate its protection into territorial and urban planning instruments, the Ministry of Science, Technology, and Environment is to adopt measures to prioritise research in the areas of conservation, resilience, adaptation to climate change, and socioeconomic processes; and

For archaeological sites that have not preserved their integrity and whose degree of deterioration is such that it does not allow for the identification of structures, the study of the context, or the social use of this heritage, full excavation of the site is permitted, and if necessary, it is subject to archaeological rescue when affected by construction or by the effects of climate change.

Document Title: Climate Change and Gender Action Plan (Phase II)
Family Title: Climate Change and Gender Action Plan (Phase II)
Family Summary:
The Ministry for Coordination of Environmental Affairs (MICOA) invited the Global Gender Office of the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN GGO) on behalf of the Global Gender and Climate Alliance (GGCA) to facilitate a process of revisiting and enhancing the action plan portion of the 2010 Gender, Environment and Climate Change Strategy and Action Plan. The 2010 Plan was a trailblazer as Mozambique was the first country in the world to create such a plan.

MICOA selected six sectors to focus on for this Plan: water, agriculture, health, mitigation (including energy and forests), DRR, and coasts and fisheries.

Document Title: National Strategy on Gender and Climate Change
Family Title: National Strategy on Gender and Climate Change
Family Summary: The National Strategy for Mainstreaming Gender in Climate Change is outlined into six priority sectors, each comprising sub-sections on women as agents for change, a situation analysis and the state of gender, a set of recommendations and examples of actions for implementation. The priority sectors are: agriculture; water; health; energy; forests; integrated coastal management; and cross-cutting elements relevant to all sectors.

Document Title: National Action Plan on Gender and Climate Change
Family Title: National Action Plan on Gender and Climate Change
Family Summary:
The main goal of this Plan is to ensure that national climate change efforts in Nigeria mainstream gender considerations so that women, men, youth and other vulnerable groups can have access to, participate in, contribute to and hence optimally benefit from climate change initiatives, programs, policies and funds. It serves as a guide for states and local governments to mainstream geneder considerations to address climate change challenges in Nigeria, and is meant to be socialised through Climate Change desk offices in states and subsequently cascaded to local communities.

This Plan focuses on the priority sectors of agriculture, forestry and land use; food security and health, energy and transport, waste management; and water and sanitation.

Document Title: Decree-Law 345/2019 on the development of renewable energy
Family Title: Decree-Law 345/2019 on the development of renewable energy
Family Summary:
The purpose of this Decree-Law is to establish regulations for the development of renewable sources and the efficient use of energy, in order to contribute to:

a) Increasing the share of renewable energy sources in electricity generation;

b) The progressive replacement of fossil fuels;

c) The diversification of the structure of fossil fuels used in electricity generation;

d) Increasing energy efficiency and savings;

e) the stimulation of investment, research, and the increase in energy efficiency, as well as the production and use of energy from renewable sources, through the establishment of incentives and other instruments that stimulate their development;

f) the development of the production of equipment, resources, and spare parts by the national industry for the use of renewable sources and energy efficiency; and

g) the establishment of a work system in the state sector, which includes the planning of tasks that enable the achievement of the established objectives.

The Cuban government stated in its 2024 Biennial Transparency Report that a fundamental transformation of the national legal framework occurred with the promulgation of this Decree-Law. Future expansion of the national electricity system's (SEN) generation will be essentially based on the increase in renewable energy sources, the strengthening of conventional thermal generation, and the increase in combined cycle gas generation capacity from petroleum-based natural gas.

Document Title: Climate Change Gender Action Plan
Family Title: Climate Change Gender Action Plan
Family Summary:
The objective of this Plan is to ensure that gender equality is mainstreamed into Liberia’s climate change policies, programs and interventions so that both men and women have equal opportunities to implement and benefit from mitigation and adaptation initiatives in combating climate change and positively impact on the outcome of “Liberia Rising 2030”.

This Plan elaborates on the context of Liberia recovering from the history of civil war, position of women in Liberia, the case for gender equality, and covers the priority sectors of agriculture and food security; coasts; forestry and REDD; health; water and sanitation; and energy.

Document Title: National Strategy for Mainstreaming Gender in Climate Change in Egypt
Family Title: National Strategy for Mainstreaming Gender in Climate Change in Egypt
Family Summary:
This National Strategy for Mainstreaming Gender in Climate Change in Egypt is the result of collaboration between the IUCN Gender Office, the IUCN Regional Office for West Asia (ROWA), the Center for Environment and Development for the Arab Region and Europe (CEDARE), the Global Gender Office of the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and other key national institutions in Egypt to develop a national policy framework on gender and climate change.

This Strategy covers the following priority sectors: integrated coastal management; agriculture; water; tourism; health; energy and transport; urbanisation; and waste management.

It also covers the following institutional imperatives to ensure the successful implementation of the Strategy:

  1. Intergovernmental coordination for supporting the mainstreaming of gender in climate change efforts;
  2. Ensure that Gender Criteria (where relevant) are Incorporated in the Development of Projects and Programs Associated with Climate Change in Egypt;
  3. Strengthen Capacity of Implementers of the Strategy; and
  4. Secure on-going commitments from funders to support the Strategy for Mainstreaming Gender in Climate Change Efforts in Egypt.

Document Title: National Action Plan on Human Rights, Gender and Climate Change (PNADHG-CC) [Plan Nacional de Acción de Derechos Humanos, Género y Cambio Climático (PNADHG-CC)]
Family Title: National Action Plan on Human Rights, Gender and Climate Change (PNADHG-CC) [Plan Nacional de Acción de Derechos Humanos, Género y Cambio Climático (PNADHG-CC)]
Family Summary: The Mexican National Action Plan on Gender and Climate Change acknowledges Mexico's vulnerability to climate change, with rising temperatures, altered precipitation patterns, and vegetation loss disproportionately impacting vulnerable populations, particularly indigenous communities and women. The plan notes that Mexico´s CO2 emissions are significant on a global scale. These communities heavily rely on natural resources and often act as stewards of biodiversity. The plan aims to integrate a gender perspective into national climate change mitigation and adaptation efforts, as well as Mexico's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), to address the differentiated effects of climate change on women, girls, and youth.The National Action Plan is structured around three pillars: promoting the leadership of women; building and consolidating institutional capacities; and ensuring financing and cooperation. Actions include guaranteeing women's participation in climate change decision-making, strengthening institutional capacity on gender equality and human rights within climate action, and improving the availability of financial and technical resources for integrating gender perspectives into national climate change strategies. The plan will be reviewed biennially with the involvement of government, civil society, and international organisations, and is intended to be updated to reflect evolving needs and roles.

Document Title: National Environmental Strategy 2021-2025
Family Title: National Environmental Strategy 2021-2025
Family Summary:
This Strategy aims to acheive a higher level of conservation, protection and rational use of natural resources, environmental quality in human settlements, and climate change mitigation, with an ecosystem approach, to ensure the constitutional right of Cubans to live in a healthy and balanced environment.

This Strategy covers the national and international context for the development of a new strategic environmental cycle to 2030; the main environmental problems in Cuba; the conceptualisation of the Strategy; environmental indicators; and the implementation mechanisms.

Document Title: Programme for the generalisation of analysis according to gender in efforts to combat climate change in Haiti
Family Title: Programme for the generalisation of analysis according to gender in efforts to combat climate change in Haiti
Family Summary:
This Programme aims to ensure that gender considerations are integrated into all environmental policies and initiatives, particularly issues related to climate change, biodiversity management and conservation, and soil degradation, with a view to achieving sustainable development goals and the Millennium Development Goals.

This Programme covers adaptation, mitigation, technology transfer, and capacity building and four priority areas of agriculture and food security; water resource management; disaster risk management; and health. It also covers the following means of implementing the programme - the resource mobilisation strategy, institutional requirements and project ideas.

Document Title: National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2018
Family Title: National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2018
Family Summary: The vision of this Policy is to build a climate-adapted and climate-resilient nation safe from disaster risk. The goal of this policy is to reduce disaster mortality and number of affected people substantially, increase resiliency by reducing disaster damage to means of livelihoods as well as critical infrastructures and disruption of basic services such as agriculture, industry, roads, communication, water supply and sanitation, education and health facilities, and reduce direct disaster economic loss. It mainstreams diverse areas of disaster management, risk reduction, and efficient and effective response as well as adopting the approach of Build Back Better (BBB) for rehabilitation and reconstruction in the post-disaster period.

Document Title: Decree-Law No. 83 on the National System of Protected Areas
Family Title: Decree-Law No. 83/2024 on the National System of Protected Areas
Family Summary:
The purpose of this Decree-Law is to regulate matters concerning the National System of Protected Areas, regarding the exercise of its governance, control, and administration, management categories, their proposal and declaration, the protection regime, and the granting of authorisations for carrying out activities within them.

This Decree-Law is meant to contribute to climate change adaptation and mitigation.

The delimitation and categorisation of protected areas, as well as any modifications to both aspects, shall be carried out based on scientific assessments and consultation with the agencies of the Central State Administration and the entities involved, taking into account, amongst other factors: -

  1. The magnitude, significance, and degree of conservation of their values, especially in relation to biological diversity; and
  2. The degree of naturalness of the area, which considers the incidence of environmental impacts, including those related to the effects of climate change.

Document Title: 2018-2032. Prodesen. National Electric System Development Program (2018-2032. Prodesen. Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional)
Family Title: National Electric System Development Program 2018-2032 (Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2018-2032)
Family Summary: Mexico’s energy transition strategy, outlined in the Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2018-2032, prioritises diversifying the electricity matrix through conventional and clean technologies while addressing climate commitments. Conventional technologies (such as combined cycle, coal, and internal combustion plants) currently supply most of the nation’s electricity but contribute significantly to greenhouse gas emissions (18% of national GHG output). To mitigate environmental impacts, the strategy emphasises phasing out high-pollution units, promoting dual-fuel conversions, and integrating carbon capture technologies. The document declares these measures align with national decarbonization targets, including the Contribución Prevista y Determinada a nivel Nacional (INDC), which aims to cap electricity-sector emissions at 139 million tons of CO2 equivalent by 2030.

Document Title: Climate Change Budget Code
Family Title: Climate Change Budget Code
Family Summary: This Code documents the process by which a multi-sectoral consensus on the climate budget code was formulated. The Code is meant to contribute towards demonstrating the importance of focusing on the impacts of climate change, through the size of the budget allocated. The Code will track climate public expenditure and facilitate prioritisation of allocating development investment on the most vulnerable areas and key sectors. In Annex V (pages 41 to 50) of this document, there is a Quick Reference Guide to the Code. If more than 60% of the allocated budget of the programme is to be spent on climate-related activities, the programme will be considered highly relevant to climate change and marked as such. Otherwise, it would be marked relevant (20 to 60% of the total budget related to climate change), or neutral (less than 20% of the budget spent on climate change).

Document Title: Vanuatu National Waste Management and Pollution Control Strategy 2016-2020
Family Title: Vanuatu National Waste Management and Pollution Control Strategy 2016-2020
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Waste Management and Pollution Control Strategy 2016-2020 aims to reduce the negative impacts of waste and pollution, in response to growing waste production. The strategy acknowledges strong climate impacts on waste management systems, i.e. through extreme rainfall, and promotes adaptation to such threats. Provisions include enhanced capacity building for waste monitoring and response (i.e. systematic local waste management plans), and the introduction of performance standards for waste systems such as sanitation. Other provisions include tax incentives for scrap metal recycling, enhanced vehicle emissions inspection and the introduction of new public awareness campaigns.

Document Title: Agreement amending the Operating Rules of the Program for the Comprehensive Well-being of Indigenous Peoples, managed by the National Institute of Indigenous Peoples, for the 2023 fiscal year (Acuerdo por el que se modifican las Reglas de Operación del Programa para el Bienestar Integral de los Pueblos Indígenas a cargo del Instituto Nacional de los Pueblos Indígenas, para el ejercicio fiscal 2023)
Family Title: Agreement amending the Operating Rules of the Program for the Comprehensive Well-being of Indigenous Peoples for fiscal year 2024 (Acuerdo que modifica las Reglas de Operación del Programa para el Bienestar Integral de los Pueblos Indígenas, para el ejercicio fiscal 2024)
Family Summary: This policy establishes the operational rules for Mexico’s 2024 Programme for the Integral Well-being of Indigenous Peoples (PROBIPI), administered by the National Institute of Indigenous Peoples (INPI). It aims to advance the development of 68 recognised indigenous and Afro-Mexican communities as collective rights holders, emphasising self-determination, cultural preservation, and territorial integrity. The programme supports community-led projects across five pillars: rights implementation, economic development, infrastructure, cultural heritage, and healthcare. Key mechanisms include participatory planning, direct resource transfers, and coordination with federal agencies to address structural inequalities. Projects must align with indigenous governance systems and cultural practices, prioritising collective benefits over individual aid.The policy integrates climate change and energy transition objectives through dedicated funding for mitigation and adaptation actions. It finances ecosystem conservation, sustainable resource management, and climate-resilient practices (e.g., agroecology, community-based tourism) under its "Fortification of Indigenous Economies and Environment" component. It supports community-owned "gas stations for well-being" to improve energy access in remote regions while promoting low-carbon economic chains. The programme explicitly prohibits funding for fossil fuel-dependent activities (e.g., livestock purchases, vehicle acquisitions) and infrastructure unrelated to climate goals, instead favouring renewable energy-compatible initiatives like sustainable agriculture and nature-based tourism.

Document Title: Vanuatu National Environment Policy and Implementation Plan 2016-2030
Family Title: Vanuatu National Environment Policy and Implementation Plan 2016-2030
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Environment Policy and Implementation Plan 2016-2030 aims to provide an overarching framework for protecting the natural environment of the country. Climate change resilience is one of five key goals, and the section of this plan on climate change seeks primarily to support the existing aims and actions of Vanuatu's 2016-2030 Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction Policy.

Document Title: National Climate Change Adaptation Strategy (NCCAS) for Land-based Resources. 2012-2022
Family Title: National Climate Change Adaptation Strategy (NCCAS) for Land-based Resources. 2012-2022
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Climate Change Adaptation Strategy (NCCAS) for Land-based Resources from 2012-2022 seeks to promote and enhance the adaptation of land-based resources, activities and environments to threats from climate change. The strategy is long-term and programmatic, rather than project-focused, and follows the following guiding principles/requirements for its provisions. Adaptation projects and concepts must be: relevant, appropriate and proportional; collaborative and coordinated; facilitated by traditional knowledge; integrative and synergistic; evidence based and adjustable; well measured and flexible. As this strategy is programmatic, it emphasises institutional capacity building and taking stock of adaptation provisions in existing policy instruments.

Document Title: Local Disaster and Climate Resilience Planning (LDCRP) Guidelines 2017
Family Title: Local Disaster and Climate Resilience Planning (LDCRP) Guidelines 2017
Family Summary: These Guidelines provide a strategic framework for local governments to develop and implement plans aimed at enhancing disaster resilience and climate adaptation. These guidelines emphasise community participation, risk assessment, and integration of disaster risk reduction and climate resilience into local development planning. They outline steps for identifying vulnerabilities, prioritising actions, and mobilising resources, aiming to build resilient communities capable of withstanding and recovering from disasters and climate impacts.

Document Title: Decree No. 103-2002, Regulations for the Operation of the Sectoral Working Committees of the National System for Disaster Prevention, Mitigation, and Response
Family Title: Decree No. 103-2002, Regulations for the Operation of the Sectoral Working Committees of the National System for Disaster Prevention, Mitigation, and Response
Family Summary: The purpose of this Regulation is to establish the terms and conditions of operation of the sectoral working commissions of the national system for the prevention, mitigation, and attention to disasters, created by Law No. 337 and by the National Committee, in order to guarantee the highest level of coordination, effectiveness, and efficiency in the actions of prevention, mitigation, attention, and recovery of populations affected by natural or man-made disasters.

Document Title: Vanuatu National Coconut Strategy 2016-2025
Family Title: Vanuatu National Coconut Strategy 2016-2025
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Coconut Strategy 2016-2025 addresses the role of coconut products in climate change adaptation and mitigation. It includes provisions to standardise monitoring of climate impacts on coconut planations - a significant proportion of Vanuatu's agricultural production - and introduce tax incentives for the use of coconut oil byproducts as biofuels.

Document Title: National Environmental and Climate Change Strategy Action Plan 2010-2015
Family Title: National Environmental and Climate Change Strategy Action Plan 2010-2015
Family Summary:
To confront environmental problems and the current and potential effects of climate change, the implementation of the National Environmental and Climate Change Strategy is necessary to guarantee the participation of organized people and government institutions in developing conservation and preservation actions for our natural resources. as the practical expression of the principles of the Universal Declaration of the Common Good of the Earth and Humanity that asks us to understand the Earth as alive and subject to dignity.

The National Environmental and Climate Change Strategy is based on Article 60 of the Political Constitution of the Republic of Nicaragua and the principles of the National Development Plan, restoring the population's right to a healthy environment.

Document Title: National Disaster Risk Management Policy to 2050
Family Title: National Disaster Risk Management Policy to 2050
Family Summary:
The National Disaster Risk Management Policy for 2050 establishes six priority objectives:

  • Improve understanding of disaster risk for decision-making at the level of the population and state entities;
  • Improve conditions for land occupation and use, taking disaster risk into account;
  • Improve the coordinated implementation of disaster risk management in the territory;
  • Strengthen the incorporation of disaster risk management into public and private investment;
  • Ensure public care in the event of emergencies and disasters;
  • Improve the recovery of populations and their livelihoods affected by emergencies and disasters.

Document Title: Electricity Sector Outlook 2017-2031 (Prospectiva del Sector Eléctrico 2017-2031)
Family Title: Electricity Sector Outlook 2017-2031 (Prospectiva del Sector Eléctrico 2017-2031)
Family Summary: The Mexican Electricity Sector Outlook 2017-2031 outlines Mexico's energy policy, highlighting the modernization of its electricity sector through energy reforms and increased private investment. These reforms have facilitated a rise in clean energy generation, from under 18% to an estimated 30% in the coming years, driven by the Ley de Transición Energética (LTE). The document emphasizes the successful completion of long-term electricity auctions, projecting substantial investments in new clean energy generation capacity and the establishment of a fund to provide electricity access to impoverished communities, reinforcing Mexico's leadership in combating climate change through a diversified and cleaner energy matrix.

Document Title: National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2018
Family Title: National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2018
Family Summary: The vision of this Policy is to build a climate-adapted and climate-resilient nation safe from disaster risk. The goal of this policy is to reduce disaster mortality and number of affected people substantially, increase resiliency by reducing disaster damage to means of livelihoods as well as critical infrastructures and disruption of basic services such as agriculture, industry, roads, communication, water supply and sanitation, education and health facilities, and reduce direct disaster economic loss. It mainstreams diverse areas of disaster management, risk reduction, and efficient and effective response as well as adopting the approach of Build Back Better (BBB) for rehabilitation and reconstruction in the post-disaster period.

Document Title: 5. Indicative Program for the Installation and Removal of Power Plants (PIIRCE) [5. Programa Indicativo para la Instalación y Retiro de Centrales Eléctricas (PIIRCE)]
Family Title: Indicative Program for the Installation and Decommissioning of Power Plants (PIIRCE) [Programa Indicativo para la Instalación y Retiro de Centrales Eléctricas (PIIRCE)]
Family Summary: The Indicative Program for the Installation and Decommissioning of Power Plants (PIIRCE) is a planning tool mandated by Mexico’s Electricity Industry Law (LIE) to guide the installation and retirement of power plants, ensuring sufficient resources to meet the demand of the National Electric System (SEN) while fulfilling clean energy objectives. Developed by the Secretariat of Energy (SENER), the PIIRCE is integrated into the broader Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional (PRODESEN) and coordinates with programmes for the expansion and modernisation of the National Transmission Network (RNT) and General Distribution Networks (RGD), as well as gas pipeline infrastructure planning. It aims to enhance the reliability of the SEN, reduce electricity tariffs, and strengthen the role of the state-owned Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) as a key driver of national development, while encouraging private investment under a framework of legal certainty and transparency. The programme includes plans for the medium-term addition of combined-cycle plants, the rehabilitation and modernisation of existing hydroelectric facilities, and the equipping of new hydroelectric projects at existing sites.

Document Title: Framework for Local Adaptation Plans of Action (LAPA) 2019
Family Title: Framework for Local Adaptation Plans of Action (LAPA) 2019
Family Summary:
The objective of this framework is to focus on development and construction at the local level to build a climate-resilient society. It emphasises climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction in the overall process of resource management and mainstreaming management. The LAPA framework also aims to integrate climate change considerations into local development and resource management processes. 

This Framework covers the following areas:

  • Resilient Infrastructure: Constructing flood-resistant housing and infrastructure in high-risk areas.
  • Water Resource Management: Promoting rainwater harvesting and improved irrigation systems.
  • Climate-Resilient Agriculture: Supporting adaptive agricultural practices to ensure food security.
  • Disaster Preparedness: Reducing community vulnerability to floods, landslides, and extreme weather.
  • Social Protection Inclusion: Safeguarding women, children, the elderly, and marginalised groups from climate impacts.

Document Title: Nature Conservation National Strategic Framework for Sustainable Development (2015-2030)
Family Title: Nature Conservation National Strategic Framework for Sustainable Development (2015-2030)
Family Summary:
This Framework aims to make development sustainable and environmentally sensitive by integrating nature conservation into all development efforts, and guides the concerned sectoral agencies, private sector, civil society and development partners in how to best ensure that the plans, programmes and projects they conduct are nature-sensitive. This Framework also contributes to poverty alleviation.

It covers forest, biodiversity and environmental services, agriculture, land management, physical infrastructure development and environment, society, culture and education, climate change and energy, water resource and disaster risk management, environmental education, health and law, and policy provisions.

Some examples of climate-related actions included in the Framework are:

  • While formulating development plans, adopt climate adaptation and impact reduction processes.
  • Make provision to assess the contribution of local genetic resources to climate change adaptation in the investment process.
  • All development programmes to assess climate change risks.

Document Title: Climate Change Gender Action Plan
Family Title: Climate Change Gender Action Plan
Family Summary: The overall of this Plan is to operationalise gender concerns in climate change efforts to enhance implementation and contribute to the promotion of gender equality in Nepal. There are six priority sectors: : (i) Agriculture and Food Security; (ii) Forests and REDD; (iii) Water, (iv) Energy, (v) Health and (vi) Urbanisation. This Plan is a catalyst for further action to be taken through the inclusion of gender in national climate change processes, policy development, decision-making and project development and implementation.

Document Title: Agreement issuing the General Rules of the Natural Disaster Fund (Acuerdo que emite las Reglas Generales del Fondo de Desastres Naturales)
Family Title: Agreement issuing the General Rules of the Natural Disaster Fund (Acuerdo por el que se emiten las Reglas Generales del Fondo de Desastres Naturales)
Family Summary: The Agreement issuing the General Rules of the Natural Disaster Fund (FONDEN) establishes a framework for managing resources to address natural disasters in Mexico, emphasising a transition from reactive to preventive civil protection measures. Rooted in the Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2007–2012 and the "Programa Nacional de Protección Civil", the policy mandates coordination across federal, state, and municipal governments to mitigate disaster impacts. The fund comprises three instruments: a revolving fund for emergency supplies (Fondo Revolvente FONDEN), an annual federal budget program (Ramo General 23), and a trust fund. Key objectives include rapid response to natural phenomena (e.g., hurricanes, floods), infrastructure repair (transport, energy, health sectors), and reducing vulnerabilities exacerbated by climate change. Regulatory mechanisms prioritise transparency, timely resource allocation, and the use of digital tools to enhance efficiency in disaster response. The policy targets regions exposed to hydro-meteorological risks, particularly those with high social and physical vulnerability.The policy acknowledges climate change stressing the rising frequency and intensity of natural disasters linked to global warming, such as floods and hurricanes. FONDEN focuses on adaptation measures, including infrastructure resilience and emergency preparedness. The Fondo Revolvente provides immediate aid (e.g., food, medical supplies) during crises, while longer-term funding supports post-disaster reconstruction.

Document Title: Decree issuing the Law on the State-Owned Enterprise, the Federal Electricity Commission; the Law on the State-Owned Enterprise, Petróleos Mexicanos; the Electricity Sector Law; the Hydrocarbons Sector Law; the Energy Planning and Transition Law; the Biofuels Law; the Geothermal Energy Law; and the Law on the National Energy Commission; amending various provisions of the Law on the Mexican Petroleum Fund for Stabilization and Development; and amending, adding to, and repealing various provisions of the Organic Law of the Federal Public Administration.
Family Title: Law of the State Public Enterprise, Federal Electricity Commission (Ley de la Empresa Pública del Estado, Comisión Federal de Electricidad)
Family Summary: The Law of the State Public Enterprise, Federal Electricity Commission (Ley de la Empresa Pública del Estado, Comisión Federal de Electricidad 'CFE') regulates the structure, operation, and responsibilities of the CFE as a public enterprise under the Mexican federal government. It establishes the CFE’s legal and administrative autonomy and mandates its core purpose: to provide affordable, reliable, and accessible electricity as a social right, in pursuit of energy justice and national development. The CFE is entrusted with the transmission and distribution of electricity and may engage in a broad range of activities, including fuel procurement, infrastructure development, and technological research, both domestically and abroad.Crucially, the law positions the CFE as a key agent in Mexico’s energy transition, responsible for integrating clean and renewable energy sources into its operations. It requires the annual formulation of a Development Programme with a five-year scope and a fifteen-year outlook, addressing energy security, sustainability, and the use of renewables. The CFE is further tasked with supporting national energy sovereignty, minimising profit motives in electricity provision, and contributing to universal internet and telecommunications access. The law thus institutionalises the CFE’s dual role as a guarantor of public welfare and a strategic actor in Mexico’s transition toward a sustainable and inclusive energy system.

Document Title: Nepal Agriculture and Food Security Country Investment Plan
Family Title: Nepal Agriculture and Food Security Country Investment Plan
Family Summary:
The overall goal of this Plan is to reduce poverty and household food insecurity on a sustainable basis and to strengthen the national economy. Another objective is to minimise the adverse effects of the environment, climate variability and climate change in the agriculture sector. This Plan outlines agriculture and food security programmes, identifying sub-program/components and activities that will be carried out by Nepalese Ministries, in particular the Ministry of Agriculture and Cooperatives (MoAC).

Actions include:

  • Increasing the institutional and technical capacity of MoAC at the national and district levels to address climate risk management and disaster prevention / preparedness related issues from an agricultural perspective;
  • Adapting crop varieties, seeking suitable cropping patterns, fruit tree or hedge row intercropping, identifying suitable seed systems, reducing risk through water management in fields, and in the area of livestock management practices; and
  • Reforestation, soil conservation and watershed management.

Document Title: National REDD+ Strategy (2025-2034)
Family Title: National REDD+ Strategy (2025-2034)
Family Summary: This Strategy provides a guiding framework for the implementation of result-based REDD+ and forest-based emissions reduction in the emerging international and national context. This new Strategy resolves the challenges from the previous 2018-2022 Strategy and comprises general background information on REDD+-related international context, Nepal’s REDD+ journey, policy, and legislative provisions, a brief review of the previous Strategy, vision, goal, objectives, strategies, and priority actions, implementation arrangement, safeguard measures, benefit sharing mechanism, financing mechanism, monitoring and evaluation of the strategy. The drivers of deforestation and forest degradation, a detailed implementation plan with an indicative budget and timeline, and a monitoring and evaluation framework are included in the annex of the strategy.

Document Title: Biofuels Law (Ley de Biocombustibles)
Family Title: Biofuels Law (Ley de Biocombustibles)
Family Summary: The Biofuels Law establishes a national framework to regulate and promote the sustainable development of biofuels in Mexico, explicitly positioning them as a component of the country’s energy transition and diversification strategy. Its primary objective is to enhance energy sovereignty, justice, and self-sufficiency through biofuel deployment, while directly contributing to climate change mitigation by targeting reductions in atmospheric pollutants and greenhouse gas emissions. To ensure alignment with national energy transition goals, the law stipulates a formal review and update process for its instruments and programmes every three years, or sooner if justified by new data or adjustments required by the Energy Transition National Strategy (Estrategia Nacional de Transición Energética).
Keyword: Biofuels;Energy Transition;National Energy And Climate Plans

Document Title: Agreement approving and publishing the updated Transition Strategy to Promote the Use of Cleaner Technologies and Fuels (Acuerdo por el que se aprueba y publica la actualización de la Estrategia de Transición para Promover el Uso de Tecnologías y Combustibles más Limpios)
Family Title: Transition Strategy to Promote the Use of Cleaner Technologies and Fuels (Estrategia de Transición para Promover el Uso de Tecnologías y Combustibles más Limpios)
Family Summary: This document represents an update to Mexico's strategy for promoting cleaner technologies and fuels, as mandated by the Ley de Transición Energética (LTE). The strategy aims to guide national policy on clean energy obligations, sustainable energy use, and improvements to the electricity industry in the medium to long term, with the goal of reducing pollutant emissions and the country's dependence on fossil fuels. The update acknowledges challenges, including the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and legal challenges to planning instruments, which have hindered progress towards established clean energy targets, whilst also highlighting the need for greater coordination across government sectors and more in-depth research into energy consumption trends to better inform policy decisions.Despite these obstacles, the update affirms that Mexico is progressing towards a less fossil fuel-dependent economy for electricity generation, with a notable increase in solar photovoltaic and wind energy contributions, reaching 31.2% clean energy generation in 2022. The document also acknowledges that energy efficiency gains have been uneven, necessitating more profound energy efficiency measures to stabilise energy consumption across sectors. The updated strategy emphasises the importance of continued efforts to incorporate cleaner, more efficient technologies and minimise transmission, distribution, and storage challenges to achieve national clean energy goals.

Document Title: Water Resources Strategy - Executive Summary
Family Title: Water Resources Strategy
Family Summary:
This Strategy involves the reconciliation of a range of problems and constraints to sustainable water resource development, including those related to government policies, financial and human resources, institutions and actions. A key objective of WRSF is to identify effective, scientific, sustainable and consensus-based mechanisms to facilitate the implementation of action-oriented initiatives and programs and in doing so, successfully bring about this reconciliation. The goal is to meet Nepal's water supply needs and achieve long-term sustainability.

This Strategy involves the development of a Himalayan Climate Change Study Center, to be established under the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, Ministry of Science and Technology (MOST), to foster understanding of global climate change and its effects on freshwater supply.

Document Title: National Water Policy 2017-2030
Family Title: National Water Policy 2017-2030
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Water Policy 2017-2030 recognises that water insecurity and extreme rainfall patterns among the greatest threats posed by climate change, and includes provisions to improve the nation's resilience to these threats. It aims broadly to improve water quality, accessibility and security. A key provision in the policy is for increased capacity building for collaboration between government ministries on addressing long-term water system threats. Suggested projects include improved water use/availability mapping systems, funding for greater storage capacity, the introduction of a water abstraction permitting system, and low-carbon redevelopment of energy-intensive water system elements such as pumps.

Document Title: Prodesen 2024-2038
Family Title: National Electric System Development Program 2024-2038 (Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2024-2038)
Family Summary: The National Electric System Development Program (PRODESEN) 2024-2038 is one of the Mexico’s principal public policy instrument for the annual planning of the National Electric System (SEN) over a fifteen-year horizon, aligned with the National Development Plan (PND) 2019–2024 and embodying the current government’s energy policy objectives in the electricity sector. It integrates key components from related planning frameworks, such as the Indicative Programme for the Installation and Retirement of Power Plants (PIIRCE), and the expansion and modernisation programmes for the National Transmission Network (RNT) and General Distribution Networks (RGD). The PRODESEN prioritises the role of the state-owned Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) in generation, transmission, and distribution, with plans to develop new power plants, rehabilitate and modernise hydroelectric facilities, and enhance system reliability, efficiency, and affordability.In terms of climate change and energy transition, the PRODESEN is underpinned by Mexico’s commitments to international environmental agreements, including the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the Paris Agreement, and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, with a focus on reducing GHG emissions and promoting sustainable energy practices. It outlines a structured approach to increasing clean and renewable energy generation, emphasising the gradual and orderly integration of these sources into the energy mix, supported by necessary grid infrastructure development. The programme also highlights energy efficiency, electromobility, and the expansion of electricity access to rural and marginalised urban areas, aligning energy policy with environmental protection and sustainable development goals, while ensuring system stability and economic viability.

Document Title: National Biosecurity Policy 2016-2030
Family Title: National Biosecurity Policy 2016-2030
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Biosecurity Policy 2016-2030 aims to strengthen the country's biosecurity, motivated signifcantly by the enhanced threat of pests to agricultural systems under climate change. The policy emphasises international collaboration, staff training, data collection and data-sharing to build capacity for responses to these threats, as well as more funding for testing and compliance systems.

Document Title: Vanuatu National Energy Roadmap (2016-2030) implementation plan
Family Title: Vanuatu National Energy Roadmap (2016-2030) implementation plan
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Energy Roadmap (2016-2030) Implementation Plan aims to make energy accessible, secure, sustainable and affordable, promoting the green growth of the national economy. It primarily supports increased renewable energy installation and the improved electrification of currently off-grid rural areas. Other provisions include energy efficiency projects for transport, household appliances, biomass end-use and diesel electricity generation. The plan also emphasises improved data collection, aiming to build on the success of previous energy usage censuses.

Document Title: National Forestry Policy 2019
Family Title: National Forestry Policy 2019
Family Summary: This Policy aims to promote sustainable management of forest resources and enhance forest productivity. It places strong emphasis on soil and water conservation at the watershed level, advocating for planning and studies based on catchment areas. To support these goals, the policy encourages forest user groups to adopt scientific forest management practices that help strengthen ecosystems and enhance the provision of environmental services. The policy also highlights the importance of land use planning and prioritising the conservation of biodiversity, ecosystems, and genetic resources. It calls for the effective production and utilisation of forest resources while integrating forest management, biodiversity conservation, and community development in a holistic and coordinated manner.

Document Title: Vanuatu National Adaptation Programme for Action (NAPA). 2007
Family Title: Vanuatu National Adaptation Programme for Action (NAPA). 2007
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Adaptation Programme for Action (NAPA) from 2007 aims to give project-based provisions for urgent climate adaptation in vulnerable priority sectors. It covers proposed projects in: agriculture and food security; water management; sustainable tourism; sustainable forest management; and community-based marine resource management. The programme explicitly ranks agricultural and food security alongside water management as its highest-priority interventions

Document Title: Sustainable Taxonomy of Mexico (Taxonomia Sostenible de México)
Family Title: Sustainable Taxonomy of Mexico (Taxonomia Sostenible de México)
Family Summary: The Mexican Sustainable Taxonomy is a national framework designed to classify economic activities, projects and investments that contribute positively to environmental and social objectives. It establishes a science‑based, transparent system of criteria and thresholds that allow financial markets to identify “sustainable” assets, thereby reducing green‑washing and directing capital toward climate‑friendly and socially inclusive projects. The taxonomy’s first phase focuses on four core objectives (climate‑change mitigation, climate‑change adaptation, gender equality, and sustainable cities) while also incorporating a broader set of environmental goals such as water management, biodiversity conservation, and circular economy practices. Activities are evaluated against “technical assessment criteria” that include a primary metric, a substantial contribution threshold, non‑harm criteria, and minimum safeguards covering human rights, labour standards and governance.In practice, the taxonomy covers six key sectors (agriculture, energy, construction, manufacturing, transport and waste management) and identifies 124 eligible activities that meet the established criteria. For climate‑change mitigation, metrics such as CO₂e emissions reductions and energy‑efficiency gains are used, while adaptation is assessed qualitatively through resilience to climate risks.

Document Title: Protected Area Management Strategy 2022-2030
Family Title: Protected Area Management Strategy 2022-2030
Family Summary:
This Strategy provides a clear roadmap to move ahead, creating climate-resilient ecosystems and self-sustaining protected area management in Nepal by 2030. The guiding principles of this strategy are as follows:

  • Species-focused ecosystem approach
  • Climate resilient and adaptive management
  • Human-wildlife coexistence
  • Balancing conservation and development needs
  • Zero tolerance on wildlife crime
  • Inclusive and good governance
  • Sustainable financing mechanism
  • Towards carbon neutrality.

Climate-related actions include:

  • Establish hydro-meteorological stations to monitor impacts of climate-induced risks
  • Develop an early warning system in each protected area, prepare a disaster risk reduction plan, and create climate refugia
  • Generate information on climatic variables, climate change impacts, risks, and vulnerabilities for integration in PA management
  • Collaborate with academic and research institutions and conservation partners
  • Develop climate smart species conservation action plans
  • Conduct periodic carbon inventory and designate carbon neutral protected areas
  • Develop climate smart protected area infrastructures, including all weather roads

Document Title: Decree issuing the Internal Regulations of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (Decreto por el que se expide el Reglamento Interior de la Secretaría de Agricultura y Desarrollo Rural)
Family Title: Internal Regulations of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (Reglamento Interior de la Secretaría de Agricultura y Desarrollo Rural)
Family Summary: The Internal Regulations of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (SADER) establishes a structured framework for advancing sustainable agricultural development in Mexico, emphasising climate resilience, biodiversity conservation, and resource efficiency. Organised into specialised coordinations and directorates (including the Coordinación General de Sustentabilidad y Resiliencia Climática and Dirección General de Sustentabilidad), the policy mandates inter-institutional collaboration to integrate climate adaptation into agricultural planning. Key responsibilities include designing public policies to mitigate climate risks (e.g., droughts, floods), promoting sustainable production systems, and aligning national efforts with international agreements (e.g., Paris Agreement). The policy explicitly addresses climate change. The Coordinación General de Sustentabilidad y Resiliencia Climática oversees initiatives such as promoting agroecological practices, restoring degraded soils, optimising water use, and reducing pesticide reliance. It also emphasises deforestation prevention and the adoption of regenerative livestock systems to curb greenhouse gas emissions. The Dirección General de Sustentabilidad further mandates the development of climate-resilient strategies, including early-warning systems for extreme weather, land-use planning to avoid deforestation, and biodiversity integration into agriculture. Similarly, financing mechanisms under the Dirección General de Financiamiento Verde seek international partnerships to fund sustainable projects, aligning with global climate goals.

Document Title: Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF 2023)
Family Title: Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF 2023)
Family Summary:
This Framework serves as a tool to continuously identify nature, magnitude, extent and duration of environmental and social impacts. The environmental assessment to determine environmental and social costs, includes an assessment of climate change related impacts to build robust strategies to address and mitigate escalating impact on essentail structures like roads, bridges, tunnels and flyovers.

This Framework contains the procedures for environmental and social assessment; the baseline study of environmental and social components; impact assessment and mitigation measures; the environmental and social management plan; stakeholder consultation and information disclosure; the resettlement policy, indigenous people development and vulnerable community development framework, the grievance redress mechanism; occupational health and safety management; the gender equality and social inclusion and risk management plan; the environmental and social monitoring and environmental audit; and the institutional arrangements and implementation.

Document Title: Gender and Social Inclusion Action Plan for Climate Change Policy 2020-2030
Family Title: Gender and Social Inclusion Action Plan for Climate Change Policy 2020-2030
Family Summary: This Policy aims to mainstream gender and social inclusion in policy formulation, institutional structures, and program implementation related to climate change. It emphasises facilitating livelihood enhancement by integrating and simplifying gender and social inclusion considerations. Furthermore, based on the experiences gained from various studies and research, as well as recommendations derived from different practices in the field of adaptation, a deeper analysis has been conducted in Nepal's climate change policies. This analysis aims to comprehensively address the various societal, economic, and political aspects to address social justice issues as high priorities.

Document Title: National Forest Integrated Strategic Plan (2025-2043)
Family Title: National Forest Integrated Strategic Plan (2025-2043)
Family Summary:
This Plan ensures sutainable forest management and biodiversity conservation, and is provided for under the Forest Act. The integrated strategic plan will guide the provincial governments to sustainably manage national forests and to face the challenges seen in forest management in inter-provincial coordination and cooperation, and to increase the production and productivity of forest products. This will contribute to promoting a clean environment, self-reliance in forest products, export promotion, and green economy development.

Climate-related actions include:

  • Mapping climate change vulnerability and poverty analysis in the forest sector;
  • Formulating forest management action plans at all levels and ecosystem risk analysis;
  • Recognition and priorisation of climate change options in the forestry sector;
  • Climate change adaptation capacity development;
  • Plantation and promotion of forest vegetation adapted to climate change for the provision of goods and services from forests;
  • Diversification of income generation to increase the resilience of the poor, women, Dalits, indigenous peoples, and marginalised groups and forest management groups at risk of climate change;
  • Climate change and natural disaster risk analysis, risk reduction plan preparation and calculation.

Document Title: Fifteenth Development Plan (2019/20–2023/24)
Family Title: Fifteenth Development Plan (2019/20–2023/24)
Family Summary:
This Plan sets the target to ensure that there are 460 localities that have prepared and implemented a climate change adaptation plan by FY 2023/24. One of the national objectives is to implement strategies of climate change adaptability and disaster risk reduction, mainstreaming disaster management into the development process through institutional and structural reforms at the federation, province, and local levels for preparedness, rescue and relief, and rehabilitation.

A section covers the strategies for climate change adaptation and mitigation, and accessing international finance and technologies, including forest management, green development, and electric vehicles.

There are also sectoral goals that are climate-relevant. For instance, the goal for the agricultural sector is to acheive inclusive and sustainable economic growth through the transformation of the agricultural sector into a competitive, climate-resilient, self-reliant and export-oriented industry, by developing climate-adaptive and resilient organic farming. For tourism, sensitive tourist destinations and cultural heritage sites vulnerable to climate risks will be identified and protected. For water, the objective is to ensure climate change-resilient and disaster management-friendly drinking-water and sanitation services.

Document Title: National Strategy for the implementation of the 2030 Agenda in Mexico. Leaving no one behind: For the good of all, putting the poor first, protecting the environment, and an inclusive economy (Estrategia Nacional para la implementación de la Agenda 2030 en México. Para no dejar a nadie atrás: Por el bien de todos, primero los pobres, el cuidado del medio ambiente y una economía incluyente)
Family Title: National Strategy for the implementation of the 2030 Agenda in Mexico (Estrategia Nacional para la implementación de la Agenda 2030 en México)
Family Summary: Mexico's National Strategy for the 2030 Agenda establishes a framework for sustainable development, placing climate change action as a central pillar. It commits to transitioning towards a low-greenhouse-gas emission development model by 2030, prioritising sustainable natural resource management, clean and renewable energy adoption, and the integration of climate resilience into economic growth. The strategy underscores alignment with international objectives to limit global temperature increase to below 2°C and pursue efforts towards 1.5°C, emphasising the urgency of both mitigating emissions and adapting to climate impacts to safeguard ecosystems, communities, and future prosperity.The policy details specific climate-focused measures, including strengthening ecosystem adaptation through protected area management, reforestation, and community-based adaptation plans; promoting low-carbon technologies and processes across industry, energy, and waste sectors via regulations, incentives, and carbon pricing mechanisms; and consolidating institutional coordination through the National Climate Change System (SINACC) to ensure policy coherence and effective implementation across all government levels. It further stresses inclusivity, integrating gender and human rights perspectives to address disproportionate climate vulnerabilities, and highlights the mobilisation of public and private finance—through strategic investment, insurance mechanisms, and international cooperation—to support mitigation, adaptation, and disaster risk reduction efforts.

Document Title: National Energy Efficiency Strategy, 2019
Family Title: National Energy Efficiency Strategy, 2019
Family Summary: This Strategy aims to ensure the accessibility of affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all and to promote sustainable and accountable production and use. It recognises that energy efficiency can help in achieving the goals of sustainable development, in reducing carbon emissions and environmental imbalance and in minimising the negative effects of climate change. Actions include developing minimum energy performance standards for electrical and mechanical equipment used in various sectors and conducting energy audits.

Document Title: Least Cost Generation Plan (2021)
Family Title: Least Cost Generation Plan (2021)
Family Summary: Lebanon's Least Cost Generation Plan (2021), written by the Ministry of Environment in collaboration with the World Bank, presents a roadmap for enhancing energy security and increasing production levels by 2030, while optimising for energy generation cost. The plan promotes increased adoption of solar and wind power, alongside hydroelectric pumped storage capacity and some natural gas development replacing more carbon-intensive fossil fuels.

Document Title: Programs for the Expansion and Modernization of the National Transmission Network and the elements of the General Distribution Networks that correspond to the Wholesale Electricity Market - PAMRNT 2024 - 2037 (Programas de Ampliación y Modernización de la Red Nacional de Transmisión y de los elementos de las Redes Generales de Distribución que correspondan al Mercado Eléctrico Mayorista - PAMRNT 2024 - 2037)
Family Title: Expansion and Modernization Programs for the National Transmission Network and the Elements of the General Distribution Networks of the Wholesale Electricity Market (PAMRNT) 2024-2038 [Programas de Ampliación y Modernización de la Red Nacional de Transmisión y de los elementos de las Redes Generales de Distribución del Mercado Eléctrico Mayorista (PAMRNT) 2024 - 2038]
Family Summary: This policy document details programmes for the expansion and modernisation of Mexico's National Transmission Network (RNT) and General Distribution Networks (RGD) associated with the Wholesale Electricity Market. It operates within the context of the country's Energy Reform, with the Ministry of Energy (SENER) and the National Energy Control Centre (CENACE) coordinating efforts to ensure the efficiency, quality, reliability, continuity, and security of the National Electricity System (SEN). The overarching aim is to strategically plan and develop grid infrastructure, integrating demand forecasts and generation capacity plans. A key objective is to facilitate the increased integration and utilisation of clean energies, thereby modernising the electricity sector to support national development and meet evolving energy policy objectives.The policy significantly emphasises climate change mitigation and adaptation. It supports Mexico's international commitments, such as the Paris Agreement, by promoting the transition to a higher proportion of clean energy in electricity generation, projected to increase to 61.41% by 2038. This involves planning for new capacity from renewable sources and energy storage, alongside measures aimed at reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through fuel substitution and grid efficiency improvements. The policy also incorporates strategies for enhanced resilience, such as ensuring flexible generation to counter the impact of climate events on variable renewable sources. Furthermore, it acknowledges the influence of climate phenomena, like heat waves, on electricity demand patterns and system reliability, and promotes electromobility as a key strategy for reducing transport sector emissions, integrating considerations for the broader energy transition.

Document Title: National Agricultural Planning 2017-2029 (Planeación agrícola nacional 2017-2029)
Family Title: National Agricultural Planning 2017-2030 (Planeación agrícola nacional 2017-2030)
Family Summary: The National Agricultural Planning 2017-2030 was designed to align stakeholders in the agri-food sector towards shared objectives. It focuses on 38 strategic crops, outlining market strategies, optimal production regions based on agroclimatic and logistical factors, and measures to enhance productivity while reducing costs. The policy emphasises climate-smart agriculture and sustainable practices to address stagnating productivity, alongside strategies to mitigate cross-border pests and diseases exacerbated by climate change threatening food security. It also highlights the need for risk-responsive approaches to natural disasters and conflicts, which disproportionately affect food-insecure regions due to climate-agriculture interdependencies. The framework promotes a regionally tailored development model, prioritising agroclimatic suitability, innovation, and infrastructure investment. It encourages public-private collaboration, capacity-building, and resource efficiency to strengthen resilience and market competitiveness.
