Document Title: National action plan to combat desertification aligned with the 2008-2018 ten-year strategic framework plan
Family Title: National action plan to combat desertification aligned with the 2008-2018 ten-year strategic framework plan
Family Summary:
To address the serious threats of desertification and the degradation of its natural resources, Madagascar has adopted a National Action Plan (PAN) to combat desertification aligned with the ten-year strategic framework plan 2008-2028. The overall objective of the aligned NAP is to improve productive capital (land, water and natural biological resources) as a means of combating desertification and land degradation.

To achieve this objective, the PAN is structured around two main axes: the development of knowledge, the promotion of awareness and attitude of stakeholders, the improvement of productivity, and the restoration of affected areas.

Document Title: National Electric System Development Program 2021-2035 (Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2021-2035)
Family Title: National Electric System Development Program 2021-2035 (Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2021-2035)
Family Summary: The Programa para el Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional (PRODESEN) 2021-2035 is a key planning instrument for Mexico’s National Electric System (SEN), outlining a fifteen-year strategy for electricity generation, transmission, and distribution, in alignment with the National Development Plan. It integrates various planning tools, such as the Indicative Programme for the Installation and Retirement of Power Plants (PIIRCE) and programmes for the expansion and modernisation of the National Transmission Network (RNT) and General Distribution Networks (RGD). The PRODESEN aims to ensure a reliable electricity supply for over 120 million users across two million square kilometres, while addressing the growing demand, reducing electricity costs, and enhancing system reliability. A core objective is to strengthen the role of the state-owned Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) in generation and transmission, including the reactivation of combined-cycle plants and the modernisation of hydroelectric facilities, to support national energy sovereignty and economic development.In relation to climate change and energy transition, the PRODESEN explicitly incorporates Mexico’s international commitments under frameworks such as the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the Kyoto Protocol, the Paris Agreement, and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. It emphasises the reduction of GHG emissions, targeting a limit of 139 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030, as part of Mexico’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). The programme promotes the orderly integration of clean and renewable energy sources into the national energy mix, with a significant focus on distributed generation, particularly solar photovoltaic systems, which are projected to grow substantially by 2035. Additionally, it underscores energy efficiency measures and the expansion of electricity access to rural communities, aligning energy policy with sustainable development goals and environmental protection.

Document Title: Nepal: Zero Hunger Challenge National Action Plan (2016-2025)
Family Title: Nepal: Zero Hunger Challenge National Action Plan (2016-2025)
Family Summary:
This Plan is a cross-sectoral plan to ensure the right to food by improving food and nutrition security of people to achieve a society free of hunger and malnutrition by 2025.

The third strategic pillar under the Zero Hunger Challenge (ZHC) Initiative is about ensuring that all food systems are sustainable: Ensuring that all farmers, agribusinesses, cooperatives, government, unions and civil society establish standards for sustainability; verifying their observance and being accountable for them; encouraging and rewarding universal adoption of sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture practices; pursuing cross-sectoral policy coherence (encompassing energy, land use, water and climate); implementing responsible governance of land, fisheries and forests.

Climate-related actions include training farmers to cope with the adverse effects of natural disasters and climate change; and conducting research on climate-resilient agriculture development practices.

Document Title: National Policy for Disaster Risk Reduction 2020-2030
Family Title: National Policy for Disaster Risk Reduction 2020-2030
Family Summary: This National Policy for Risk Reduction is in response to the international commitments made by the Chilean State and the need to establish guidelines to strengthen Disaster Risk Management in the country by 2030. It is comprised of a set of principles, cross-cutting approaches, priority axes and strategic objectives, which will be implemented through its respective National Strategic Plan for Disaster Risk Reduction, which will address gaps identified in previous processes and consider the territorial particularities and diversity of communities through the implementation of strategic actions emanating from the guidelines established in this public policy.

Document Title: Sustainable Tourism Policy 2019-2030
Family Title: Sustainable Tourism Policy 2019-2030
Family Summary: Vanuatu's Sustainable Tourism Policy (2019-2030) aims to develop the country's tourism sector while aligning with existing environmental, cultural and sustainability goals. Its objectives attempt to embed and mainstream sustainability principles in major elements of the tourism sector such as transport, infrastructure and land-use planning. Its provisions revolve primarily around improved capacity-building and data collection, with further suggestions for compliance regulation and promotion of funding for sustainable technology in tourism-related developments.

Document Title: Setting Lebanon’s Electricity Sector on a Sustainable Growth Path (2022)
Family Title: Setting Lebanon’s Electricity Sector on a Sustainable Growth Path (2022)
Family Summary: 'Setting Lebanon’s Electricity Sector on a Sustainable Growth Path (2022)' is a policy statement and plan by the Lebanese Ministry of Environment, based on the Least Cost Generation Plan (Ministry of Energy and Water, World Bank, EDF Energy; 2021). It promotes enhancing renewable generation capacity to meet Lebanon's climate mitigation commitments and energy demand forecasts, alongside significant natural gas development. The plan aims for a 15% renewable share in the energy mix by 2026, reaching 30% by 2030.

Document Title: National Action Programme to Combat Desertification (NAP)
Family Title: National Action Programme to Combat Desertification (NAP)
Family Summary: The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in those Countries Experiencing Serious Drought or Desertification, Particularly in Africa (UNCCD) was adopted on 17 June 1994 in Paris and entered into force on 26 December 1996.

Document Title: Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Rules 2019
Family Title: Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Rules 2019
Family Summary: These Rules, formulated under section 47 of the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act, set out the functions, duties and powers of the Executive Committee in addition to those mentioned in the Act. Their duties shall include providing suggestions with the identification of a variety of disaster risk reduction and management aspects by discussing with the experts and stakeholders on the impact of climate change.

Document Title: Law No. 29664, creating the National Disaster Risk Management System (SINAGERD)
Family Title: Law No. 29664, creating the National Disaster Risk Management System (SINAGERD)
Family Summary:
This policy regulates the objectives, composition, and operation of SINAGERD, which aims to identify and reduce the risks associated with dangers, minimize their effects, and address dangerous situations through management guidelines. The rule specifies that the law applies to all public entities and companies at all levels of government, the private sector, and citizens in general.

Likewise, it defines disaster risk management, as well as establishes the guidelines of the National Disaster Risk Management Policy and defines it as the set of guidelines aimed at preventing or reducing disaster risks, avoiding the generation of new risks and carrying out adequate preparation, care, rehabilitation and reconstruction in the event of disasters.

Document Title: Mexican Standard NMX-AA-173-SCFI-2015 for the registration of forest carbon projects and the certification of carbon stock increases (Norma Mexicana NMX-AA-173-SCFI-2015 para el registro de proyectos forestales de carbono y la certificación del incremento en el acervo de carbono)
Family Title: Mexican Standard NMX-AA-173-SCFI-2015 for the registration of forest carbon projects and certification of carbon stock increases (Norma Mexicana NMX-AA-173-SCFI-2015 para el registro de proyectos forestales de carbono y certificación del incremento de acervo de carbono)
Family Summary: The Mexican Standard NMX‑AA‑173‑SCFI‑2015 provides a national framework for the registration of forest carbon projects and the certification of increases in carbon stocks. Developed in the context of Mexico’s General Law on Climate Change, the National Climate Change Strategy, and the Special Climate Change Programme, it seeks to strengthen mitigation efforts by promoting sustainable forest management as a means to reduce deforestation and degradation, preserve ecosystem services, and enhance natural carbon sinks.

Document Title: Resolution 252/2021 to approve the Catalogue of Cuban Beaches
Family Title: Resolution 252/2021 to approve the Catalogue of Cuban Beaches
Family Summary: The Catalogue of Cuban Beaches is the basis on which the concept, baseline and analysis of progress in the conservation and restoration of the country's beaches will be established. This Catalogue establishes administrative control of sandy beaches and includes as priority the coastal zone sectors identified in the State Plan for Combating Climate Change. The Institute of Marine Sectors is the agency responsible.

Document Title: Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Rules 2019
Family Title: Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Rules 2019
Family Summary: These Rules, formulated under section 47 of the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act, set out the functions, duties and powers of the Executive Committee in addition to those mentioned in the Act. Their duties shall include providing suggestions with the identification of a variety of disaster risk reduction and management aspects by discussing with the experts and stakeholders on the impact of climate change.

Document Title: National Gender Equality Policy 2020-2030
Family Title: National Gender Equality Policy 2020-2030
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Gender Equality Policy 2020-2030 acknowledges the disproportionate impact of climate change on women and girls, making community-driven gender-inclusive climate/disaster resilience one of its five core strategic areas. It aims to promote the incorporation of gender-responsiveness into climate adaptation and disaster laws, and build institutional capacity (including a National Gender Action Plan) for ensuring these elements are considered.

Document Title: Decree No. 4612 establishing the Presidential Commission for Climate Change (Decreto No. 4612 que establece la Comisión Presidencial para el Cambio Climático)
Family Title: Decree No. 4612 establishing the Presidential Commission for Climate Change (Decreto No. 4612 que establece la Comisión Presidencial para el Cambio Climático)
Family Summary: Venezuela established a permanent Presidential Commission for Climate Change through Decree No. 4.612. This commission serves as an advisory body to the President on climate change matters and comprises representatives from five ministries: ecosocialism (presiding), planning, foreign relations, industries and national production, and science and technology. The commission operates under a technical secretariat exercised by the Ministry of Popular Power for Ecosocialism and may convene additional government bodies and subject matter experts as required.The commission's primary functions encompass advising the President on climate change issues, developing proposals for national climate change regulations, and coordinating the creation of the National Climate Change Strategy alongside National Adaptation and Mitigation Plans for presidential approval. Additional responsibilities include ensuring effective technical, administrative and financial information management; strengthening state, regional and municipal monitoring, reporting and verification capacities for climate adaptation and mitigation; and promoting risk management measures to address climate change vulnerabilities and impacts. The commission is empowered to establish working groups for specific topics and must develop its internal operating regulations within ninety days of the decree's publication.

Document Title: Sustainable Finance Mobilization Strategy (EMFS) [Estrategia de Movilización de Financiamiento Sostenible (EMFS)]
Family Title: Sustainable Finance Mobilization Strategy (EMFS) [Estrategia de Movilización de Financiamiento Sostenible (EMFS)]
Family Summary: Sustainable Financing Mobilization Strategy (EMFS), developed by Mexico's Ministry of Finance and Public Credit, represents a comprehensive framework for redirecting financial flows towards sustainable development whilst addressing climate change challenges. The strategy identifies a substantial financing gap of 13.6 trillion mexican pesos between 2023 and 2030, requiring annual mobilisation of 1.7 trillion pesos (equivalent to 5.4% of 2023 GDP) to achieve the country's sustainable development targets. Through its three foundational pillars (Sustainable Public Financial Management, Sustainable Finance Mobilisation, and Cross-cutting Actions) the EMFS aims to mobilise up to 15 trillion pesos during this period by engaging public, private, and social sectors in voluntary adoption of sustainable finance practices.The strategy places significant emphasis on climate change mitigation and adaptation, acknowledging that approximately 40% of Mexican territory and 68% of its population are exposed to climate impacts due to the country's geographical location and socioeconomic structure. The EMFS integrates climate risk management into public financial planning, promotes investment in resilient infrastructure and nature-based solutions, and addresses biodiversity loss as a critical environmental challenge. Underpinned by principles of climate justice, environmental justice, and social justice, the strategy seeks to align Mexico's economic development with international climate commitments, including the Paris Agreement and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The framework particularly emphasises the nexus between poverty and climate vulnerability, incorporating gender perspectives and social inclusion measures to ensure that sustainable finance mobilisation addresses both environmental degradation and socioeconomic inequalities simultaneously.

Document Title: National Flood Risk Management Strategy
Family Title: National Flood Risk Management Strategy
Family Summary:
The national flood risk management strategy pursues three priority objectives, the achievement of which must be analyzed in the long term by the various stakeholders for 20 or 30 years through progressive implementation by conducting a quantified evaluation of current and future performance.

Increase the safety of exposed populations.

Stabilize in the short term and reduce in the medium term the cost of damage linked to flooding

Significantly shorten the time it takes for disaster-stricken areas to return to normal.

Document Title: Disaster Risk Management Act no. 23 of 2019
Family Title: Disaster Risk Management Act no. 23 of 2019
Family Summary: The Disaster Risk Management Act no. 23 of 2019 acknowledges climate change as a key natural disaster threat to Vanuatu, and introduces legal provisions for responding to major disasters of any kind. It defines the structure, function and responsibilities of national and subnational committees dedicated to co-ordinating disaster response, and defines a framework for the official declaration of national emergencies. These committees at the provincial and municipal levels are explicitly named 'Disaster and Climate Change Committees', combining climate risk management with general disaster management responsibilities. This act replaces and repeals the National Disaster Act [CAP267].

Document Title: Lebanon's National Forest Fire Management Strategy
Family Title: Lebanon's National Forest Fire Management Strategy (2008)
Family Summary: Lebanon's National Forest Fire Management Strategy (2008) acknowledges climate change as a major and increasing contributor to forest fires, alongside changes in land use. The strategy recommends several climate-related measures such as fine-scale spatial mapping of climate change predictions to help target risk reduction measures, and using carbon sequestration funding to restore habitats with high fire risk to improve their resilience.

Document Title: Agreement on the Implementation of the Clean Development Mechanism
Family Title: Agreement on the Implementation of the Clean Development Mechanism
Family Summary: This is an Agreement adopted by the Executive Committee of the Council of Ministers on the national implementation of the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) under the Kyoto Protocol. The Ministry of Science, Technology and the Environment is responsible for said implementation and shall establish measures within 90 days of this Agreement, while the National Group for the Implementation of the CDM is established to evaluate and propose actions for the implementation and make proposals to the Ministry. This Group will be permanently composed of the Ministry of Foreign Investment and Cooperation, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Economy and Planning, the Ministry of Finance and Prices, and any other agencies that may be convened as needed.

Document Title: National Water Sector Strategy (2024-2035)
Family Title: National Water Sector Strategy (2024-2035)
Family Summary: Lebanon's National Water Sector Strategy (2024-2035) emphasises the importance of enhancing resilience to climate change in the country's water systems. By 2035 he strategy aims to: increase storage capacity; introduce a comprehensive digital monitoring system for national water usage and resources; increase hydropower production capacity by 15%; expand access and public management of water and wastewater systems; achieve a 30% energy cost reduction in the water sector through efficiency measures; and promote stronger governance in the water sector. Further adaptation-related measures include setting up a water resilience research program, and a stormwater management plan due to the increased incidence of extreme rainfall events under climate change.

Document Title: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2018-2030
Family Title: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2018-2030
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2018-2030 acknowledges climate change as a significant threat to the nation's biodiversity and ecosystem services, and emphasises the importance of ecosystems such as mangroves in climate mitigation via carbon sequestration. It contains measures for monitoring biodiversity changes, and enhancing funding to nature recovery projects which include nature-based solutions expected to feed into carbon credit markets. Organic carbon stock is given as a factor for the prioritisation of habitats for restoration and protection efforts.

Document Title: Regulations of the Federal Budget and Fiscal Responsibility Law (Reglamento de la Ley Federal de Presupuesto y Responsabilidad Hacendaria)
Family Title: Regulations of the Federal Budget and Fiscal Responsibility Law (Reglamento de la Ley Federal de Presupuesto y Responsabilidad Hacendaria)
Family Summary: The Federal Budget and Fiscal Responsibility Law Regulation establishes the framework for the planning, allocation, execution, oversight, and evaluation of federal public expenditures in Mexico. It mandates that all federal agencies adhere to mandatory budgetary control systems designed to ensure efficient and transparent management of public resources. These systems are aligned with the principles outlined in the parent law, emphasizing accountability, fiscal responsibility, and strategic resource allocation.

Document Title: Lebanon National Agriculture Strategy (NAS). 2020-2025.
Family Title: Lebanon National Agriculture Strategy (NAS). 2020-2025.
Family Summary: Lebanon's National Agriculture Strategy (NAS). 2020-2025 recognises climate change as a major threat to the security of the agricultural sector, and names climate resilience among its five overarching pillars: restoring the livelihoods of producers; increasing agricultural production; enhancing efficiency of value chains; improving climate change adaptation and sustainable management of agrifood systems and natural resources; strengthening and enabling the institutional environment. Climate-related provisions include plans for significant afforestation, both for climate mitigation and to build landscape-level resilience, and the use of renewable energy in the agricultural sector where possible. The strategy also notes that more efficient water usage is a key element of agricultural adaptation to climate change, and promotes the adoption of modernised irrigation techniques.

Document Title: Law on the national policy for risk and disaster management (Law No. 2015-031)
Family Title: Law on the national policy for risk and disaster management (Law No. 2015-031)
Family Summary: At the international level, the Third World Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction took place from March 14 to 18, 2015, in Sendai, Japan. Delegates to this Conference noted the existence of complex emergency situations in many parts of the world. They solemnly reaffirmed their determination to redouble efforts to strengthen disaster risk reduction and reduce human losses in the event of calamities. To achieve this, it is necessary to strengthen the integration of disaster risk reduction into all national development policies. This document therefore presents a revised version of Madagascar's National Disaster Risk Management Policy, in order to align it with developments in the national and international context. This law defines the primary mission of disaster risk management, its fundamental structures, and the principles governing relationships between the various stakeholders. Furthermore, the organizational structures take into account the existing achievements and institutional capacities of the various structures comprising the risk and disaster management mechanism, as well as the fundamental guidelines for risk and disaster management policy, including the Hyōgo Framework for Action, the Sendai Framework, and the new laws on Decentralized Local Authorities. Indeed, the decentralization policy is clearly suited to risk and disaster management, as effective decentralization, accompanied locally by strengthening institutions and skills, promotes community participation and the active participation of civil society and the private sector. This law comprises 33 articles and is divided into six major divisions.

Document Title: Agreement establishing the methodology for the direct measurement of carbon dioxide emissions (Acuerdo por el que se establece la metodología para la medición directa de emisiones de bióxido de carbono)
Family Title: Agreement establishing the methodology for direct measurement of carbon dioxide emissions (Acuerdo que establece la metodología de medición directa de emisiones de bióxido de carbono)
Family Summary: This Mexican agreement establishes the methodology for the direct measurement of carbon dioxide emissions for facilities subject to emissions reporting under the General Law on Climate Change. It specifies that the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources (Secretaría) will identify facilities that must use direct measurement when alternative methodologies outlined in Article 7 of the National Emissions Registry Regulation are not technically feasible, or when the carbon content of fuels is imprecise or varies by more than 10%.

Document Title: The Vanuatu Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2016-2030
Family Title: The Vanuatu Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2016-2030
Family Summary: The Vanuatu Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2016-2030 was published by the Vanuatu government in combination with the Secretariat of the Pacific Community in 2015 to envision the country's response to climate change and make its communities resilient on the long term. The country initiated this process with the establishment of the National Advisory Board on Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction in 2012. It is a broad set of measures based on accountability, sustainability, equity, community focus, collaboration, and innovation. The policy was updated in 2022 to incorporate the perspective of more recent climate-related policies across sectors. The policy insists on 1) establishing appropriate governance and strengthen institutional structures so they can effectively tackle the tasks they are pursuing, 2) to ensure that adequate resourcing is available for climate change and disaster risk reduction activities, notably via the implementation of entity accreditation and small grants schemes, 3) ensure that traditional knowledge and existing and new information such as data analysis, research and risk assessment are shared, 4) adaptation and disaster risk reduction, integrating the two targets and adopting community and ecosystem-based approaches to protect and economically assess losses, 5) low carbon development via an energy roadmap, renewable energy and energy efficiency, but also from a reduction in deforestation and land degradation, 6) and preparedness, planning, response and recovery to disasters by ensuring community awareness, early warning systems. The document also insists on capacity building, gender and social inclusion, multi-hazard approach and partnerships with a vast array of stakeholders. Implementation of the plan must be realised by integrating it into corporate and business plans, monitoring and evaluating the policy by the National Advisory Board on Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction (NAB), and reporting by NAB. A review of the current document should occur every three to five years to ensure it is in line with contemporary developments.

Document Title: Vanuatu Recovery Strategy 2020-2023
Family Title: Vanuatu Recovery Strategy 2020-2023
Family Summary: The aim of the Vanuatu Recovery Strategy is to support communities impacted by Tropical Cyclone (TC) Harold and COVID-19, by providing a framework to recover, rebuild and emerge stronger and more resilient. Section 1 outlines the challenge that TC Harold in combination with COVID-19 created. Section 2 responds to the social, economic and environmental impacts of the compound disaster to set out the core priorities for the next three years. It sets out guiding principles for the recovery, conducts an assessment of needs, and sets recovery objectives, strategies and outcomes.One recovery strategy is to strengthen disaster preparedness, response and recovery mechanisms and structures. This relates to climate and disaster resilience and aims at fostering a a strong and resilient nation in the face of climate change and disaster risks posed by natural and man-made hazards, as set out in the NSDP.Another climate change-related recovery strategy is to support sustainable self-reliance, including food self-sufficiency. As an outcome, this sub-strategy envisions improved farming practices, use of technology and traditional knowledge, crop choices including climate and disaster resilience and strategic import substitution.

Document Title: Green Hydrogen / Green Ammonia Policy
Family Title: Green Hydrogen / Green Ammonia Policy
Family Summary: Building on the National Hydrogen Mission released by the Prime Minister in August 2021, this document sets India's strategy to meet its goal of becoming a global green hydrogen hub. It identifies the production of hydrogen and ammonia from unconsumed renewable power and connectivity to the grid as priorities. The policy sets the framework so that hydrogen / ammonia manufacturers can purchase and use unconsumed renewable power. Waiver of inter-state transmission charges for a period of 25 years will be allowed to the manufacturers for projects commissioned before 30th June 2025. The manufacturers of Green Hydrogen / Ammonia and the renewable energy plant shall be given connectivity to the grid on priority basis to avoid any procedural delays.The document also seeks to develop bunkers near ports for storage and export or direct use by ships. The land for the storage for this purpose shall be provided by the respective Port Authorities at applicable charges.

Document Title: National Disaster Response Plan (RESPONDE Ec)
Family Title: National Disaster Response Plan (RESPONDE Ec)
Family Summary: The National Disaster Response Plan (RESPONDE Ec) establishes a comprehensive framework for addressing natural and anthropogenic emergencies, guided by constitutional provisions such as Articles 261 and 389, which emphasise state responsibility for disaster management and risk reduction. The plan outlines an organisational, technical, and operational structure for interinstitutional coordination under the National Decentralized Risk Management System (SNDGR). It prioritises timely and efficient resource utilisation, protecting lives and property, maintaining governance during crises, and fostering community resilience through early recovery initiatives.Aligned with Ecuador's climate commitments, the plan integrates climate change considerations into disaster response and risk management strategies. It acknowledges the impact of climate-driven phenomena like forest fires, emphasising their links to changing atmospheric conditions and highlighting the need for preparedness to reduce vulnerabilities. Specific measures include strengthening the capacity of emergency operations committees, improving response times, and ensuring comprehensive recovery efforts that align with sustainable development goals.

Document Title: Electricity Sector Law (Ley del Sector Eléctrico)
Family Title: Electricity Sector Law (Ley del Sector Eléctrico)
Family Summary: This regulations establish a comprehensive statutory framework governing Mexico’s electricity sector, affirming the state’s sovereign authority over strategic activities including transmission, distribution, and systemic planning; while delineating permissible private participation in non-exclusive domains. Core objectives encompass preserving national energy security and self-sufficiency, ensuring the efficiency, quality, continuity, accessibility, reliability, and sustainability of the national grid, and upholding the state’s constitutional obligation to provide electricity at the lowest possible cost to the populace. The framework further mandates universal service obligations, including non-discriminatory grid access, equitable supply provision, and adherence to social and developmental imperatives, all underpinned by principles of public utility and national strategic interest in the context of the energy transition.Explicit provisions advance climate change mitigation and sustainable transition, binding commitments to reduce contaminant emissions, achieve sectoral decarbonisation, and fulfil international environmental obligations. The regulations stipulate the integration of clean energy sources, alongside a just and orderly transition toward decarbonised infrastructure, with explicit mandates for climate risk considerations within national energy planning. These include requirements for emissions abatement aligned with global accords, alongside the state’s duty to factor climate change mitigation and adaptation criteria into all binding sectoral development strategies, thereby embedding ecological responsibility within the foundational governance of the electricity system.

Document Title: Resolution No. 43/2006 on the Environment Agency’s responsibilities in DRM
Family Title: Resolution No. 43/2006 on the Environment Agency’s responsibilities in DRM
Family Summary:
This Resolution outlines the responsibilities of the Environment Agency, belonging to the Ministry of Science, Technology and Environment, in disaster risk management. The Environment Agency has the following functions and powers:

a) To prepare proposals for regulatory and methodological documents for the conduct of hazard, vulnerability, and risk studies and environmental impact assessments;

b) Establish the necessary coordination with the centres of the Ministry of Science, Technology, and Environment and other agencies of the Central State Administration that may be necessary to carry out studies on disaster hazards, vulnerability, and risk, as well as environmental impact assessments of disasters.

c) Prepare the personnel of the institutions involved in the aforementioned work to ensure the fulfilment of their tasks.

Document Title: Law of the State Public Enterprise, Petróleos Mexicanos (Ley de la Empresa Pública del Estado, Petróleos Mexicanos)
Family Title: Law of the State Public Enterprise, Petróleos Mexicanos (Ley de la Empresa Pública del Estado, Petróleos Mexicanos)
Family Summary: This Act provides the regulatory framework governing Petróleos Mexicanos (PEMEX) as a State-owned public enterprise, established under Articles 25, 27, and 28 of the Mexican Constitution. It affirms PEMEX's legal personality, operational and management autonomy, and special regulatory regime. The law mandates that PEMEX’s core functions encompass the exploration, transformation, and commercialisation of hydrocarbons and their derivatives, as well as the development of alternative energy sources, all in service of national sovereignty, energy security, sustainability, self-sufficiency, and energy justice.Crucially, the law integrates principles of sustainability and energy transition into PEMEX’s strategic governance. It requires a five-year Development Programme to be updated annually, detailing objectives, clean energy use, and transition planning in line with international obligations. Articles 16 and 49 establish institutional mechanisms to align corporate governance with sustainability, mandating a Sustainability Plan approved by the Board and overseen by a Sustainability Committee chaired by an independent director and comprising key ministries. The law obliges PEMEX to reduce GHG emissions and promote a low-carbon economy through targeted programmes, while ensuring transparency and accountability according to national and international standards.

Document Title: The Sixteenth Plan (Fiscal Year 2024/25 - 2028/29)
Family Title: The Sixteenth Plan (Fiscal Year 2024/25 - 2028/29)
Family Summary:
This Plan has a vision of ensuring good governance, social justice and prosperity. One of the major areas of structural transformation is biological diversity, climate change and green economy.   • Develop a resilient public health system that can address climate-related health issues impacting human health., and strengthen public health surveillance to develop health structures that are resilient to climate change.
  • Strengthen the climate resilience of the education system.
  • Adopt climate-resilience in infrastructure planning.
  • Address environmental and climate-related challenges by using climate finance in infrastructure development.

Document Title: Strategic Climate Change Plan for the Agri-Food Sector (Plan Estratégico de Cambio Climático del sector Agroalimentario)

Its main objective is to provide direction and coherence to the sector's actions to promote fair, diverse, sustainable, inclusive, low-carbon agri-food systems that are resilient to the effects of climate change.

Document Title: National Environmental Restoration Program 2025-2029 (National Environmental Restoration Program 2025-2029)
Family Title: National Environmental Restoration Program 2025-2030 (Programa Nacional de Restauración Ambiental 2025-2030)
Family Summary: The National Environmental Restoration Program 2025-2030 is a national policy in Mexico, established to address the country's extensive environmental degradation and biodiversity loss. It represents a commitment from the Mexican government to a "humanist environmental policy," which views environmental restoration as fundamental to both social well-being and ecological justice. The programme outlines a long-term approach to restoring degraded ecosystems across the country, from urban parks and agricultural lands to protected natural areas. Drawing inspiration from the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, the PNRA prioritises harmonising, organising, and scaling up restoration efforts, which were previously fragmented, through a series of phased objectives and targets for various ecosystems.In the context of climate change, the PNRA is framed as an instrument for both mitigation and adaptation. The policy aims to contribute to Mexico's national and international climate commitments, including the target of a 35% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030. This is to be achieved through large-scale ecosystem restoration projects, such as restoring 100,000 hectares of forest ecosystems and achieving net-zero deforestation by 2030. Furthermore, the programme seeks to reduce the vulnerability of the population to the impacts of climate change by strengthening communities' adaptive capacity through environmental restoration. It also commits to developing a National Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation Plan that integrates restoration and nature-based solutions as key strategies.

Family Title: Disaster Management Act (No. 2 of 2023)
Family Summary:
This Act provides for comprehensive disaster management. It establishes a National Emergency Advisory Council; designates functions and powers of the National Disaster Management Agency and the personnel therein; outlines the operational regulations of various supporting infrastructure and personnel such as the National Emergency Operations Centre, shelters, volunteers and inspections; establishes the District Disaster Management Committee; and delimits specially vulnerable areas. It also contains provisions on disaster risk financing and the national multi-hazard alert system.

There are provisions to ensure that disaster risk reduction and climate change measures are gender-responsive and gender-inclusive; and to encourage the mainstreaming of disaster risk reduction and climate change in development processes, including policy formulation, socioeconomic development planning, budgeting, and governance.

Document Title: National Adaptation Programme of Action (NAPA) to Climate Change
Family Title: National Adaptation Programme of Action (NAPA) to Climate Change
Family Summary:
This National Adaptation Programme of Action (NAPA) mainstreams climate change into Nepal's development planning. The main objectives are to:

  • assess and prioritise climate change vulnerabilities and identify adaptation measures;
  • develop proposals for priority activities;
  • prepare, review and fianlise the NAPA document;
  • develop and maintain a knowledge management and learning platform; and
  • develop a multi-stakeholder framework of action on climate change.

This NAPA was prepared through a consultative process and is the summary of six thematic working groups on agriculture and food security; climate-induced disaster; urban settlement and infrastructure; public health; forests and biodiversity; and water resources and energy, and two cross-cutting reports on livelihood and governance and gender and social inclusion.

It contains sections on the framework for the adaptation programme; the NAPA preparation process; the identification of key adaptation needs, existing adaptation practices and options; and prioritised activities for climate change adaptation.

Document Title: Environment Protection Regulations, 2020
Family Title: Environment Protection Regulations, 2020
Family Summary:
These Regulations contain rules made by the Ministry of Forestry and Environment pursuant to section 44 of the Environment Protection Act. The provisions include:

  • A national report shall be prepared every five years detailing the risks arising from the state of climate change.
  • The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology shall publish a report on the climate change scenario based on climatic factors, including temperature, rainfall and water flow, every five years.
  • Based on these reports, the Government of Nepal, the provincial government or the local level may formulate and prioritise a plan related to climate change management.
  • The local level shall provide the annual progress report of the work done related to climate adaptation to the relevant provincial ministry and the relevant provincial ministry to the Ministry.
  • A proposer who is interested in participating in carbon trading from a project related to the Clean Development Mechanism shall submit a project concept paper, which includes sustainable development criteria as per the format in the UNFCCC, to be evaluated by a Technical Committee comprising various Ministries.

Document Title: Energy Conservation (Regulated Goods and Registered Suppliers) Regulations 2017, last amended in 2025
Family Title: Energy Conservation (Regulated Goods and Registered Suppliers) Regulations (S 748/2017), last amended in 2025
Family Summary: The energy conservation (Regulated Goods and Registered Suppliers) Regulations was enacted under the Energy Conservation Act (Chapter 92C) and sets out the energy efficiency standards and compliance requirements .This regulation was amended several times since then, the last amendment was in 2025. It is he primary legal instrument that details the implementation of the Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS) and the Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme (MELS) for various regulated goods, including lamps.Energy efficiency requirements is brought in the Part 2, regulation 5 and energy label requirements in regulation 6 and 7. MEPS are minimum energy efficiency requirements that regulated appliances must meet to be supplied in Singapore. Their purpose is to (i) Remove the most inefficient appliances from the market, (ii) raise the average energy efficiency of households and industries, (iii) prevent consumers from being locked into high energy consumption and costs associated with inefficient appliances and (iv) drive manufacturers and suppliers to introduce more energy-efficient models into the market. MELS requires specific household appliances, designated as "regulated goods," to carry an energy label. This label provides consumers with information about the appliance's energy consumption and costs, as well as a "tick rating" that indicates its relative energy efficiency (more ticks mean higher efficiency) The 2019 amendments strengthened Singapore's commitment to energy efficiency in lighting by both removing inefficient products from the market through stricter MEPS and by empowering consumers to make better choices through a broader and more visible MELS.

Document Title: Greenhouse and Energy Minimum Standards Act

Generally speaking, a product (a GEMS product) covered by a GEMS determination can only be supplied or offered for supply, or used for a commercial purpose, if:

(b) the product complies with the determination; and

Together with the Energy Conservation (Regulated Goods and Registered Suppliers) Regulations, it regulates the Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS) and Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme (MELS). Document Title: Regulations of the General Law on Climate Change regarding the National Emissions Registry (Reglamento de la Ley General de Cambio Climático en materia del Registro Nacional de Emisiones)
Family Title: Regulations of the General Law on Climate Change regarding the National Emissions Registry (Reglamento de la Ley General de Cambio Climático en materia del Registro Nacional de Emisiones)
Family Summary: This federal regulation operationalises the General Law on Climate Change by establishing the framework for Mexico’s National Emissions Registry. It applies across Mexican territory and is administered by the federal executive. This regulation imposes mandatory annual reporting requirements on facilities from key sectors (energy, industry, transport, agriculture, waste, commerce, and services) that emit over 25,000 tonnes of CO₂ equivalent. Reporting covers both direct and indirect emissions. Facilities must also submit an independently verified emissions report every three years, and SEMARNAT retains authority to request clarifications and corrections. The regulation also enables the voluntary registration of emission mitigation projects.To support technical implementation, the regulation mandates the adoption of specific agreements, notably one concerning the classification of GHG and compounds and their Global Warming Potential, in line with international standards and the IPCC’s Fifth Assessment Report. This regulatory instrument is central to Mexico’s climate governance, strengthening transparency and standardisation in emissions accounting across sectors.

Document Title: NDC Implementation Plan of Nepal, 2023
Family Title: NDC Implementation Plan of Nepal, 2023
Family Summary:
This Plan lays out a detailed roadmap for achieving the country’s emission reduction targets, aligning with its broader climate goals. It focuses on both mitigation and adaptation measures. For mitigation, the plan prioritises the expansion of renewable energy sources, particularly hydropower, solar, and wind power, as well as improving energy efficiency in various sectors. To adapt to climate change, the plan emphasises building climate resilience in agriculture, water resources, and infrastructure. Additionally, it prioritises disaster risk reduction, early warning systems, and community-based adaptation measures. The implementation plan aims to mobilise domestic and international resources, strengthen institutional capacity, and promote public awareness to ensure its successful execution.

The Plan highlights the importance of policy support and financial incentives to accelerate the shift towards low-emission technologies. This includes access to climate finance, government subsidies for cleaner technologies, and public-private partnerships to drive innovation. It also sets out a framework for capacity building, aiming to enhance the technical skills and knowledge of industry stakeholders and strengthen the regulatory environment to enforce compliance with emission reduction targets.

Document Title: Update of the National Climate Change Strategy Vision 10-20-40 (Actualización de la Estrategia Nacional de Cambio Climático Visión 10‒20‒40)
Family Title: Update of the National Climate Change Strategy. Vision 10-20-40 (Actualización de la Estrategia Nacional de Cambio Climático. Vision 10-20-40)
Family Summary: Mexico’s Updated National Climate Change Strategy sets out a long-term vision for achieving climate resilience and carbon neutrality by mid-century, grounded in principles of environmental justice, inclusion, and intergenerational equity. The strategy considers centring the protection and restoration of ecosystems and prioritising the needs of socially and climatically vulnerable groups, including Indigenous and Afro-Mexican communities, women, youth, and persons with disabilities. It builds on Mexico’s legal commitments under the General Climate Change Law and the Paris Agreement, positioning climate action as integral to sustainable development and human rights. With a humanist and territorial approach, the updated strategy positions climate action as a vehicle for structural economic transformation, equity, and collective well-being.The strategy is structured around three interdependent components: mitigation, adaptation, and cross-cutting climate policy. It establishes progressive milestones at 10-, 20-, and 40-year horizons (2030, 2040, and 2060), aligning with Mexico’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The mitigation component seeks sector-wide emission reductions through a just transition to a low-carbon economy. The adaptation component focuses on enhancing the resilience of communities, ecosystems, and infrastructure. The transversal policy component strengthens governance, finance, technology transfer, and public participation. It was developed through a participatory process involving government, civil society, and academia.

Document Title: National Development Plan 2025-2030 (Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2025-2030)
Family Title: National Development Plan 2025-2030 (Plan Nacional de Desarrollo -PND- 2025-2030)
Family Summary: The National Development Plan PND 2025–2030 (Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2025-2030) outlines the strategic framework for Mexico’s federal policy planning, in accordance with Article 26 of the Constitution, which mandates that the state must guide national development through a democratic and deliberative planning system. The Plan functions as a mandatory reference point for all sectoral, institutional, regional, and special programmes of the Federal Public Administration, requiring alignment in both programming and budgetary processes. In line with the Ley de Planeación, the PND includes a diagnostic overview of national priorities, general policy axes, implementation strategies, performance indicators, and a long-term vision.The 2025–2030 Plan introduces four general policy axes: governance with justice and citizen participation; development with well-being and humanism; moral economy and dignified work; and, sustainable development. The PND 2025-2030 additionally includes transversal priorities such as gender equality, public innovation, and the rights of Indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples. Environmental and climate-related goals are woven into various policy strands, including commitments to strengthen state control over the energy sector, promote renewable energy, expand access to solar panels. Climate change is also indirectly included in the goals related to securing the right to water through irrigation modernisation and water recycling, and the advance of environmental protection through circular economy initiatives, reforestation, and air quality improvement in major urban areas.

Document Title: Regulations of the National Climate Change System (Reglamento del Sistema Nacional de Cambio Climático)
Family Title: Regulations of the National Climate Change System (Reglamento del Sistema Nacional de Cambio Climático)
Family Summary: This regulation set out the organisation, functioning, and coordination principles of Mexico’s National Climate Change System (Sistema Nacional de Cambio Climático, SNCC). The SNCC comprises federal and subnational authorities (e.g. the Intersecretarial Commission, Climate Change Council, National Institute for Ecology and Climate Change), state and municipal governments, and representatives of Congress. It is designed as a permanent, multi-level governance mechanism coordinated by the federal executive, with a designated Technical Secretariat. Its primary objective is to ensure the integrated implementation of national climate policy across all levels of government, aligning mitigation, adaptation, and resilience efforts with the National Strategy and Special Climate Change Programme. It also provides a platform for cross-sectoral coordination, policy coherence, and the formulation of recommendations to strengthen climate action, including access to dedicated climate finance.

Document Title: Roadmap for Implementing the Kigali Amendment in Mexico (Hoja de Ruta para Implementar la Enmienda de Kigali en México)
Family Title: Roadmap for Implementing the Kigali Amendment in Mexico (Hoja de Ruta para Implementar la Enmienda de Kigali en México)
Family Summary: Mexico's Roadmap for implementing the Kigali Amendment represents a comprehensive policy framework for phasing down hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), which constitute 1.8% of the nation's greenhouse gas emissions. Published by the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources, the document establishes Mexico's strategy to meet its obligations under the 2016 Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol, requiring a consumption freeze by 2024 based on 2020-2022 baseline levels. The roadmap adopts a sectoral approach focusing particularly on the refrigeration and air conditioning sector, proposing short, medium, and long-term transitions to low global warming potential alternatives whilst simultaneously promoting energy efficiency measures.The policy architecture rests on four pillars: regulation (including import/export licensing systems), strategic planning, implementation, and reporting/verification mechanisms. The roadmap explicitly aligns HFC reduction efforts with Mexico's broader climate commitments, positioning the phase-down as a contribution to its Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement. By integrating considerations of commercial availability, technical viability, and energy efficiency potential, the policy seeks to transform HFC reduction into a platform for sustainable development co-benefits, thereby supporting both climate mitigation objectives and the UN's 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

Document Title: Internal Regulations of the Intersecretarial Commission on Climate Change (CICC) [Reglamento Interno de la Comisión Intersecretarial de Cambio Climático (CICC)]
Family Title: Internal Regulations of the Intersecretarial Commission on Climate Change (Reglamento Interno de la Comisión Intersecretarial de Cambio Climático)
Family Summary: This regulation establishes the organisation, structure, and operational functions of Mexico’s Inter-Ministerial Commission on Climate Change (CIcc). The Inter-Ministerial Commission on Climate Change is tasked with coordinating federal climate action across ministries and public agencies. It plays a central role in formulating and implementing national mitigation and adaptation policies, ensuring their integration into sectoral plans and programmes.Among its key responsibilities are: promoting inter-agency coordination on climate matters; developing transversal and integrated policy criteria for federal institutions; approving the National Climate Change Strategy proposed by the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources; participating in the design and implementation of the Special Climate Change Programme; supporting research, innovation, and technology transfer projects; and proposing regulatory frameworks for market-based instruments. The Inter-Ministerial Commission on Climate Change thus serves as a strategic governance body for aligning Mexico’s climate policy.

Document Title: Protected Areas Act 2011

One of the obejctives of the national protected areas sytem is to assist in combating climate change by ensuring that Guyana's existing forests are maintained and protected from degradation and their ecosystem functions are safeguarded; promoting the restoration and expansion of Guyana's natural forest cover; protecting marine ecosystems; and protecting freshwater ecosystems and important watersheds.

The specfic objectives of the policy include: a) to enhance climate change adaptation capacity b) to build resilience in at risk ecosystems c) to promote a green economy through low carbon development d) to mobilize nation and international climate finance in a just manner e) to conduct research and development and develop a climate information service f) to mainstream climate change into policies, plans and programs at all levels and sectors g) to mainstream gender equality and soical inclusion into climate change mitigation and adaptation programs The policy provides a number of sector specific and inter-sectoral strategies, including strategies on the development of necessary laws, multi-level governance, and capacity building activities.

Document Title: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (2014-2020)

Document Title: General Law on Mobility and Road Safety (Ley General de Movilidad y Seguridad Vial)
Family Title: General Law on Mobility and Road Safety (Ley General de Movilidad y Seguridad Vial)
Family Summary: The General Law on Mobility and Road Safety establishes a comprehensive legal framework to guarantee the constitutional right to mobility across Mexico. It aims to ensure safe, accessible, efficient, sustainable, and inclusive transport systems, considering vulnerable groups. The law sets out principles and responsibilities for federal, state, and municipal authorities, mandating coordinated policy-making through the National Mobility and Road Safety System. It promotes a hierarchy of mobility that prioritises pedestrians, non-motorised transport, and low-emission modes, while integrating mobility planning with urban development, public health, environmental protection, and climate resilience.Sustainability and climate considerations are included to the law's objectives. Authorities are required to reduce the environmental and social impacts of transport by encouraging cleaner technologies, reducing dependence on fossil fuels, and promoting resilient infrastructure. The law explicitly links transport policy with climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies, and mandates demand management measures to discourage the use of polluting and inefficient modes of transport. In doing so, it contributes to broader efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and to ensure intergenerational equity in access to mobility and environmental quality.

Document Title: National Urban Policy
Family Title: Jordan National Urban Policy
Family Summary: Jordan's National Urban Policy (2023) recognises climate change as a key threat to the wellbeing and economic function of the country, and aims to promote both adaptation and mitigation measures for these threats in urban environments. It suggests a range of measures from institutional capacity building to more physical interventions in the urban environment. The policy seeks to: improve water conservation; improve geospatial databases for natural assets; develop enhanced standards for air quality; plan land use around public transportation; provide equitable access to green jobs.

Document Title: National Environment Policy 2019
Family Title: National Environment Policy 2019
Family Summary: This Policy's objectives are sustainable development, improved governance, resource conservation, and climate change mitigation. Strategies focus on environmental integration into development plans, multi-sectoral collaboration, and strengthened monitoring. The policy emphasises public participation, equitable resource access and cooperative efforts between the public and commercial sectors. It also covers research and capacity development.

Document Title: Law 25080 - Investment Law for Cultivated Forests (Consolidated text)

Family Summary: This law establishes a regime for the promotion of investments made in new forestry enterprises and in the extensions of existing forests. It aims at enabling entities to benefit from the installation of new forestry-industrial projects and the extensions of existing ones, as long as the wood supply is increased through the implantation of new forests. These benefits must be related to the investments actually made in the implementation.The activities included in the regime instituted by this law are: the implementation of forests, their maintenance, management, irrigation, protection and harvesting, including research and development activities, as well as those of industrialisation of wood, when all of them are part of an integrated forest or forestry-industrial enterprise (art. 3).The ForestAR Strategy 2030 of 2018 is based on this law.

Document Title: National Development Program 2025-2029 (Programa Nacional de Desarrollo 2025-2030)
Family Title: National Development Program (PND) 2025-2030 [Programa Nacional de Desarrollo (PND) 2025-2030]
Family Summary: The 2025–2030 Mexican National Development Plan (PND) articulates the government’s vision for consolidating the country’s ongoing transformation through a model rooted in Mexican Humanism (Humanismo Mexicano). This framework prioritises social justice, democratic governance, and environmental sustainability, seeking to decouple political power from private and foreign interests while restoring the State’s leadership in economic, energy, and social policy. The Plan reaffirms commitments to universal social rights, the expansion of public infrastructure, and a transition from economic growth to holistic development that centres human wellbeing, dignity, and environmental stewardship.The PND integrates sustainability and climate resilience across policy areas. Key strategies include the promotion of clean energy through public investment and energy sovereignty via strengthened state enterprises (PEMEX and CFE); the sustainable use of natural resources; and robust adaptation and mitigation actions in response to climate change. Emphasis is placed on climate justice, rural equity, and the protection of vulnerable populations. The Plan also outlines the expansion of renewable energy capacity, the right to water, and the transition to agroecological practices.

Document Title: Local Governance Act, 2017

In the local development plan that it is responsible for developing, it should consider environment- and child-friendly governance, climate change adaptation, disaster management and gender and social inclusion.

Document Title: Alignment of Mexico's National Biodiversity Strategy and 2030 Action Plan with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework Targets (Alineación de la Estrategia Nacional sobre Biodiversidad de México y Plan de Acción 2030 con las Metas del Marco Mundial de Biodiversidad de Kunming-Montreal)

Family Summary: Mexico began aligning its National Biodiversity Strategy (ENBioMex) with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework through a national process led by CONABIO. As a result, the Alignment of Mexico's National Biodiversity Strategy (ENBioMex) and 2030 Action Plan with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) Targets recognises climate change as a critical driver of biodiversity loss, embedding it explicitly in Target 8, which calls for minimising climate and ocean acidification impacts on biodiversity through mitigation, adaptation, and disaster risk reduction. Other targets promote ecosystem-based approaches and nature-based solutions that bolster biodiversity’s role in climate resilience, reinforcing the interdependence of global climate and biodiversity goals.

Document Title: Mexico's National Biodiversity Strategy -ENBioMex- and Action Plan 2016-2030 (Estrategia Nacional sobre Biodiversidad de México -ENBioMex- y Plan de Acción 2016-2030)
Family Title: Mexico's National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan -ENBioMex- 2016-2030 (Estrategia Nacional sobre Biodiversidad de México y Plan de Acción -ENBioMex- 2016-2030)
Family Summary: This strategy sets out a comprehensive framework for the conservation, sustainable use, and equitable sharing of the benefits of biodiversity. Recognising the ecological and cultural wealth of Mexico, the strategy responds to ongoing degradation of ecosystems and biodiversity caused by unsustainable economic models and demographic pressures. ENBioMex is structured around six strategic pillars, including conservation and restoration, sustainable use, and environmental governance. The strategy also aligns with international commitments under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It was developed through a participatory process and positions biodiversity as a foundational element of national well-being, with a long-term vision of maintaining ecosystem functionality and ensuring access to environmental services by 2030.ENBioMex integrates climate change as a cross-cutting pressure on biodiversity and ecosystems, proposing targeted actions for both mitigation and adaptation. It promotes ecosystem-based adaptation, ecohydrological connectivity, and the conservation of genetic resources as key responses to hydrometeorological extremes, sea-level rise, and changing temperatures. It also highlights the need to align renewable energy development with biodiversity protection, advocating risk assessments and the creation of safeguards to minimise ecological harm. The strategy emphasises economic valuation of ecosystem services, inclusive benefit-sharing, and gender-sensitive compensation mechanisms, particularly within REDD+ and payments for ecosystem services (PES) frameworks. Finally, it calls for integrated marine monitoring, restoration of vulnerable habitats such as coral reefs and wetlands, and strengthened intersectoral governance to address biodiversity loss in the context of accelerating climate impacts.

Document Title: National Agroforestry Policy 2019
Family Title: National Agroforestry Policy 2019
Family Summary:
This policy mainstreams agroforestry, which is an integrated system of practising agriculture, livestock farming and forest activities on the same unit of land. One of the objectives is to conserve the environment and biological diversity by reducing pressure on the forest, to maintain quality and to develop a climate-resilient ecosystem.

It aims to ensure the availability of quality planting material to promote agroforestry and the establishment of value chains and market linkages through the connection, establishment, and promotion of agroforestry-based industries. It also aims to resolve challenges of a lack of credit facilities, considering trees as collateral, and an insurance system for agroforestry plantations.

Document Title: General Law on Ecological Balance and Environmental Protection (LGEEPA) [Ley General de Equilibrio Ecológico y Protección al Ambiente (LGEEPA)]
Family Title: General Law on Ecological Balance and Environmental Protection (LGEEPA) [Ley General de Equilibrio Ecológico y Protección al Ambiente (LGEEPA)]
Family Summary: The General Law on Ecological Balance and Environmental Protection is rooted in constitutional mandates, and it provides the normative basis for preserving biodiversity, restoring ecosystems, regulating pollution, and promoting sustainable development across national territory and jurisdictional waters. It enshrines the right to a healthy environment, establishes mechanisms for citizen participation, and defines the distribution of environmental competences among the federal, state, and municipal governments under a framework of concurrent authority. The law recognises environmental preservation, biodiversity protection, and ecological restoration as matters of public utility, and mandates environmental planning instruments such as ecological land-use planning and the designation of protected natural areas.This act incorporates climate action into the core of environmental governance. It assigns responsibilities across all levels of government (federal, state, and municipal) to develop and implement mitigation and adaptation measures in response to climate change (Arts. 5, 7, and 8). The law also codifies the polluter-pays principle and supports incentives for actors engaging in sustainable resource use and climate-resilient practices (Art. 15.IV). Among others, it obliges authorities to prevent human settlement in areas at high risk from climate-related hazards (Art. 15.X), underscoring a preventive and precautionary approach.

Document Title: Special Tax Law on Production and Services (Ley del Impuesto Especial sobre Producción y Servicios)
Family Title: Special Tax Law on Production and Services (Ley del Impuesto Especial sobre Producción y Servicios)
Family Summary: The Special Tax Law on Production and Services establishes a tax regime for various goods and services, including a specific section on fossil fuels. Under Article 2(H), a set of fixed quotas is applied to the sale and importation of fossil fuels such as gasoline, diesel, coal, and petroleum coke. These rates are updated annually and calculated proportionally for fuel mixtures. Additionally, Article 2-D outlines a detailed methodology for calculating equivalent carbon-based taxes for other fossil fuels not explicitly listed, based on their energy content and carbon emission factors. This law aims to work as a fiscal instrument aligned with climate policy objectives.

Document Title: Sustainable Rural Development Law (Ley de Desarrollo Rural Sustentable)
Family Title: Sustainable Rural Development Law (LDRS) [Ley de Desarrollo Rural Sustentable (LDRS)]
Family Summary: The Law on Sustainable Rural Development establishes the legal framework through which the Mexican State must promote socially equitable, economically viable, and environmentally sound development in rural areas. It mandates the State’s role in fostering a sustained transformation of the rural sector by improving livelihoods, enhancing productivity, and promoting diversification while safeguarding natural resources. Special attention is directed toward economically and socially marginalised regions, with programmes prioritising small producers and recognising cultural and ecological heterogeneity.Climate resilience is considered into the law’s provisions. It requires the implementation of risk-management strategies such as insurance systems, climate contingency funds, and productive reconversion plans in high-risk regions, as well as the development of a National Information System to support evidence-based policy. The law also emphasises climate change adaptation and mitigation through preferential financing, infrastructure development, and environmental stewardship, aiming to strengthen rural populations' capacity to respond to and recover from climatic and economic shocks.

Document Title: National Energy Program 2014-2027 (Programa Nacional de Energía 2014-2027)
Family Title: National Energy Program (ENE) 2014-2028 [Programa Nacional de Energía (ENE) 2014-2028]
Family Summary: The National Energy Program (ENE) 2014-2028 was conceived as the strategic vehicle for operationalising Mexico’s 2013 Constitutional Energy Reform, aiming to modernise the energy sector through liberalisation, technological innovation, and regional industrial development. The ENE 2014-2028 foregrounds the social and environmental dimensions of energy governance, explicitly linking energy access to human development and recognising the urgent need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and transition towards a low-carbon economy. Through a combination of legal, institutional, and financial mechanisms (including the promotion of renewable energy, energy efficiency, and regional climate strategies) the ENE 2014-2028 frames the energy transition as an environmental imperative, a pathway to social inclusion, decentralised economic growth, and long-term sustainability. The strategy declares to mark a pivotal shift in Mexican energy policy, embedding social and environmental considerations into the architecture of national energy development planning.

Document Title: Federal Budget and Fiscal Responsibility Law (Ley Federal de Presupuesto y Responsabilidad Hacendaria)
Family Title: Federal Budget and Fiscal Responsibility Law (Ley Federal de Presupuesto y Responsabilidad Hacendaria)
Family Summary: The Federal Budget and Fiscal Responsibility Law is a piece of legislation governing the management of public finances in Mexico. It sets out the legal framework for programming, budgeting, approving, executing, controlling, and evaluating federal public income and expenditures, ensuring that public resources are managed with principles of legality, efficiency, transparency, and accountability. Among its key provisions, the law establishes guidelines for the distribution of funds, including allocations for energy transition and climate change initiatives. The law outlines the operation of the Mexican Petroleum Fund (Fondo Mexicano del Petróleo), which serves to manage revenues from oil and gas activities and directs part of these funds toward energy sustainability and climate change-related projects.In terms of climate change and energy transition, the law mandates that part of the resources from the Mexican Petroleum Fund be dedicated to research and innovation in renewable energy, energy efficiency, and clean technologies. Article 88 of the law specifies that a significant portion of these funds (65%) should support scientific and technological initiatives focused on renewable energy, energy efficiency, and clean technology, as well as energy diversification. Additionally, the law directs the Ministry of Energy and the National Council of Science and Technology to collaborate on projects that advance Mexico's energy transition in line with its international commitments to mitigate climate change. Through these provisions, the law seeks to align Mexico's fiscal management with its environmental and energy goals.

Document Title: Decree issuing the General Law on Humanities, Science, Technology and Innovation, and amending and adding various provisions of the Federal Law on Parastatal Entities and the Planning Law [Decreto por el que se expide la Ley General en Materia de Humanidades, Ciencias, Tecnologías e Innovación, y se reforman y adicionan diversas disposiciones de la Ley Federal de las Entidades Paraestatales y de la Ley de Planeación]
Family Title: General Law on Humanities, Sciences, Technologies and Innovation (LGHCTI) [Ley General en materia de Humanidades, Ciencias, Tecnologías e Innovación (LGHCTI)]
Family Summary: The General Law on Humanities, Sciences, Technologies and Innovation (LGHCTI) is a comprehensive federal statute that governs the production, use, and dissemination of scientific and technological knowledge in Mexico. It affirms the human right to science and mandates that research and innovation serve the public interest, including environmental sustainability, intergenerational justice, and the realisation of other fundamental rights. The law reorients national science and technology policy under state stewardship, setting the framework for federal, state, and municipal authorities to engage in coordinated actions. It introduces National Strategic Programmes (Programas Nacionales Estratégicos) as key instruments to address complex national challenges, ranging from public health to biodiversity, through cross-sectoral, participatory, and territorial approaches.In the climate change and the energy transition realm, the law embeds these issues as priorities in the national science and technology agenda. It requires the state to support research and innovation that contribute to mitigation, adaptation, and the shift towards low-emission energy systems. Article 11 identifies the transition from fossil fuels to sustainable energy as a guiding principle for public policy, while Articles 46–47 mandate strategic programmes focused on energy and climate, including the transition to renewable sources. Additionally, the law calls for close coordination between the National Science Council and the Ministry of Energy to promote clean technologies, energy diversification, and the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, particularly through projects financed by the Mexican Petroleum Fund.

Document Title: Mexico's National Policy for Seas and Coasts. Comprehensive management of the most dynamic regions of the country (Política Nacional de Mares y Costas de México. Gestión integral de las regiones más dinámicas del territorio nacional)
Family Title: National Policy on Seas and Coasts of Mexico (Política Nacional de Mares y Costas de México)
Family Summary: This policy, developed through the Interministerial Commission for the Sustainable Management of Seas and Coasts (CIMARES), provides a cross-sectoral framework for sustainable governance of Mexico’s marine and coastal regions. Anchored in the ecological, social, and economic significance of these territories, the policy aims to improve local livelihoods while conserving marine ecosystems and enhancing resilience. The document acknowledges the growing threats posed by climate change (especially sea-level rise, increased storm intensity, and coastal vulnerability) integrating these into its risk prevention and territorial planning strategies. Specific actions include promoting climate risk atlases at the municipal level, developing State Climate Change Programs in all 17 coastal states, and mainstreaming climate considerations into infrastructure planning, making the policy a vital instrument in Mexico’s broader climate adaptation agenda.

Document Title: National Mobility and Road Safety Strategy 2023-2042 (Estrategia Nacional de Movilidad y Seguridad Vial 2023-2042)
Family Title: National Mobility and Road Safety Strategy 2023-2042 (Estrategia Nacional de Movilidad y Seguridad Vial 2023-2042)
Family Summary: The National Strategy for Mobility and Road Safety 2023–2042 (ENAMOV) provides Mexico’s long-term policy framework to guarantee the constitutional right to mobility through safe, inclusive, sustainable, and equitable transport systems. Centred on social and spatial justice, the strategy prioritises vulnerable groups and aims to reduce inequality in access to mobility by integrating national, regional, and local planning. Document Title: Energy Conservation Act (Chapter 92C)
Family Title: Energy Conservation Act (Chapter 92C)
Family Summary: This Act mandates energy efficiency requirements and energy management practices, to promote energy conservation, improve energy efficiency and reduce the environmental impact of energy use. Under the Act, large energy users in the industry and transport sectors that consume at least the equivalent of 54 tera-joules of energy per calendar year in at least two out of the three preceding calendar years must appoint at least one energy manager to manage energy use. These companies or transport facility operators are also required to monitor and report energy use and greenhouse gas emissions, and submit energy efficiency improvement plans on an annual basis to the relevant agencies. The Act also consolidates the legislation for mandatory energy labelling and minimum energy performance standards for household appliances, as well as fuel economy labelling of motor vehicles, previously stipulated under the Environmental Protection and Management Act (Cap 94A). The Act is jointly administered by the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources and Ministry of Transport. The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources oversees the measures for the industry and households sectors while the Minister for Transport oversees the measures for the transport sector.

Family Summary: The purpose of this law is to strengthen education on environmental sustainability, climate change, and disaster risk management for children, adolescents, youth, and adults throughout their educational journey.
