Document Title: CONPES 4021 - National Policy for the Control of Deforestation and Sustainable Management of Forests (POLÍTICA NACIONAL PARA EL CONTROL DE LA DEFORESTACIÓN Y LA GESTIÓN SOSTENIBLE DE LOS BOSQUES)
Family Title: CONPES 4021 - National Policy for the Control of Deforestation and Sustainable Management of Forests
Family Summary:
This CONPES document provides policy guidelines to counteract deforestation and promote sustainable forest management. Through the analysis of the causes that affect the processes of land use change and loss of natural forest, it identifies the actions that the national government should develop in coordination with the sectors, communities and other actors so that, based on the recognition of the particularities and needs of the territories, this problem can be controlled and at the same time the conservation and sustainable management of forests can be promoted.

In particular, four strategic lines are established to lead the country to achieve the goal of zero net deforestation by 2030: (i) integrate strategies for the sustainable use of forests to improve the quality of life and the local economy of communities; (ii) articulate cross-sectoral actions that allow the national government to work together to manage forests and address territorial conflicts; (iii) promote prevention strategies and territorial control to reduce illegal dynamics, and (iv) strengthen the management of information for decision-making.

This policy focuses on actions foreseen under the Integrated Strategy for the Control of Deforestation and Forest Management (EICD).

The first pillar of the national policy is the "Green Transition," which includes investments in sustainable transportation, building energy efficiency, and innovative technologies to minimize GHG emissions, with an emphasis on emission reductions, negative emissions, and adaption measures.

To boost tax collection, the Fund also levies environmental taxes. Reduced taxes on employment and enterprise are meant to be exchanged for lower environmental levies.

Sweden also contains alternative measures to implement the Green Transition in its 2021 budget, with policies meant to support its development until 2030 and 2045. The EU RRF plan includes measures to facilitate the Green Transition. All steps in the recovery plan have been examined to ensure that none of them do major damage to the environment.

Energy-related initiatives in Sweden's recovery and resilience strategy:

- Transition of industrial sector (SEK 2.9 billion)

- Climate change (SEK 5.35 billion)

- Energy efficiency of apartment buildings (SEK 4.05 billion)

- Railway investment (SEK 1.50 billion)

Around 34 billion SEK are available for Sweden's entire financial contribution within RRF. With the aid of substantial claimte-smart technology, Sweden hopes to eliminate all GHG emissions by 2045.

Document Title: Decree Law 34/2020 - Tax deduction for energy efficiency improvements (Superbonus 110)
Family Title: Decree Law 34/2020 - Tax deduction for energy efficiency improvements (Superbonus 110)
Family Summary:
The superbonus 110% is a tax deduction of 110% for costs related to energy efficiency improvements in buildings. Amongst the so-called driving interventions are thermal insulation (so-called thermal coat); replacement of boilers and air conditioning systems. Once at least one of these 'driving' interventions has been carried out, also 'towed' interventions can enter in the scheme such as the installation of solar PV and electric cars columns of charging. The interventions must involve a minimum improvement of at least two energy classes of the building.

The goal is to encourage energy efficiency as well as the installation of photovoltaic systems or infrastructures for charging electric vehicles in buildings.

Document Title: CIPE Resolution 17 March 2020, n. 7/2020
Family Title: Resolution CIPE n. 7/2020 - Allocation of additional financial resources for energy income
Family Summary: Capital grants of 200 million euros to be used by 2025 in favour of the FSC 2014-2020 plan aiming to cover the construction and and installation costs of PV for domestic use, promoting, therefore, the spread of renewable energy primary sources for families and individuals, mainly the low income ones.

Document Title: "MaPrimeRénov" Programme
Family Title: "MaPrimeRénov" Programme
Family Summary:
The Decree No. 2020‑26 of 14 January 2020 established the “prime à la transition énergétique”, now known as "MaPrimeRénov" Programme. This decree set up the rules governing eligibility, eligible works, and the application process for the programme.

This "MaPrimeRénov" Programme aims at helping low-income individuals and households to renovate their housings in order to make them more energy efficient and better isolated. The subsidy has an upper limit of 20,000€ per flat/house on a 5 year period. People who do not qualify for this scheme can apply for the Energy Transition Tax Credit (CITE).

Document Title: Decree Law 162/19 amended by Law 8/2020 (Consolidated text)
Family Title: Decree Law 162/19, amended by Law 8/2020 - Self-consumption of renewable energy (Art. 42-bis)
Family Summary:
Embedded in the EU Directive 2018/2001 about the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources , the Article 42bis of Decree-Law 162/19 outlines the methods and conditions to enable self-consumption of renewable sources. It allows individuals, collectives (located in the same building or condominium) or small energy communities who produce electricity from natural sources and not superior than 200 KWh, have access to the distribution network to trade energy. These individuals and/or collectives are rewarded with fiscal detractions due to the energy generated.

The core rule is that the production and exchange of energy is not the main activity of the actors. The ultimate goal of this legal dispositive is to provide environmental, economic and social benefits rather than financial profits.

Document Title: National Transport Policy 2019-2030
Family Title: National Transport Policy 2019-2030
Family Summary:
The policy aims to develop a sustainable transport sector that accelerates economic growth while lowering carbon emissions. It promotes the adoption of energy-efficient and electric vehicles, as well as the necessary infrastructure, such as charging stations. The policy emphasises the development of public transportation systems as a primary feature in urban areas to reduce reliance on private, fossil-fuel-powered vehicles. Additionally, it encourages the use of cleaner fuels and electric vehicles. The policy also includes education and public engagement initiatives designed to shift user behaviour toward more sustainable transport modes and practices.

The policy seeks to achieve the following objectives:

1. Create a supportive ecosystem for the transport industry to enhance productivity and competitiveness.

2. Facilitate the seamless movement of goods to boost trading activities and improve the ease of doing business.

3. Provide mobility solutions that meet the expectations of the people and promote inclusivity.

4. Increase the modal share for public transport.

5. Deliver an intelligent, safe, and secure transport system.

6. Ensure the efficient and sustainable use of resources while minimising environmental pollution.

Document Title: 20-Year Agricultura Development Plan (2017-2036)
Family Title: The Twenty-Year Agriculture and Cooperative Strategy (2017-2036) and the Agricultural Development Plan
Family Summary:
This policy sets out a framework for the development of the agricultural sector. It includes 5 key strategies:

1. Strenghtening the Farmers and Farmer Institutions

2. Increasing the productivity and quality standards of agricultural commodities

3. Increasing competitiveness in the agricultural sector through technology and innovations

4. Balanced and sustainable management of agricultural resources and the environment5. Development of public administration system

5. The strategy recognises and addresses the urgent need to promote the adjustability of the agriculture sector, especially in research and development, transfer of knowledge, and the application of adaptation technology to reduce the risk or loss of production due to climate change.The Agricultural Development Plan outlines as objectives:

  1. To establish pride in the agriculture profession for being self-sustained, through continuous transfer of technology, farmers’ groupings, strong linkages with external networks, and narrowing income gap.
  2. To promote among the farmers and their institutions the upgrade of their productivity, efficiency, and standards, as well as value added agriculture in response to market demands.
  3. To build up the competitiveness of agricultural products as well as develop applicable researches, technology and innovations.
  4. To perform efficient management of agricultural resources toward their adjustability and immunity in dealing with the climate change.

Document Title: Climate-Resilient Green Economy (CRGE) Strategy (2011)
Family Title: Climate-Resilient Green Economy (CRGE) Strategy
Family Summary:
• The Climate-Resilient Green Economy (CRGE)'s vision is achieving middle-income status by 2025 in a climate-resilient green economy, outlining four pillars: Agriculture: Improving crop and livestock production practices for higher food security and farmer income while reducing emissions
  • Deforestation: Reducing emissions by protecting and re-establishing forests for their economic and ecosystem services including as carbon stocks. The National Greening Action Program derives from this goal.
  • Power: expanding electricity generation from renewable energy for domestic and regional markets
  • Transport, industrial sectors and buildings: Leapfrogging to modern and energy efficient technologies.

The strategy targets climate change mitigation and adaptation. It sets a target to limit 2030 emissions to 150 Mt CO2e (level of 2010 emissions), approximately 250 Mt CO2e less than in the business as usual scenario. It also establishes a target to increase generating capacity by 25,000MW by 2030 - hydro 22,000MW, geothermal 1,000MW and wind 2,000MW. There are programmes to replace wood fuel for domestic use with less polluting fuels, such as biogas. There are plans to distribute 9m stoves by 2015 and 34m by 2030. The initiative establishes a national financial mechanism called the 'CRGE Facility' to mobilise, access, sequence and blend domestic and international, public and private sources of finance to support the institutional building and implementation of the strategy. The CRGE initially relies on existing institutions, notably the Environmental Protection Authority (which in 2013 was replaced by the Ministry of Environment and Forest), the Ethiopian Development Research Institute, six ministries, and several government agencies. Subsequent phases will strengthen institutions to implement the strategy.

Document Title: Republic Act No. 11285 (Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act)
Family Title: Republic Act No. 11285 (Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act)
Family Summary: This Act, approved on 12 April 2019, sets out plans to increase energy efficiency and reduce consumption within the Philippines. The law is to be implemented by the Department of Energy and the legislation provides for various new mandates of the department, as well as imposing responsibilities on other government bodies. An inter-agency committee on Energy efficiency is created. The act also provides for the creation of new performance and labelling standards, to be developed by the Department of Energy. The Act also contains provisions regarding financial and other incentives and encourages the provisions of concessionary finance for energy efficiency measures.

Document Title: Law No. 27.487 amending Law 25.080 on Investment in Forestry
Family Title: Law 25.080 for investments in cultivated forests, amended by Law 27.487
Family Summary: This law establishes a regime for the promotion of investments made in new forestry enterprises and in the extensions of existing forests. It aims at enabling entities to benefit from the installation of new forestry-industrial projects and the extensions of existing ones, as long as the wood supply is increased through the implantation of new forests. These benefits must be related to the investments actually made in the implementation.The activities included in the regime instituted by this law are: the implementation of forests, their maintenance, management, irrigation, protection and harvesting, including research and development activities, as well as those of industrialisation of wood, when all of them are part of an integrated forest or forestry-industrial enterprise (art. 3).The ForestAR Strategy 2030 of 2018 is based on this law.

Document Title: Order of May 6, 2017 setting the conditions for additional remuneration for electricity produced by electricity production facilities using mechanical wind energy, with a maximum of 6 wind turbines
Family Title: Order of May 6, 2017 - Establishing the Conditions of the Compensation Mechanism for Electricity Generated from Wind Energy with a Maximum of 6 wind turbines
Family Summary:
Order of May 6, 2017 taken pursuant to Article D. 314-23 of the Energy Code setting out conditions for benefiting from the additional remuneration for electricity production installations using mechanical wind energy with a maximum of 6 wind turbines.Before July 2022, producers may benefit from a supplementary remuneration contract, under the conditions provided for in this decree, for the installations mentioned in 7° of article D. 314-23, within the limit of 6 wind turbines per installation and 3MW of nominal power for each wind turbine at most.

In 2022 it was amended by other orders ( Order April 27, 2022 and Order December 29, 2022), which brought new specific conditions regarding the eligibility to the compensation mechanism and the amount of the allocated premium.

Overall, the order aims at promoting wind energy through a market premium. The premium tariff is allocated over a limited period of time, 20 years in the case of wind energy.

Document Title: Law 21.118 on the promotion of residential-scale power generation
Family Title: Law 21.118 on the promotion of residential-scale power generation
Family Summary: This law encourages the development of residential generators and makes its provisions applicable to all electrical systems in the country. Its objective is to foster the development of residential-scale distributed generation systems by encouraging the development of residential generator . Users subject to price fixing who use non-conventional renewable energy generation equipment or efficient cogeneration facilities for their own consumption, whether individually or collectively, will have the right to inject energy into the distribution grid, which may be deducted from the electricity supply charges on the corresponding bill. Through this law, the allowed nominal capacity increases up to 300MW.

Document Title: Public Policy for the Promotion of Distributed Generation
Family Title: Public Policy for the Promotion of Distributed Generation
Family Summary: Distributed Generation is the generation of electrical energy carried out by a generating plant whose capacity must be less than 500 kW and it must be interconnected to a distribution circuit containing a high concentration of Load Centers. It consists of a set of short, medium and long-term measures.

Family Title: Contingency Plan for the 2006/7 season

This Plan describes the main activities to be carried out to reduce the country's vulnerability to natural disasters and defines the preparedness system for responding to emergencies. Based on this Plan, the Contingency Plan is anticipated and guided each year to respond to eventualities of extreme events that exceed prevention measures.

Document Title: Evaluation of the cost the impact of climate change and adaptation in France (EVALUATION DU COÛT DES IMPACTS DU CHANGEMENT CLIMATIQUE ET DE L’ADAPTATION EN FRANCE Rapport de la deuxième phase)

Document Title: Decree 919 - National System for Disaster Prevention and Response ( Decreto 919 - Sistema Nacional para la Prevención y Atención de Desastres)
Family Title: Decree 919 - National System for Disaster Prevention and Response
Family Summary:
A decree published in May 1989 names the public and private entities that make plans and constitute the national disaster prevention system. The decree refers to regional and local committees for disaster prevention and attention and mentions decentralized entities at the national level insofar as their competence and functions are related to the activities of prevention and attention to catastrophe.

Article IV deals with the participation of public and private entities and organizations in the elaboration and execution of the prevention plan. Article VI requires that all territorial entities consider in their development plans the component of disaster prevention and, especially, provisions related to urban planning, risk zones and human settlements, as well as the appropriations that are indispensable for this purpose in the annual budgets.

Document Title: National Risk Management Plan 2010-2015 (Plan Nacional de Gestión del Riesgo 2010-2015)
Family Title: National Risk Management Plan 2010-2015
Family Summary:
The Executive Secretariat of the National System for the Prevention, Mitigation and Response to Disasters (SE-SINAPRED) presents the National Risk Management Plan 2010-2015 (PNGR), a national, regional, municipal and local planning instrument developed from an integrative, multisectoral and inter-institutional perspective by government entities, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), local organizations and with the active participation of the population in general.

The PNGR 2010-2015 is the short--, medium-- and long-term strategy to address the challenges of disaster risk reduction in Nicaragua. It is the nation's challenge to advance policies, strategies and mechanisms to incorporate comprehensive risk management in development planning and poverty reduction at all levels.

The PNGR 2010-2015 is structured in five chapters. The first chapter presents the background on the relevant policies, strategies, and plans that have been implemented from a multisectoral and inter-institutional effort aimed at risk reduction, and the framework of public policies associated with risk management is described. In the second, the conceptual framework that supports the plan is presented; The third describes the state of the risk in Nicaragua; and finally, the fourth chapter sets out the development, strategic and operational objectives, and the actions to be undertaken between 2010 and 2015.

Document Title: Master plan for Spanish cooperation 2013-2016 (Plan director de la cooperacion Española 2013-2016)
Family Title: Master plan for Spanish cooperation 2013-2016
Family Summary:
Disaster risk reduction and the strengthening of resilience mechanisms will be axed, not only of the humanitarian work of Spanish Cooperation but of all actions, especially those carried out in contexts of fragility or scenarios of extraordinary vulnerability to disasters. The necessary working or coordination groups of experts in the field will be proposed to reinforce the resilience approach.

Spanish Cooperation is committed to a prevention policy in all fields in the face of external or structural shocks, especially the fight against hunger, food and nutritional and health security. It is, therefore, about coordinating and guiding humanitarian action and development strategies towards a standard risk analysis and planning to address the different forms of vulnerability, emphasizing the need to incorporate elements of rights protection into resilience components. In this sense, disaster risk reduction management (DRR) is one of the prevention policies that will continue to be implemented by the Spanish Cooperation.

Document Title: Decree no. 275-13 - National plan for comprehensive disaster risk management in the Dominican Republic (Decreto 275-13: Plan nacional de gestión integral del riesgo de desastres en la República Dominicana)
Family Title: Decree no. 275-13 - National plan for comprehensive disaster risk management in the Dominican Republic
Family Summary:
The President of the Dominican Republic, Danilo Medina, approved through Decree No. 275-13 the “National Plan for Comprehensive Disaster Risk Management in the Dominican Republic”, whose purpose is to define the policy guidelines and fundamental principles that must be developed institutions of the public and private sectors, as well as social organizations, for the execution of programs and actions aimed at reducing the risk of disasters, guaranteeing better safety conditions for the population and protecting their economic, social, environmental and cultural.

The Plan prepared by the National Emergency Commission and the Dominican Civil Defense has its origin in Law 147-02 and the National Risk Management Plan and the National Plan for the Reduction of Seismic Risk; instruments that define the strategic objectives, programs and subprograms through which institutional activities for risk prevention and mitigation, preparations for response and rehabilitation and reconstruction in cases of disasters are guided.

It should be noted that the document was prepared thanks to the specialized heritage of the National Technical Committee for Risk Prevention and Mitigation and makes explicit reference - as one of the background information that makes up the contents of the Plan - to the results of the interagency evaluation on vulnerability to natural threats. , led by the Regional Office for the Americas of the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNISDR) in 2010.

The writing of the “National Plan for Comprehensive Disaster Risk Management in the Dominican Republic” required a team of consultants, who in turn relied on bibliographic references, interviews and participatory workshops, the latter two being key in the writing of the diagnosis above and the formulation of a document adapted to the Dominican institutional and social reality.

Document Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 008-2016-MINAM - Technical and Methodological Procedure for the preparation of the Specialised Study of Disaster Risk Assessment and Vulnerability to Climate Change for territorial planning ( Resolución Ministerial N° 008-2016-MINAM: Procedimiento Técnico y Metodológico para la elaboración del Estudio Especializado de Evaluación de Riesgos de Desastres y Vulnerabilidad al Cambio Climático para el ordenamiento territorial)
Family Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 008-2016-MINAM - Technical and Methodological Procedure for the preparation of the Specialised Study of Disaster Risk Assessment and Vulnerability to Climate Change for territorial planning
Family Summary: In order to effectively incorporate disaster risk management in land-use planning processes and contribute to decision-making for risk prevention and mitigation, the Ministry of Environment approved the Ministerial Resolution No. 008-2016-MINAM detailing the technical and methodological procedures surrounding the specialized study of Disaster Risk Assessment and Vulnerability to Climate Change for land-use planning. This includes identifying and characterizing of hazards, analyzing the conditions of vulnerability and establishing the levels of risk.

Document Title: National policy for disaster risk management (Política nacional para la gestión de riesgo de desastres)
Family Title: National policy for disaster risk management
Family Summary:
Chile is a country permanently exposed to threats of both natural and anthropogenic origin, unleashed by countless disasters of different kinds, so following global trends regarding the subject, comprehensive risk management of disasters has increasingly been prioritised at the national level.

In 2005, the State of Chile signed the Hyogo Framework for Action (MAH), by which countries commit to considerably reducing the losses caused by disasters, both in terms of human lives and social goods, economic and environmental. Subsequently, in October 2010, a United Nations mission evaluated the state of progress, establishing 75 recommendations to comply with the MAH, the first of which was the formulation of a National Policy for Disaster Risk Management.

In this way, a National Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction was established, led by ONEMI, whose first mission was formulating the policy above, which allows for the development of comprehensive disaster risk management in the country.

For more than a year, the members of the National Platform, divided into five sectoral tables – corresponding to the five priorities of the Hyogo Framework for Action – worked on formulating this document, which will contribute to progress in planning. Safe and sustainable development, effectively incorporating sectoral policies for territorial planning, poverty reduction, adaptation to climate change, culture of self-care, financial protection, capacity building, research and risk analysis and comprehensive care for vulnerable populations, among others.

Document Title: National strategic plan for disaster risk management 2015-2018 ( Plan estratégico nacional para la gestión del riesgo de desastres 2015-2018
Family Title: National strategic plan for disaster risk management 2015-2018
Family Summary:
This plan aims to become a guiding instrument whose objective is to promote disaster risk management in the country in a transversal and priority manner, to establish a baseline of concrete actions already in development, and to establish other feasible ones. Promote on the current national stage. This plan will facilitate the project of a long-term strategy by the Sendai Framework 2015-2030 and the renewed responsible institutional framework in disaster risk reduction, thus providing the necessary tools and resources to implement this and other management instruments in the country.

The National Strategic Plan for Disaster Risk Management is the instrument that defines strategic objectives, programs, actions, deadlines and responsible parties that allow the materialization of what is established in the National Policy for Disaster Risk Management in force in Chile.

Document Title: National action program to combat desertification (Plan d’action national pour la lutte contre la désertification (PAN/LCD))
Family Title: National action program to combat desertification
Family Summary:
This National Action Plan to Combat Desertification complies with the vision of the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (CLD).

This Action Plan is also in line with the final declaration of the "Rio+20" conference, which states that: "desertification, land degradation and drought are global challenges that continue to pose serious difficulties for the sustainable development of all countries, particularly developing ones." Also, "…we must act without delay to reverse the process of land degradation".

The preparation of this report was preceded by a critical analysis of the PAN, which was updated in 2013. This analysis highlighted key data and directions to follow to align the PAN with the 2008-2018 Ten-Year Strategy.

This "updated" and "aligned" Action Plan is the result of collective work which involved several national and international actors, including government institutions, the 5 services of autonomous entities, civil society organizations, as well as relevant technical and financial partners.

Document Title: National action program to combat desertification ( Programme d’action national de lutte contre la désertification)
Family Title: National action program to combat desertification
Family Summary: The National Action Programme to Combat Desertification (NAP) aims to identify the factors contributing to desertification and the concrete measures to be taken to combat desertification and mitigate the effects of drought. The general objectives are: to strengthen the capacities of the different categories of actors (state, local populations and communities, NGOs and other development associations, private sector) to ensure the sustainable management of natural resources Improve the institutional and legislative framework for combating desertification; improving the living conditions of the population and rehabilitating areas affected by desertification. The NAP envisages measures aimed at: (i) strengthening basic knowledge and developing information and observation systems for vulnerable areas; (ii) combating water erosion, including by intensifying soil conservation activities; (iii) developing and strengthening integrated land and water management programmes in the context of the diversification of income sources and the eradication of poverty; (iv) establishing comprehensive plans for prevention and relief in the event of drought. In order to solve the problem of food security, the NAP envisages increasing the production of foodstuffs while ensuring the sustainability of production factors, the increase of productivity and, in particular, the involvement of groups vulnerable social groups such as women and young people.

Document Title: National plan for disaster risk reduction 2018-2023 (Plan nacional para la reducción del riesgo de desastres 2018-2023 (PNRRD))
Family Title: National plan for disaster risk reduction 2018-2023 (PNRRD)
Family Summary: The National Plan for Disaster Risk Reduction constitutes a public policy tool that contemplates objectives and goals that define the policies' guidelines for comprehensive risk management and the basic principles that must be developed to execute programs. It is the first document of national scope on the subject, which allows projecting a short-, medium- and long-term strategy consistent with the new regulations regulating risk management in Argentina (SINAGIR - Law 27,287) and with the Sendai Framework 2015-2030. Likewise, it should be interpreted as a multisectoral and interdisciplinary coordination mechanism between public sector institutions, the private sector and social organizations.

Document Title: Arming our country against crises and climate impacts: a new start in civil protection (Unser Land gegen Krisen und Klimafolgen wappnen: Neustart im Bevölkerungsschutz)
Family Title: Arming our country against crises and climate impacts: a new start in civil protection
Family Summary:
For a crisis-proof Germany, the strengthening of civil protection is being addressed as part of the programme. All projects and measures therefore follow the four guidelines: Always prepared, early warning, efficient action, good post-crisis care. Ensuring the safety of citizens in the event of crises and disasters is a core task of the state. A well-equipped and efficient civil defence system is essential for the safety of all.

The pandemic, disasters caused by climate impacts such as the floods in summer 2021 or forest fires and the changed security situation in Europe due to the Russian war of aggression against Ukraine, which violates international law, have significantly increased and changed people's need for protection and security: Civil protection must be reorganised and Germany's federal structure must be made more crisis-proof and resilient. Civil protection must offer people effective protection across administrative levels and sectors. The focus must be on well thought-out preparation for crisis management.

This law includes the participation of civil society in disaster prevention, as well as giving the State full responsibility for preventing disasters, and urging state institutions to include prevention programs in their plans.

Through regional, municipal and communal emergency committees, the commission fulfills its function of coordinating public and private institutions, non-governmental organizations, and civil society that work in dealing with emergencies or disasters. The law establishes an emergency plan as well as the management of funds for emergency cases.

This Decree sets out that the Ministry is to propose all measures aimed at adapting crops and livestock farming to climate change in consultation with the relevant sectors, and to develop an outreach programme in this area, through its Directorate for the Development of Rural Territories and the Adaptation of Agriculture to Climate Change.

The Sub-Directorate for Irrigation and Adaptation of Climate Change is responsible for, inter alia, the establishment of a system to monitor climate change in agriculture; to participate, with the relevant sectors, in the development, implementation and evaluation of climate change adaptation programmes related to agriculture; and to initiate studies on the effects on climate change on agriculture.

Family Title: Work Plan for Strengthening the Higher Education Talent Training System for Carbon Peak and Carbon Neutrality
Family Summary: This Work Plan sets out the actions for cultivating various talent pools to achieve carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, which requires broad and profound eocnomic and social systemic change. The key tasks include strengthening green and low-carbon education; building a high-level science and technology platform; accelerating the development of disciplines and talents for energy storage, hydrogen energy, carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS), and carbon finance and trading; upgrade traditional energy education; and deepening the integration of industry and education sector collaboration.

Document Title: Implementation Plan to Accelerate the Comprehensive Utilization of Industrial Resources

Document Title: Measures for the Management of GHG Voluntary Emissions Reduction Trading (Trial)

Document Title: Implementation Plan for Synergies of Pollution-Carbon Reduction
Family Title: Implementation Plan for Synergies of Pollution-Carbon Reduction
Family Summary: To achieve the goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, this Plan was issued, promoting the synergies of pollution-carbon reduction through integrated planning, deployment, implementation, and assessment. The guiding principles are capturing synergy and efficiency gains, strengthening source control, optimising technical approaches, fostering innovative mechanisms, and encouraging pilot programs. The goals are, by 2025, establish a basic framework for synergies of pollution-carbon reduction, achieve significant progress in structural optimization and green low-carbon development in key regions and sectors, develop a number of replicable best practices, and effectively improve the synergy between pollution control and carbon reduction; and by 2030, significantly enhance the synergy capacity of pollution-carbon reduction, contributing to the carbon peaking target, and achieve significant progress in collaborative efforts of carbon peaking and air quality improvement in key regions for air pollution control". By 2030, the sales volume of new energy vehicles in the key regions for air pollution control will account for around 50% of the total new vehicle sales.

Document Title: Notice on Carrying Out Pilot Carbon Emission Environmental Impact Assessments for Key Industry Construction Projects
Family Title: Notice on Carrying Out Pilot Carbon Emission Environmental Impact Assessments for Key Industry Construction Projects

These programmes cover carbon monitoring and assessment, along with pilot programs for collaborative control of pollution-carbon reduction. The programme is meant to develop high-quality technical methods and operational models for carbon monitoring and assessment, and for emissions reductions.

Document Title: Implementation Plan for Emissions Reduction and Carbon Sequestration in Agriculture and Rural Areas
Family Title: Implementation Plan for Emissions Reduction and Carbon Sequestration in Agriculture and Rural Areas
Family Summary: This Plan lays out key tasks in three areas: crop farming; animal husbandry. These tasks include reducing methane emissions from rice paddies, lowering the intensity of enteric methane emissions from ruminants, and decreasing methane and nitrogen dioxide emissions from livestock manure management. Low-carbon practices will also be used for the fisheries sector. Document Title: Guiding Opinion on Promoting the Development of the Energy Electronics Industry
Family Title: Guiding Opinion on Promoting the Development of the Energy Electronics Industry
Family Summary: This Opinion aims to prompt the development of energy equipment; to focus on core technology research; to train talent; to revolutionise the production and consumption of energy; to accelerate the construction of an "ecological civilisation"; and to achieve the carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals. This would enable the energy electronics industry to become a key force in promoting the realisation of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality. In addition, the Opinion also includes the actions relating to strengthening the overall coordination of supply and demand of energy; promoting coordinated development in the supply chain; and improving the technical innovation support system.

Document Title: Guiding Opinion on Accelerating the Green and Intelligent Development of Inland River Vessels
Family Title: Guiding Opinion on Accelerating the Green and Intelligent Development of Inland River Vessels

Document Title: Work Plan for Promoting the Development of Multimodal Transport and Optimizing the Transport Structure (2021-2025)
Family Title: Work Plan for Promoting the Development of Multimodal Transport and Optimizing the Transport Structure (2021-2025)

It promotes the shift of bulk cargo and medium-long distance freight transport from highway to railway, and from highway to waterway. It continues the application of innovative "single-bill" and "single-container" systems for multimodal transport. Through this Work Plan, actions are set out for the optimisation of the transport structure for multimodal transport development, the formulation of standards such as Intermodal loading unit identification and Classification and codes of intermodal transport cargo, and the strengthening of the connection between different modes of transport. According to China's 2024 Biennial Transparency Report, by the end of 2022, a total of 116 multimodal transport demonstration projects had been launched in four batches. In 2022, the demonstration routes covered the national integrated transport hubs and the main framework of the three-dimensional transport network. In 2022, the national railway and waterway freight volume increased by 432 million tons and 937 million tons, respectively compared to 2020, with growth rates of 9.49% and 12.31% respectively.

Document Title: 14th Five-Year Plan for Green Development of Civil Aviation

Document Title: Correction - EPA New Source Performance Standards and Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units
Family Title: EPA New Source Performance Standards and Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units
Family Summary:
This regulation establishes new standards and guidelines under Section 111 of the Clean Air Act to limit greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs). Key provisions include:

  • New Source Performance Standards (NSPS): Sets emission limits for new, modified, and reconstructed fossil fuel-fired EGUs.
  • Emission Guidelines: Provides guidelines for existing fossil fuel-fired EGUs to reduce GHG emissions.
  • Repeal of the Affordable Clean Energy (ACE) Rule: Revokes the previous ACE rule, which had set less stringent standards.

The EPA determined that the best system of emission reduction (BSER) for new coal-fired units is the most efficient demonstrated steam cycle combined with best operating practices, rather than carbon capture and storage, due to cost and feasibility considerations. The BSER is determined based on (i) technological feasibility, (ii) cost-effectiveness, (iii) environmental impact and (iv) energy requirements.The EPA has categorised new and reconstructed combustion turbines into three subcategories based on their operational load (low, intermediate and base) and also set compliance timeline.

Document Title: Economic Recovery Plan 2020-2024
Family Title: Economic Recovery Plan 2020-2024
Family Summary:
The Plan recognises that the Algerian economy has been affected to varying degrees by all the ills of rentier economies -- it is very poorly diversified and relies heavily on public spending. The Plan aims to promote inclusive industrial and economic development through the better use of natural resources and consideration of environmental impacts within a sustainable development framework; reforming the investment climate; and building better infrastructure.

The Plan also mentions that exports are more than 90% (2020) from the hydrocarbon sector, and the state budget's dependence on oil taxes ranges from 40% (2019) to 60% (2010). The Algerian economy is therefore highly vulnerable to oil price shocks. These tend to occur more frequently; the most recent ones occurred in 2008, 2014, and 2020. Furthermore, since hydrocarbons are non-renewable resources, an economic model based primarily on their exploitation cannot be sustainable.

The Plan discusses the need for energy and food security in the context of climate change, and the necessity of the energy transition and transformation in consumption patterns. The strategies therfore include producing and preparing an export strategy for the renewable energy sector; and decentralising the production of renewable energy.

Document Title: EPA New Source Performance Standards and Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units - webpage
Family Title: EPA New Source Performance Standards and Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units
Family Summary:
This regulation establishes new standards and guidelines under Section 111 of the Clean Air Act to limit greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs). Key provisions include:

  • New Source Performance Standards (NSPS): Sets emission limits for new, modified, and reconstructed fossil fuel-fired EGUs.
  • Emission Guidelines: Provides guidelines for existing fossil fuel-fired EGUs to reduce GHG emissions.
  • Repeal of the Affordable Clean Energy (ACE) Rule: Revokes the previous ACE rule, which had set less stringent standards.

The EPA determined that the best system of emission reduction (BSER) for new coal-fired units is the most efficient demonstrated steam cycle combined with best operating practices, rather than carbon capture and storage, due to cost and feasibility considerations. The BSER is determined based on (i) technological feasibility, (ii) cost-effectiveness, (iii) environmental impact and (iv) energy requirements.The EPA has categorised new and reconstructed combustion turbines into three subcategories based on their operational load (low, intermediate and base) and also set compliance timeline.

Document Title: Decree 978/2024

4. Strengthen disaster risk governance for efficient and effective disaster risk management and climate change adaptation.

5. Strengthen preparedness for response to the possible materialization of risk, guaranteeing the integration of the social dynamics of the territory.

Document Title: Green Construction through Wood (GCWood) Program
Family Title: Green Construction through Wood Program
Family Summary:
The Green Construction through Wood (GCWood) program encourages the use of innovative wood-based building technologies in construction projects. This program supports Canada’s commitment to reach 2030 and 2050 emissions reduction targets under the Paris Agreement and advance long-term priorities regarding greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction.

GCWood invests in wood construction projects that generate many benefits, including:

  • reduced GHG emissions from renewable and sustainable resources that help decarbonize the built environment
  • accelerated adoption of innovative building technologies and systems
  • updated building codes that allow for taller and larger wood buildings
  • affordable housing and community infrastructure

Since its launch in 2017, the GCWood program has supported 16 demonstration projects aimed at reducing risks and promoting the broader use of wood-based products in construction. As of March 2023, it has funded 4 tall wood buildings, 10 low-rise non-residential buildings, and 2 timber bridge projects. The program also developed the 2021 State of Mass Timber in Canada report and an interactive map to track and analyse mass timber construction progress. These resources help applicants understand Canada’s advancements in the field.

Upon renewal, the program broadened its scope to include support for schematic designs, innovative wood construction systems, and the use of advanced bio-based building materials in both new and existing low GHG emission buildings. It offers non-repayable funding of up to $1.4 million for eligible project costs.

Future funding will prioritise projects in areas such as prefabrication, modular construction, retrofitting, and adaptable or disassemblable design.

Document Title: EPA New Source Performance Standards and Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units
Family Title: EPA New Source Performance Standards and Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units
Family Summary:
This regulation establishes new standards and guidelines under Section 111 of the Clean Air Act to limit greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs). Key provisions include:

  • New Source Performance Standards (NSPS): Sets emission limits for new, modified, and reconstructed fossil fuel-fired EGUs.
  • Emission Guidelines: Provides guidelines for existing fossil fuel-fired EGUs to reduce GHG emissions.
  • Repeal of the Affordable Clean Energy (ACE) Rule: Revokes the previous ACE rule, which had set less stringent standards.

The EPA determined that the best system of emission reduction (BSER) for new coal-fired units is the most efficient demonstrated steam cycle combined with best operating practices, rather than carbon capture and storage, due to cost and feasibility considerations. The BSER is determined based on (i) technological feasibility, (ii) cost-effectiveness, (iii) environmental impact and (iv) energy requirements.The EPA has categorised new and reconstructed combustion turbines into three subcategories based on their operational load (low, intermediate and base) and also set compliance timeline.

Document Title: Green Construction through Wood Program - APPLICANT GUIDEBOOK 2023
Family Title: Green Construction through Wood Program
Family Summary:
The Green Construction through Wood (GCWood) program encourages the use of innovative wood-based building technologies in construction projects. This program supports Canada’s commitment to reach 2030 and 2050 emissions reduction targets under the Paris Agreement and advance long-term priorities regarding greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction.

GCWood invests in wood construction projects that generate many benefits, including:

  • reduced GHG emissions from renewable and sustainable resources that help decarbonize the built environment
  • accelerated adoption of innovative building technologies and systems
  • updated building codes that allow for taller and larger wood buildings
  • affordable housing and community infrastructure

Since its launch in 2017, the GCWood program has supported 16 demonstration projects aimed at reducing risks and promoting the broader use of wood-based products in construction. As of March 2023, it has funded 4 tall wood buildings, 10 low-rise non-residential buildings, and 2 timber bridge projects. The program also developed the 2021 State of Mass Timber in Canada report and an interactive map to track and analyse mass timber construction progress. These resources help applicants understand Canada’s advancements in the field.

Upon renewal, the program broadened its scope to include support for schematic designs, innovative wood construction systems, and the use of advanced bio-based building materials in both new and existing low GHG emission buildings. It offers non-repayable funding of up to $1.4 million for eligible project costs.

Future funding will prioritise projects in areas such as prefabrication, modular construction, retrofitting, and adaptable or disassemblable design.

Document Title: Framework for Climate Adaptive Buildings (Part 2 - Building Score)
Family Title: Framework for Climate Adaptive Buildings
Family Summary:
The Framework for Climate Adaptive Buildings has been developed by the Dutch Green Building Council (DGBC), in collaboration with more than 40 parties, and is meant for parties operating in the real estate sector: real estate parties, financiers, housing corporations and government authorities. This standard methodology enables the identification of the biggest physical climate risks within a portfolio. It can also be used to report on alignment with the EU Taxonomy relating to climate goal 2: climate adaptation. The methodology has been set up based on open climate data and is transparent on the methods used. The goal is to assess the climate impacts at the building level as accurately as possible. The methodology comprises three steps:

Part 1: Assessing the climate impacts for the area surrounding a building (the building environment score)

Part 2: Determining the building-specific vulnerability (the building score)

Part 3: Deciding on measures at the area and building levels (the adaptation strategy)

It provides an overview of climate change vulnerabilities in Algeria and proposes over 70 action measures, including: - adoption of cleaner energy consumption model by substituting liquid fuels by natural gas and liquefied propane; - achieving 35,000 hectares of forests and developing another 175,000 hectares; -waste recovery (13.5 million tonnes / year), - electrification of railway transport and intensification of urban public transport (including constructing the Algiers metro and tramway infrastructure in several cities). The Plan further promotes uptake of renewable energies and sets a target of installing of 22,000 MW of renewable power capacity between 2011 and 2030, divided between 12, 000 MW to be dedicated to cover the national demand for electricity and 10,000 MW for export.

Document Title: Ordinance (2018:1428) on government climate adaptation work
Family Title: Ordinance (2018:1428) on government climate adaptation work
Family Summary:
According to this Ordinance, 32 national authorities and all county administrative boards must conduct climate and vulnerability analyses, develop government targets for their work on climate adaptation and an action plan to achieve the targets. The latest versions of the action plans are shown below.

The Ordinance states that designated authorities must initiate, support and evaluate work on climate adaptation within their areas of responsibility and within the framework of their assignments. They must conduct climate and vulnerability analyses for their operations and develop current government targets for their work on climate adaptation. The targets must contribute to the government achieving its climate adaptation targets and be measurable to the extent that is practically possible.

The authorities must have an action plan for the work of achieving these government targets. Resources, approaches, timeframes and division of responsibilities that apply to the work shall be stated in the action plan. The work according to the action plan is followed up and evaluated with the aim of continuously improving the work. The action plan is updated in the event of significant changes in the operations or at least every five years.

Document Title: National Transport Strategy 2050
Family Title: National Transport Strategy 2050
Family Summary:
The Strategy establishes the strategic goal of using transport to promote environmental and urban sustainability. Specific aspects identified so far are as follows:

• Reduce and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions

• Ensure efficient and sustainable use and management of resources

• Ensure adaptation to climate change

• Minimise the impact of transport to enhance the landscape and townscape

• Preserve the natural habitats and biodiversity

• Respect historical and heritage resources

Document Title: National Strategy of Forests 2030
Family Title: National Strategy of Forests 2030
Family Summary:
The objectives include promoting a sustainable circular forest bioeconomy through long-lasting wood products, where the forest sector contributes to Romania's climate neutrality objectives by improving the use of wood and wood products, to stimulate the growth of absorbed CO2 stocks and reduce emissions.

Another objective is to protect, restore and expand forests in Romania, to have stable forests in the context of climate change, with rich biodiversity and a greater share in the surface area of ​​Romania,

Document Title: National Transport Master Plan 2025
Family Title: National Transport Master Plan 2025
Family Summary:
Climate-related measures include the following:

  • Establish the share of greenhouse gases from transport that would contribute fairly to climate change targets and monitor the progress of this master plan in line with these targets.
  • Assess the impact of climate change and sea level rise on transport infrastructures and incorporate climate change considerations at the planning and design stage to reduce retro-fitting costs.

Document Title: Law no. 292/2018 on assessing the impact of certain public and private projects on the environment.
Family Title: Law no. 292/2018 on assessing the impact of certain public and private projects on the environment.
Family Summary:
Romania transposed Directive 2011/92/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2011 on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment through Law no. 292/2018 on assessing the impact of certain public and private projects on the environment.

The authority responsible for the environmental assessment procedure is the Ministry of Environment, Water and Forests and the subordinate institutions represented by the environmental protection agencies across the country.

All institutions that develop plans / projects / programs which could generate significant environmental impacts must submit and go through the environmental assessment procedure. The procedure involves the assessment of the risks of major accidents and/or disasters relevant to the project in question, including those caused by climate change, according to scientific information, and the assessment of the impact of the project on climate change. The procedure shall introduce measures to reduce the impact of the project on the climate and/or, as applicable, measures adapted to the vulnerability of the project to climate change.

Document Title: Framework for Climate Adaptive Buildings (Part 1 - Building Environment Score)
Family Title: Framework for Climate Adaptive Buildings
Family Summary:
The Framework for Climate Adaptive Buildings has been developed by the Dutch Green Building Council (DGBC), in collaboration with more than 40 parties, and is meant for parties operating in the real estate sector: real estate parties, financiers, housing corporations and government authorities. This standard methodology enables the identification of the biggest physical climate risks within a portfolio. It can also be used to report on alignment with the EU Taxonomy relating to climate goal 2: climate adaptation. The methodology has been set up based on open climate data and is transparent on the methods used. The goal is to assess the climate impacts at the building level as accurately as possible. The methodology comprises three steps:

Part 1: Assessing the climate impacts for the area surrounding a building (the building environment score)

Part 2: Determining the building-specific vulnerability (the building score)

Part 3: Deciding on measures at the area and building levels (the adaptation strategy)

Document Title: Decision No. 563/2022 on the establishment, organisation and functioning of the Inter-ministerial Committee on Climate Change
Family Title: Decision No. 563/2022 on the establishment, organisation and functioning of the Inter-ministerial Committee on Climate Change
Family Summary: The members of this Committee are the ministers of different Ministries of the Romanian Government, and it is led by three vice-presidents, the president being the Prime Minister of the Romanian Government.The Committee has the following main objectives:a) analyses and proposes solutions in order to ensure the consistency of policies in sectors that have an impact on climate change, proposed by the relevant ministries, with the commitments made at national level, towards the European Union, the United Nations and other international organisations to which Romania is a party, and monitors the progress made by Romanian institutions in their implementation;b) analyses, monitors and proposes annual priority policies in the field of climate change in accordance with the commitments made at the national level, towards the European Union, including through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan of Romania, the United Nations and other international organisations to which Romania is a party or in the process of acceding, which will be subject to annual approval by the Government, under the terms of the law;c) analyses, monitors and evaluates the degree of fulfilment of the measures that fall to the authorities and institutions responsible for implementing the policies provided for in the Integrated National Plan for Energy and Climate Change, hereinafter referred to as PNIESC, to fulfil the commitments assumed by Romania, regarding our country's contribution to achieving the European targets established in the field of energy and climated) analyses, monitors and evaluates the degree of achievement of the objectives of the National Long-term Strategy for the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and proposes solutions for achieving these objectives, including intermediate targets, in accordance with the provisions of art. 15 of Regulation (EU) No. 2018/1999;e) analyses and monitors the application of the methodology for budgeting climate change initiatives, developed by the General Secretariat of the Government in collaboration with the Ministry of Finance, in accordance with the obligations assumed in the National Recovery and Resilience Plan of Romania and the international agreements to which Romania is a party;f) analyses and proposes indicators for measuring Romania's climate commitments, starting from existing, internationally recognised indicators, by reporting to the requirements of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Paris Agreement, as well as to other initiatives in the field, such as the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction;g) proposes the communication of a unified and coherent message on the topic of climate change based on scientific data, in line with the studies and recommendations of the International Panel on Climate Change, the World Meteorological Organization and the National Meteorological Administration and other relevant structures, by public institutions in Romania that develop policies with impact in the field of combating climate change.

Document Title: Plan of Action for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA) (2011-2015)
Family Title: Plan of Action for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA) (2011-2015)
Family Summary:
This Plan sets out the intended outputs and activities for DRR and CCA. The broad-level actions are: ensure that DRR is a national and a local priority with a strong institutional basis for implementation; identify, assess and monitor disaster risk and enhance early warning; use knowledge, innovation and education to build a culture of safety and resilience at all levels; reduce the underlying risk factors; and strengthen disaster preparedness for effective response at all levels.

Activities include preparing national strategies; providing technical support to district authorities and inter-ministerial coordination.

Document Title: Climate Action Roadmap For Buildings and Construction
Family Title: Climate Action Roadmap For Buildings and Construction
Family Summary:
This Roadmap transforms the building and construction sector to be resilient and inclusive while emitting less carbon. It covers spatial and urban development; existing buildings; new buildings; and the construction supply chain.

The objectives are as follows:

Embodied and operational carbon

  • Increase low-carbon electricity generation and promote clean rural households lighting leading to acombined emission reduction
  • Promote energy efficiency in homes, industry and commerce leading to emission reduction

Adaptation

  • Achieve city-wide resilient infrastructure planning for climate change adaptation
  • Build well-planned and safe communities, while protecting the natural environment

Well-being and inclusion

  • Identify, develop and promote the use of sustainable local materials in building and construction
  • Create an equitable, healthy and prosperous society

Document Title: Investing for Food and Jobs (IFJ): An Agenda For Transforming Ghana's Agriculture (2018-2021)
Family Title: Investing for Food and Jobs (IFJ): An Agenda For Transforming Ghana's Agriculture (2018-2021)
Family Summary:
The agricultural sector, a key to the national development agenda, is expected to lead the growth and structural transformation of the economy and maximise the benefits of accelerated growth.

This Plan is developed to provide structured public investment and leverage private investments under three main categories: (i) developing critical infrastructure to modernise the agri-food system; (ii) building both public and private sector systems to generate the enabling results and the outcome results respectively; and (iii) direct transfer to farmers, agri-food enterprises and other value chain actors.

This Plan seeks to address cross cutting issues including biodiversity, climate change and environmental management. Actions include Support the development and introduction of climate resilient, high-yielding, disease and pest-resistant, short duration crop varieties taking into account consumer health and safety; promoting agricultural insurance instruments

Document Title: Water Sector Strategic Development Plan (2012-2025)
Family Title: Water Sector Strategic Development Plan (2012-2025)
Family Summary:
This Plan sets out Ghana’s commitment to and provides the framework for achieving the vision in respect of water, which is “sustainable water and basic sanitation for all by 2025.” It identifies and addresses existing and emerging challenges in delivering water and basic sanitation services in the country and proposes strategies towards ensuring that all people in Ghana have access to basic levels of water and sanitation services by 2025.

One of the specific objectives of the water sector is to ensure sustainable harnessing, utilisation and management of water resources by 2025, by developing a framework for managing and protecting water resources for improved water security and enhanced resilience to climate change. The strategies to achieve this objective aere: (1) Enhance the implementation of existing regulations on WRM; (2) Develop and implement additional regulations on Dam Safety and Effluent discharges; and (3) Ensure the protection and conservation of river basins and wetlands for water security as well as enhanced resilience and adaptation to climate change.

Document Title: Ghana REDD+ Strategy (2016-2035)
Family Title: Ghana REDD+ Strategy (2016-2035)
Family Summary:
This Strategy has been designed to meet the requirements of the Warsaw Framework on REDD+ and other decisions of the Conference of the Parties of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) - it contains strategies on institutional arrangements; policy and legal frameworks; grievance mechanisms; and tracking. In developing the national REDD+ strategy, significant attention has been paid to national circumstances and developmental aspirations, and the process also took due cognisance of major national policies, including the national climate change policy (2013) and the revised forest and wildlife policy of Ghana (2012).

One of the goals of the Strategy is transforming Ghana's major agricultural commodities and Non Timber Forest Products (NTFPs) into climate-smart production systems and landscapes.

Countries that intend to undertake REDD+ (reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation in developing countries) activities are required to develop a national strategy that clearly articulates measures aimed at addressing the drivers of deforestation and forest degradation and other associated issues including land and tree tenure, forest governance, gender and safeguards.

Document Title: Ghana Climate Prosperity Plan
Family Title: Ghana Climate Prosperity Plan
Family Summary:
The Climate Prosperity Plan (CPP) embeds the aspirational pathway for Ghana from climate vulnerability to climate prosperity, meanwhile creating quality jobs, stimulating the economy while making it resilient, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

The CPP is centered around two principal goals: Climate Secure Ghana and Climate Prosperous Ghana. These goals are focused on promoting a range of priority efforts in the following sectors: energy, water, human mobility, food security, and finance. The former goal has two targets:

  • Ghana achieves a 100% electrification rate through deployment of renewable energy by 2035; and
  • Ghana’s population (100%) has access to at least basic water services by 2030.

The latter goal targets that:

  • In 2035, 100% of major urban centers in Ghana benefited from an extended public transportationnetwork running on electric vehicles;
  • 90-100% of national food and beverage consumption is domestically produced by 2035; and
  • Ghana’s coverage of biodiversity corridors and touch points to favor biodiversity conservation increasesby 30% in 2035.

Document Title: National Water Policy (2007)
Family Title: National Water Policy
Family Summary:
This Policy has an overall goal of ensuring the efficient utilisation and management of available water resources and enabling equitable access to sustainable, safely managed and affordable water for all. It contains sections on (i) water resources management; (ii) urban water services and (iii) community water services, and also highlights the legal framework for the domestic and transboundary utilisation of water resources.

Policy measures include:

  • ensure the preparation and periodic review of national, basin and sub-basin IWRM plans and strategies and address climate change and variability;
  • mitigate the effects of climate variability and change and prevent damage caused by extreme hydrological and meteorological occurrences (#oods and droughts);
  • institute climate adaptation measures to minimise the effects of climate variability and change on agriculture,energy, water supply and other competing water uses;
  • promote appropriate farming methods and varieties that withstand the adverse effects of climate variabilityand change;

Document Title: National Environment Policy
Family Title: National Environment Policy
Family Summary:
This Policy outlines the vision for environmental management, which is aimed at sustainable development: to manage the environment to sustain society at large. The purpose is to guide environmental governance in Ghana; serve as a reference material for research and development; guide the country’s development along sustainable path; and ensure the country’s commitment to conventions, protocols and international agreements.

In accordance with this policy, the Ghanian government will adopt measures to reduce vulnerability to climate variability and change and promote community participation in environmental governance and natural resource management as well as mitigate the impact of natural and man-made disasters. Measures include preparing a guidebook to facilitate the integration of climate change and Disaster Risk Reduction into National Development Policies and Planning.

Document Title: Food and Agricultural Sector Development Policy (FASDEP II)
Family Title: Food and Agricultural Sector Development Policy (FASDEP II)
Family Summary: One of the objectives of this Policy is to mainstream and support the scaling up of sustainable land management practices in addressing issues of productivity in agriculture and environmental services, and in serving as an entry point to address the interactions between agriculture and climate change and biodiversity loss. The Policy contains strategies including to create awareness about environmental issues among stakeholders, and improve incentive and compulsion measures to encourage users of the environment to adopt less exploitative and non-degrading pracices in agriculture.

Document Title: Ghana’s Medium-Term Agriculture Sector Investment Plan (METASIP II), 2014-2017

Document Title: National Water Policy
Family Title: National Water Policy
Family Summary:
This Policy has an overall goal of ensuring the efficient utilisation and management of available water resources and enabling equitable access to sustainable, safely managed and affordable water for all. It contains sections on (i) water resources management; (ii) urban water services and (iii) community water services, and also highlights the legal framework for the domestic and transboundary utilisation of water resources.

Policy measures include:

  • ensure the preparation and periodic review of national, basin and sub-basin IWRM plans and strategies and address climate change and variability;

  • facilitate assessment and analysis of water resources availability and the impact of climate change and catchment degradation on water resources; and
  • ensure sustainability of climate-sensitive and appropriate technology to deliver safe and sustainable water.

Document Title: Ghana Forest Plantation Strategy: 2016-2040
Family Title: Ghana Forest Plantation Strategy: 2016-2040
Family Summary:
This Strategy aims to increase forest cover and restore degraded lands. Landscape restoration strategies proposed include trees-on-farm (climate smart agriculture), woodlot establishment, enrichment planting interventions, watershed restoration, etc., which together with commercial forest plantation development will significantly contribute to achieving Ghana’s commitments both under the Bonn Challenge - a global landscape restoration initiative, as well as the Paris Agreement on Climate Change.

The implementation plan covers four areas: establishment and management of planted ofrests; forest plantation investment promotion; employment creation and sustainable livelihoods; and investments in research and development, extension, training and capacity building for forest plantation development.

Document Title: Forestry Development Master Plan (2016-2036)
Family Title: Forestry Development Master Plan (2016-2036)
Family Summary:
This Plan aims to achieve a just, prosperous and sustainable forestry sector that inclusively and continuously optimises welfare and provides adeqaute means of livelihood to all Ghanaians. It builds on the Ghana Forest and Wildlife Policy issued in 2012.

This Plan seeks to contirbute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions from deforestation and forest degradation, climate and temperature regulation, sustainable supply of timber and woodfuels, reducing poverty and helping to conserve biodiversity. It is meant to be implemented in three phases: short-term continuation programmes (2016-2020); medium-term structural transformation programmes (2021-2030); and long-term consolidation programmes (2031-2036).

Document Title: Ghana Forest and Wildlife Policy
Family Title: Ghana Forest and Wildlife Policy
Family Summary: The Policy sets out the strategic directions and policy strategies to halt and reverse the pace of deforestation and forest degradation in Ghana, including the promotion of climate change mitigation and adaptation. The Policy calls for the development of capacities in public institutions and civil societies to engage in future international and domestic mechanisms that will respond to climate change. This includes enacting the necessary legislation to guide allocation of carbon rights and related matters; supporting training and education in forest resource management at district levels in carbon rights allocations; creating national awareness about the role of forests in climate change mitigation and adaptation; and making efforts to develop a sustainable wildlife management framework with active involvement of landowners and resource users and a savannah eco-restoration fund.
