Document Title: Vision 2057: Long-Term National Development Perspective Framework
Family Title: Vision 2057: Long-Term National Development Perspective Framework
Family Summary: This framework is a Vision document that reflects the development aspirations of the people of Ghana from which current and future Medium-Term Development Plans will be derived. Strategic directions include: Promote climate-smart agriculture, enhance the resilience of communities, food systems and their associated supply chains, and reduce exposure to climate-, energy- and water-related risks; Enhance climate change resilience; and Incorporate climate-resilient and user-friendly designs as well as sustainable practices in infrastructure development.

Document Title: National Migration Policy
Family Title: National Migration Policy
Family Summary: This Policy contains a section on "Migration, the Environment and Climate Change" (MECC). The listed strategies includde mainstreaming migration in the National Climate Change Policy 2013 (MCCP), increasing research and data gathering on MECC and mitigating the effects of environmental and climate change on migrants.

Document Title: Agenda For Jobs II (2022-2025): Creating Prosperity And Equal Opportunity For All (2022-2025)
Family Title: Agenda For Jobs II (2022-2025): Creating Prosperity And Equal Opportunity For All (2022-2025)
Family Summary:
This Agenda contains climate-related actions, including: supporting the youth to create and sustain climate-smart agribusiness and creating an investment culture among the youth to spur economic growth; implementing specific climate-responsive intervenetions and supporting the youth to harness opportunities in the green economy; production of climate-resilient agricultural produce.

The Agenda For Jobs II (2022-2025): Creating Prosperity And Equal Opportunity For All (2022-2025) is informed by the Long-Term National Development Policy Framework (LTNDPF), 2018-2057, also known as Ghana@100, which envisions a democratic, inclusive, self-reliant developed country by 2057; and other national and international documents and commitments such as the Coordinated Programme of Economic and Social Development Policies (CPESDP), 2017-2024; Ghana Beyond Aid Charter and Strategy; Ghana COVID-19 Alleviation and Revitalisation of Enterprises Support (CARES) Obaatanpa Programme; Agenda for Jobs - “Creating Prosperity And Equal Opportunities For All” (2018-2021); Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 2030); Paris Climate Agreement; Africa Union Agenda 2063; African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Agreement; and ECOWAS Vision 2050.

Document Title: National Climate Change and Green Economy Learning Strategy
Family Title: National Climate Change and Green Economy Learning Strategy
Family Summary: The action plans in this strategy have been developed to address the capacity building and learning components of the National Climate Change Policy and will be a critical tool in implementing Ghana’s National Climate Change Masterplan (2015-2020) and the Nationally Determined Contributions from 2020. Actions include training farmers and fishermen on conservation agriculture and providing technical and financial assistance to businesses to undertake pilot initiatives.

Document Title: Ghana Shared Growth and Development Agenda II (2014-2017)
Family Title: Ghana Shared Growth and Development Agenda II (2014-2017)
Family Summary: The Ghana Shared Growth and Development Agenda (GSGDA) II, 2014-2017, is the fifth in the series of medium-term national development policy frameworks prepared over the past two decades. It includes actions such as promoting climate change mitigation in the energy sector; promoting climate change adaptation in water resources management; integrating climate change into sectoral and district plans; increasing resilience to climate change impacts through early warning systems; and implementing alterantive livelihood strategies to minimise impacts of climate chnage on the poor and vulnerable, especially women.

Document Title: Guidelines for the Preparation of the 2025-2028 Budget
Family Title: Guidelines for the Preparation of the 2025-2028 Budget
Family Summary: These Guidelines cover Climate Change/Gender Mainstreaming. Under these Guidelines, ministry departments and agencies are to mainstream climate change activities into their budget by using the revised Climate Change Finance Tracking Tools. MDAs should use the tool to track budget allocations, including grant disbursements. MDAs are also advised to budget for gender mainstreaming activities as part of their programmes.

Document Title: Ghana National Cooling Plan (Framework for Green and Efficient Cooling)
Family Title: Ghana National Cooling Plan (Framework for Green and Efficient Cooling)
Family Summary: This Plan serves as a roadmap to transform Ghana's refrigeration and air conditioning (RAC) sector to the best available technologies to achieve sustainable cooling that will support economic growth and reduce overall impact on the environment, mitigating climate change. It examines the state of each RAC sub-sector, identifies the deficiencies facing the sub-sector and presents technical proposals to guide its transformation to clean and efficient cooling. The plan aims to bring together all cooling-related stakeholders, such as the Ministries, academic institutions, professional bodies, estate developers, the private sector, financial institutions, etc., to synergise and to transform the RAC industry to achieve clean and efficient cooling that is affordable, sustainable, and accessible to all.

Document Title: National Climate Smart Agriculture Food Security and Action Plan (2016-2020)
Family Title: National Climate Smart Agriculture Food Security and Action Plan (2016-2020)
Family Summary: This Action Plan provides the implementation framework for an effective development of climate-smart agriculture in the ground. It formulates specific strategies that will contribute developing climate-resilient agriculture and food systems for all agro-ecological zones, as well as the human resource capacity required for a climate-resilient agriculture promotion in Ghana.

Document Title: National Strategy for Agricultural Development (SENDA)
Family Title: National Strategy for Agricultural Development (SENDA)
Family Summary: This document contains the National Strategy for Agricultural Development (SENDA), which is part of state policies aimed at increasing the productivity of agro-industrial chains, fishing, and aquaculture in a sustainable manner. SENDA thus contributes to the national goal of stimulating long-term economic growth, promoting social inclusion, and improving human well-being. SENDA also seeks to facilitate compliance with environmental commitments, such as the Paris Agreement (United Nations, 2015b) to combat climate change, the Sendai Framework (2015a) for disaster risk reduction, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (2022), and other multilateral environmental agreementsIn response to the Paris Agreement of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), Uruguay set the goal of reducing absolute emissions (in the Second Nationally Determined Contribution or NDC2) with specific targets for the agricultural sector - for instance stabilizing methane and nitrous oxide emissions to ensure they do not generate additional warming. Following a national and international diagnosis, the document outlines six strategic dimensions identified as key to organizing public policies for sector development, namely: 1) International integration; 2) Infrastructure and logistics; 3) Sustainability of agroecosystems; 4) Productive and social development; 5) Information technologies for agriculture; and 6) Institutional capacities.

Document Title: Law No. 3991-IX on the State Climate Policy
Family Title: Law No. 3991-IX on the State Climate Policy
Family Summary:
Law No. 3991-IX (the Law) establishes Ukraine's overarching response to mitigate and adapt to climate change. The Law is aimed at implementing the EU's Regulation (EU) No. 2018/1999 on the governance of the Energy Union and the mitigation of climate change and Regulation (EU) No. 2021/1119, establishing a framework for achieving climate neutrality (the "European Climate law"). The law establishes a target to achieve climate neutrality of Ukraine by 2050 in a "socially fair and economically efficient transition", and aims to set out a framework for achieving low carbon and sustaianble development, ecological and food and energy security in Ukraine. To achieve its net zero target, the law also establishes an interim target of reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by at least 65 percent by 2030, in accordance with 1990 levels.

 The law mandates that the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine (the Cabinet) must ensure the development and implementation of measures to create infrastructure and other material and technical conditions that are needed to implement the state’s climate policy. The Cabinet is also required to issues act on state climate policy issues (that fall within its powers) including approving the National Energy and Climate Plan, Ukraine’s nationally determined contribution to the Paris Agreement, the Long-Term Low-Carbon Development Strategy of Ukraine (the Long-Term Strategy), the Strategy for Adaptation to Climate Change, and sectoral programme documents that seek to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and provide for adapting to climate change. Every year (and no later than 1 June), the Cabinet must submit to the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine a progress report on the implementation of the mitigation and adaptation policies, and progress to implementing the Long-Term Strategy, the National Energy and Climate Plan, and the Climate Change Adaptation Strategy.

The law requires the central body of executive power, which ensures the formation and implementation of state policy in the electric power, nuclear industry, coal industry, peat mining, oil and gas, and oil and gas processing complex, to be involved in the development of the National Energy and Climate Plan, in addition to developing sectoral plans for reducing ghg emissions and adapting to climate change, in accordance with its powers.

The law also requires the Council of Ministers of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea, local state administrations, and local self-government bodies to develop and ensure the implementation of regional plans for mitigating and adapting to climate change (that fall within their jurisdiction), and to report on the implementation of regional plans to the relevant council.

The law establishes a Scientific and Expert Council on Climate Change and Ozone Layer Preservation to provide scientific support and aid in the preparation of reports on achieving Ukraine’s climate policy, and to monitor the implementation of measures, amongst other responsibilities. Section IV of the law sets out fiscal and market mechanisms for achieving the objectives of Ukraine’s policy, in addition to measures on informing the public and access to information on climate change.

Document Title: Integrated Power Sector Master Plan 2023
Family Title: Integrated Power Sector Master Plan 2023
Family Summary: This Plan sets out the long-term Least-Regrets power sector resource plan to meet Ghana's future electricity demand, through optimising existing and future power plants and other energy systems, and transmission capability, and to increase the resilience of the power system to potential risks including climate change. One of the objectives is to meet Ghana's local environmental and climate change commitments, amidst other objectives such as achieving cost-competitiveness in power generation and delivery; meeting local demand and exports; and increasing the resilience in the power system.

Document Title: Energy Commission (Energy Efficiency Standards and Labelling) (Public Lighting) Regulations, 2022
Family Title: Energy Commission (Energy Efficiency Standards and Labelling) (Public Lighting) Regulations, 2022
Family Summary: These Regulations apply to lamps and lumniaries manufactured in or imported into Ghana for public lighting services. These Regulations promote the efficient use and conservation of energy in Ghana, mitigating climate change by providing for minimum energy performance standards, the labelling of and supplementary product information on electric mains-operated lamps and luminaries, and the registration of models of lamps and luminaries. The Regulations also prohibit the manufacture, importation, sale, storage, donation, disposal, installation or use of lamps and luminaries that do not meet the stipulated minimum energy performance standards.
Collection Description(s):
The Act established a National Energy Commission to regulate, manage, develop, and utilise energy resources (including hydro power, solar biomass, wind, geothermal and hydrocarbon) and control the granting of licences for transactions and operations related to electricity and natural gas. The Act established an Energy Fund. Among its objectives are: 1) the promotion of energy efficiency and productive uses of electricity, natural gas and petroleum products; and 2) the promotion of projects for the development and utilisation of renewable energy resources, including solar energy.

The Act was amended in 2016 to incorporate provisions on local content and local participation in the energy supply industry.

Document Title: National Energy Policy
Family Title: National Energy Policy
Family Summary: The National Energy Policy serves as a blueprint to transform Ghana's energy sector into a sustainable, climate-resilient, low-carbon energy economy that will accelerate development and provide quality service to homes and industry. This Policy provides the policy context; an overview of Ghana's energy sector, including the institutional and legal framework; and sub-sector policy goals, objectives, issues and policy directions. The policy directions include evaluating the impact of climate change interventions on petroleum activities and resolving inadequate climate change interventions in the energy sector.

Document Title: National Energy Transition Framework (2022-2070)
Family Title: National Energy Transition Framework (2022-2070)
Family Summary:
This Framework is aimed at decarbonising the energy sector and is a long-term net-zero framework, expected to complement existing efforts with new measures, such as increased renewable energy penetration, conversion of thermal plants to natural gas and the integration of nuclear power into the energy mix. Ghana is determined to extract critical (green) minerals, including lithium and graphite, to make efficient use of them and establish Ghana as a hub for electric vehicles and the production of battery technologies.

Ghana will establish the National Energy Transition Implementation Committee, and set up the National Energy Transition Coordinating Office to drive the implementation of this framework, with participation by the key institutions including the Ministry of Energy, Ministry of Transport, and Ministry of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation.

Family Summary: This Plan outlines the burden of climate-sensitive diseases; health impacts from climate risks; and adaptation options. Other measures proposed in the policy include the use of financial instruments such as insurance; increased climate change education, training and public awareness at all levels; promote the use of prediction models and technologies to determine regional vulnerability of the sectors to climate change; and support higher learning and research institutions on climate related applied research.

Document Title: National Water Policy 2024 Implementation Plan
Family Title: National Water Policy 2024
Family Summary:
The Policy discusses water security in the context of climate change. It states that groundwater resources offer essential livelihood mechanisms and its strategic importance will probably intensify under climate change and human development (population growth, urbanisation) in the future. Groundwater constitutes the most important buffer and reserve of water during surplus periods as well as a source of water for streams and/or direct withdrawals in times of shortage, and thus is expected to play an essential role in climate change adaptation.

The Policy also states that Zambia faces the issues of inadequate climate resilient water harvesting infrastructure; inadequate framework for rainwater harvesting; and inadequate groundwater exploration and aquifer mapping.

To harness water resources and ensure water security for enhanced access and utilisation, the Policy lists the measure of establishing mechanisms that ensure environmental considerations are included in the design for water resources infrastructure and mitigate the effects of climate change.

Document Title: The Environmental Management Act, 2011
Family Title: The Environmental Management Act, 2011
Family Summary: The Zambia Environmental Management Agency shall research or sponsor research on the effects of climatechange on human beings and the environment. The Ministry shall, in consultation with the Agency and relevant appropriate authority, prepare guidelines for the management of environmental emergencies including natural and climate change related disasters such as floods, cyclones, droughts and major pest infestations or the introduction and spread of invasive alien species. In 2023, the Act was amended such that the Agency shall promote actions on climate change adaptation and mitigation in collaboration with an appropriate authority.

Document Title: Agricultural Sector Transformation and Growth Strategy (ASTGS) (2019 – 2029)
Family Title: Agricultural Sector Transformation and Growth Strategy (ASTGS) (2019 – 2029)
Family Summary: The Strategy has the following aims: increasing small-scale farmer incomes, increasing agricultural output and value-addition, and boosting household food resilience. It has a chapter on Sustainability and Crisis Management: Actively monitor 2 key food system risks: i. sustainable and climate-smart natural resource management including sustainable irrigation and water basin health, soil quality and land use; and ii. crisis management for pests diseases, climate and global price shocks.

Document Title: National Tourism Policy 2015
Family Title: National Tourism Policy 2015
Family Summary: The Policy includes a section on Environmental Management and Conservation, where the stated policy measure is to promote a “green” environmentally responsible tourism that enhances the country’s natural and cultural resources and addresses environmental threats such as climate change, poaching, over-fishing, deforestation. This includes promoting the increased use of sustainable waste disposal, green packaging and recycling, water and energy conservation, renewable energy, energy monitoring technology, integrated environmental management, social and environmental audits; and developing plans for tourism management and promotion that address environmental sustainability.

Document Title: Eighth National Development Plan (8NDP) 2022-2026
Family Title: Eighth National Development Plan (8NDP) 2022-2026
Family Summary:
The Eighth National Development Plan (8NDP) sets out Zambia’s strategic direction in terms of the development priorities and implementation strategies for the period 2022 to 2026. The 8NDP introduces strategic interventions anchored on:

  • Economic Transformation and Job Creation;
  • Human and Social Development;
  • Environmental Sustainability; and
  • Good Governance Environment.

Under environmental sustainability, the development outcomes include enhanced mitigation and adaptation to climate change, and enhanced disaster risk reduction and response. The Plan sets out programmes to achieve these outcomes.

Document Title: Forest Code
Family Title: Forest Code
Family Summary:
Through the Forest Code of 2006, the responsibility of managing the country forests has been given to the provinces and their respective authorities. This responsibility has been transferred between the provinces and the federal authorities many times over the years, leading to difficulties in action for forest conservation and regenerations.

As a result of the strong fires in 2010, the Forestry Program to 2020 was introduced to finance forest fire protection.

Document Title: The Fifth Basic Plan for Use, Supply and Technology Development of New and Renewable Energy (Fifth New and Renewable Energy Basic Plan) 2020-2034 Summary
Family Title: The Fifth Basic Plan for Use, Supply and Technology Development of New and Renewable Energy (Fifth New and Renewable Energy Basic Plan) 2020-2034
Family Summary: The Fifth Basic Plan for Use, Supply and Technology Development of New and Renewable Energy (Fifth New and Renewable Energy Basic Plan), outlines government plans for new and renewable energy between 2020 and 2034. New energy includes hydrogen, fuel cells, energy from liquified or gasified coal, and from gasified heavy oil. The plan targets 25.8% new and renewable power generation by 2034, 22.2% of which from renewable energy and 3.6% from new energy. These targets are reflected in the Ninth Basic Plan on Electricity Demand and Supply that was published at the same time.

Document Title: Forest Restoration Action Plan
Family Title: Forest Restoration Action Plan
Family Summary: This policy plans to increase the annual planting of temperate native species to 85 ha in 2022, compared to 40 ha in 2021.

Family Summary:
The Romanian Transport Master Plan 2016-2030 and 2021-2030 Investment program for the development of transport infrastructure in Romania for the period 2021-2030 represents an update of the Romanian Transport Master Plan approved in 2016, without modifying its important aspects, but using the experience gained at the level of the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure and the beneficiaries it aims at an efficient course of projects so that at the end of the decade a large part of the development gap compared to the other Member States is recovered, as well as an active participation in the modernization of European connectivity and the introduction of new sustainable technologies.

Considering the transition period between the two multiannual financial years 2014-2020 and 2021-2027 respectively, considering the fact that the General Transport Master Plan and the related Implementation Strategy were adopted in 2016, as well as analysing the need to correlate the relevant public policies in in order to achieve the necessary infrastructure objectives at the national level, this document has a triple role of:

Document Title: National Policy on Gender Equality and Rights of Women and Girls 2021-2031
Family Title: National Policy on Gender Equality and Rights of Women and Girls 2021-2031
Family Summary: This policy aims to achieve gender equality and women empowerment by 2030. It sets out the commitments of the Government of Samoa and its partners to  gender equality and provides a common framework to guide, coordinate, monitor and account for  all work and investments to realise gender equality and empower all women and girls of Samoa. The seventh priority area of the policy is the environment, and aims to increase visibility, contribution and engagement of women and girls in agriculture, climate  change, natural resources management and disaster preparedness and response, especially  those facing multiple and intersecting barriers and forms of discrimination. Specific actions promoted by this policy include the following:Ensure that a gender transformative approach is incorporated into all aspects of climate  change and natural resource managementInclude women in all climate change-related planning and consultationsEncourage women and girls, including through the use of temporary special measures, to  take courses in the fields of disaster risk management and climate change, including in climatology, fishery and water management  Strengthen collection of gender-related data on the management of marine and costal re sources, with a view to supporting gender equality, ecosystem conservation, sustainable  livelihoods and climate resilience.

Document Title: Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE-2023-053. Technical standard for Ecuador's Greenhouse Gas Emissions Compensation Scheme
Family Title: Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE-2023-053. Technical standard for Ecuador's Greenhouse Gas Emissions Compensation Scheme
Family Summary: Rooted on constitutional provisions on sustainability, living well philosophy (Buen Vivir - Sumak Kawsay), this agreement establishes the regulatory framework for Ecuador’s National Greenhouse Gas Emissions Compensation Scheme, designed to facilitate voluntary initiatives that reduce or remove GHG emissions through mitigation projects. It applies to public, private, community, or mixed-sector initiatives developed within Ecuador, allowing national and international stakeholders to offset their carbon footprints by supporting certified projects. The scheme supports the broader goals of Ecuador's climate commitments, including the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement.The compensation scheme includes mechanisms for creating and trading Carbon Equivalent Units (Unidades de Carbono Equivalente - UCEs), representing verified emission reductions or removals equivalent to one ton of CO₂. Proponents must first reduce their emissions before compensating for any residuals via approved initiatives, such as forest conservation, renewable energy projects, or sustainable agricultural practices. The scheme ensures environmental and social safeguards, equitable benefit distribution, and alignment with national climate strategies, such as the REDD+ Action Plan and the National Climate Change Strategy.The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Ecological Transition (MAATE) oversees implementation through its Climate Change and Natural Heritage Subsecretariats, supported by accredited certification and verification bodies. It maintains a comprehensive registry for monitoring and tracking initiatives, UCEs, and compliance with program requirements. The system encourages transparency, additionality, and real, measurable outcomes that align with sustainable development goals while fostering multistakeholder collaboration across public and private sectors, Indigenous communities, and civil society.

Document Title: Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE-2021-047: Technical Standard for the Ecuador Carbon Zero Program with Organisational Scope
Family Title: Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE-2021-047: Technical Standard for the Ecuador Carbon Zero Program with Organisational Scope
Family Summary: This Ministerial Agreement establishes the guidelines and technical criteria for implementing the Ecuador Carbon Zero Program (PECC) at an organisational level, aligning with Ecuador’s constitutional provisions on environmental sustainability, the living well (buen-vivir or sumak kawsay) and the rights of nature. It enables organisations (public, private, national, or international) to voluntarily measure, reduce, and neutralise their greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from operational activities. The program applies a tiered certification system to encourage participants to advance from carbon footprint quantification (Level 1) to emission reduction (Level 2) and ultimately achieve carbon neutrality (Level 3).Proponents must develop an inventory of their organisational GHG emissions, covering direct (Scope 1), indirect (Scope 2), and selected value-chain emissions (Scope 3) for neutrality certification. The program follows international standards, such as the ISO 14064 series and the GHG Protocol, ensuring consistent methodologies for emission accounting and verification. Participants are required to set reduction targets, implement mitigation projects (e.g. renewable energy adoption, energy efficiency, and waste management) and engage in ongoing monitoring and reporting. Remaining emissions can be offset through nationally regulated compensation schemes.
Keyword: Climate Finance;Mitigation;Energy Transition;Carbon Accounting;Carbon Credits;Carbon Pricing

Document Title: Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE - 2021 - 046. Technical framework focused on products for implementing the Ecuador Carbon Zero Program (PECC)
Family Title: Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE - 2021 - 046. Technical framework focused on products for implementing the Ecuador Carbon Zero Program (PECC)
Family Summary: This Ministerial Agreement introduces the technical framework for implementing the Ecuador Carbon Zero Program (PECC) with a focus on products. It establishes guidelines for organisations to quantify, reduce, and neutralise greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across the life cycle of their products, aligning with Ecuador's constitutional provisions on environmental preservation, living well philosophy (“sumak kawsay” - buen vivir), and sustainable development. The program aims to promote cleaner production practices, reduce the carbon footprint of products, and support national and international climate goals.Central to the framework is the calculation of the Product Carbon Footprint (HCP), guided by international standards such as ISO 14067 and the GHG Protocol. Organization are required to inventory emissions, identify opportunities for reductions, and implement action plans for measurable mitigation. The program introduces certifications for Carbon Footprint Reduction and Carbon Neutrality, which incentivise continuous improvement. Through this policy, it is expected that businesses can achieve both environmental stewardship and competitive advantage, contributing to Ecuador’s transition to a low-carbon economy. Verification processes are handled by accredited conformity assessment bodies, ensuring transparency and adherence to rigorous standards.

Document Title: Master Plan for Electricity  2023 – 2032
Family Title: The Master Plan for Electricity  2023 – 2032
Family Summary: The Master Plan for Electricity 2023–2032 serves as a strategic policy framework to ensure Ecuador's electricity supply meets national demand sustainably and efficiently over the next decade, in a current energetic crisis. Guided by constitutional principles, it prioritises renewable energy expansion, energy efficiency, and infrastructure modernisation to support a transition toward a clean and resilient energy matrix. This plan outlines objectives and strategies for electricity generation, transmission, distribution, public lighting, and regional projects, including a specialised focus on the Galápagos Islands.The plan highlights Ecuador's commitment to diversifying its energy matrix through renewable energy sources like hydropower, green hydrogen, and distributed generation technologies. It incorporates climate resilience measures, integrating risk management for natural, anthropogenic, and climate-related threats. By aligning with the National Development Plan and global sustainability goals, the plan addresses the challenges posed by climate change, emphasising decarbonization and energy security. According to this policy, investment from public and private sectors is integral to achieving its goals, promoting a sustainable energy future while ensuring equitable access to electricity for all citizens, including those in remote regions.

Document Title: Law 18621 - Creation of National Public and Permanent Emergency System (2009)
Family Title: Law 18621 - Creation of National Public and Permanent Emergency System (2009)
Family Summary:
This law creates the National Fund for Disaster Prevention and Response. This Fund will be exclusively used to cover the prevention, mitigation, response and rehabilitation activities of the National Emergency System. The National Emergency System will have ownership and availability of the entire Fund.The system involves a series of actions by competent state bodies to:

  • Prevent risks related to natural or human-made disasters, whether predictable or unpredictable, periodic or sporadic.
  • Mitigate and address the impacts of disasters when they occur.
  • Provide immediate rehabilitation and recovery efforts as needed.

Document Title: Recovery and reconstruction plan with transformation - adaptation and mitigation to climate change (Plan de recuperación y reconstrucción con transformación - adaptación y mitigación al cambio climático)
Family Title: Recovery and reconstruction plan with transformation - adaptation and mitigation to climate change
Family Summary:
This program aims to improve society's response capacity to the threats and risks generated by climate change by applying land management instruments.

This document summarizes the actions to be carried out in the Adaptation and Mitigation of Climate Change. The Plan focuses on three phases:

1) Recovery: Attention to the affected population;

2) Reconstruction: With a comprehensive approach to risk and safe investment; and

3) Transformation: Preparation of the territory, citizens, public sector and private sector in the face of climate change.

Document Title: National action plan for adaptation to climate change of the Republic of Guinea (Plan d'action national d'adaptation aux changements climatiques de le République de Guinée)
Family Title: National action plan for adaptation to climate change of the Republic of Guinea
Family Summary:
By ratifying the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in 1993, Guinea committed to working towards a sustainable development policy based on the rational use of natural resources and improving production techniques. The National Action Plan for Adaptation to Climate Change (NAPA) aims to set out urgent and immediate measures to adapt to the adverse effects of climate change.

It is the result of participatory work. It sets out existing endogenous knowledge, identifies the targets most vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change and proposes adaptation options. Twenty-five project profiles have been developed, divided according to the state of vulnerability of resources and socio-economic groups and covering the entire country. These projects improve water supply for various needs, particularly in rural areas, protecting the coastal zone, improving agricultural and livestock yields, safeguarding forest formations, promoting information, education and communication, etc.

Document Title: Water sector contingency plan (Plano de contingênciado sector de águas)
Family Title: Water sector contingency plan
Family Summary:
The country has been cyclically affected by extreme events caused by hydroclimatic factors. To respond to these events, the Water Sector has met annually to jointly develop a Contingency Plan, which constitutes a response instrument for floods and droughts.

The Contingency Plan now prepared presents the actions to be carried out during the rainy season by the Water Sector and the respective budget, taking into account the forecast of the hydrological scenario.

Document Title: Law 337 - Consolidated text, Law creating the national system for disaster prevention, mitigation and response (2019) (TEXTO CONSOLIDADO, LEY CREADORA DEL SISTEMA NACIONAL PARA LA PREVENCIÓN, MITIGACIÓN Y ATENCIÓN DE DESASTRES)
Family Title: Law 337 - Law creating the national system for disaster prevention, mitigation and response
Family Summary: The purpose of this Law is to establish the principles, norms, provisions and general instruments necessary to create and allow the operation of an inter-institutional system aimed at reducing risks through prevention, mitigation and response activities to disasters, whether natural or man-made.

Document Title: Forest fire prevention and fight policy in a context of extension and intensification of the risk due to climate change - Volume 1( Politique de prévention et de lutte contre l’incendie de forêt dans un contexte d’extension et d’intensification du risque dû au changement climatique - Rapport Tome 1)
Family Title: Forest fire prevention and fight policy in a context of extension and intensification of the risk due to climate change
Family Summary:
Faced with the increasingly worrying developments in the risk of ‘forest fires’ in the context of climate change, the Minister of the Interior, the Minister of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty, the Minister of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion and the Secretary of State for Biodiversity have entrusted the CGAAER, the Inspectorate General of Administration (IGA) and the Inspectorate General of the Environment and Sustainable Development (IGEDD) to carry out two missions relating to the intensification of the risk of forest and other vegetation fires and the extension of areas at risk by the middle and end of the century, and to forest and other vegetation fire prevention policies.

The report is in two volumes. The first is entitled ‘Coping in the short term’, and the second is entitled ‘Adapting to the change of era: learning to live with fire in the medium and long term’. The mission met with a very wide range of stakeholders (around 1,000 people) at national level and in the areas historically affected by fires and those where the risk of fire spreading is emerging. In addition, the team summarised the most recent scientific studies on climate projections up to 2100.In the first volume, the two missions put forward recommendations for significantly adapting the prevention strategy and continuing to improve fire-fighting, mainly through proposals for short-term action. Longer-term strategies, based on an analysis of the intensification and extension of the risk, are presented in Volume 2.

Document Title: Ordinance MF 964, of June 11, 2024
Family Title: Ordinance MF 964, of June 11, 2024, on the Eco Invest Brasil Programme
Family Summary: This Ordinance from the Ministry of Finance (MF) establishes the criteria for the eligibility of investments to the Eco Invest Brasil Programme, the allocation of resources, the processes for the qualification of financial agents and the rendering of accounts, as well as the governance structure of the External Private Capital Mobilisation and Exchange Protection Line, within the scope of the Programme, establishes the composition and powers of the Programme's Executive Committee and makes other provisions. It defines the economic activities eligible for funding under the Eco Invest Brasil Programme as those that contribute to ecological transformation, decarbonisation and increased resilience to climate change impacts, specifying the priority activities.

Family Title: Law 14.995/2024 on the Eco Invest Brasil Programme and other provisions
Family Summary:
The law establishes the Foreign Private Capital Mobilisation and Exchange Protection Programme (Eco Invest Brasil Programme), within the scope of the National Climate Change Fund (FNMC), established by Law No. 12,114 of 9 December 2009, with the following objectives:

I - to foster and encourage investments in projects that promote ecological transformation, especially in the areas of transition to sustainable practices and technologies, technological densification, bioeconomy, circular economy, energy transition and infrastructure and adaptation to climate change, among others;

II - to attract foreign investment to the country;

III - to make capital market operations feasible for companies, investors and financial institutions based in the country to raise funds abroad to finance projects that comply with the provisions of item I of this article;

IV - to support the development, liquidity and efficiency of the long-term foreign currency hedge market in the country.

The PCVR's actions focus on the population of urban areas, observing the criteria of diversity of gender, race, ethnicity, age, disability, income and location in the territory, and will prioritise metropolitan regions and municipalities with high social and climate vulnerability.

Document Title: Resolution CEFONTE 1 of January 13, 2025
Family Title: CNPE Resolution 5 of August 26, 2024, on the National Energy Transition Policy (PNTE)
Family Summary:
This Resolution from the National Energy Policy Council (CNPE) establishes the National Energy Transition Policy (PNTE), the National Energy Transition Plan (Plante), the National Energy Transition Forum (Fonte), and makes other provisions. The Resolution establishes that the aim of the National Energy Transition Policy is to guide national efforts to transform the national energy matrix into a low-carbon economy, contributing to the achievement of net greenhouse gas emission neutrality in the country. The Policy consists of a mechanism to support the integration and coordination of government policies and actions at the federal level, in conjunction with sub-national entities, and for dialogue with civil society and the productive sector, to consolidate national efforts. It must observe the objectives of the national energy policy for the rational use of energy sources in harmony with the international policies and commitments made by the country concerning climate change. It must also consider the other objectives of public policies, including initiatives and strategies to enable the ecological transformation of the Brazilian economy, the increased density of production chains and adding value in the country, and mitigation and adaptation to climate change.

The CEFONTE Resolution from October 1st, 2025 defines the criteria for appointing members to the Plenary of the National Energy Transition Forum - Fonte.

The CEFONTE Resolution from January 13th, 2025 provides for the Regulation of the Public Selection Process for the selection of civil society representatives to make up the Plenary of the National Energy Transition Forum - Source Plenary, for the 2025/2026 biennium.

Document Title: National Strategy for the Use of Carbon Markets (ENUMeC)
Family Title: National Strategy for the Use of Carbon Markets (ENUMeC)
Family Summary:
The National Strategy for the Use of Carbon Markets (ENUMeC) in the Argentine Republic is a framework that facilitates the development of carbon markets with the objective of reducing emissions and promoting sustainable development. These markets allow companies and governments to buy and sell emission rights, thus incentivizing emissions reduction and environmental compensation. The ENUMeC deepens the national position regarding the use of carbon markets and creates a common framework for their implementation in the national territory. Among the axes of the strategy are:

- Strengthen national and subnational access to climate financing.

- Participate in carbon markets regulated in the Paris Agreement and other national and international compliance markets.

- Accompany the participation of the private sector in voluntary markets.

- Generate non-commercial approaches and support subnational governments in the implementation of market schemes to fulfill their climate change response plans.

Document Title: National Climate Change Action Plan (NCCAP) III 2023-2027
Family Title: National Climate Change Action Plan (NCCAP) III 2023-2027
Family Summary:
The National Climate Change Action Plan (NCCAP) III 2023 – 2027 is the third five-year plan that presents the detailed priority actions that Kenya will embark on to address climate change in the medium-term planning period and contribute to the achievement of our NDC under the Paris Agreement. Its development has involved deliberate consultations with the youth and children’s representatives.

NCCAP 2023–2027 proposes priority actions for implementation over the five-year period. These actions are classified in eight (8) Climate Change Priority Areas: Disaster Risk Management; Food Security and Nutrition; Water, Fisheries and the Blue Economy; Forestry, Wildlife and Tourism; Health and Human Settlements; Manufacturing; Energy and Transport; and Children and the Youth. The priority actions, building on achievements from the 2018–2022 period, propose adaptation and mitigation interventions, as well as enabling actions to facilitate their implementation. An implementation matrix has been prepared for each priority area, with an estimated budget that will guide execution. Each Climate Change Priority Area has a set of discrete National Indicators, as well as Key Performance Indicators to enable tracking and reporting of progress over the 2023–2027 period.

Document Title: 10th Development Plan
Family Title: 10th Development Plan
Family Summary:
Key drivers adopted in the 10th plan are as follows:

- Introduce new programs and projects to increase value added of oil and gas resources in all production activities, and promote industries using these resources.

- Increase real value added of non-oil sectors annually by an average of 8.5% of GDP (at constant prices of 2010) and its share from 59.1% in 2014 to 66% in 2019.

- Growing the share of private sector in the GDP (at constant prices of 2010) from 44.9% in 2014, to 50.6% in 2019.

- Increasing the annual growth rate of the manufacturing industries sector from 8.36%in 2014 to 10.58% in 2019, and the Mining and Quarrying sector from 5.98% in 2014 to 8.56% in 2019.

- Increase in public investment is planned for the coming five years, about 2.4 trillion Riyal to finance development projects of the major sectors, including human resources, economic resources, social and health, and infrastructure. The 10th development Plan allocates 372 billion Riyals for spending on infrastructure, which is about 76% more than what was allocated in the 9th Plan. This will be accompanied by new measures for the rationalization of government spending. (http://g20.org.tr/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/g20_comprehensive_growth_strategy_saudi_arabia.pdf)

As a first step towards greater diversification, the plan envisages raising utilisation rates of mineral resources, diversifying sector activities and developing local processing of mining raw materials. In terms of petrochemicals, this will involve developing upstream and downstream industrial activities that depend on oil and gas. Production capacity in the industrial sector will also be expanded in line with the National Industrial Strategy, with an emphasis on projects related to the diversification of energy sources away from oil. The plan aims to increase the contribution of the services sector to GDP, with an emphasis on financial, tourism, transport, engineering, communications and IT services, according to the Ministry of Economy and Planning (MEP).(http://www.oxfordbusinessgroup.com/analysis/long-game-new-development-plan-shows-clear-commitment-education-and-private-sector)

Document Title: Corporate Average Fuel Economy Standards (CAFE)
Family Title: Corporate Average Fuel Economy Standards (CAFE)
Family Summary:
In 2014, Saudi Arabia established corporate average fuel economy standards (CAFE) to reduce domestic oil consumption. The standards aim to improve fuel economy in Saudi Arabia for total road transportation by 2025. (http://www.unep.org/transport/airquality/SaudiArabia.pdf)

The Saudi CAFE standard targets an improving in the overall fuel economy with an average of 4% annually. This would lift up the Kingdom’s fuel economy LDVs from its current level of 12 km per liter to 19 km per liter by 2025. (http://www.ecomena.org/saudi-arabia-fuel-economy/)

This regulation defines the fuel economy standard for all light duty vehicles (new vehicles and used import vehicles that weight less than 3.5t) incoming to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. This standard covers the period extending from July 1st, 2015 until June 31st, 2020.

Upper fuel consumption limit of 15.3 km/l (min 11.9 km/l) in 2015, to 18.5 km/l (min 13.9 km/l) in 2020 for passenger vehicles. For light trucks, the upper limits are 12.7 km/l (min 9.5 km/l) in 2015 and 15.4 km/l (min 10.7 km/l) in 2020. (http://www.puntofocal.gov.ar/notific_otros_miembros/sau810_t.pdf)

The standard asks for a minimum fuel consumption average of 10.3 liter for every 100 km for sedans. While an average of 9 liters for every 100 km for light pickup trucks. Document Title: Environmental Protection Act, 2025
Family Title: Environmental Protection Act 2025
Family Summary:
In 2025, Ghana passed its Environmental Protection Act 2025 (the Act) to consolidate laws related to environmental protection and formalise duties for the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to regulate and protect the environment, including the development of regulations around pesticide control and the management of hazardous waste (including electronic waste), and to act as the coordinating body for the country’s response to climate change.

Chapter 5 of the Act sets out the provisions on climate change, including the EPA’s responsibility for mainstreaming of climate change responses into national, sectoral and district plans, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders.

The EPA is also tasked with supporting the development of adaptation plans to enhance community resilience to the impacts of climate change, and to coordinate with various stakeholders (including relevant Ministries, departments, agencies, and private and civil sector organisations) to establish and operationalise enhanced data systems for planning and implementing adaptation measures. The EPA must also mainstream climate change disaster risk reduction into strategies and develop measures around the loss and damage resulting from climate change impacts.

The Act also establishes the Ghana Carbon Registry, to serve as a database for carbon market project activities both within and outside of the country, and to track the transfer of internationally transferred mitigation outcomes. The Act further establishes the Carbon Market Committee to approve various procedures related to the administration of the carbon market, including the approval of procedures related to determining eligible mitigation projects for the voluntary carbon market.

The Act establishes the Mitigation Fund to provide financial support for the implementation of authorised internationally transferred mitigation outcomes, and to provide funds to invest in additional mitigation measures and activities, and to support the operations of the Carbon Market Committee.

Document Title: Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (R-IRR) of Republic Act No. 9729, otherwise known as the Climate Change Act of 2009, as amended by Republic Act No. 10174
Family Title: The Climate Change Act (RA 9729), and its Implementing Rules and Regulations
Family Summary: The Act acknowledges the Philippines' vulnerability to climate change and the need for appropriate adaptation. It creates a comprehensive framework for systematically integrating the concept of climate change, in synergy with disaster risk reduction, in various phases of policy formulation, development plans, poverty reduction strategies and other development tools and techniques. The Act states the main principles of climate change policy: common but differentiated responsibilities; the Precautionary Principle; UNFCCC objectives (GHG mitigation and adaptation), and the Hyogo Framework for Action addressing disaster risk reduction. It adopts a gender-sensitive, pro-children and pro-poor approach. The Act establishes the Climate Change Commission as the sole policy-making body within government, which overseas, co-ordinates and evaluates climate change policies and plans. The commission is established under the office of the President (abolishing the Presidential Task Force on Climate Change, established in 2007) and has a diverse advisory board composed of government ministries and agencies. The Act requires the Commission to draft several policies: - A National Climate Change Framework, as a basis for research and action planning - A detailed National Climate Change Action Plan - A Local Climate Change Action Plan - guidelines developed by the Commission Additional powers and functions include: - Mainstreaming of climate change, in synergy with disaster risk reduction, into the national, sectoral and local development plans and programmes and co-ordinating climate change programmes of national government agencies - Recommending legislation, policies, strategies, programmes on adaptation and mitigation - Recommending key development investments in climate-sensitive sectors such as water resources, agriculture, forestry, coastal and marine resources, health and infrastructure - Creating an enabling environment for the design of relevant and appropriate risk-sharing and risk-transfer instruments and promotion of broader multi-stakeholder participation and integrate climate change mitigation and adaptation - Representing the Philippines in the climate change negotiations - Formulating and implementing guidelines for determining vulnerability to climate change impacts and adaptation assessments - Facilitating capacity building for local adaptation planning, implementation and monitoring of climate change initiatives in vulnerable communities and areas.

Document Title: Law No. 74/2024 on Climate Action
Family Title: Law no. 74/2024 on climate action
Family Summary: This law establishes the legal framework for Moldova to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 and the regulatory framework to make progress towards the global objective on adaptation to climate change. This law establishes the National Commission on Climate Change (the Commission), an inter-institutional governmental body which will coordinate and approve climate change policies and public capital investment projects in the context of climate change mitigation and adaptation, as well as natural disaster risk management. The Commission is to promote cooperation between different economic sectors; stimulate the inclusion of climate change measures in sectoral socio-economic development policy; coordinate the allocation of finances; and ensure transparency in implementation of climate change policy. This law also sets out the tasks for various ministries and agencies across the government.This law sets out the steps that should be followed and the information that should be taken into account in setting national GHG emission reduction targets; climate change adaptation targets; the Public Policy Strategy Paper on Long-term Low-Emission Development; the National Adaptation Programme for Adaptation to Climate Change; sectoral and local policy documents. It also includes articles on reducing fuel consumption such as in transport; monitoring and reporting; transparency; carbon pricing; liability for violation of this framework law and other laws approved pursuant to this law.

Family Title: Law on Climate Change
Family Summary:
This law determines Kosovo's mitigation and adaptation measures to climate change in line with binding international agreements, and its commitments to sustainable development and the transition to a carbon-neutral economy. It further establishes a monitoring, reporting, and verification system and defines the obligations and responsibilities of relevant state authorities.

The objectives of the law include 1) the reduction of anthropogenic emissions, 2) the strengthening of adaptation capacities, 3) the conservation and growth of carbon sinks, and 4) the promotion of economic development and job creation through the sustainable management of natural resources. To oversee the implementation of these objectives, the law establishes the Council of Climate Change, an inter-ministerial body, and the Scientific Advisory Board. To monitor, report, and verify greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, it relies on the National Inventory System, the Greenhouse Gas Inventory, and the Information System on Climate Change.

This law further aims to develop the Long-term Strategy for Decarbonization, and the Strategy and Action on Adaptation to Climate Change.

Document Title: Republic Act No. 10174 (amending Republic Act No. 9279)
Family Title: The Climate Change Act (RA 9729), and its Implementing Rules and Regulations
Family Summary: The Act acknowledges the Philippines' vulnerability to climate change and the need for appropriate adaptation. It creates a comprehensive framework for systematically integrating the concept of climate change, in synergy with disaster risk reduction, in various phases of policy formulation, development plans, poverty reduction strategies and other development tools and techniques. The Act states the main principles of climate change policy: common but differentiated responsibilities; the Precautionary Principle; UNFCCC objectives (GHG mitigation and adaptation), and the Hyogo Framework for Action addressing disaster risk reduction. It adopts a gender-sensitive, pro-children and pro-poor approach. The Act establishes the Climate Change Commission as the sole policy-making body within government, which overseas, co-ordinates and evaluates climate change policies and plans. The commission is established under the office of the President (abolishing the Presidential Task Force on Climate Change, established in 2007) and has a diverse advisory board composed of government ministries and agencies. The Act requires the Commission to draft several policies: - A National Climate Change Framework, as a basis for research and action planning - A detailed National Climate Change Action Plan - A Local Climate Change Action Plan - guidelines developed by the Commission Additional powers and functions include: - Mainstreaming of climate change, in synergy with disaster risk reduction, into the national, sectoral and local development plans and programmes and co-ordinating climate change programmes of national government agencies - Recommending legislation, policies, strategies, programmes on adaptation and mitigation - Recommending key development investments in climate-sensitive sectors such as water resources, agriculture, forestry, coastal and marine resources, health and infrastructure - Creating an enabling environment for the design of relevant and appropriate risk-sharing and risk-transfer instruments and promotion of broader multi-stakeholder participation and integrate climate change mitigation and adaptation - Representing the Philippines in the climate change negotiations - Formulating and implementing guidelines for determining vulnerability to climate change impacts and adaptation assessments - Facilitating capacity building for local adaptation planning, implementation and monitoring of climate change initiatives in vulnerable communities and areas.

Family Title: Working Guidance for Carbon Dioxide Peaking and Carbon Neutrality in Full and Faithful Implementation of the New Development Philosophy
Family Summary: This Guidance from the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council states that to realise the goals of carbon peaking and neutrality, the principles of national coordination, prioritising conservation, public-private collaboration, international competition and collaboration, and risk prevention must be followed. By 2030, the carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP shall decrease by more than 65% compared to 2005 levels and non-fossil fuel consumption shall reach around 25%. The Opinion contains actions including for green and low-carbon development planning; green production; adjustment of the industrial infrastructure and curbing the development of high-emission projects; accelerating the construction of a low-carbon and efficient energy system; accelerating the construction of a low-carbon transportation system; scientific and technological development; and improving the ability of carbon sinks. Document Title: National Action Programme for Adaptation to Climate Change (NAPA) (Programme d’Action National d’Adaptation aux changements climatiques (PANA))
Family Title: National Action Programme for Adaptation to Climate Change (NAPA)
Family Summary:
The development of the National Action Program for Adaptation to Climate Change (PANA) resulted from a participatory process based on fundamental studies, field surveys, consultations and numerous working meetings and workshops. This Action Program results from a preliminary analysis of the climate. This analysis revealed a climate change marked, over the last thirty years, by fluctuations in precipitation and a shift in the season, early and prolonged droughts, and an increase in the average temperature of around 1°C.

Particularly vulnerable are regions with low rainfall, generally located to the east of each island, with relatively high demographics and incidence of poverty and presenting conditions favourable to the development of malaria and water-borne diseases, with abundant water—precarious housing. Most degraded soils are found in these areas where coastal erosion is also very pronounced.

The PANA is structured around the following four main axes:

1. A general view of the geographical, environmental and socio-economic context of the Comoros;2. An analysis of climate variability and observed and projected climate changes; the influence of climate change and climate variability on biophysical processes and key sectors, as well as the identification of particularly vulnerable groups and areas;3. The objective of the NAPA, the implementation strategy, including its links with development programs and Multilateral Environmental Agreements;4. An inventory of adaptation options in the face of climate change, the conditions for systematic integration of adaptation into development planning, and the methodology used to classify and prioritise adaptation options.

Family Summary:

This revised Haitian strategic framework for disaster risk management integrates the issue of climate change and human security. It emphasizes gender sensitivity, the inclusion of people living with disabilities and universal access during the intervention and reconstruction phases. Investment protection, risk transfer, public and community governance of disaster risks, the organization of volunteering and accountability are also integral parts of it. Furthermore, this plan is based on a common vision by focusing action on the role of individuals and communities in disaster risk management. It favours a participatory, inclusive approach and an integrated and holistic strategy.

Document Title: National action plan for adaptation to climate change (Plan d'action national pour l'adaptation aux changements climatiques)
Family Title: National action plan for adaptation to climate change
Family Summary:
In Senegal, a poor country where rural populations experience this poverty intensely, there is a need to understand climate change better to develop adaptation measures to this vulnerability.

The adaptation options identified in this policy and prioritized with the participation of the populations constitute programs favourable to the increase of actual capacities to cope better, over time, with climatic variabilities, which are still challenging to predict, and to which our countries, in particular those listed among the least advanced, are faced. These programs contribute not only to the fight against resource degradation but also to capacity building to improve sources of income.

The current vulnerability is mainly linked to the strong dependence of Senegalese agriculture on rainfall, which is becoming rarer over time and whose interannual variability is difficult to predict. The recommended adaptation solutions are inspired by technological achievements, whether nationally or internationally. They also take into account feasibility and, as far as possible, economic profitability. Some of these techniques are long-term investments that public authorities must support and subsidise.

Document Title: Master plan for the prevention and mitigation of natural disasters ( Plano director para prevenção e mitigação das calamidades naturais)
Family Title: Master plan for the prevention and mitigation of natural disasters
Family Summary:
With the consolidation of the Action Program for the Reduction of Absolute Poverty, the Government considers that preventing the effects of natural disasters cannot be reduced only to short-term actions identified in the PAC.

To achieve these objectives, the Government has identified the following actions:

  • Carry out mapping of risk areas.
  • Strengthen the means of the early warning system.
  • Mobilize resources to prevent and mitigate the effects of natural disasters.
  • Strengthen intersectoral institutional coordination in response to the effects of disasters.
  • Strengthen regional and international coordination, particularly in river basin management.
  • Create a database that enables studies to be carried out in the areas of climate and its impacts.
  • Promote the construction and use of water storage systems in dry zones for human and animal consumption and irrigation.
  • Intensify civic training actions.

Document Title: National risk management program (Programa nacional de gestion de riesgos)
Family Title: National risk management program (2017)
Family Summary:
The Ministry of Defense, through the Vice Ministry of Civil Defense - VIDECI, develops actions to institutionalise Risk Management in Bolivia in its role as responsible for defining policies strategies and coordinating and implementing risk management tasks, creating the four processes established by the Risk Management Law No. 602: identification and knowledge of risk, risk reduction, disaster and/or emergency care and financial protection; which are part of the supreme goal of the State "Living Well" within the scope of the 2025 patriotic agenda. The present National Risk Management Program responds to the initiatives framed in RM No. 0613, which projects the strategies for risk management, contributing to the construction of schemes to coordinate and articulate the different territorial, institutional and social areas, including guidelines, directives, tools, technical and operational actions, to increase the resilience capacity of the Bolivian population.

The Bolivian National Risk Management Program is the instrument for the National System for Risk Reduction and Disaster Response (SISRADE) to carry out actions protected by Law 031, Law 602 and DS 2342 and other legal provisions, which define the processes, objectives, actions, those responsible and budgets for Risk Management in Bolivia. This document is structured based on 2 components: One general, which includes the objectives of the project, the legal framework, the national policy, the goals and those responsible for the implementation for the period 2016-2020 to ensure its continuity; and another specific, corresponding to the strategic part that seeks to strengthen the national capacity in the different aspects of risk management based on 3 strategic lines.

1. Strengthen VIDECI to promote resilience in recurring municipalities under a culture of prevention through equipment, training and dissemination.

2. Strengthen municipalities at high risk of disasters to reduce their vulnerability through institutionalising UGRs with guidelines, directives and methodologies.

3. Implement in recurring municipalities, early warning systems, consolidated and integrated into the national early warning system, through the technical and scientific strengthening of SINAGER-SAT.

Document Title: German strategy to strengthen resilience to disasters: Implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030) - Germany's contribution 2022-2030 (Summary)
Family Title: German strategy to strengthen resilience to disasters: Implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030) - Germany's contribution 2022-2030
Family Summary:
The Federal Government's strategy for strengthening resilience to disasters (resilience strategy for short) will make Germany more resilient to crises in the long term. The Federal Government is pursuing a holistic strategic approach in order to invest in prevention and to better cope with and recover from disasters and crises: The resilience strategy shows what efforts are already being made to this end and where overarching action is required in five specific fields of action:

  • Understanding disaster risk.
  • Strengthen intuitions to manage disaster risk.
  • Invest in disaster risk reduction to strengthen resilience.
  • Improve disaster preparedness and enable better recovery.
  • International cooperation

Crises and disasters have accompanied mankind since time immemorial. However, our recent past, our present and a look into the future show that crises and disasters present us with new and changing challenges. In Germany, risk and crisis management are national tasks and an integral part of our security architecture. Security is a fundamental human need for which the state bears a special responsibility. We must therefore place people at the centre of our initiatives to strengthen resilience to disasters.

Family Title: National Response Plan with a Multi-Threat and Health Approach 2020
Family Summary:
In 2008, the Government of Reconciliation and National Unity (GRUN) presented the National Response Plan (PNR) as a regulatory instrument of SINAPRED reference for the coordination of response plans, as well as for the development of policies, strategies, conceptual and methodological instruments that allow for the generation of common planning for all response actors at the institutional, sectoral, and territorial levels. In light of the achievements and progress of the last 12 years, a new version of the National Response Plan is being presented, updated and in line with the state of risk management in our country.

This document is organized into 10 chapters. The first three are introductory and contextual aspects (this Introduction, Regulatory Framework, and Objectives). This is followed, in a logical order, by the definition of scenarios from a multi-hazard approach, the national response organization, alert systems, the sectoral and institutional response strategy, activation of the National Risk Management Plan (PNR), and support systems and resources. A chapter on post-disaster recovery concludes the PNR, emphasizing that pre-disaster recovery planning and preparation must occur alongside response preparation, and highlighting progress and prospects for strengthening this aspect of comprehensive risk management.

Family Summary:
The Congo is engaged in the process of developing its national action program (PAN) to combat desertification by defining priority actions. According to article 10 of the CCD, the National Action Program to Combat Desertification aims to identify the factors that contribute to desertification and the concrete measures to be taken to combat it and mitigate the consequences—effects of drought. The PAN specifies the role falling respectively to the State, local authorities and land users, and the available resources. To this end, and because of the very significant impact of anthropogenic factors on land degradation, mainly Due to the poverty of the populations, the specific objectives targeted by the Congo PAN are as follows:

  • improve knowledge of land degradation (mapping);
  • develop and strengthen capacities (monitoring and evaluation system);
  • improve the institutional and legislative framework for the fight against land degradation;
  • improve the living conditions of populations;
  • rehabilitate areas affected by land degradation.

As part of the fight against rural poverty, the program provides for improving the living conditions of populations through developing projects to combat poverty and creating income-generating activities. About improving the resilience of livelihoods in the face of threats and crises having repercussions on agriculture, nutrition and food security, a project entitled “Support for capacity building to finalize the National Action Plan to Combat Land Degradation » was initiated in 2004 by the Republic of Congo and submitted to the GEF for financing. Its objective is to contribute to capacity building and develop the National Action Plan to combat land degradation for sustainable management. The activities planned in this framework are:

  • appropriate and popularize legal standards in the fight against land degradation;
  • develop and strengthen human and institutional capacities;
  • improve knowledge of the state of the land;
  • strengthening institutional capacities and national and international partners for mobilizing funds;
  • develop strategies aimed at mitigating factors contributing to land degradation;
  • raise awareness, educate and train all national stakeholders.

As part of governance, the national coordinating body was established to implement the convention on combating land degradation. This body, the National Committee for the Fight against Degradation, is under the supervision of the Ministry in charge of the environment. To combat land degradation, the PAN plans to ensure the participation of all stakeholders or all human resources (technical services, civil society) in designing, implementing and monitoring the actions envisaged in this program. Therefore, the capacities of those involved in the program are needed. Alongside NGOs, several public education and research establishments must participate in developing and implementing the NAP.

Document Title: National disaster risk reduction strategy (Estratégia nacional de redução de riscos de desastres)
Family Title: National disaster risk reduction strategy
Family Summary:
The National Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy (ENRRD) responds to and implements a series of national instruments and policies relevant to implementing the various elements and dimensions of disaster risk reduction. This strategy complies with and respects all the basic principles and provisions of the Constitution and fundamental laws of the Republic of Cape Verde. It is interconnected and supported by other national policies, plans and legislation relevant to disaster risk reduction. Provides the mechanisms to align, validate and strengthen all policies, strategies, regulations and other instruments relevant to disaster risk reduction, such as spatial planning, building codes and standards, sustainable management of natural resources, environmental conservation and protection ecosystems, social protection systems and public health, among others. It provides the motivation (incentives and sanctions) to ensure compliance and reinforce compliance with these instruments designed to reduce exposure and vulnerability.

The policy provides a framework for the systematic and cross-cutting integration of disaster risk reduction into national and sectoral policies and plans and those relating to decentralization, development and local governance. ENRRD wants to encourage reviewing or modifying some of these policies and other instruments to strengthen the integration of disaster risk reduction or give more explicit and practical formalization to disaster risk reduction. For sectors currently in a strategic planning phase, ENRRD aims to demonstrate the relevance of the integration of risk reduction and provides general guidelines for the sector's contribution to the general objectives of disaster risk reduction and resilience of Cape Society Verdiana.

The policy lays the foundation for an efficient cross-sectoral legal framework for disaster risk reduction to be promoted by key sectors and partners and enacted by Parliament to provide the necessary authority for its implementation.

This strategy affirms the government's commitment to the integration of disaster risk reduction and adaptation to climate change in a coherent way in national, sectoral and local development plans and policies, resulting in integration in instruments such as the Strategic Plan of Sustainable Development (PEDS); in fiscal instruments, frameworks and public investment systems; in strategic policies, plans and sectoral programs; and in decentralization frameworks and local development programs.

In principle, the addition of new self-provided coal-fired units will no longer be permitted. The PNPC has planned results for the public administration period 2014-2019 based on the Five-Year Development Plan and expected results until 2030 based on the international commitments to implement the 2030 Agenda, The Paris Agreement, COP 21, and the Sendai Framework, these international commitments are country commitments and the following public administrations must take up their implementation in their five-year planning cycles.

The approach used in planning for the GIRRD is intersectoral, interinstitutional and multidisciplinary. It includes prevention, mitigation, response, and post-disaster recovery in its design, and its actions indicate that all public entities, the private sector, and civil society are involved in its execution. The premise of the planning is that to the extent that the risk is known, the person will be better prepared to prevent, mitigate and confront them in a timely and effective manner for recovery.

The PNPC is divided into five chapters: the first addresses the national and international regulatory legal framework that regulates the PNPC; the second the institutional framework that, due to its intersectoral nature, is needed to execute the PNPC; The third chapter interrelates the PNPC with the Sendai Framework, the SDGs and the Five-Year Development Plan 2014-2019 of El Salvador; The fourth articulates the conceptualization of the prevention, mitigation, response and post-disaster recovery components. The fifth chapter develops the strategic framework of planning, its philosophy and executive direction by establishing the mission, vision, objectives, priorities and strategic lines of action; finally, the sixth chapter defines the guidelines for post-disaster recovery.

Document Title: National strategy on Community Forestry
Family Title: National strategy on Community Forestry
Family Summary:
This National Strategy for Community Forestry aims to strengthen the capacity of provincial authorities and ensure that the country’s community forestry laws do in fact include and benefit communities. The plan calls for an “experimental phase” over the next five years to gradually provide access to areas of the roughly 700,000 square kilometres of available forest through community management permits and to test different approaches to community forestry through a number of officially recognised pilot projects.

The implementation of the National Strategy should be ensured on four axes:

1. the establishment of a steering committee (national and provincial);

2. the regular convening of the Roundtable on Community Forestry (at both national and provincial levels) to intensify the dialogue between stakeholders involved;

3. establishing a database of local community forest concessions;

4. ongoing monitoring of these concessions to assess the impact on forest protection, as well as drivers of deforestation and degradation.

In French: Stratégie Nationale pour la Foresterie Communautaire.
